# ✅ FIXED 2026-10-16 — AUTOSAVE-ERR (data-loss): `check_auto_save` discarded
# `save_binary`'s `Err` (`is_ok()` toasted only on success) and still advanced the
# 120s timer, so a failed auto-save was invisible. Serialize failures were
# stderr-only. The write already went through `save_binary` → `atomic_write`
# (sibling temp, sync_all, rename) and did not open the previous auto-save or
# the project file. Fix: log every failure in full, toast `Auto-save failed:`
# plus that error once per distinct text, retry on the next normal interval,
# and toast `auto-save restored` when a later write succeeds.

# byte-for-byte: v=741 f=542, closed/manifold/fold-free — so every topology gate PASSED — but
# 9 faces BENT by up to 0.011 (a 27-gon floor that had swallowed the rounded channel, five
# 18-gon arch facets that had swallowed grazing cutter strips) and vol 12.662348 vs the exact
# kernel's 12.657803 (0.8 % of the carved volume; invisible to the whole-mesh 1e-3 gate).
# ROOT CAUSE (stage by stage): the exact kernel + rebuild were CORRECT (raw v=743 f=598);
# `post_boolean_polish` step B `dissolve_coplanar_edges_iter` (core_math mesh_boolean/
# rebuild.rs) merged faces whose NORMALS agreed within POST_BOOL_DISSOLVE_DEG = 12° — an angle
# test, not a coplanarity test (its own doc said "unsafe for N≥30"). Every merge re-averaged
# the merged face's normal, so the chain walked strip by strip around the round. Steps A
# (limited dissolve) and D (T-pin spur / dissolve_vertex) used the same 12° rule, and
# `merge_coplanar` (2.56° + 2.5e-3 slab) ate the cutter's 1.4° strips the same way. The bent
# n-gons then re-triangulated for display as the stray edges / slivers in the screenshots.

# faces lies within float precision (`surface_eps` = bbox·1e-5, the scale mark_contact_verts
# already uses for "on the surface") of ONE plane, anchored on the LARGEST face (a CSG sliver's
# normal is noise, its vertices are not). B and D now use it; A protects every candidate edge
# that fails it (`bent_half_edges_of`); `merge_coplanar` anchors on the larger region root at
# the same precision. AFTER: v=743 f=600, 0 bent faces (worst 1e-6), vol 12.657803 == exact,
# big faces still restored as n-gons (137-gon, 69-gon). Gates:
# `difference_keeps_every_strip_of_a_fine_round_bevel_cutter` (core_math; 32/64 strips,

# before: 9 bent, worst 0.01115). core_math: only the 3 known reds (+ pre-existing

# ✅ FIXED 2026-10-11 — KNIFE-K-REPRESS-SILENT-CANCEL (owner: "when i try to k rectangular,
# pressing r do not trigger"; poly edit, K by key, R → nothing, no toast). The dispatch was
# sound: driving the REAL `handle_keyboard` with synthetic egui key events (new
# `knife_r_key_dispatch_tests`, poly_knife.rs) proves `K` → knife armed → `R` → rectangle armed
# from poly edit AND from the sculpt room. ROOT CAUSE was the repeat chord: since 2026-08-06 a
# shape cut KEEPS the knife armed (rect mode, by design — `shape_release_keeps_kind_armed`),
# so the user's next `K` landed on an already-armed knife, and `poly_activate_knife`'s same-key
# path (2026-07-18, written when the knife still exited after every cut) CANCELLED the tool with
# no toast. R then had no knife to arm → nothing, no toast; the drag fell through to click-select.
# FIX: same-key `K` on an armed knife follows the sibling convention (bevel `B` / hinge): a cut in
# progress (shape being dragged / ≥2 free points) is COMMITTED like Enter/release; an idle armed
# knife RESTARTS fresh (free line, points cleared, toast) and stays armed, so `K, R, drag` means
# the same thing on every cut. Esc / RMB remain the exits. Tests:
# `k_on_armed_idle_knife_restarts_it_and_r_arms_rectangle_again`,
# `k_with_free_points_in_progress_commits_the_cut`, `k_then_r_arms_rectangle_from_poly_edit`,
# `k_then_r_arms_rectangle_from_poly_sculpt_room`. Ruled out on the way (worth not re-deriving):
# egui 0.29 multipass does NOT replay key events (`begin_pass(new_input.take())`), clicking a
# button never takes keyboard focus (`request_focus` only in TextEdit/DragValue), no other
# dispatcher acts on R (`ACT_ROTATE` is read only in handle.rs), user keybinds.json is empty.

# ✅ FIXED 2026-08-19 — SMOOTHTOOWEAK (owner: "smooth strength is capped too low, need
# much more powerful"): poly Smooth ran ONE Jacobi step per frame under an ABSOLUTE
# 0.45·mean-ring-edge travel clamp — on dense meshes that is glacial no matter the
# strength. The clamp is a STABILITY bound (raising it overshoots the neighbor average and
# folds dense meshes), so strength now scales the number of clamped passes per frame
# instead: s ≤ 0.5 → 1 pass (old feel), s 1 → 2, s 2 → 4 (cap 6) — up to ~2 mean-edges of
# travel per frame, stable at every step. Brush-region verts iterate against each other;
# out-of-brush neighbors stay pinned (natural boundary).

# ✅ FIXED 2026-08-18 — POLYGRAB-NOSYM (owner: "move tool does not work with symmetrie"):
# the anchored poly Grab (Move brush) bypassed the stamp path's octant mirror entirely —
# one anchor, no mirrored instances. FIX: poly_grab_begin expands the anchor across each
# enabled LOCAL mirror axis (same octant expansion as stamps) and folds all instances into
# ONE per-axis SIGNED weight per vert (PolyGrabAnchor.weight: Vec<f32> → Vec<Vec3>):
# mirrored verts move with the mirrored offset; overlapping contributions blend as
# Σ(w·mask)·(max_w/Σw) so a vert ON the mirror plane loses its cross-plane component and
# stays welded to the plane (no seam split, no doubled tangential pull); symmetry-off is
# bit-identical to the classic scalar grab (w·(1,1,1)). The per-frame update rule is
# unchanged (`orig + offset_local * weight`, now component-wise) — zero per-frame cost.
# Deterministic frozen set (HashMap sorted). Pinned by poly::sculpt::grab_symmetry_tests
# (exact mirror, on-plane weld, sym-off parity); all 4 pre-existing grab pins green.
# NOTE: the VOXEL Move (GPU mesh_grab) also lacks symmetry — separate path, not touched.

## 2026-08-15 (master) — BEVELFLATSEAMCAP: a flat boolean seam landing on a corner breaks the rounded cap — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner + screenshots: *"bevel bug, the edge from the boolean create a 4 eges that break rounded cap."*
A cylinder-subtract leaves coplanar support seams running from the hole rim out to the box corners.
Bevel everything except those seams (what Smart Select does) and the corners they land on come out
as a flat facet with hard edges instead of a rounded corner.

- ❗ **ROOT CAUSE — a BROKEN RIM, not a cap problem.** At a corner where a lone unbeveled edge sits
  between two beveled ones, each of the two flanking rails was slid onto that edge **independently**
  (`rail_endpoint_pos`'s `w/sin` terminal slide) and they land on **two different points** unless the
  corner is symmetric. The corner rim was therefore a 10-point ring, not the 9-point chained arc ring
  the M_ADJ dome requires, so the dome declined it.
- **Blender's actual rule, measured against the oracle** (`docs/planning/poly/flat_edge_corner_ref.py`,
  new): ONE BoundVert = the two edges' rail meet **projected onto the in-between edge**. Verified
  vertex-exact on a box stretched to sx ∈ {0.5,1,2,3}. ⚠ **A cube is a trap fixture** — there every
  candidate rule gives the same point, which is how this survived so long.
- **The 2026-08-04 "skip the cap when every unbeveled sector is flat" fix was a BANDAID and is
  REVERTED.** It was only ever measured at seg=1, where the end-of-pipeline seal's flat n-gon happens
  to be the right shape; at seg>1 the same skip discards the dome. The cap was never redundant — it
  was duplicating the seal, because the rim was broken.
- **Why it was invisible:** the closed-input SEAL closed the leftover rim with one flat n-gon, so the
  result was watertight, manifold, fold-free and passed `bevel_result_installable` with no log line
  anywhere. Classic watertight-but-wrong (BEVEL.md §0 rule 6). The seal now logs `[BEVEL] SEAL:` at
  seg>1 so the next instance of this class is visible instead of silent.
- **Second, louder failure fixed by the same change:** on that mesh at width 0.1 the bevel came out
  **non-manifold with a hole** at seg=1 AND seg=3, so the install guard rejected it and the user saw
  **no bevel at all**. Now watertight at every width tested.
- FIX (all in `core_math/src/bevel_op`): new `project_meet_onto_edge` (`offsets.rs`) used by
  `build_boundary_flat`'s one-between-edge branch (`loop_slide_meet2` demoted to degenerate fallback);
  STEP 2b routes **every** mixed corner (`3 ≤ n_bev < degree`) through `build_boundary_flat`, no longer
  only span corners and no longer only when rounding; the flat-sector cap skip deleted.
- GATES: `flat_unbeveled_edge_must_not_break_the_rounded_corner` (oracle lock, symmetric + asymmetric),
  `boolean_seam_corner_rounds_like_a_clean_corner` (the owner's real boolean geometry, 4 width/segment
  combos, asserts installability). **151 bevel gates green; core_math lib 1183 passed**; `cargo build
  -p app` dev + release clean. Full account: BEVEL.md §11 2026-08-15 + the superseded-entry note in §6.
- ⚠ Pre-existing REDs in the tree, confirmed by revert-and-rerun, NOT from this change:
  `edge_select::directed_loop_crosses_pole_straight`,
  `mesh_ops::{apply_in_place_refusal_leaves_mesh_untouched, clean_mesh_still_refuses_slit_creating_dissolve}`,
  `serde_golden::golden_scene_graph_deserializes_exactly`, and the flaky timing bench
  `bench_display_mesh_ops`. Also fixed one committed-broken call so the suite could build at all:
  `core_math/tests/measure_bevel.rs` still passed 3 args to `bevel_edges_offset_mut` after it gained
  the `BevelWidthPolicy` parameter.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — REMESHSPIKE: Voxel Remesh always grew blades, internal shells and torn patches outside the source mesh — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner report + screenshot: *"REMESH ALWAY PRODUCE WEIRD GEON OUTSIDE OF ORIGINAL MESH"* — a row of
thin blades along the model's back ridge and a torn patch at the ear.

- ✅ **FIXED 2026-08-11.** **The remesh decided inside/outside from the nearest triangle's
  facing.** `band_scatter` (`io_bridge/src/mesh_to_sdf.rs`) signed each in-band cell with
  `(p − q)·n` of the single closest triangle. That predicate answers "inside?" only for a mesh
  that is closed, consistently outward-wound **and free of self-intersection**. Everything else
  got a full ±band error in exactly the cells the iso-surface is extracted from — hence blades.
  The sign flood could not repair it: `band_finalize` only rewrote *far* (NaN) cells and
  unreachable in-band *positive* cells, so a wrongly-negative in-band cell survived untouched.
- **REPRO (headless, `poly::remesh::tests::remesh_stays_on_the_source_surface`).** A remesh vertex
  is a lattice-quantised point on the source surface, so it cannot sit further from that surface
  than the quantisation. Measured at res 64, distance in cells, `>2cell` = defect count:

  | fixture | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | two interpenetrating boxes, one mesh (kitbash) | **3841 / 31798 verts**, max 2.46 cells, verts 31798 (vs 15950 correct — an internal shell) | **0**, max 0.00 |
  | sphere with **3** of 1472 faces reversed | **6521 / 28750**, max 2.53 | **0**, verts back to 15394 — identical to the clean sphere |
  | `new_torus` / `new_cone` (inside-out builders, see below) | **6256** / **8437**, whole surface bloated ~2.5 cells | **0** |
  | box, cylinder, both spheres (well-formed) | 0 | 0, byte-identical output |

  The kitbash case is the owner's model: at a point genuinely inside one part, the nearest
  triangle belongs to the OTHER part and faces away, so the cell reads AIR. Three flipped faces
  are worse than they look — they punch a channel through the near shell, the border flood pours
  into the interior, and the solid comes out as a hollow double shell.
- **FIX — sign is now topological, not directional** (`band_edge_crossings` + `flood_reach_crossings`
  + `band_finalize_topological`). Per lattice segment, a two-sided Möller–Trumbore test records
  whether a source triangle crosses it; the border flood is blocked by those crossings instead of
  by field sign, and a cell is air iff it is reachable from the region border **without passing
  through the surface**. No normal enters the decision, so winding cannot affect it, and enclosure
  by *any* part of a self-intersecting union is enclosure. Jordan–Brouwer makes the barrier
  watertight whenever the input surface is. Magnitudes still come from the scatter; cells where old
  and new agree are left untouched, so a well-formed mesh is bit-identical (golden gates pass).
- **Open meshes keep their crust.** If the flood reaches every cell, nothing is enclosed (open
  sheet, or a hole wider than a cell) — enclosure cannot define a sign, so the legacy facing-based
  flood runs instead, unchanged. Self-detecting: no watertightness test, no new parameter.
- **Not a perf regression — a perf win.** res 256, 51k-tri sphere: the crossing pass costs 5.4 ms,
  and the new flood is *faster* than the one it replaces (56.7 ms vs 77.6 ms) because a `u8`
  crossing test beats an f32 NaN/positive test. Net ≈ −15 ms.
- `sealed_pocket` keeps its meaning (enclosed cells the facing test put on the air side) and now
  also fires on self-intersecting / mis-wound input — which correctly forces those meshes onto the
  full stateless path instead of an incremental splice. `incremental_engages_on_a_closed_solid`
  still passes, so REMESHSOLIDNOINCR stays fixed.
- TESTS: 6/6 `io_bridge` golden gates (incl. the two bit-exact ones and
  `seeded_region_splice_matches_full_resample`), all 25 app remesh tests, plus the new gate above.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — PRIMINSIDEOUT: the Torus primitive (and a TriFan-capped Cone) were built INSIDE-OUT — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Found while proving REMESHSPIKE above, fixed on the owner's go-ahead.

- ✅ **FIXED 2026-08-11.** `HalfEdgeMesh::new_torus` and `new_cone`
  (`core_math/src/half_edge/builders.rs:399/436`) emitted reversed winding. Product-visible, not
  just a helper: `build_torus` routes **every full-arc torus** to `new_torus`, and `build_cone`
  routes a full, single-vsegment, sharp-tipped **TriFan-capped cone** to `new_cone`; every other
  configuration goes through `revolve` and was correct. That inconsistency is the tell — a 350°
  torus was wound outward while a 360° one was not.
- MEASURED (`primitive_spec::tests::every_closed_primitive_is_wound_outward`), signed volume of
  the built mesh, before → after:

  | primitive | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `torus` (default, and every full arc) | **−1.19453** | +1.19453 |
  | `torus minor_segs=8` | **−1.10360** | +1.10360 |
  | `cone cap=TriFan` | **−2.08096** | +2.08096 |
  | box / sphere / icosphere / cylinder / cone (NGon, None, frustum, vseg 3) | positive | unchanged |

- ROOT: the cone's base ring runs counter-clockwise seen from +Y, so sides wound
  `ring[s] → next → apex` and a base wound `centre → next → s` both face inward — reversed to
  `[next, s, apex]` and `[bc, s, next]`. The torus quad ran `a→b→c→d` = `∂θ × ∂φ`, which points at
  the major axis — reversed to `a→d→c→b` = `∂φ × ∂θ`. **Vertex indexing is untouched** (only the
  face ring direction changed), so the several callers that address the minor ring as
  `major*minor_segs + minor` are unaffected.
- WHY IT SURVIVED: viewport shading is double-sided, so an inside-out primitive looks perfectly
  normal. It is wrong for face normals, OBJ/glTF export, boolean operand orientation and mesh→SDF
  conversion — and the last of those is what made it visible at all, via REMESHSPIKE.
- GATE: `every_closed_primitive_is_wound_outward` sweeps all 8 kinds plus the cap-fill / arc /
  frustum / vsegment variants that switch between the two build routes, and asserts signed volume
  > 0 for every CLOSED result (open ones — plane, circle, uncapped tube — are skipped, since an
  open mesh encloses no volume and the check would be meaningless). Volume is the right total
  check here: it cannot be fooled by a locally-consistent but reversed patch.
- **Existing scenes are NOT retro-fixed.** A `.fl4` stores the built mesh, not the spec's geometry,
  so a torus created before today keeps its old winding — Mesh Cleanup → Recalculate Normals fixes
  it in place.

## 2026-08-12 (master) — BEVELCHANNELESCAPE: Smart Select silently cancels the Bevel's Geometry Channel — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner: *"review the bevel modifier, find bug, look at all toggles if they work."*

Full field audit of `PolyModifier`'s `bevel_*` state (UI → display-cache hash → evaluation → kernel
→ save/load). **The three historical trap classes are all clean on bevel**: no toggle is unread, no
toggle is missing from `hash_modifier_stack_into` (so none of them "look inert until a reset"), and
every `#[serde(skip)]` bevel field has a verified tail-section carrier — `bevel_consume` → `FL4PMODF`,
`bevel_var_width`/`bevel_width_min`/`bevel_auto_merge` → `FL4PBVAR`, channel extras → `FL4PSMTH`. The
`REMESHPARAMSAVE` class does not recur here. Painted edge weight (W) is genuinely live now: cache key
and rebuild gate share `PolyModifier::reads_edge_weight()`.

- ❗ **BEVELCHANNELESCAPE** (`poly/mesh_sync.rs`, the Bevel arm of `apply_one_poly_modifier`) — the
  near-90° "always bevel" safety net built its set by scanning **the whole mesh**
  (`all_live_half_edge_ids(result)`) and then re-inserted it unconditionally. The Geometry Channel
  had already narrowed `selected` twenty lines earlier, so every hard corner the channel excluded
  came straight back. **What the user sees:** mask a Bevel to a polygroup / edge-weight range /
  N-gon count, tick Smart Select, and the bevel jumps to the entire object's corners; untick Smart
  Select and the mask works again — i.e. "Smart Select ignores my selection". The rule is meant to
  override the exclusions Smart Select *infers* (geometry, tags), never the one the user chose by
  hand. Fixed by scoping the scan to `in_channel`, captured right after the channel filter and
  before any inferred rule (so the force-keep still overrides those, which is its job). When no
  channel is set `in_channel` is the full live set, so the unmasked path is bit-identical.
  **Gate:** `smart_select_never_escapes_the_geometry_channel` — measured 6 → **26** faces before the
  fix (a channel matching nothing still beveled all 12 cube edges), 6 → 6 after.
- ⬜ MINOR — the Segments slider is capped at `1..=8` (`properties_poly.rs`) while the field doc and
  the kernel clamp both say 1–32; 9–32 is only reachable by loading a file. Widen if 32 is intended.
- ℹ️ Toggles traced and WORKING: Width, Segments, Shape, Clamp Overlap, Consume Geometry (3-step
  fallback chain, fails closed, exclusivity with Variable Width is hard-cleared not just greyed),
  Variable Width + driver combo, Auto Merge Vertices, Limit by Angle + its slider, painted W weight.

## 2026-08-12 (master) — INTRUDEDEBRIS: the intrude push-through shatters the flat side planes, and it COMPOUNDS every cut — ✅ FIXED (poly), with its own setting

Owner: *"my intrude from extrude tool no longer works properly, it's supposed to clean the plane on
the side — maybe this came from the work on mesh clean up; if yes make sure that this tool has its
own setting for the clean up pass."*

**His hypothesis was wrong, and it is worth recording why.** The Mesh Cleanup work touched
`manifold_boolean` only to make it *more* aggressive (polish cap 2048→8192, soup dissolve promoted
to always-run and looped twice) and added `merge_by_distance_ex` — all strictly improvements. The
intrude tool also ALREADY had its own cleanup setting (`tweak.extrude_wall_cleanup`, Tool Parameters
→ "Wall cleanup", Off / Intrude only / Always). Neither was the cause.

**Diagnosed from his own data, not from theory.** `write_extrude_repro` had captured the exact
failing operation at `%TEMP%\azra_extrude_repro.json` seven minutes before he reported it. Replayed
through `replay_extrude_capture`:

```
target v=45 f=48        (already debris-laden from EARLIER cuts)
result v=41 f=42 tris=21 folds=3 zero_area=1 min_edge=0.000230
[POLISH] ... faces=42<=42          ← post_boolean_polish merged NOTHING
[SOUP]  re_dissolve_soup returned None   ← no coplanar candidate at all
[BOOL]  debris cleanup: eps=2.89e-5 ... folds 3->3   ← collapsed NOTHING
```

The flat side planes are pinned into triangle fans by clusters of near-duplicate vertices ~2.3e-4
apart, left where the cutter grazes an existing corner. **The kernel's own `collapse_epsilon_debris`
is capped at `bbox·1e-5` = 2.9e-5 — an order of magnitude BELOW the debris it is meant to remove**,
so it welds nothing; and `merge_coplanar` cannot dissolve across the resulting folds. Because each
cut takes the previous result as input, the debris accumulates — which is why the tool *degrades*
rather than failing outright, and why it feels like a regression.

**Threshold sweep on his mesh** (`diag_debris_threshold_sweep`, `#[ignore]`, `AZRA_BOOL_REPLAY=`):

| radius | welded | v | f | tris | zero-area | vol drift | manifold |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≤1e-4 | **0** | 41 | 42 | 21 | 1 | 0% | yes |
| 3e-4 – 5e-4 | 2 | 36 | 33 | 13 | **0** | 0.016% | yes |
| 1e-3 – 2e-3 | 4–5 | 33 | 34 | 13–15 | 0 | 0.015% | yes |
| 5e-3 | 18 | 22 | 24 | 11 | 0 | 0.034% | **no** |
| 1e-2 | 23 | 18 | 25 | 15 | 0 | 0.324% | **no** |

**Fix:** a debris-merge pass owned by the TOOL — `AzraApp::poly_extrude_merge_debris`
(`poly_drag_tools/extrude_drag.rs`), run inside `poly_extrude_try_push_through` and the redo-panel
re-run, so scrubbing depth reproduces the drag exactly. New setting `tweak.extrude_debris_merge` =
weld radius as a FRACTION of the mesh's bbox diagonal (Tool Parameters → "Debris merge", default
1e-4, 0 = Off) — his requested "own setting for the cleanup pass", and separate from "Wall cleanup",
which only collapses stacked coplanar walls. On his capture the default resolves to 3.3e-4, landing
in the measured-good band.

**Deliberately NOT done: loosening the kernel.** Both kernel limits — the `bbox·1e-5` epsilon and the
`preserved_vert_count` locality gate — are load-bearing ("a boolean must not change geometry it did
not cut"; owner 2026-08-08 *"mesh cleanup after a cut cleaned all my geo"*). Note the second gate
would refuse this weld even with a larger epsilon, because the debris verts ARE input verts of the
next cut. Relaxing either changes every boolean in the app. The tool that knows it just pushed a
prism through its own solid is the right owner of a more aggressive pass.

Authored edges (Smart Select `op_created`, Mark Sharp, seam, crease) are passed to
`merge_by_distance_ex` as protected pairs and are never welded. The pass fails CLOSED — any of
valid / manifold / closed / face-count / volume-drift(≤0.5%) tripping returns the unwelded result.

**Gates:** `epsilon_debris_welds_without_moving_the_surface` (`mesh_boolean/tests.rs`) pins all
three properties on a two-T-pin cube: a radius below the debris scale welds NOTHING (why `bbox·1e-5`
did nothing), a radius above it welds while keeping the mesh closed/manifold with zero volume
change, and a protected edge vetoes its own collapse. Plus the two `#[ignore]` iteration rigs
(`replay_extrude_capture`, `diag_debris_threshold_sweep`) and `[POLISH]`/`[SOUP]` gate tracing added
to `manifold_boolean` under the existing `AZRA_BOOL_DEBUG`.

**⚠️ NOT verified against the owner's own `.fl4` fixtures.** `intrude_owner_fixtures_pinned`,
`test_020_intrude_boundary_and_ctrl_x` and `test_021_along_normals_inward_keeps_planar_walls` — the
three end-to-end intrude gates — are currently red for an unrelated reason (SGBLOBSHIFT below), so
this change is pinned only at kernel level. Re-run them once that lands.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — BOOLCUTNOCARRY + APPLYNOCARRY + TAGSNOPERSIST: Smart Select tags (and every authored layer) were destroyed by Boolean **Cut**, Knife Cut, Join, Add-to-Mesh and Apply-modifier — and never survived a save — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner: *"smart select after boolean cut still forgets the tag on geo that was not touched — we need
to make sure the tag persists."*

**Not a kernel bug.** Measured first: `CustomData::remap_by_position` carries `op_created` across a
boolean with ZERO loss on geometry the cut did not reach (new gate
`op_created_survives_a_boolean_on_untouched_geometry`, `core_math/src/mesh_boolean/tests.rs` — a
beveled cube cut at the opposite corner keeps 100% of its tags). The loss was entirely in the app's
INSTALL sites.

- ❗ **BOOLCUTNOCARRY** — `poly_boolean_execute_cut` (`app/src/poly/boolean.rs`, the X-pie's **Cut**)
  installed a `merge_meshes(diff, inter)` REBUILD while leaving `cache.poly_custom_data` keyed by the
  OLD mesh's ids. That is worse than a clear: surviving entries land on unrelated edges of the new
  mesh, so untouched geometry loses its do-not-bevel tag while strangers gain one. Subtract / Union /
  Intersect have carried since BOOL-STALECD; **Cut never did** — which is exactly the op the owner
  named. Same hole in `poly_join` (Ctrl+J), `poly_add_primitive_to_body` (Shift+A), and both knife
  boolean installs (`Knife Cut`, `Knife Slice (Boolean)`).
- ❗ **APPLYNOCARRY** — `apply_poly_modifier_through` (the modifier card's **Apply**) had the same
  hole, plus a second one: it evaluated the stack with `&Default::default()` for BOTH the tag set and
  the authored channels, while the live display path evaluates the same stack WITH them. So Applying
  a Smart Select bevel (or any polygroup-/edge-weight-masked modifier) baked geometry the viewport
  had never shown.
- ❗ **TAGSNOPERSIST** — `op_created` was SESSION-ONLY. `PolyLayerRecord` carries uv/crease/seam/
  sharp/groups but not the tags, so a reopened file handed Smart Select nothing to skip and every
  operation-created edge beveled again (`SIDECAR_SURVIVES_BOOLEAN.md` §OPEN, owner TEST_06).

**Fixes.** ONE install entry point, `AzraApp::poly_install_rebuilt_mesh(nid, new_mesh, created)`
(`poly/mesh_sync.rs`), that replaces the mesh AND re-keys the sidecar in the same step via the
existing `carry_op_tags` policy — the class was "26 hand-rolled `*mesh = Arc::new(..)` sites, each
having to remember the sidecar separately", so the fix is structural, not per-site. Six sites routed
through it. `created` is `&[]` for Cut on purpose: the imprint seam is what the user asked the op to
draw, and tagging it would stop him beveling the loops he just made (fail closed — a tag is never
invented). Tag persistence rides a new self-delimiting **`FL4PTAGS`** tail section (`PolyOpTagRecord`
= node_id + half-edge ids), written last, emitted only when a body actually carries a tag → an
untagged scene stays byte-identical to a pre-feature save. This is the third attempt at persistence
and the first safe one: the two earlier ones put the data IN the blob (a field on `PolyLayerRecord`,
then a trailing `#[serde(default)] Vec`) and both corrupted every existing `.fl4` — bincode is
positional. The doc that concluded "version bump, re-derive, or give up" predates the tail-section
pattern; a tail section costs zero blob bytes, which is the whole reason it works.

**Gates.** `boolean_cut_keeps_tags_on_geometry_it_did_not_touch` + `applying_a_modifier_keeps_the_sidecar`
(`poly/mesh_sync.rs`, driven through the real app ops — both verified to FAIL with the carry removed,
`left: Some(false)`), `poly_op_tags_round_trip` (`project/tests.rs` — round-trip + the zero-bytes
half + FL4PBVAR still decoding after it), `op_created_survives_a_boolean_on_untouched_geometry`
(kernel). `cargo build -p app` clean.

**STILL UNCARRIED (audited, not fixed here — none is a boolean/cut path):** the Bevel *adjust* panel
re-run (`poly/bevel.rs:167`, re-bevels from `before` so the sidecar is keyed to the post-bevel mesh),
`poly/circle.rs` ×4, `poly/tosphere.rs` ×2, `poly/slide.rs` ×2, `poly/hinge_rotate.rs`,
`poly/primitive_source.rs`, `body_library.rs`. Loop cut is ID-stable in place and needs no carry;
`bool_material.rs` only re-stamps materials on unchanged topology.

**Also measured, NOT a significant contributor (recorded so it is not re-chased):** the whole-body
boolean runs the kernel in WORLD space and installs the LOCAL round-trip, then remaps local-vs-local.
`M⁻¹(M·p)` perturbs coordinates by ~1e-7, against a 1e-5 quantized key — a coordinate only changes
bucket when it lands within ~0.01 quantum of a boundary. A rotated+translated fixture lost ZERO tags
to it. Real but rare; if it ever surfaces, the fix is to remap in the kernel's own space
(`t_world_mesh` vs `res_world` — ids are identical either side of `transformed`).

## ❗ 2026-08-11 — SGBLOBSHIFT: `mirror_object_nid` breaks EVERY existing `.fl4` (found while testing the above; NOT fixed here — someone else's live edit)

`PolyModifier` gained an in-blob field in the working tree
(`core_math/src/scene_graph/node.rs`: `#[serde(default)] pub mirror_object_nid: u64`, inserted after
`mirror_merge_threshold`). Its comment says *"Append-only; pre-field .fl4 loads as 0"* — that is
false for bincode, which is positional and has no field tags, so `serde(default)` cannot rescue bytes
that were never written. Every existing save containing a poly modifier now fails to load.

Proof, independent of any other change: `cargo test -p core_math --test serde_golden` →
`golden_scene_graph_deserializes_exactly` FAILS with *"SceneGraph layout changed — .fl4 saves are
broken: Io(Kind(UnexpectedEof))"*. Downstream: `intrude_owner_fixtures_pinned`
(*"failed to fill whole buffer"*), `dc_gate0_committed_ref_fl4_loads_unchanged` (*"invalid u8 while
decoding bool, expected 0 or 1, found 63"*), `owner_bevel_segment_fl4_no_spoke_fan`,
`test_020_intrude_boundary_and_ctrl_x`, `test_021_along_normals_inward_keeps_planar_walls` — 5 app
tests + 1 core_math gate, all pre-existing relative to the tag work above and all one cause.

Fix direction: `#[serde(skip)]` the field and carry it on a tail section, exactly like `FL4PBVAR` /
`FL4PTAGS`. Left untouched here because `node.rs` had a live writer during this session.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — SYMFACECROSSTWICE + SYMWIPESILENT: Alt+X with a FACE chosen as the center punched holes and could silently delete the whole object — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner: *"can you check symmetrize alt x for bug, I feel when I chose a poly as center it create bad geo"*

Confirmed, two independent defects on that exact path. Reproduced headlessly with
`core_math/examples/sym_face_probe.rs` (new — it derives the plane the way the app does:
`app/src/sym_pie.rs::poly_sym_plane_from_selection` = average face centroid + average face normal,
then calls `HalfEdgeMesh::symmetrize`). Every pre-existing kernel test used an axis-aligned plane at
the GEOMETRY CENTER, so neither defect was covered.

- ✅ FIXED — **SYMFACECROSSTWICE: `bisect_plane` only split faces that cross the plane ONCE, and
  `delete_half` then KEPT the ones it failed to split.** After the edge-split pass, a sign change
  around a face ring can only happen through an on-plane vertex, so the ring reads as runs of `+`
  and `−` separated by zeros. A face crossing once has one `+` run and one `−` run and needs ONE
  chord — the old pass looked for exactly that ("one arc all-nonnegative, the other all-nonpositive")
  and gave up when it found none. A **non-planar** quad crosses its own plane TWICE: the ring reads
  `+,0,−,0,+,0,−,0` and NO single chord separates the sides. That face stayed straddling;
  `delete_half_eps` keeps any face owning a `+` vertex, so it survived into the kept half with its rim
  **0.087 off the plane — 87× the 0.001 weld threshold** — which `mirrored_across` could not weld:
  **8 boundary (open) edges plus a mirrored copy crossing back through the plane.** That is the "bad
  geo": holes and interpenetration. **Why a FACE plane triggers it specifically:** the plane is derived
  FROM a face, and any non-planar face straddles its own plane in exactly this alternating pattern —
  so the trigger is not rare, it is guaranteed (a Catmull-Clark-subdivided box hits it too).
  **Fix** (`core_math/src/half_edge/ops_misc.rs::bisect_plane`): split off ONE sign-pure arc at a time
  and re-queue both halves until nothing straddles, instead of one chord per face. Both arcs are
  required non-empty, so each split strictly shrinks both pieces (`k+2 < n`, `n−k < n`) — it
  terminates, and a straddling face always HAS such a chord (take a non-empty `+` run and the zeros
  bounding it). A `debug_assert!` now states the postcondition: no live face straddles the plane.
  Measured on the probe: still-straddling 1 → 0, boundary 8 → 0, max |signed distance| on the seam
  0.087 → 0.000000.
- ✅ FIXED — **SYMWIPESILENT: symmetrize could commit an EMPTY mesh and still toast "Symmetrized".**
  The kept half is the `+normal` side, and a plane taken from a selected face is TANGENT to the
  surface — every face of a convex body has such a plane — so the whole body sits on ONE side and one
  of the two flick directions keeps the side with nothing on it. `delete_half` then drops every face
  and the object is gone (undo-able, but silent). `poly_symmetrize_op` / `poly_mirror_instance`
  (`app/src/symmetry.rs`) now build the result on a CLONE, refuse a zero-face outcome with
  *"nothing on the kept side — flick the other way"*, and leave no empty undo entry behind.
- ⏸ **KNOWN, NOT FIXED — tangency pinch.** When the plane cuts a non-planar face, the pure-piece
  decomposition necessarily leaves one chord with the SAME sign on both sides (with 4 crossing points
  and diagonally-opposite `+` corners, no chordal decomposition avoids it). That chord lies in the
  mirror plane with kept faces on both sides, so the mirror adds two more faces to it → one 4-face
  edge (`is_manifold()` reports "directed edge a->b used by 2 faces"). The result is CLOSED, welded
  and correctly shaped — this is the surface genuinely touching the mirror plane. Removing it needs a
  saddle-center vertex and a fan split, which trades the edge pinch for a vertex pinch. Not attempted.
- ❓ **OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OWNER — is "the face's own plane" the intended meaning of a face
  selection?** The pie labels it `CENTER: SELECTION`, next to GEOMETRY / ORIGIN / PIVOT, which are all
  pure ORIGIN choices where the flick picks the axis; only SELECTION also overrides the normal
  (`sym_pie.rs::sym_resolve`). Using the face's own plane is what makes the plane tangent (half the
  flicks keep nothing) and what guarantees the plane cuts the selected face. Alternative, one line:
  use the face CENTROID as the origin and keep the flick axis as the normal. The EDGE branch
  ("the plane CONTAINS the selected edges", center-seam workflow) is unaffected either way.
  Left as-is — the face-normal behaviour is documented as deliberate and is not mine to change.
- Coverage: `bisect_plane_splits_a_face_that_crosses_twice`,
  `symmetrize_non_planar_face_plane_leaves_no_hole`,
  `symmetrize_tangent_face_plane_empty_side_is_detectable` (`core_math/src/half_edge/tests.rs`).
  Falsified against the old rule — the first two FAIL without the fix. 325 `half_edge` tests green,
  including `symmetrize_sweep_no_open_seams` (12 edges × 36 axis pairs) and
  `symmetrize_after_bevel_stays_closed`.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — CLEANUPCLOSEDGATE + CLEANUPMISSINGPASSES + RECALCNORMALSNOOP: Mesh Cleanup was a NO-OP on every open mesh, was missing 7 of Blender's 9 Clean Up passes, and Recalculate Normals never touched winding — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner: *"mesh clean up does not do a good job clean de mesh, can you look at blender mesh clean up
and add missing feature of our mesh clean up"*

- ⚠ **CLEANUPCLOSEDGATE — the headline.** `cleanup_mesh_with` grew out of the BOOLEAN repair path,
  where both operands are solids by contract, and it inherited that path's result bar:
  `boundary_half_edge_count(&out) == 0`. As the bar for a general Mesh Cleanup that was a silent
  OFF switch — **ANY mesh with a rim** (a plane, a sheet, an open shell, a scanned import: most of
  what a cleanup is aimed at) failed it, cleanup returned `None`, and the popup said *"Mesh is
  already clean — nothing to repair"* over a mesh that plainly was not. The correct invariant is
  that cleanup must not **tear** the mesh, so the gate is now
  `boundary_half_edge_count(&out) <= boundary_half_edge_count(m)` — the boundary may shrink (hole
  fill, loose-face removal, coplanar merge) but never grow, and a closed input still has to come
  back closed because 0 is the only count that is `<= 0`. Full `is_manifold()` is likewise now
  demanded only of inputs that HAD it (the 2026-08-03 `integrity()` directive: "all tools must work
  even on open / non-manifold shapes"); `integrity()` + `validate()` are required unconditionally.
- **CLEANUPMISSINGPASSES** — AZRA had 2 of Blender's `Mesh > Clean Up` menu (Limited Dissolve, plus
  its own fold/coplanar/T-junction repair). New kernel module `core_math/src/half_edge/ops_cleanup.rs`
  adds the rest: **Delete Loose** (verts / wire edges / isolated faces), **Degenerate Dissolve**
  (short-edge collapse + zero-area faces), **Fill Holes** (boundary-loop cap with a sides limit),
  **Make Planar Faces**, **Split Non-Planar Faces**, **Split Concave Faces**, and
  **Recalculate Normals**. **Merge by Distance** existed in the kernel but was never wired into
  Cleanup. All are reachable three ways: the Mesh Cleanup dialog (10 knobs), left Tool Parameters
  (same widget block — ONE `draw_mesh_cleanup_controls`, not two copies), and a new
  `Mesh > Clean Up ▸` submenu of single-pass commands. Every single-pass command routes through
  `poly_mesh_cleanup_apply` — the SAME install path as the dialog — so each inherits its gates,
  transaction, sidecar carry and report instead of growing a second path.
- ⚠ **Protection extended to the new welds.** `merge_by_distance_ex` / `dissolve_degenerate_ex` take
  the same protected-edge position list `CleanupOptions` already carried, and the union-find
  DECLINES the specific merge that would fuse a protected edge's two ends (per-cluster, not global —
  unrelated doubles still weld). Without this, adding Merge by Distance would have re-opened the
  2026-08-05 "cleanup breaks the tag system" bug from a new direction.
- **RECALCNORMALSNOOP** — `poly_recalculate_normals` (Shift+N) called `recompute_normals()`, which
  derives each face's normal FROM its winding. On the only mesh anyone presses Shift+N on — one with
  inconsistently wound faces — that computes a correct normal for a wrong-way face, i.e. changes
  nothing (`UNT_SUITE_REPORT.md` had already recorded it as a visual no-op after a flip). Now runs
  `recalculate_normals_consistent`: BFS winding propagation, then signed-volume orientation on
  CLOSED shells only (an open shell has no "outside" to orient to, so it is made self-consistent and
  left facing its seed). Detection detail worth keeping: this kernel twins `a→b` with `b→a` only, so
  two faces that both traverse a shared edge `a→b` **cannot be twinned at all** — an inconsistency
  shows up as two unpaired SAME-DIRECTION half-edges, which is the signal the pass keys on.
- ⚠ **Split Non-Planar uses |cos|, not signed cos.** The obvious test (angle between each corner's
  triangle normal and the face normal) reads a REFLEX corner of a perfectly FLAT concave n-gon as
  180° off, so a signed test shreds flat concave faces that have nothing wrong with them.
  Concavity is the OTHER op. Regression-tested (`split_non_planar_does_not_shred_a_flat_concave_ngon`).
- **No-op gate generalised.** It compared verts/faces/folds, with a hand-rolled exception for
  T-junction repair (invisible to all three). Filling a hole and splitting a concave face RAISE face
  count; re-winding a face or flattening an n-gon move no counter at all — all would have been
  computed and then thrown away. `CleanupStats::did_something()` is now the escape hatch, and the
  same per-pass tally drives the result popup ("Passes that fired"), because a run that welds a
  double AND fills a hole nets out to "nothing changed" on counts alone.
- **Defaults.** Merge by Distance 1e-4, Degenerate Dissolve 1e-4 and Delete Loose verts+edges are ON
  (they repair, and remove nothing the user authored). Loose FACES, Fill Holes, Make Planar and both
  Splits are OFF — they add, move or delete geometry, which is a modelling decision. **Recalculate
  Normals is OFF in Cleanup** for a specific reason: Blender does not put it in Clean Up either, and
  on a model with a deliberately INVERTED interior shell (a hollow import, a room, the inner surface
  of a glass) "orient outward" turns that cavity inside out. It stays one checkbox away, and it is
  its own menu command. Ctrl+X (empty edit selection) sets the full preset explicitly so the
  shortcut is deterministic whatever the panel was left at.
- **Scope note:** the `MeshCleanup` MODIFIER keeps its original three knobs. Exposing the new passes
  there means new SERIALIZED `PolyModifier` fields = a save-format change, which belongs in its own
  task; the stack's behaviour is byte-identical.
- Tests: 20 new kernel tests (`ops_cleanup::tests`), 4 new gate tests (`mesh_boolean::tests`), 4 new
  APP-path tests (`poly::mesh_sync::tests`) — the app path is what the owner uses, so an open sheet
  is verified through `poly_mesh_cleanup_now` → gates → transaction → installed mesh → report.
  `cargo test -p core_math` and `cargo test -p app` are at their pre-existing failure set (3 in
  core_math, 5 `.fl4` fixture-load failures in app — all present at HEAD `810d945`, none touched
  here: no serialized type changed).

## 2026-08-11 (master) — KNIFEBOOLTYPE / KNIFEDEPTHONEWAY / KNIFESELRESULT: the shape knife could only subtract, its E extrude went one way only, and a cut selected nothing — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner: *"knife cut should also auto set selection, set the resulting geo from boolean"* and *"with
shape knife tool pressing [I] should let you change the boolean type to intersection, U to union.
On the E extrude I can only go one direction, need to be able to go in and out for the union (watch
out for perfect plane alignment on the union, when drawing the shape on the surface)."*

- **KNIFESELRESULT** — `knife_select_after_cut` shipped OFF and, when on, only ever selected the rim
  EDGES. After a boolean the useful selection is what the boolean *created*: the cut walls, the
  pocket floor, the boss cap. New `knife_apply_boolean_result_selection` selects faces whose EVERY
  vertex is new (a face the boolean merely reshaped keeps a pre-cut vertex and is excluded), in Face
  mode, and falls back to the rim edges when the cut made no new face — which is exactly the
  open-mesh cookie-cut, since it REMOVES faces. Default flipped ON.
- **KNIFEBOOLTYPE** — `U` = Union, `I` = Intersect, same chord again = back to Subtract
  (`ACT_POLY_KNIFE_BOOL_UNION` / `_INTERSECT`). `I` shares its chord with poly Inset by STATE and is
  consumed first in `poly_handle_keys`, the pattern `E`/Extrude already uses. Only the `BoolOp`
  handed to `mesh_boolean` changes — one drawn outline, three operators. Also in Tool Parameters.
- **KNIFEDEPTHONEWAY** — `poly_knife_shape_depth_track` clamped the depth at 0, so the outward half
  of the axis was dead: the cursor moved, the number stayed 0, and a Union could never be given a
  height. Depth is now SIGNED (`> 0` into the surface = pocket, `< 0` out of it = boss) and
  `knife_cut_depth()` thresholds on `abs()`.
- ⚠ **The owner's coplanar warning, made structural.** A shape drawn ON the surface and extruded OUT
  gives the union a base cap exactly coincident with the face it stands on — two coplanar faces, the
  degeneracy the boolean fold class is worst at. The outward prism therefore spans `[-bite,
  +height]` with `bite = big*1e-3`, sinking its base INTO the solid. Costs nothing (that material is
  added anyway) and removes the coincidence. Height clamped `> 2*bite` so the cap can never fall
  below the base.
- Three refusals, all fail CLOSED with a message naming the key that fixes it: Union with no height
  (the unbounded prism would weld a rod 4× the scene bound through the model), Subtract pulled
  outward (it would shave a sliver), Union/Intersect on an open mesh or open outline.
- ⚠ **KNIFESELSCOPE — the regression the auto-select shipped with, caught the same day** (owner:
  *"you broke the click and drag cut feature with shape"*). Every knife verb reads a Face-mode
  selection as "cut only these polys", and the auto-select now WRITES one: after a rect cut the tool
  sat in Face mode holding the cut walls, so the next rect drag scoped itself to them and scribed
  instead of punching a hole. The gesture was fine — the *verb* had changed. **A tool's output must
  never read back as its input.** `knife_has_user_face_scope()` is now the one definition of "the
  user scoped this cut", used by all five read sites; it compares the live selection to
  `knife_last_result_faces` BY VALUE, so it self-invalidates the moment the user touches the
  selection (a flag would have needed clearing from writers that cannot run while the knife owns the
  pointer). Gate: `two_shape_cuts_in_a_row_both_punch_a_hole`.
- KB: `docs/planning/poly/KNIFE.md` §6.2 + §6.3. 53 app knife tests green (11 new).

## 2026-08-11 (master) — SAVEPARTNOSHOW: "Save to Part" wrote the .flb but the part never appeared in the library — ✅ FIXED (library)

Owner: *"SAVE TO PART NO LONGER WORK"* — the part never shows up in the Library panel.

- **The save was never broken.** `DETAIL.flb` (14:47) and `DETAILbox.flb` (14:48) were on disk in
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Azra/library/` with valid 21 KB matcap thumbs. The *catalog* was stale:
  `library_index.json` was last written 12:32 and listed 6 Bodies, none of them the new parts.
- **Root cause — a disk cache with a half-honoured invalidation contract.**
  `library_index_cache.rs` is a FOREVER index: no mtime, no directory stamp, no staleness check
  of any kind. It is only rewritten when a full scan installs (`poll_library_scan`). So every
  library-content mutation must do BOTH halves — clear `library.scanned` *and*
  `request_library_scan()`. Rename / delete / duplicate / folder ops all do. `poll_library_save`
  (`body_library.rs`) did only the first half.
- **Why half was not enough.** `ensure_library_scanned()` is gated on `ui2.library.open`
  (`app_update.rs:842`). Save a part with the Library dock collapsed — the normal case, since the
  entry point is an outliner right-click — and no walk is ever requested. On the next launch the
  cold-start path reinstalls the pre-save index and sets `scanned = true`, so the part is
  invisible **permanently**, not just until the panel opens. Only "Refresh library"
  (`force_library_rescan`) or `AZRA_LIB_RESCAN=1` could recover it.
- **Fix:** `mark_library_catalog_dirty()` (`content_library.rs`, beside `force_library_rescan`)
  does both halves with the contract in its doc comment; `poll_library_save` calls it instead of
  writing the bare flag. The rescan now runs whether or not the dock is open, which rewrites the
  index immediately — so a restart shows the part.
- **Note:** parts saved *before* this fix are still missing from the on-disk index. One
  "Refresh library", or any new save, rebuilds it with them included.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — VERTCONCAVEPICK: verts at sharp concave corners invisible + unselectable — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner: *"in certain angle or situation the certain vertex mostly in sharp concave shape are not
visible or selectable"* — screenshot: the inside corner of an open box, every other corner
carrying its green vert square, the circled one carrying none.

- **One root cause, both symptoms.** The overlay (`draw_poly.rs` `vert_visible`) and the picker
  (`poly_selection/pick.rs`) both ask the same question of the GPU select buffer: *did this
  vertex write its OWN id?* The vertex never wrote it, so it neither drew nor picked.
- **Why it never wrote it** (`render/src/poly_pick.wgsl` `fs_poly_pick_elem`): elements are drawn
  in a second pass with no depth attachment, keeping their id only when their own depth clears
  the **3×3 window MAX** of the pass-1 face depth. That reference assumes *some* neighbouring
  texel is FARTHER than the element. **At a concave corner none is** — an inside corner is a
  strict LOCAL MAXIMUM of surface depth, every direction along the surface leading toward the
  camera. Face depth is sampled at pixel CENTRES while the vertex sits at an arbitrary sub-pixel
  position, so the surface reads up to one pixel of depth slope NEARER than the vertex's exact
  depth and the vertex discarded itself. **Widening the window cannot fix it** — a local maximum
  stays the maximum at any radius, which is why this survived the 2026-08-07 PICKELEMID rework.
  Grazing angles make the per-pixel slope large, hence "in certain angles".
- **Fix:** the reference is now `window_max + (gx + gy)`, where `gx`/`gy` are the per-axis MAX of
  the two one-sided differences of the face depth around the element's texel — the sub-pixel
  error's own bound, measured from the depth buffer. No tunable constant, no backend dependence;
  where the window already reached background or farther geometry the term is irrelevant because
  the window max has won outright.
- **Proof (headless GPU, `render/src/tests_poly_pick_concave.rs`, 3 probes):** box inside corner
  at a grazing 3/4 view — corner vert id absent before / present after, with a convex silhouette
  vert as the control that always worked; a vert behind a solid quad stays absent; a vert buried
  0.4 units under a near-edge-on floor stays absent (the adversarial case for a slope-derived
  tolerance). The probes drive the SHIPPING encode: the two-pass wiring moved from
  `app/src/poly_select_gpu.rs` into `PickingPipeline::encode_poly_select` so the app and the
  tests cannot drift apart.

Owner: *"I was trying to subtract the yellow piece and it did not work"* —
`EDGE SELECT PROBLEM, BOLEAN PROBLEM.fl4`.

- **What the file actually contains** (dumped by the new `project::diag_edgesel_bool` diag, run

  * island 1 — 74 faces, **CLOSED** — the box (−1…3, −1…2.444, −1…1)
  * island 2 — 146 faces, **OPEN**, 36 boundary half-edges, at z −2.668…−0.939 — an unrelated
    shell about 3 units away in −Z, with **zero AABB overlap** with the cutter
- **Root cause.** The edit-mode island planner (`poly/boolean.rs`, `poly_boolean_plan`) extracted
  the selected island as the cutter and then fused **every remaining face** into ONE "remainder"
  mesh as the target — `mesh_from_faces(&mesh, &island_faces, /*invert*/ true)` — AABB-testing that
  fusion as a whole. So the target inherited island 2's 36 boundary edges, and
  `poly_boolean_execute`'s closed-input preflight refused the run: *"target is open (boundary
  edges) — solid boolean needs a closed mesh; fill holes or Solidify first"*. Both operands the
  user cared about were perfectly closed; a shell the cut cannot even reach decided the outcome.
  Twenty lines further down the same function already AABB-filters other **bodies** one by one —
  the remainder was the only place that skipped that rule.
- **Fix.** The remainder is split per island (`face_islands`, a new module-local partition that
  reuses `AzraApp::bfs_linked_vertices` — the same flood fill the cutter island uses, one BFS per
  component, O(faces+verts)) and AABB-filtered against the cutter. `IslandPlan` now carries
  `remainder_target` (islands the cutter reaches → the boolean target) and `remainder_passthrough`
  (islands it cannot reach → concatenated back **untouched**, never handed to the solid kernel),
  plus `remainder_exists` to keep the "island was the whole mesh → delete the node" case exact.
  The boolean result stays the FIRST part of the concatenation so `mat_plan`'s face indices still
  line up; passthrough, then the kept cutter, follow.
- Gates (`poly::diag_bool_island`, APP-PATH through the real X-pie `poly_boolean_execute`):
  `island_subtract_ignores_an_unreachable_open_island` (no operand reported open; body's
  `content_signature()` changes; the far island keeps exactly its own 4 boundary edges; result
  validates + manifold), `..._removes_the_cutter_and_carves_the_target` (islands 3 → 2),
  `..._keep_cutter_still_carries_the_unreachable_island` (islands stay 3), and
  `the_fused_remainder_is_open_but_the_reached_island_is_closed` — which pins the BUG as an
  assertion (the fused remainder the old planner built is OPEN, the reached island is CLOSED), so
  the regression cannot silently stop testing anything. Existing `poly::diag_bool_material` +
  `poly_knife` boolean suites unchanged and green; `cargo test -p app poly` 197 passed.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — POLYHOVERFREEZE: the poly hover highlight froze when the cursor left the viewport — ✅ FIXED

Owner: *"when I select a poly and click in viewport I still have a pale highlight sticking even if
the poly is no longer selected."*

- **Root cause.** `poly_hover_pick` is the ONLY writer that resets `poly_sel.hovered_vertex /
  hovered_edge / hovered_face / hovered_face_other` (it clears them at its top), and
  `input_viewport.rs` called it **only** under `response.hovered()`. Move the cursor to the
  properties panel, the outliner, the menu bar or another window and the hover state froze at its
  last value with the overlay still painted. A hovered edge draws in `hover_color` at `0.7 ×`
  width (`overlay_lines.rs:585`) — i.e. a *pale* version of the selection line — and it is
  independent of `selected_edges`, so deselecting does not remove it. The two sibling paths in the
  same function already do this correctly: `tool.hovered_face = None` and `tool.hovered_prim =
  None` are unconditional every frame, then refilled only when hovered. The poly sub-element hover
  simply never got its unconditional clear.
- **Not only cosmetic:** `poly_click_select` selects `poly_sel.hovered_edge` / `_face` /
  `_vertex`, so a frozen value is a click that lands on the element the cursor last touched rather
  than the one under it.
- **Fix.** Clear all four fields unconditionally before the `response.hovered()` gate, matching
  the two adjacent paths. Distinct from RIMSCOPELEAK below (that was the object-level green rim
  from `gu.selected_body_index`; this is the poly sub-element hover overlay).
- Manual: Edge mode → hover an edge → move the cursor onto the properties panel → the pale hover
  line disappears immediately instead of sticking.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — EDGESELDECAY: past 65 536 projected elements the pick grid silently stopped indexing them — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner: *"edge select works well when I start using the program but after a while it starts to bug /
degrade, I don't understand why."*

- **Root cause — a hard capacity cliff, not a race.** `PolyPickCache.grid` (the 24×16 screen-space
  bucket grid that is the ONLY structure `poly_hover_pick` iterates) was `Vec<Vec<u16>>`, so
  `rebuild_pick_cache` registered elements behind `if idx <= u16::MAX as usize { … }`
  (`poly_selection/pick.rs:113` vert, `:154` edge). `vert_screen` / `edge_screen` themselves are
  unbounded `Vec`s. **Past 65 536 projected elements the surplus was pushed into `*_screen` but
  into no cell at all** — invisible to every hover query, therefore unhoverable and unclickable,
  with no toast, no log, no counter.
- **Measured** (`poly_selection::tests_pick_grid`, headless, real `poly_hover_pick`):
  a 200×200-quad sheet (40 000 faces / 80 400 undirected edges — squarely in the owner's working
  range) leaves **14 864 of 80 400 edges (18.5 %) unreachable**; a 260×260 sheet leaves
  **2 585 of 68 121 vertices** unreachable.
- **Why it reads as "degrades over time" and not "broken".** (a) The ceiling is crossed by
  *modelling*: ~2 edges per quad, so ~32 800 quads on screen is already over it and every loop cut
  / subdivide / bevel pushes further. (b) `canonical_edges` walks half-edge index ≈ **creation
  order**, so the elements that fall off the end are the NEWEST geometry — the edges the user just
  made are the first to stop responding. (c) Only *projected* elements count, so zooming and
  orbiting change which ones make the cut, which makes it feel intermittent. (d) Nothing recovers
  it except deleting geometry, so "it was fine when I started" is literally true.
- **Fix.** `grid: Vec<Vec<u32>>`, both capacity gates deleted. The field now carries a doc comment
  stating the invariant (the cell type must address every `*_screen` entry; never narrow it, never
  re-add a gate that drops instead of indexes). Perf is a non-event: the grid already carried
  81 % of these entries, and `u16`→`u32` on ~80 k indices is ~160 KB.
- **The pattern this violated already exists in the codebase**: `MAX_OVERLAY_SEGMENTS`
  (`overlay_lines.rs:107`) is capped too, but *loudly* — counter + one-shot toast, commented
  "hard caps are Frame Budget protection — never silent (Goal 4 honesty)". The pick grid was the
  one place that capped in silence.
- Gates: `every_projected_edge_is_reachable_from_the_pick_grid`,
  `every_projected_vertex_is_reachable_from_the_pick_grid` (both assert a PRECONDITION that the
  fixture exceeds the old ceiling, so they cannot silently stop testing), and
  `the_last_created_edges_are_the_ones_the_ceiling_used_to_drop` (pins that the casualties were the
  high half-edge ids). All three fail on the pre-fix code with the numbers above.
  `cargo test -p app --bins`: 762 passed, 5 failed — the same 5 pre-existing `.fl4`-load gates,
  unrelated.

### EDGESELDECAY — two adjacent findings NOT fixed here (no evidence they fired; do not re-derive)

1. ⬜ **OPEN — the GPU select buffer can freeze permanently, with no recovery path.**
   `PickingPipeline::start_full_readback` (`render/src/picking.rs:390`) sets its `map_ready` flag
   **only on `Ok`** — `move |result| { if result.is_ok() { flag.store(true, …) } }`. A failed map
   is discarded, against the CLAUDE.md GPU rule ("`map_async` calls must capture `Result` … never
   discard"). `poll_poly_select_buffer` (`poly_select_gpu.rs:196`) then returns early **every frame
   forever**: the only exits from `poly_pick_pending = Some(..)` are a successful decode or
   `self.gpu == None` — no timeout, no watchdog, no retry, and `blocking_readback_full` itself
   gives up silently after 64 `Maintain::Wait` polls. Once stuck, every visibility question falls
   back to the CPU ray + `distance * 0.02` bias the 2026-08-09 per-element rework deleted as the
   root of the "selection fails often" class. *Fix shape:* tri-state the flag
   (pending / ok / **failed**), surface failure to the poller, drop the pending readback and
   recreate `full_staging` so the next frame re-renders.
2. ⬜ **OPEN (minor) — `MAX_FACE_OVERLAY_VERTS` (`overlay_faces.rs:21`, 100 000) truncates the
   selected-face FILL silently** (`break`, no toast/counter), unlike its `MAX_OVERLAY_SEGMENTS`
   sibling. Display only — the faces stay selected — but it reads as "some selected faces lost
   their green" on a large selection.
3. Considered and set aside: `reconcile_poly_sel_body` (`poly_selection/pick.rs:34`) clears
   component id sets only when `active_poly_nid` changes, never on mesh change, so a stale id that
   stays *in range* addresses a different element after a renumbering op. Every draw site guards
   bounds but not identity. Weakest of the three — most ops clear or remap selection — recorded so
   it is not re-derived.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — RIMSCOPELEAK: green object rim stayed lit with NOTHING selected — ✅ FIXED

Owner (screenshot, at the scene root): *"WHEN AT ROOT NOTHING SELECTED NO HIGHLIGHTS ON OBJECT
SHOULD BE SEEN"* — a body kept its full green silhouette rim after every deselect.

Three code paths can light an object green, and two of them were already correct — they derive from
`sel.usel.selected` only: the raster `sel_bit` rim (`raster_gbuffer.rs:71`, deferred edge-detect) and
the CPU walk (`draw_node_selection_outlines`, whose comment already records removing exactly this
force: *"do NOT force active_body — that was the deselected 80ms leak"*). The third —
`gu.selected_body_index`, which drives `apply_body_outline` in `post_process.wgsl` (screen-space
edge-detect on `body_index`, the rim in the owner's shot) — still read **edit SCOPE**:

- **Root cause.** `viewport_render.rs` resolved the rim node as `active_node()`, then
  `.or_else(|| { if active_n.is_some() { return None } … self.scene.active_body_nid })`.
  `active_node()` is `None` **precisely when the selection is empty**, so the fallback fired on
  exactly the case it claimed to exclude — its own comment said *"empty selection → no outline via
  this path"* while the code did the opposite. And `clear_selection_unified()` deliberately never
  touches `active_body_nid` (scope survives a deselect, by design), so *every* deselect — empty
  viewport click → `deselect_all()`, Alt+A, clicking the Scene root — left it pointing at the last
  body and re-lit that body's rim. The fallback is a leftover of the pre-selection design: before
  `e1d26ec` this uniform was 100% `active_body_nid` with no selection input at all.
- **Fix.** The rim is now selection-derived only, and the active id is **validated against the
  selection set** before use (`.filter(|n| selected.contains(&SceneItemId::Node(*n)))`), so a stale
  `active` can never rim an unselected body either. The `active_body_nid` fallback is gone. Scope is
  still shown where it belongs — the outliner's amber active-body bar — not as a viewport rim.
  All three highlight paths now agree on one invariant: **highlight ⊆ selection**.

Build: `cargo build -p app` green. Manual: select a body (green rim) → click empty viewport space →
rim disappears the same frame and stays gone through orbit/zoom; re-select → rim returns; select body
A then Ctrl+click body B → both rim (raster `sel_bit`, unchanged); Tab into poly V/E/F on a selected
body → object rim still suppressed, component highlights unaffected.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — LIGHTDUPNODE / LIGHTRADIUSNOOP / LIGHTSELFORM: duplicating a point light did nothing, S-scaling its attenuation radius reverted on release, and G/R/S was dead on outliner-selected lights — ✅ FIXED

Owner: *"duplicate point light does not work, scaling to change point light attenuation size is not
persistent, snaps back to the set number in settings"*. Two independent bugs, both in code that
handles lights as a special case of a general path and forgot one field/kind.

- **LIGHTDUPNODE — Shift+D / outliner ▸ Duplicate on a light produced nothing.** Lights are graph
  nodes (`NodePayload::Light`) and the ui2 outliner selects every row as `SceneItemId::Node` (its
  rows only carry `OlItem::Node` / `OlItem::Prim` — there is no Light variant). `duplicate_selected()`
  tests the **node** arm before the light arm, so an outliner-selected light went to
  `duplicate_node_no_undo` → `duplicate_scene_node_no_undo`, whose payload match ends in
  `_ => return None`. The arm then `return`ed with *"Nothing duplicated — selected node kind(s) not
  duplicable"* and the `SceneItemId::Light` arm below it never ran. Exactly the route that made the
  default Sun undeletable in 2026-08-06 (`delete_selected` was fixed then; duplicate was not).
  **Fix:** `duplicate_node_no_undo` (`gizmo/scene_edit.rs`) now dispatches `NodePayload::Light` to
  the canonical `duplicate_light_no_undo()` core and returns the copy's NodeId — one light-copy
  path, not two, so id allocation / `Point.NNN` naming / the +X offset stay in one place. Viewport
  picks (`SceneItemId::Light`) keep using the light arm and produce an identical copy.
- **LIGHTRADIUSNOOP — S on a light scaled the attenuation radius live, then snapped back on
  release.** `gizmo_drag_is_noop()` and `modal_transform_is_noop()` each inlined their own light
  comparison, and **both compared position / azimuth / elevation only — never `range`**. Scale on a
  light writes `range` and nothing else (owner 2026-08-07: *"S should modify the radius of the
  light"*), so a pure radius drag read as "nothing moved": `finish_gizmo_drag` / `confirm_modal_transform`
  routed it to `cancel_*`, and cancel restores `snap.original_range` — the radius reverted to its
  pre-drag value the instant the mouse released. The properties slider was never involved; it just
  showed the value the cancel had restored.
  **Fix:** ONE `light_snapshot_matches()` helper (`gizmo/transform_modal.rs`, beside
  `prim_snapshot_matches`) compares position, azimuth, elevation **and range**; both no-op tests
  call it. A no-op test that ignores a field the drag writes cancels real work, and the next field
  added to `LightTransformSnapshot` now has one place to be handled.

- **LIGHTSELFORM (found while fixing the two above, owner-directed same session) — G/R/S did
  nothing at all on an outliner-selected light, and the gizmo drew at the world origin.** Same root
  as LIGHTDUPNODE, wider blast radius: `start_gizmo_drag`, `start_modal_transform`,
  `resolve_transform_targets` and `selection_median` all read `usel.has_lights()` /
  `selected_lights()` — the `SceneItemId::Light` form ONLY. An outliner-selected light is
  `SceneItemId::Node`, so every light arm was skipped and the generic **node** path ran instead,
  writing `local_position` / `local_rotation` / `local_scale` on the Light node. Those three fields
  are dead state: a light's transform lives in `LightData` (`position` / `azimuth` / `elevation` /
  `range`), and no renderer, light packer or gizmo ever reads the node's. So the gizmo appeared
  armed, the drag ran, and nothing moved — and because `selection_median()` averaged the same
  unused `local_position` (a default `ZERO`), the gizmo itself drew at the world origin instead of
  on the light.
  **Fix — partition the selection instead of testing one form:** two canonical accessors beside
  `selected_light_ids()` in `scene_actions.rs` — `is_light_node(nid)` and
  `selected_transform_nodes()` (= `selected_nodes()` minus lights). Together with
  `selected_light_ids()` they partition the selection, so a light is transformed by exactly ONE
  path regardless of route and a light node can never reach a node-transform site. Converted:
  `start_gizmo_drag` (light gate + node targets), `start_modal_transform` (light gate + the
  `active_node` arm now excludes lights), `resolve_transform_targets`, `selection_median`,
  `frame_selected`, `build_frame_lights_gpu`'s force-include list, the C colour popup, the
  light-gizmo overlay gate, and the transform HUD (which printed `X:0 Y:0 Z:0` under a Light node,
  and printed X/Y/Z under **S** where only the radius changes — both forms now share one
  `light_hud_data`: G = position, R = aim, S = radius).
  Left alone deliberately: the delete / duplicate / copy arms in `scene_edit.rs` + `clipboard.rs`
  reach lights through their **node** arms already (`delete_node_no_undo` / `snapshot_subtree` /
  now `duplicate_node_no_undo`), and `draw_light.rs` was fixed for this class earlier.

**This is the FOURTH time the two selection forms have shipped a bug** (properties panel drew
nothing 2026-07-28 · default Sun undeletable 2026-08-06 · range sphere + handles vanished ·
today's duplicate + transform). Rule going forward: never test `usel.has_lights()` /
`selected_lights()` / `selected_nodes()` directly when the question is *"which lights / which
transformable nodes has the user selected"* — use `selected_light_ids()` /
`active_light_id_any()` / `selected_transform_nodes()`.

Build: `cargo build -p app` green. Manual: (1) select a point light in the outliner → Shift+D →
`Point.NNN` appears offset +1 X, selected, Ctrl+Z removes it; (2) select a point light in the
viewport → S → drag right → release: the range sphere keeps its new size and the Attenuation Radius
slider reads the dragged value; Ctrl+Z restores the old one; (3) S then release without moving still
cancels the episode (no wasted undo); (4) select the SAME light in the OUTLINER → the gizmo now
appears ON the light (not at the origin) → G moves it, R re-aims it, S resizes the radius, and the
HUD reads `Radius:` under S; (5) F frames it at a sane distance and C opens the colour popup.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — MIRRORFLIPDEAD / MIRRORCUT: Volume Mirror's Flip checkboxes did nothing, and the mirror cost 2ⁿ evals per voxel — ✅ FIXED (sdf)

Owner: *"sdf mirror is very slow … also it need a toggle default on delete the other half"*.

Two findings in the Volume Mirror (Field Modifiers → the GPU-baked mirror; the SLOW one the owner
first hit is the separate post-DC **Mesh** Mirror, which folds on the CPU):

- **`mirror_sign` was inert.** The 2026-07 union rework made the body mirror `min` over all 2ⁿ
  reflection combos, and every eval path documented *"mirror_sign is IRRELEVANT to a union — both
  sides are always evaluated."* The `Flip: X Y Z` checkboxes were still in the properties panel,
  still saved, still hashed into the bake identity — and could not change one voxel.
- **The union walks the whole scope body once per combo** (`volume_bake.wgsl` SCOPE_CLOSE re-seeks
  to SCOPE_OPEN): 2× for one axis, 4× for two, 8× for three, forever, with no way to opt out.

- ✅ ADDED **Cut ("delete the other half")** — `mirror_sign` bit 7 (`body_field_ops::MIRROR_CUT_BIT`),
  ON by default for new Volume Mirrors. The point is folded onto the source half
  (`p_axis = c ± |p_axis − c|`) instead of unioning combos: the discarded half is gone, straddling
  geometry is bisected at the plane (Blender's Bisect), and the field costs **ONE** eval at any axis
  count. Flip bits 0-2 become live — they pick which half is the source.
  Measured (12 prims, 884k samples, release): X 417→215 ms (1.95×), XY 838→200 ms (4.19×),
  XYZ 1955→286 ms (6.8×) — a cut mirror now costs the same as no mirror at all (215 vs 213 ms).
- **Save compatibility:** bit 7 is 0 in every `.fl4` written before it existed → those files keep
  the union, byte-identical. The flag rides spare bits of the existing `u8` rather than a new field,
  so `BodyFieldModKind::VolumeMirror`'s bincode shape is unchanged (the field-modifier records
  round-trip through `ProjectFile.body_field_modifiers`).
- Landed in lockstep across every eval path (the "must work in BOTH paths" rule): CPU
  `field_eval::fold_for_cut` + `eval_scene_body_mirrored` + `FieldScope`, GPU bake
  `volume_bake.wgsl`, analytical `sdf_scene.wgsl`/`sdf_prim_eval.wgsl` (reflections/fog/PT), and the
  `BrickClassifier` containment proofs — the interior proof used the UNREFLECTED center, sound only
  because a union always evaluates the identity combo; under a cut it is not, so it now probes the
  FOLDED center (1-Lipschitz, so the region ball still covers it). Cut also makes the proofs test
  ONE point instead of 2ⁿ.
- Gates: `body_mirror_bake_matches_cpu_eval` gained 4 cut cases (real GPU bake vs CPU evaluator, 0
  sign flips / 0.0000 max delta) with explicit kept-solid / discarded-empty probes so an
  all-deleting regression cannot pass by CPU and GPU agreeing on nothing; plus 5 core_math tests
  including `body_mirror_without_cut_bit_is_still_the_union` (the old-saves guard).
- ✅ ADDED **Center from…** on the Volume Mirror card — pick the mirror center line from the current
  work plane, any SAVED work plane (they already persist in `ProjectFile.editor.wp_saved`), the
  selection (`selection_pivot_world`, honours a custom pivot), or the body/world origin. Sources are
  converted into the body-local frame the center lives in. A source whose normal is an X/Y/Z axis of
  the body also sets the mirror axis; a TILTED plane sets the center only and says so — the volume
  mirror reflects per axis and cannot mirror about an arbitrary plane, so it is not rounded to the
  nearest axis behind the user's back.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — MESHMAPSTALL: Bake Mesh Maps froze the UI (~43 s at panel defaults) — ✅ FIXED (mesh maps)

**Found by RUNNING it, not by a test** — the whole point of the exercise. Three soak steps were
added (`uv.unwrap`, `meshmap.bake_all`, `meshmap.mode_baked`) so the texturing-prep chain is driven
through production APIs on every soak run; the first run reported:

```
033 meshmap.bake_all   997.5ms  px=0.0%  baked 5 maps, skipped: ID
```

- **Root cause.** The entire bake — rasterise + curvature + AO + Thickness + Position + Normal —
  ran INLINE in `poll_mesh_map_bakes`, i.e. on the frame thread. 998 ms at 256² with 24 rays; at
  the panel's own defaults (1024², 64 rays) that is 16× the texels and ~2.7× the rays ≈ **43 s of
  frozen UI on the feature's main button**. Rayon already parallelised the inner ray loop, which
  made it faster but not asynchronous — the stall survived, and no test could see it because every
  test calls the compute path directly.
- ✅ FIXED — split by what actually needs the app. Frame thread: snapshot the display mesh, UVs and
  polygroups (`&mut self`), and later `upload_map` (GPU creation — Frame Ordering Contract). Worker
  (`MeshMapJob::run`, 8 MB stack): rasterise + every map, pure CPU over owned buffers, reporting
  through `BakeNotes` since a worker cannot toast. Poll drains with `try_recv` and returns
  immediately while the worker runs.
- The five compute functions were `&mut self` methods reading `self.ui.*` and calling `toast`;
  they are now free functions taking data, which is what made the move possible and also makes
  them testable without an app.
- **Evidence the poll no longer blocks:** the soak step previously completed in ONE
  `poll_mesh_map_bakes()` call and now requires a bounded pump loop — the call returns without
  doing the work, by construction.
- Verified in the app both before and after: `FAIL=0`, 5 maps baked (ID correctly skipped, that
  body has no polygroups).

## 2026-08-11 (master) — IMPORTCONVERTNOFACES: Convert to Poly on an imported mesh produced a FACELESS point cloud (and dropped its UVs) — ✅ FIXED (convert)

Found while chasing the "I have UVs but AZRA doesn't" thread. The UV loss was the visible half; the
topology loss was worse and had gone unnoticed.

- **Root cause.** `MeshCache::insert_imported` builds `cpu_mesh` with `quads: Vec::new()`
  ("imported meshes use triangles directly"), and `HalfEdgeMesh::from_mesh` treats an empty-quad
  `Mesh` as *"No topology — treat as point cloud (no faces)"*. `convert_imported_to_poly` called
  exactly that, so **every imported asset converted to poly came out with all its vertices and
  ZERO faces.** Probed, not inferred: `core_math::mesh::convert_probe::
  from_mesh_without_quads_yields_no_faces` reports 4 verts / 0 faces.
- **Second loss, same line.** `core_math::mesh::Mesh` has no UV field at all (positions, normals,
  quads), so the imported unwrap was dropped too. That is why AZRA's own Smart UV Unwrap was the
  only source of UVs, and why "I have UVs" did not mean AZRA had them.
- ✅ FIXED — conversion now reads `MeshCache::imported_raster_persistent` (new accessor), the ONLY
  place an imported mesh's topology and UVs survive on the CPU: `[p,n,uv]` per vertex + indices.
  `build_poly_from_raster_impl` welds by quantised position (raster verts are per-corner, so
  building triangles over them directly gives isolated faces with no shared edges — faces, but not
  an editable mesh), builds the half-edge mesh from triangles, and installs per-corner UVs into
  `cd.uv`. UVs are matched by **welded vertex id, not corner order** — `from_triangles` gives no
  guarantee that half-edge corner *k* is input corner *k*, and a rotated ring would shift every UV
  by one and produce a subtly wrong unwrap that still looked like an unwrap.
- **Not yet compiled**: `app_types/src/keymap/ctx.rs` is mid-edit (owner adding `ActiveTool::
  PolyEdgeWeight`; that match is deliberately exhaustive). `render` and `core_math` are green.

## 2026-08-11 (master) — SEAMIGNORED: Mark Seam could not affect the unwrap, and the unwrap DELETED marked seams — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Found while checking (owner: *"grok did a seam mark tool"*) whether the seam tool needed building.
It exists on master and works — `poly_mark_seam_apply`, key `C`, Mark/Toggle Seam menu entries.
But it was wired to nothing:

- `smart_uv_unwrap` took **no seam input**. Charts were computed from dihedral angle + normal cone
  alone, so a marked seam had zero effect on the result.
- `apply_unwrap_to_custom_data` opened with `cd.seam = BitLayer::new()` — every unwrap **deleted
  the author's marked seams** and substituted its own chart boundaries.

Net: mark seams → unwrap → the marks are ignored AND destroyed. Authored data silently replaced by
derived data; the tool could not do its job.

- ✅ FIXED — `smart_uv_unwrap_with_seams(mesh, params, seams)`: an authored seam is an absolute
  chart boundary, tested BEFORE the geometric tests (it is the author overriding them). Marked on
  either half-edge marks the edge, mirroring `poly_mesh::edge_is_sharp`. The app passes
  `cd.seam` and reports how many were honoured.
- ✅ FIXED — `apply_unwrap_to_custom_data` now UNIONS computed boundaries into `cd.seam` instead of
  replacing it, so re-unwrapping keeps honouring the author.
- Gate: `authored_seam_splits_a_chart_and_is_preserved` — a flat 4-quad strip has no geometric
  reason to split, so any extra island can only come from the seam; the mark must also survive the
  apply.
