## 2026-08-10 (master) — UVUNWRAP: Smart UV Project self-overlaps on curves, wastes 59% of the map, has no settings UI — ✅ FIXED (poly)

Owner: "THE UNWRAP IS PROLY INTEGRETED, DOES NOT HAVE PROPER TOOL PARAMETER SETTING AND SO NOT
PRODUSE ANY GOOD RESULT EVEN ON BASIC CUBE, I DONT HAVE A PACK FONCTION TO" — surfaced while
diagnosing POLYCURV, which depends on UVs.

Three defects, all **measured** (rasterise every UV triangle into a coverage counter; see
`uv_overlap_fraction` and the `dump_uv_unwrap` diagnostic in `poly_curvature.rs`):

- **Curved charts fold onto themselves — a correctness bug, not a quality one.** Each chart is
  projected along its average normal, which is only sound while the chart's normals stay inside a
  <90° cone. The dihedral test bounds NEIGHBOURS, not the chart, so a cylinder's side grew into ONE
  chart wrapping 360°: **39% of used texels carried 2+ surface points**, area distortion 956×.
  Every baked map on such a body was silently wrong. ✅ FIXED — new `UvUnwrapParams::max_cone_deg`
  (default 75°, hard-capped at 89°) refuses a face whose normal leaves the chart's running
  area-weighted cone. Cylinder now: **0.00% overlap**, distortion 956× → 20×, 3 → 5 islands.
- **Packer wasted 59% of the texture.** `shelf_pack` computed one scale from an "aim for 85% area"
  heuristic and returned the first fit, never growing. A cube — six equal squares that tile a 3×2
  grid perfectly — packed into **41%** of the map, i.e. every texture effectively baked at half
  resolution. ✅ FIXED — bisection on scale (fit is monotonic in scale), keeping the largest that
  packs. Cube: 41% → **57%**. Remaining gap is margin + no island rotation; a rotating/MaxRects
  packer would reach ~75-85% and is NOT done.
- **No settings UI at all.** `uv_unwrap_angle_deg` / `uv_unwrap_margin` lived on `UiState` with
  defaults, were read by the unwrap, and **nothing anywhere wrote them** — the tool had exactly one
  hardcoded behaviour. ✅ FIXED — Tool Parameters redo panel (`draw_tool_params_uv_unwrap`, Blender
  F9 model) with Angle / Max Cone / Margin, island+corner readout, and an "Unwrap again" button.

**Round 2 — owner: "still does not have setting do control the smart unwrap … curvature was not
able to appear, i was on uv, texture".** The panel existed but was unreachable, and curvature had
three more silent-failure paths:
- **Panel gated on "an unwrap has already run".** UV Unwrap is a one-shot menu command with no
  armed state, so there was NO moment at which the settings were reachable before running it —
  the user had to run it blind and the panel only appeared after. ✅ Now shows whenever a poly body
  is selected AND (UV layout is open OR an unwrap ran), and renders with no prior result.
- **`snapshot_poly_curv_source` hard-failed on a missing panel doc** (`material_panel_docs.get(mid)?`)
  → no curvature at all, silently. ✅ Falls back to the material's own `TexMap` (`projection` /
  `uv_scale` / `blend`), which is what the shader actually samples.
- **`poly_curv_body()` required the mesh to be the ACTIVE node.** Working in the Material panel can
  move `usel.active` onto a material/light node while the mesh stays selected → resolved to `None`
  → no curvature. ✅ Falls back: active node → any selected poly body → `active_body_nid` if poly.
- **Added a deduped diagnostic toast** reporting what the bake resolved (faces, UV corners,
  projection, normal map) plus the specific blocking reason. Every failure above was previously
  indistinguishable from "the feature doesn't work".

**Round 3 — owner supplied `curvature.fl4`. Loaded it headlessly (`inspect_fl4` diagnostic in
`poly_curvature.rs`) and ran the FULL curvature pipeline on the real asset.** Decisive:

| Precondition | Actual |
|---|---|
| Body | `Poly.box` — 90 faces, 111 verts, 0 modifiers |
| UV sidecar | **382 corners, 46 seams — present and round-tripping through save/load** |
| Projection | **UV** (`albedo_map.projection == 1`), uv_scale 1 |
| Normal map | none (`tex_id 0`) — geometry is the only source |
| `uses_uv_writer()` | **true** |
| Baked result | **46.3 % written coverage, peak convex 0.996** — a correct map |

So the kernel, the UV writer, the UVs, and the projection are all CORRECT on the owner's own
asset. The failure is in the app wiring between the snapshot and the display, not in any of the
things four rounds of inference blamed.

**And the reason it presented as silence:** `snapshot_poly_curv_source` opened with two bare `?`
bails (`poly_curv_body()?`, `poly_cached_display_mesh(nid)?`) that returned BEFORE the round-2
diagnostic — so the two most likely failures produced no toast at all, which is exactly the
"still nothing / no message" the owner reported. ✅ Both now report through a deduped
`curv_diag()`, along with "display mesh has no live faces".

2 new gates (`curved_chart_does_not_self_overlap`, `packer_fills_the_map_on_a_cube`).
**Still open:** island rotation in the packer; a standalone Pack command; and `convert.rs`
(imported mesh → PolygonalBody) drops the source UVs entirely, so an imported asset's existing
unwrap is lost and AZRA's own unwrap is the only way to get UVs.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — POLYCURV: Curvature / Cavity greyed out on polygonal bodies — ✅ FIXED (materials)

Owner: "I TOUGH WE SUPPORTED CURVATURE FOR POLY MESH, I HAVE UV, I DONT UNDERSTANDE DO I NEED TO
PRECUMPUTER LIKE SUBSTANCE PAINTER" → "WIRE IT PROPERLY TO WORK WITH POLY MESH"

- **Root cause.** The generator family was never wired for poly at all. Every entry in the Add-mask
  / Add-generator menu was gated on one flag, `GenCtx::has_sdf` = "`body_primitives(active_body)`
  is `Some` and non-empty", and `body_primitives` returns `None` for a `PolygonalBody`. UVs were
  never the blocker: the generators measure an **analytical SDF field**, and a poly body has none.
  No precompute step existed to run — the code path did not exist.
- **Two pre-existing defects the gate was masking** (either would have shipped a lying control if
  the flag had simply been flipped):
  - **B2a** — `SdfFieldSources::sdf_at` fell through to `sn_field_h`, a hardcoded procedural height
    field. A fieldless body did not read as "no curvature", it read as *the curvature of a
    synthetic pattern* — plausible-looking, unrelated to any geometry.
  - **B2b** — `has_field()` and `body_aabb` both fell through to `by_uid`, which is **scene-wide**.
    A poly body in a mixed scene measured and bounded itself against *another body's* prims, so a
    poly-only scene and a mixed scene disagreed about what "no field" meant.
- ✅ FIXED — `NO_FIELD_D` (finite, so nothing downstream produces NaN) replaces the synthetic
  fallback; `has_field()`/`body_aabb` no longer consult `by_uid`; the `Curvature`/`Cavity` nodes
  lost their synthetic branches. Curvature is now **measured** on the post-modifier half-edge mesh
  (`core_math/src/mesh_curvature.rs`, signed: convex +, concave −, exactly 0 on flat, scale
  invariant) and written into an ordinary `CurvGrid` (`app/src/poly_curvature.rs`) — UV-raster when
  the material samples by UV, triplanar-raster matching `sample_mat_triplanar_b`'s own coordinates
  and weights otherwise. Downstream is byte-for-byte the SDF path: same shaping, same compositor,
  same map install, same Path Trace. No shader edit, no save-format change, no new render path.
- **Scope held:** AO / Thickness / Direction / Position stay SDF-only (each needs ray casting or a
  field gradient) and now say so in their hover text instead of "SDF bodies only".
- **Round 2 — owner: "I SEE NOISE APPEAR BUT THIS IS FAR FROM CURVATURE MAP. EVEN IN UV MODE THIS
  DONT WORK"** (with a Blender `LP_stone` reference). Three causes, found by rendering the output
  to PNG rather than trusting the gates — all 15 gates were green through all three:
  - **The noise was an aliasing bug in my rasteriser.** The inside-test tolerance was
    `1e-3·max(|area|,1)/|area|` — unbounded for sub-texel triangles — so every one flooded a 3×3
    block with its own κ, and on a dense mesh those blocks average into mottling. Now 4×4
    supersampled coverage-weighted rasterisation with a fixed epsilon.
  - **The map was a binary mask, not a gradient.** `POLY_DISPLAY_SCALE = 1.0` clipped the shared
    shaping at κ = 0.30, so a 90° and a 60° edge both baked pure white. Now `1/√3` (a right-angle
    box corner = the white point).
  - **The reference is unreachable from mesh geometry.** Crack detail on a low-poly asset lives in
    the NORMAL MAP. Added Substance's per-pixel source: `∂n.x/∂u + ∂n.y/∂v`, which is already
    positive-on-convex and so sums directly onto the geometric term; honours `green_dx`. The
    writer now accumulates raw κ and shapes ONCE at the end, since `shape(a)+shape(b) ≠ shape(a+b)`.
- 17 gates. Plan + full session log: `docs/planning/render/POLY_CURVATURE_PLAN.md` §9.
  **Not yet run in the app** — the §8 manual checklist is outstanding.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — MIRRORNIDBLOB: `mirror_object_nid` added to `PolyModifier` with `#[serde(default)]` — ⚠ OPEN, BREAKS EVERY EXISTING `.fl4` (not mine — concurrent in-flight work)

Found while verifying BEVELAUTOMERGE below. **`core_math/src/scene_graph/node.rs:389`** now carries

```rust
/// Optional mirror-plane origin object (`NodeId.0`). 0 = local mesh origin.
#[serde(default)]
pub mirror_object_nid: u64,
```

inside `PolyModifier`, which is serialized INSIDE the monolithic bincode blob. This is the exact trap
this tracker and `node.rs`'s own `remesh_*` comment already document: **bincode is positional and
`#[serde(default)]` is inert for it**, so 8 bytes now appear mid-struct that no existing file has.

- **Evidence:** `cargo test -p core_math --test serde_golden` →
  `golden_scene_graph_deserializes_exactly` FAILS with
  `SceneGraph layout changed — .fl4 saves are broken: Io(Kind(UnexpectedEof))`.
- **Time-bisected, not guessed:** that same gate was **3/3 green at ~13:15 today** with the two
  `#[serde(skip)]` bevel fields already in place, and the only serialized-layout change since is this
  field. `#[serde(skip)]` fields emit zero bytes and cannot move a position.
- **Impact:** priority-ladder #3 (save/load). Every `.fl4` containing a poly modifier fails to load.
- **FIX (do not use `#[serde(default)]`):** make it `#[serde(skip)]` and persist it out of band. Since
  it is per-(node, modifier-index) state exactly like its neighbours, the cheapest correct carrier is
  a new 8-byte-magic tail section written LAST (the `FL4PRMSH` / `FL4PBVAR` pattern:
  `app/src/project/io.rs` + a record in `project/mod.rs` + `collect_*` in `project_save.rs` +
  reattach in `project_load.rs`), emitted only when non-default so unused scenes stay byte-identical.
- Left for its author — that area is being actively edited and the fix belongs with the mirror feature.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — BEVELAUTOMERGE: Clamp Overlap's limit was GLOBAL, so one tight spot froze the whole bevel — ✅ FIXED (Bevel modifier)

Owner: "another toggle we could have inside the bevel modifier is auto merge vertex that touch each
other. I don't want a merge by distance because this will break small, but if 2 edges that are beveled
too near one and other (clamp) limit — past the clamp it will merge vertex at the clamp position."
Plus: "the merge will only affect geo created by bevel."

- **Measured BEFORE designing, and it reframed the task: the merge already worked.** The kernel's
  `WeldMap` merges any two rail points landing on the same spot, so at exactly the clamp limit the
  collision already resolves to ONE vertex — thin plate, all edges: 24v/26f at w=0.02, **16v/18f with
  0 degenerate faces, watertight and valid at w=0.05 (the limit)**, and identical at 0.10/0.30 because
  the clamp freezes there. Nothing needed a merge algorithm.
- **Root cause was the ceiling's SCOPE:** STEP 1 computes a real per-edge capacity then collapses it
  with `cap.values().min()`, so the single tightest edge governs everything. Cube + a 0.06-wide
  loop-cut band, request 0.2 → **the entire cube bevels at 0.030**. Per-edge → **the roomy corners
  reach 0.200** and the band pins + welds at its own limit; 32v/34f either way, 0 degenerate faces, at
  segments 1 and 3.
- ✅ FIXED — `BevelWidthDriver::Uniform` (every edge targets `params.width`; only the per-edge ceiling
  moves it), riding the ceiling + `opposing_pair_caps` machinery BEVELVARWIDTH already added.
  `BevelVarWidth` → **`BevelWidthPolicy`**, since it now carries a per-edge ceiling independently of
  whether the target is graded; `is_graded()` stops the graded `width_min` leaking into single-width
  mode.
- ⚠ **Two sabotage results kept in BEVEL.md because I was wrong twice about the mechanism:** guarding
  the global clamp with `&& var.is_none()` changes no gate (the policy path reads `width_req`, never
  `w`), and `lo` cancels out under `Uniform` because `t = 1`. The live gate is "discard a `Uniform`
  policy" → roomy corner 0.2 → 0.0299 → FAILED. Sabotage what you claim is the mechanism.
- **Owner's constraints met structurally, not by a threshold.** *Not a merge by distance:* no distance
  pass exists; the only vertices that can coincide are rails this bevel computed, pinned at
  `sep · w_a/(w_a+w_b)` — literally "the clamp position". Nothing scans for nearby vertices, so small
  detail cannot be swallowed; per-edge ceilings give small features *smaller* bevels. *Only
  bevel-created geo:* the weld joins new rail points and no original vertex is displaced — gated on a
  PARTIAL selection so untouched originals exist to check.
- Stops AT the meet, never past it (owner's wording). Mutually exclusive with Consume Geometry, whose
  absorb decides from ONE width — the UI disables both per-edge toggles under Consume and zeroes them,
  so hidden state can never drive visible geometry. Needs Clamp Overlap (no limit ⇒ no meet position);
  implied by Variable Width (grading is meaningless under a global minimum), shown as
  checked-and-disabled there.
- **Persistence:** `bevel_auto_merge` is `#[serde(skip)]` and rides the existing `FL4PBVAR` record as a
  third field — legitimate ONLY because that section was created hours earlier in the same unreleased
  change and is still uncommitted, so no file carries a narrower record. The record's doc comment
  states that the rule flips to "new magic, written last" the moment it is committed. (Contrast
  MIRRORNIDBLOB above, which put a field in the blob itself.)
- **Gates:** 5 new kernel including a 30-configuration sweep (3 fixtures × segments {1,3} × 5 widths)
  asserting **0** collapsed faces, plus app round-trip / collect / stack-hash / an e2e gate through
  `apply_poly_modifiers_tagged` that also pins the Clamp-Overlap dependency and the Variable-Width
  implication. 135 bevel gates green. No degenerate-face cleanup written: every measurement returns 0,
  so `remove_degenerate_face` stays unwired and the sweep will report if that changes.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — BEVELVARWIDTH: one Width for the whole selection breaks small detail — ✅ FIXED (Bevel modifier)

Owner: "CAN WE ADD A VARIABLE WIDTH TOGGLE, HAVING THE SAME WIDTH EVERYWHERE CAUSE PROBLEM ON
SMALLER DETAIL, I COULD SET 2 WIDTHS SMALL AND LARGE AND THE BEVEL WILL ADJUST IN BETWEEN OF THOSE
DEPENDING OF THE SIZE"

- **Root cause (structural, not a feel issue).** STEP 1 of `bevel_edges_offset_mut` computes a real
  per-edge capacity (Blender's `geometry_collide_offset`: collapse limit + slide walks) and then
  **throws the per-edge detail away** — `let mut limit = f32::INFINITY` … `limit = limit.min(…)` over
  every beveled half-edge … `w = w.min(limit)`. One number for the whole selection. So with Clamp
  Overlap ON the single smallest edge sets everyone's width (measured: a big cube + a 0.05 cube in one
  mesh, request 0.3 → the BIG cube gets **0.05**), and with it OFF the small detail folds. Blender
  has the same global limit; its answer (per-edge bevel weight) is manual painting.
- ✅ FIXED — per-edge widths, `w_e = lo + (width − lo)·t_e` then capped by `cap_e`, with
  `t_e = cap_e/cap_max` (driver **Auto by size**) or the authored 0..1 weight (**Authored weight**).
  New `BevelVarWidth` spec passed BESIDE `BevelParams` (which stays `Copy` and untouched — it is a
  full struct literal at ~60 call sites); `bevel_edges_offset` keeps its signature and delegates with
  `None`, so the entire existing suite exercises the old path unchanged.
- **No new corner math was needed, and that was the enabling finding:** `adjust_offsets` already
  produces unequal per-edge widths that ride `Rail.w` through the corner/boundary solvers, gated
  against the Blender ring oracle since 2026-07-23. Its least-squares now fits per-edge targets
  (`d = Σ(g_i·w_i)/Σg_i²`); the uniform branch keeps the original `w·sg/sg2` expression **verbatim**
  because the algebraically-equal form differs in the last f32 bits and every prior gate is pinned.
- **NEW RULE, found by sabotage (`opposing_pair_caps`, `bevel_op/clamp.rs`).** Going per-edge removes
  a protection the global minimum gave BY ACCIDENT. A 0.1-thick plate's long edges have 1.0 of *local*
  room, so a 0.3 target flies past the opposite wall — verified by disabling the rule: the bottom
  edge's rail lands at **z = +0.25 on a plate surfaced at 0.05**. Vertex-local terms cannot see it
  (the colliding edges are two steps apart in the face ring, never adjacent). Now bounded by
  `w_a + w_b ≤ separation` for facing non-adjacent pairs, split proportionally so the width ratio
  survives. Opposition threshold −0.95 (~18° off antiparallel) and the number is load-bearing: at
  −0.5 a 32-gon cylinder cap cuts a legitimate 0.97·r rim bevel to ~0.82·r.
- **Persistence** (category-1 risk, so it ran first): `bevel_var_width: u8` + `bevel_width_min: f32`
  are `#[serde(skip)]` on `PolyModifier` and ride a NEW `FL4PBVAR` tail section written LAST. Never
  an in-blob field (positional bincode corrupts every existing `.fl4`) and never a widened
  `PolyModFlagRecord`/`PolyRemeshRecord` (a section decode error propagates with `?` and fails the
  ENTIRE load). Off ⇒ no record ⇒ no magic bytes ⇒ byte-identical to pre-feature saves.
- **Display cache:** both fields are in `poly_modifier_stack_hash`, and the authored-channel key
  predicate now also matches a Bevel with driver = authored weight (its `geo_channel` can stay `All`,
  so the channel test alone missed it). Without either, the toggle looks inert until an unrelated
  edit forces a rebuild — the trap the Smart Select tags hit on 2026-08-05.
- **Consume Geometry is mutually exclusive** — the UI disables Variable Width while Consume is on
  AND zeroes the field, because Consume can fall back to the plain bevel path where hidden state
  would otherwise still drive visible geometry. Absorb decides which rings to dissolve from ONE
  width.
- **Gates:** 6 new kernel (`bevel_op/tests.rs var_width_*`) + 4 app —
  `poly_bevel_var_params_round_trip` (round-trip, no-magic-when-unused, and `FL4PRMSH` still decodes
  after the new section), `collect_poly_bevel_var_emits_only_enabled_modifiers`,
  `bevel_variable_width_changes_stack_hash`, and
  `bevel_variable_width_reaches_the_kernel_through_the_stack` (drives the REAL path through
  `apply_poly_modifiers_tagged`: OFF ⇒ the big box gets the tiny one's 0.05, ON ⇒ 0.3, authored
  weight 1 ⇒ 0.3, unweighted ⇒ `width_min`). core_math 1085 passed with the same 3 pre-existing
  failures as the pre-change baseline; `app --bins` 731 passed with the same 5 pre-existing failures
  (all main-blob `.fl4` decode, before any tail section is read); serde_golden 3/3.
- **Out of scope, stated:** the interactive `B` drag tool and Adjust-Last-Bevel keep uniform width
  (they compile untouched); no live width-range readout in the panel — the telemetry is thread-local
  and the modifier evaluates off the display-sync path, so it would read stale from the UI thread.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — BEVELOPPWALL: uniform bevel can also overrun a thin wall — ⚠️ OPEN (pre-existing, NOT introduced above)

Found while building BEVELVARWIDTH; deliberately **not** fixed there (it would change existing
uniform bevels and risk the cylinder-cap width the STEP-1 comment warns about — out of that task's
scope).

- **Repro:** a 0.1-thick plate (`new_box(1,1,0.05)`), select ONLY the 8 long edges, width 0.1, Clamp
  Overlap ON. Each long edge's constraint comes from the slide walk over its unbeveled short
  neighbour ⇒ ~0.1 allowed, while the wall between two facing long edges is only 0.1 total. Both
  rails advance 0.1 into a 0.1 gap and cross.
- **Why the clamp misses it:** every STEP-1 term is vertex-local (collapse over in-face neighbours,
  slide over collinear runs). The colliding edges are two steps apart in the face ring, so no term
  ever compares them. The global minimum usually hides this because a thin wall's own short edges
  contribute a smaller limit — but only when those edges are IN the selection.
- **Fix already written and available:** `core_math::bevel_op::clamp::opposing_pair_caps` does
  exactly this bound and is currently called only on the variable-width path. Extending it to the
  uniform path is a one-line call; the risk is behaviour change on existing bevels, so it needs the
  cylinder-cap / owner-ring oracles re-run before it lands.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — LOOPCUTPARAMS / LOOPCUTCURVE: no Ctrl+R tool parameters, and the cut ignored curvature — ✅ FIXED

Owner: "CTRL R DOES NOT HAVE TOOL PARAMETER, AND I NEED A TOGGLE THAT FOLLOW CURVATURE, IN THIS
IMAGE THE EDGE DO NOT FOLLOW CURVATURE."

- **LOOPCUTPARAMS root cause:** `ui2_draw_tool_params` gated the Loop Cut panel on
  `tool.current.is_poly_loop_cut_slide()` — the *slide session*, which
  `poly_loop_cut_session_tick` only creates once an edge is under the cursor. Press Ctrl+R while
  hovering nothing and the panel fell through to the "active tool catalog" branch and rendered
  nothing, which reads as "this tool has no parameters". ✅ FIXED — gated on
  `poly_loop_cut_is_active()` (armed OR sliding); with no session the panel edits the tool-settings
  defaults the session will latch. The panel also never re-cut after an edit, so in Live mode
  changing Cuts did nothing until the next drag — it now calls `poly_loop_cut_regenerate()`.
- **LOOPCUTCURVE root cause:** the inserted vertices come from `split_edge(he, t)`, a straight lerp
  along the rail. On a rounded form the chord lies INSIDE the surface, so the new loop flattens the
  round — visible in the owner's screenshot as a cut that ignores the curve it sits on. ✅ FIXED —
  `HalfEdgeMesh::rail_curve_point()` returns the point on the CIRCULAR arc through the rail's two
  endpoint normals (cubic Bézier, tangent offset `k = 4/3·tan(α/4)·R`, α = angle between the
  normals), and `apply_loop_cut_curvature()` moves each inserted vertex there using the parent map
  from `loop_cut_multi_with_delta`. Exposed as a **Follow Curvature** toggle + 0–2 strength, default
  OFF (Blender's `smoothness = 0`), in both Tool Parameters and the Tool Properties strip.
- **Why the delta and not a post-hoc walk:** in a multi-cut a new vertex's rail NEIGHBOURS are the
  other new vertices, not the original rail ends. `TopoDelta::vert_parents` records
  `(bottom, 1−t), (top, t)` at insertion, which is the only place the true rail and parameter
  survive.
- **Fails closed:** equal endpoint normals (flat surface) collapse the tangent scale to the classic
  1/3, the control points land evenly on the segment and the result is EXACTLY the straight lerp —
  the toggle can never dent a flat face. A rail parallel to its endpoint normal has no tangent, and
  a zero-normal endpoint has no curvature; both return the chord.
- **Preview is not a lie:** `draw_loop_cut_preview` and the K through-cut both call the same
  `rail_curve_point`, over the new `loop_cut_preview_rail_verts` (ids instead of positions, one
  shared strip walk with `loop_cut_preview_rails`). The yellow line bulges exactly where the loop
  will land.
- **Not covered:** segment mode (`edge_series_cut`, the no-quad-ring fallback) reports no parent map
  and a lone edge has no strip curvature to follow — it stays a straight lerp.
- Tests: `rail_curve_point_is_exact_lerp_on_flat_geometry`,
  `loop_cut_curvature_puts_the_new_loop_back_on_the_sphere` (curved midpoint lands within 0.5% of
  the unit sphere; the chord midpoint does not), `loop_cut_with_curvature_keeps_inserted_verts_on_the_sphere`
  (end-to-end through the delta plumbing). All 15 loop-cut tests green.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — LOOPCUTMULTIRING: Ctrl+R did not support multi-selection — ✅ FIXED

Owner, on a bored rounded box with both rim loops selected: "CTRL R DOES NOT SUPPORT MULTI
SELECTION."

- **Root cause:** `poly_start_loop_cut_session` (`app/src/poly/loop_cut.rs`) modelled a session as
  ONE seed edge plus one optional span limit. A multi-edge selection was fed in whole as the
  *limit* and the seed was taken with `selected_edges.iter().next()`. Two consequences: a selection
  spanning several rings could only ever produce ONE cut, and since `selected_edges` is a
  `HashSet`, WHICH ring that was is nondeterministic. The kernel was never the limitation —
  `loop_cut_multi` cuts one ring per call and was only ever called once.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-10 — `HalfEdgeMesh::loop_cut_ring_groups()` (`half_edge/ops_loop_cut.rs`)
  partitions an edge selection into independent rings, and the session carries the extras in
  `PolyLoopCutSlide::extra_rings`. Every apply path (live regenerate, confirm, preview draw, R
  rotate, K through-cut, and the menu/command one-shot) runs over the full ring list.
- **The partition is exact, not heuristic:** a rail belongs to exactly ONE ring — the ring seeded
  at that rail — so no edge can land in two groups. Grouping walks each ring once and claims the
  selected edges on it: O(Σ strip lengths), not O(selection²).
- **Per-ring rules are the OLD single-ring rules**, extracted to `loop_cut_resolve_ring()` so the
  two cannot drift: a 2+-edge group limits the span (partial cut), a single-edge group is a free
  full ring, a limit that kills its own ring is dropped, no quad ring falls back to segments.
  A single-ring selection resolves to exactly one group, so old behaviour is unchanged.
- **Two traps found while building it:**
  1. Segment-mode groups must NOT be split — `edge_series_cut` creates cut segments by connecting
     cut points that share a face, so one edge at a time would split each edge and join none.
     All segment groups collapse back into one segment ring (`loop_cut_rings_from_selection`).
  2. The result-selection filter that drops same-rail chords compared every new edge against ONE
     seed direction. With rings at different orientations (16 meridians around a hole) ring A's
     real cut loop is parallel to ring B's seed rail, so it would be dropped. The filter is now
     per ring, keyed by which ring inserted each vertex.
- **Unchanged by design:** hovering an edge OUTSIDE the selection is still a fresh free single cut
  (owner rule 2026-08-07 — leftover result selection must not become a limit). To get the
  multi-ring cut, invoke Ctrl+R while hovering one of the selected edges or off the geometry.
- **Cap:** `MAX_LOOP_CUT_RINGS = 256`, toasted when clamped — live mode re-cuts every ring on every
  drag frame (Frame Budget Rule). A full edge loop on a dense cylinder is legitimately hundreds of
  rings, hence the generous ceiling.
- Tests: `loop_cut_ring_groups_partitions_selection`, `loop_cut_two_rings_from_one_selection`
  (`core_math/src/half_edge/tests.rs`). All 12 loop-cut tests green.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — FILLWELD: Fill could create a face welded to NOTHING — ✅ FIXED

Found while adding single-vertex Quad Fill. Latent in the shipped 3+-vertex Fill path, not new.

- **Root cause (still open, guarded at the callers):** `create_face_no_normals`
  (`half_edge/euler.rs:478`) returns `None` **only** when `vertex_ids.len() < 3`; after that it
  unconditionally allocates and returns `Some`. Its twin pass (`:507-517`) is best-effort — when
  `find_half_edge(dst, src)` misses it silently leaves `twin == NO_TWIN`. So Fill's long-standing
  "dry-run `create_face` on a clone" proved nothing beyond the length check.
- **Compounding:** `delete_face` can leave a hole corner's disk pointer aimed at the rim
  half-edge, so `vertex_fan` yields one edge and never covers the sector — and `find_half_edge`
  fans. The twinning is therefore least reliable exactly at hole boundaries, which is where Fill
  is used.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-10 — `prove_weld()` in `app/src/poly/fill.rs` is now the single weld proof for
  both the 3+-vertex and single-vertex paths: clone → `create_face` → `validate()` →
  `is_manifold()`. Each check is held against the result **only when the ORIGINAL passed it**, so
  an already-broken body stays repairable (owner directive 2026-08-03: "all tools must work even
  on open / non-manifold shapes").
- **The guard alone would have been a regression** — `is_manifold` check (a) fires on precisely
  the ring camera-facing winding produces from the wrong side of a hole, so it would have turned
  ~half of all camera angles from "silent bad face" into "refuses". Winding for a boundary fill is
  **topological, not view-dependent**, so a refused ring is retried REVERSED; camera winding is
  tried first, preserving previous behaviour for free-floating rings where both windings weld.
- **Remaining limit (documented in code):** on an already-non-manifold body the manifold gate is
  off by design, so the retry cannot fire and the camera choice stands — byte-identical to
  pre-guard behaviour, but a dirty body can still take a badly-wound fill.
- **Root-cause fix NOT done:** a `create_face` that can actually refuse. `install_face_rings_local`
  already twins via an edge map and is the honest basis for it.
- Gates: `a_clean_hole_still_fills_from_either_camera_side`,
  `a_ring_that_welds_to_nothing_is_refused_and_the_mesh_is_untouched`,
  `an_already_non_manifold_body_can_still_be_filled`. Rebuild required.

## 2026-08-10 (master) — EPISODECANCEL: cancelled keyboard-armed poly modals leave a junk undo entry — ⬜ OPEN

Found during Offset Edge Loop P4. Affects SEVEN tools, so the fix belongs in one place.

- `auto_commit_episodes` (`undo.rs:1006-1011`) commits whenever `!pointer.any_down()`. A modal
  armed by a KEY (Ctrl+B bevel, Ctrl+B vertex bevel, `I` inset, `I` offset loop, shrink/fatten,
  face hinge) has no pointer down at arm time, so its episode is committed at the end of the arm
  frame. The later `cancel_episode()` then finds `pending_episode == None` and is a **no-op**.
- **Not data loss** — every one of these tools restores its `original_mesh` manually on cancel, so
  the geometry is correct. The defect is a spurious undo entry after a cancelled modal. Confirm
  still yields exactly ONE entry per drag.
- **Fix belongs in `auto_commit_episodes`, once, for all of them** — never per-tool (CLAUDE.md
  § No Bandaids: "Two code paths for the same operation MUST share one path"). The exemption
  pattern already sits immediately above the offending block (`shift_duplicate` and `array_dup`
  both early-return), and `ActiveTool::is_poly_modal()` already exists as the predicate.

Owner: *"app just crash"* — exit `0xcfffffff`, dump `app.exe.*.dmp`, panic file

## 2026-08-09 (master) — OPENEDGESEL: edge selection silently drops the rim of any OPEN mesh — ✅ FIXED

Owner: *"selection on an open shape, plane-like, does not work — not able to select poly. Also
another bug related to selection: sometimes the highlight of an edge does not render even if the
edge gets selected."*

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-09 — **Five selection paths each carried their own copy of "walk the mesh's
  edges", and the copy was wrong on open meshes.** The legacy inline rule was
  `if he.face == NO_FACE { continue }` followed by a min-of-pair test
  (`if twin != NO_TWIN && i > twin.0 { continue }`). On an OPEN mesh those two tests
  **annihilate each other**: `dissolve_face` / Delete-Only-Faces / a knife cut that stops inside
  a face all KEEP the half-edge and merely clear its `face` back-pointer
  (`half_edge/euler.rs:362`), and the surviving faceless half holds the **LOWER** id of its pair.
  The faceless half is then dropped by the face test, and its faced twin is dropped by the
  min-of-pair test — so the edge is enumerated by **nobody**.
- **Measured** (`make_cube()` + `dissolve_face(FaceId(1))`, 12 undirected edges): the canonical
  walk yields `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9,11,13,15]`; the legacy walk yields `[0,1,2,3,9,11,13,15]`.
  The four rim edges `4,5,6,7` are live, faceless, lower-id, and **absent from every legacy
  path**.
- **What the user saw.** Those same edges ARE enumerated by the pick cache
  (`rebuild_pick_cache`), the GPU select buffer (`render_poly_select_buffer`) and the wire
  overlay (`collect_poly_local_edges`), which all use `is_edge_live` + min-of-pair. So a rim edge
  drew, hovered and single-clicked normally — but Box / Circle / Lasso / **Paint** select
  (`poly_screen_test`), **Select All** (`poly_select_all_toggle`), **Invert**
  (`poly_invert_selection`) and **Select Linked** (`poly_select_linked_hover` /
  `_from_sel`) could never reach it. Pressing A on an open shape highlighted every edge except
  the rim, which reads exactly as *"the edge got selected but the highlight doesn't render."*
- **Fix (structural, not per-site).** ONE definition —
  `HalfEdgeMesh::canonical_edges()` (`core_math/src/half_edge/nav.rs`): every undirected edge
  once, as the lower id of its twin pair, **liveness the only filter**. Its doc states why a
  `face == NO_FACE` filter must never come back. All nine walks now route through it: the five
  broken ones plus the four that were already correct (`rebuild_pick_cache`,
  `render_poly_select_buffer`, `poly_edges_or_all`, `collect_poly_local_edges`) — so there is no
  second copy left to drift.
- **Also fixed in the same walk:** `poly_screen_test`'s back-face-cull fallback called
  `world_face_normal(he.face)` unguarded. With faceless edges now enumerated that would index
  `face_vertices(NO_FACE)` and **panic**. It now reads both incident faces via `edge_faces()`,
  guards dead/absent faces to a ZERO normal (which `faces_camera` already treats as "don't
  cull"), and **never culls a pure wire edge** — an edge with no incident face has no facing to
  test and is visible from every direction.
- Gates: `canonical_edges_visits_each_undirected_edge_once`,
  `canonical_edges_keeps_the_rim_of_an_open_mesh` (asserts the legacy walk loses exactly those
  four — the bug pinned as an assertion), `canonical_edges_keeps_wire_edges_and_skips_freed_slots`.
  `cargo check -p app` green.
- ⚠️ UNBLOCKED IN PASSING (pre-existing, owner WIP) — `cargo test -p core_math` did not compile
  at all: `half_edge/tests.rs:470` built a `HalfEdgeMesh` struct literal missing the new
  `free_index` field. Replaced with `HalfEdgeMesh::new()`, which is what the field's own doc
  demands (a literal bypasses `rebuild_free_index`). Without this the mandatory core_math gate
  could not be run.
- ⚠️ OPEN (pre-existing, NOT this task — owner's in-flight `validate.rs` +304 /
  `ops_dissolve.rs` +114 rework): 3 core_math tests fail on the current working tree —
  `edge_select::tests::directed_loop_crosses_pole_straight` ("plain loop must stop at the pole"),
  `mesh_ops::tests::apply_in_place_refusal_leaves_mesh_untouched` and
  `clean_mesh_still_refuses_slit_creating_dissolve` (both "`is_manifold()` must refuse a
  slit-creating dissolve"). `canonical_edges` has **zero callers inside core_math**, so it cannot
  reach them. 1045 pass.
- ⬜ OPEN — the owner's second report ("highlight sometimes does not render") is **plausibly but
  not provably** the same root cause. The rim-edge dropout explains it for open meshes; if it
  still reproduces on a CLOSED mesh it is a separate bug and needs its own repro (see the
  candidate list in the session notes: object-wire overpaint ordering when shaded+wire is on,
  and the base-cage-vs-display-mesh depth test with a live modifier stack, which
  `overlay_faces.rs` escapes via `modifier_cage` X-ray but `append_poly_selected_edges` does not).

## 2026-08-09 (master) — EXTRUDEREPROCLOBBER: the intrude repro rig destroyed its own failure captures — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-09 — **A refused through-cut's repro dump was overwritten by the next
  successful cut**, so the rig lost exactly the case it exists to preserve. Found while
  triaging an owner console log: the log showed `[EXTRUDE-PT] kernel refused: target
  boundary=10 folds=0 vol=14.85256 | cutter vol=8.99950`, but by the time
  `%TEMP%\azra_extrude_repro.json` was read it held the *following* successful cut (its
  `cutter vol=2.36549` matched the success line exactly). The failing mesh was unrecoverable.
- Root: `poly_drag_tools/extrude_drag.rs` had **two** dump sites — the always-on pre-boolean
  capture and the kernel-refusal capture — both writing the SAME path
  (`azra_extrude_repro.json`). Any success after a failure clobbered it.
- Fix: refusals now write `azra_extrude_repro_FAIL.json`; the rolling per-cut capture keeps
  `azra_extrude_repro.json`. The two byte-identical `dump` closures (differing only in local
  names and comments — a No-Duplication violation) collapsed into one shared
  `repro_mesh_soup()` + `write_extrude_repro()` pair. Index-preserving behaviour unchanged.

## 2026-08-09 (master) — UNBEVELRAIL: Ctrl+Alt+B resized the WHOLE last bevel and refused a rail-edge pick — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-09 — owner: *"unbevel ctrl alt b in this situation should just affect the
  selected segment letting user resize and collapse the edge bevel"* (screenshot: one lengthwise
  edge of a rounded corner selected in edge mode).
- Defect 1 (app, `poly_drag_tools/bevel_drag.rs`): `poly_activate_unbevel` preferred the
  `poly_bevel_history` entry whenever its `post_signature` matched. That entry holds the ENTIRE
  edge set the last bevel ran on, so the restore+live-rebevel session resized/removed every one
  of those bevels regardless of what the user had selected. Fix: an explicit face/edge selection
  is an explicit SCOPE — it now skips history and goes to the reverse-math path, which
  reconstructs the sharp edge for that strip only. Empty selection still gets the exact history
  restore (unchanged default).
- Defect 2 (`core_math/src/unbevel.rs`): a RAIL (lengthwise) edge — what the user actually clicks
  — was the documented KNOWN LIMIT from the 2026-08-08 fix. It borders the bevel strip and the
  flat wall equally, so seed 1 (incident faces) is strip+wall by construction and seed 2
  (crossed) spans nothing. New seed 3 `rail_strip`: walk ACROSS the strip from the seed edge,
  starting on the narrower of its two faces, stopping at the first face >3× that width. That
  walk is also the scoping — only the strip column at the selected edge is collected.
- Ordering: seed 3 runs FIRST, gated on `saw_wall` (an unambiguous rail). Tried last it still
  failed, because seed 1 does not refuse a rail selection on a cube — it succeeds *wrongly*,
  collapsing the strip+wall pair into a plausible 7-face mesh. Cross-edge/face selections see no
  asymmetry, get `None`, and keep every prior seed order and gate.
- KNOWN LIMIT (documented): where flanking faces are as narrow as the bevel itself the walk can
  overshoot; the reverse-math gate, the app manifold gate and the undo episode are the guards.
- Gate: `unbevel_from_one_rail_edge_restores_exact_cube`. core_math 1037 pass / 3 pre-existing
  failures (verified identical with the change stashed). `cargo build -p app` green.

## 2026-08-10 (feat/remesh-gpu) — REMESHSOLIDNOINCR: incremental remesh NEVER engages on a solid — ✅ FIXED

  `voxel_remesh_full` latches `had_enclosed_void` on `sealed_pocket` alone. A solid's interior is
  all far cells, so it no longer arms the lockout; a hollow shell's cavity lining is in-band air and
  still does. A named struct rather than a re-defined `usize` so the two counts cannot be

  solids would land where the crust is (~26 ms). They land at 61.7 ms — 3.1× better, not 7.3×. A
  solid drag frame is genuinely more work than a crust one at the same resolution, and *why* is not

  and `REMESH_INCR_MAX_DIRTY_FRAC` forces a full eval. That is the documented counter-fixture
  behaviour, not a residue of this bug.

  stateless reference bit-for-bit) paired with the existing
  `incremental_refuses_fields_with_sealed_voids` (a real void must still refuse). Both directions

  **V1 incremental voxel remesh is inert for every closed solid mesh.** A drag under Remesh on a
  solid takes the FULL stateless path on every single frame.

  | 256 | uv sphere (solid) | 188.2 ms | **191.1 ms** | **0/6** |
  ROOT CAUSE — `enclosed` conflates "solid interior" with "sealed void". `band_finalize`
  (`io_bridge/src/mesh_to_sdf.rs:901`) increments `enclosed` for **every far cell the border flood
  did not reach**, which for any closed solid is its entire interior: a solid cube at res 128
  reports `enclosed = 512000`. `voxel_remesh_full` then does `had_enclosed_void: enclosed > 0`
  (`app/src/poly/remesh.rs`), and the incremental path refuses any cache carrying that flag — a
  deliberate one-way lockout, because filling a genuine void cannot be undone by a local splice.
  So the lockout fires on the wrong signal and never releases.
  **This is the SAME SYMPTOM as SEALFALSEFILL below, via a second, independent route.** That fix
  (`da65fbb`) corrected `seal_enclosed_air`'s false seals and concluded closed meshes could go
  incremental again. They cannot — the band sampler's own counter re-arms the same lockout on the
  first eval, before `seal_enclosed_air` is ever consulted. The earlier entry's premise is
  falsified by the table above.
  WHY IT WENT UNSEEN — every incremental fixture in `app/src/poly/remesh.rs` is `new_plane`, an
  open crust with no far interior, which is the one shape class where the flag stays false. The
  hollow-cube gate (`incremental_refuses_fields_with_sealed_voids`) passes for the wrong reason: it
  would refuse for any solid, void or not. And the octree plan's headline "24.9 ms drag frame @256"
  is a plane measurement — the solid number is **191 ms (~5 fps)**, 7.3× worse.
  PROPOSED FIX (own task, not done here) — split the counter. `band_finalize` has two branches:
  far-and-unreached (`v.is_nan()`, = solid interior, NOT a void) and **in-band-positive-and-
  unreached** (`*v > 0.0 && !outside[i]`, = a cell the surface says is air but which is
  unreachable — the lining of a genuine sealed pocket). Return them separately and key
  `had_enclosed_void` on the second only. A solid cube's interior is all NaN-far, so branch 2 is 0;
  a hollow cube's cavity lining fires it. GATE: the existing
  `incremental_refuses_fields_with_sealed_voids` must still refuse, and a new solid-cube case must
  now go incremental. Red line 1 of `REMESH_GPU_PLAN.md` still binds — the lockout is not being
  weakened, it is being pointed at the right signal.
  IMPACT IF FIXED: solid drag @256 191 → ~26 ms without touching the GPU. This outranks the entire
  GPU plan on effort-to-payoff and re-sequences it.

## 2026-08-09 (feat/remesh-adaptive-octree) — SEALFALSEFILL: seal_enclosed_air filled REACHABLE air — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ **FIXED 2026-08-09 — `VoxelGrid::seal_enclosed_air` emitted FALSE SEALS: it filled air that is
  genuinely reachable from the grid border, and then latched the one-way `had_enclosed_void` on the
  strength of it.** Found by the new parity gate while replacing the flood for speed (Gate 1b of
  `REMESH_ADAPTIVE_OCTREE_PLAN.md`); the function had no test of any kind before that.
  ROOT CAUSE — aliased walkable/visited mask. The flood's `air: Vec<bool>` meant BOTH "is air" and
  "not yet visited". `visit_row` pushed only the FIRST cell of a run it found, then cleared the rest
  of that run **without pushing it**, and bounded the clear to the parent span's `x1`. On popping
  the pushed cell, its right-expansion immediately saw the next cell already cleared and stopped.
  So (a) the cleared tail never seeded a neighbour-row scan, and (b) anything beyond `x1` in that
  run was never visited at all → counted unreachable → filled solid.
  IMPACT: not cosmetic. On an analytic SOLID BALL (no cavity at all) it filled **3310 cells**. And
  the poly remesh does `if c.grid.seal_enclosed_air() > 0 { c.had_enclosed_void = true; }`
  (`app/src/poly/remesh.rs:403`), so a false seal **permanently banished an ordinary closed mesh to
  the full stateless remesh path** for the rest of that cache's life — i.e. the incremental remesh
  silently stopped working for closed meshes, and the drag got slower, for a bug.
  FIX: replaced the flood with connected components over RUNS (air is run-structured: ~131k runs
  vs 16.7M cells). Per-row run extraction in parallel, union-find where two runs in y±1/z±1
  neighbour rows are 6-connected iff their x ranges overlap, then fill any run not joined to a
  virtual OUTSIDE node. Border seeding matches the original seed loop exactly.
  Sphere fixture now fills **0** (correct). Seal @256³: 24.1 → 3.7ms as a side effect.
  TESTS: `core_math/tests/seal_enclosed_air_parity.rs` — the oracle is now a plain 6-connected BFS
  with a SEPARATE `seen` array (aliasing those two is what caused the bug), bit-exact over 8
  fixtures × 5 resolutions, plus `does_not_false_seal_reachable_air` pinning the specific
  two-steps-from-the-border cells the old code sealed. `incremental_refuses_fields_with_sealed_voids`
  still passes, so the lockout still fires for REAL voids — red line #1 intact.
  SEE ALSO memory `project_seal_enclosed_air_false_seals` — the same aliased-mask class bit once
  before elsewhere. Worth treating as a recurring class, not an instance.

## 2026-08-09 (feat/remesh-adaptive-octree) — REMESHPARAMSAVE: every Voxel Remesh param resets on load — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ **FIXED 2026-08-09 — all four authored Voxel Remesh modifier params were silently discarded by
  save→load.** Found during Gate 0 recon of `REMESH_ADAPTIVE_OCTREE_PLAN.md` (not a remesh *perf*
  issue — a data-loss one). Priority ladder #3 (save-load regression).
  REPRO: add a Voxel Remesh modifier to a poly body, set resolution 256 / smooth off / padding 0.3
  / project 0.5, save `.fl4`, reload → the modifier comes back at **32 / true / 0.1 / 1.0** and the
  displayed mesh silently changes with it.
  ROOT CAUSE: `remesh_resolution`, `remesh_smooth`, `remesh_padding`, `remesh_project` are all
  `#[serde(skip)]` on `PolyModifier` (`core_math/src/scene_graph/node.rs:577-599`) — correctly, since
  bincode is positional and putting them in the blob would corrupt every existing `.fl4` (the
  documented field trap). **But the side-channel they claim to use was never written.** The doc
  comment at `node.rs:571-576` states *"They ride the `FL4PMODF` tail instead, same as
  `bevel_consume`"* — aspirational, not implemented. `PolyModFlagRecord`
  (`app/src/project/mod.rs:194-198`) is exactly `{ node_id, mod_index, bevel_consume }`, and
  `grep -rn "remesh_" app/src/project/ app/src/project_save.rs app/src/project_load.rs` returns
  **zero hits**. `remesh_resolution`'s only live uses are evaluation (`mesh_sync.rs:541/2439`), the
  stack hash (`:1730`), and the UI (`properties_poly.rs:2005`). Nothing persists it.
  So the fields fall back to `default_remesh_*()` on every load. Of the four tail magics that do
  exist — `FL4PNORM`, `FL4PPRM\0`, `FL4PMODF`, `FL4PSMTH` (`app/src/project/io.rs:74-105`) — none
  carries a remesh value.
  FIX (do NOT widen `FL4PMODF`): appending a field to `PolyModFlagRecord` breaks loading every
  `.fl4` an older build already wrote, because `load_binary` propagates a section decode error with
  `?` and fails the ENTIRE load, not just that section (`io.rs:310-317`) — this is documented
  in-tree at `io.rs:101-104` as the exact reason `FL4PSMTH` was created rather than widening
  `FL4PMODF`. Correct fix is a NEW 8-byte-magic tail section written LAST, carrying all four values,
  emitted only when non-default so unused scenes stay byte-identical; reattach by
  (node_id, mod_index) skipping dangling ids / out-of-range indices / non-poly nodes. Model the
  round-trip test on `poly_smooth_falloff_round_trip` (`app/src/project/tests.rs:493`) and assert
  BOTH round-trip and absence-of-magic-when-unused.
  FIX AS SHIPPED: new `FL4PRMSH` tail section (`POLY_REMESH_MAGIC`, `app/src/project/io.rs`)
  carrying `PolyRemeshRecord { node_id, mod_index, resolution, smooth, padding, project }`
  (`app/src/project/mod.rs`), written **LAST** after `FL4PSMTH`; `collect_poly_remesh`
  (`app/src/project_save.rs`) emits a record ONLY for modifiers whose params differ from
  `PolyModifier::default()`, so a scene that never touched a Remesh slider produces no section and
  stays byte-identical to earlier saves; reattached by (node_id, stack index) in
  `app/src/project_load.rs` with the same forward-tolerance as its siblings (dangling id /
  out-of-range index / non-poly node are skipped, never a crash). Deliberately NO
  `geo_channel.is_all()` gate — that gate is correct for `FL4PSMTH`'s mask params (inert without a
  channel) and would be wrong here, since a resolution is authored state either way.
  The false doc comment at `node.rs:571-576` (which claimed the `FL4PMODF` carrier) is corrected.
  TESTS: `poly_remesh_params_round_trip` pins all four values through save→load, pins that an
  unused feature writes no magic at all, and pins that `FL4PSMTH` (written immediately before the
  new section) still decodes intact — append-newest-last is only safe if each section is
  self-delimiting. `collect_poly_remesh_emits_only_authored_params` pins the non-default filter.
  Regression check: the 4 pre-existing `project::` failures (`owner_bevel_segment_fl4_no_spoke_fan`
  + 3 intrude gates) are unchanged — they fail in the MAIN BLOB deserialize (`io.rs:269`, "invalid
  u8 while decoding bool"), before any tail parsing, and a `#[serde(skip)]` field cannot move a
  bincode position.
  NOTE: `REMESH_ADAPTIVE_OCTREE_PLAN.md` Gate 3 step 3 was written on the false premise that a
  carrier already existed. Gate 3 should add `remesh_detail_levels` to `PolyRemeshRecord` — but
  **only while this branch is still unreleased.** Widening `FL4PRMSH` is safe exactly as long as no
  shipped build has ever written it; the moment one has, widening it becomes the same trap that
  forbids widening `FL4PMODF` (a short record fails the ENTIRE load via `?`, not just that
  section). If this lands before Gate 3, Gate 3 needs its own section instead.

## 2026-08-09 (master) — DFBGL15: deferred + fog pipelines invalid (binding 15) — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-09 — **PBR viewport completely frozen; `set_pipeline("deferred")` failed every
  frame** (owner: *"i can no longer zoom (scroll) in pbr render"* — reported as an input
  regression, actually a dead render path). Log signature: repeating
  `InvalidPipelineId(Id(41,1,vk))` on `ComputePass::set_pipeline label="deferred"`, followed by
  `Command encoder is invalid` cascading through `tonemap`, `overlay_lines`, `overlay_faces`.
  Nothing was submitted, so the presented image never changed — the camera *was* zooming, the
  viewport just never redrew. **Zoom/scroll input was never involved.**
  ROOT CAUSE: commit `8ad21f5` ("T1 live-march image displace — full prim + binding 15") added
  `@group(0) @binding(15) height_maps` to `sdf_prim_eval.wgsl`, on the assumption recorded in its
  own comment that *"Naga DCE strips when entry never samples."* True for raymarch (which declares
  `buf_ro(15)`) and prim_outline (auto-layout). **False for deferred and fog**: deferred calls
  `scene_sdf()` for SDF reflections (`deferred_entry.wgsl:1287,1297-1299`) and `pass_fog` calls it
  at `fog_entry.wgsl:129`; both reach `eval_prim` → `sample_height_map_live` → `height_maps`, so
  Naga keeps binding 15 LIVE. Neither `deferred_bgl_entries()` nor `fog_bgl` declared it, so
  `create_compute_pipeline` failed and the invalid pipeline was cached and reused forever.
  Note `FOG_EXCLUDE` strips neither `SDF_PRIM_EVAL` nor `SCENE_EVAL` (only `SCENE_QUERY`), which
  is why the fog build retains the call.
  WHY THE SHADER TESTS MISSED IT: `cargo test -p graphics` validates WGSL *modules* (Naga parse +
  validate). It never pairs a module with its `bgl.rs` layout, so a shader/BGL mismatch is
  invisible to all 85 tests — they passed both before and after.
  FIX (5 sites, BGL and bind group must move together): `buf_ro(15)` added to
  `graphics/src/bgl.rs deferred_bgl_entries()`; binding 15 added to the `deferred_bg` entries
  (`viewport_render.rs:1227` block); and the same pair added to fog's **four** duplicated sites —
  `app_new.rs` `fog_bgl`, `app_update.rs` `bg_fog_bgl`, `gpu_init/bgl.rs` `fog_bg`,
  `viewport_render.rs` `fog_bg`. Buffer is `gpu.buffers.height_map_buffer` (dummy 4-byte when
  empty) with the `brick_pool_dummy_buf` fallback, matching the prim_outline site.
  Deferred-lite is unaffected (it strips `SDF_REFLECT`) and legally tolerates the superset layout.
  🔵 **OPEN (follow-up, not fixed here): no structural guard against shader/BGL mismatch.** This
  class recurs by construction — see `feedback_bgl_binding_sites`. Wanted: a headless test that
  builds each pipeline from `build_*_wgsl()` + its real `*_bgl_entries()` on a device, so a new
  binding fails CI instead of the viewport.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-09 (follow-up) — **fog BGL/bind-group duplication eliminated ("BGL Single
  Source" violation).** The layout was hand-written in TWO places kept in sync only by comment
  ("MUST match bg_fog_bgl in app_update.rs") and the bind group built in TWO more — four places
  a new binding had to land, which is precisely how binding 15 was missed above. Now:
  `graphics::bgl::fog_bgl_entries()` is the sole layout definition, called by `app_new.rs`
  `fog_bgl` and `app_update.rs` `bg_fog_bgl`; `gpu_init::bgl::rebuild_fog_bg()` is the sole
  bind-group builder. The inline `fog_bg` in `viewport_render.rs` was deleted — it could not
  simply call the helper in place, because the helper reads the fog textures off `gpu` and
  `fog_tex`/`fog_prev_tex` are still locals at that point, so the build was **moved down** to
  just after the texture-assignment line (verified: nothing between the two points reads
  `fog_bg`). Dead `fog_prev_view` local removed; `fog_view` still feeds the upsample bind group.
  Behaviour-preserving by construction: `app_new.rs`'s local `uni_entry`/`buf_ro`/`tex_entry`/
  `sto_entry` closures were byte-identical to `bgl.rs`'s `uni`/`buf_ro`/`tex`/`sto`, and
  `app_update.rs`'s expanded entries matched both. Verified: 0 hand-written fog BGL entry lists
  and exactly 1 `fog_bg` builder remain. Build green, `cargo test -p graphics` 85/85.

## 2026-08-09 (master) — BEVELCONSUMEROUND: Consume Geometry ignored Segments/Shape — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-09 — **Bevel "Consume Geometry" cut a FLAT chamfer regardless of Segments /
  Shape** (owner: *"geometri consume does not support segment and roundness"*). Consume runs a
  four-path chain — fuse → wedge → absorb+bevel → plain bevel — and three of them already took
  `&BevelParams`. `consume_wedge_cut` took `width: f32`, so on **boolean-rim topology** (retraced
  n-gons / support edges / micro-clusters, where the fuse refuses — the owner's EAT class) the
  params could not physically reach the cutter. Fix: the sweep's cross-section is now the consume
  profile itself. New `consume_profile_point()` in `bevel_absorb.rs` is the SINGLE profile
  definition, called by both the fuse loft and the wedge, so the two paths cannot disagree about
  roundness; `build_rim_wedge` emits rings X, P_0=A … P_segs=B (segments=1 reproduces the old
  triangular wedge face-for-face); `consume_wedge_cut` takes `&BevelParams`; the drag records
  `record_external_bevel(width, segments)` instead of a hardcoded 1. The profile's rim control is
  LIFTED off the surface by the same 2%-of-width the a/b rails use — at shape=1 the profile passes
  through its control point, which unlifted would make the cutter tangent to the surface along the
  whole rim (the known boolean degeneracy). Gate is geometric, not topological:
  `wedge_cut_rounds_with_segments_and_shape` measures the cut's closest approach to the original
  sharp rim locus and pins flat > chord foot, seg=4 at least 20% nearer, shape=0 retreating and
  shape=1 advancing. Verified RED pre-fix (round == flat to the last digit, 0.1470). Refusal
  behaviour unchanged — every gate still fails closed to absorb+bevel. Full autopsy in
  `docs/planning/poly/BEVEL.md` §11 (2026-08-09).
- ✅ ADDED 2026-08-09 — **SHIFT toggles Consume Geometry while the bevel is live** (owner request).
  Rising-edge latch (`PolyBevelDrag.shift_was_down`, same shape as the existing `ctrl_was_down`
  unbevel latch) — SHIFT is a modifier, not an `egui::Key`, so it has no `ACTION_DEFS` chord and
  cannot appear in the rebind editor. **Collision resolved, not ignored:** SHIFT was the
  profile-shape gate in `poly_update_bevel_drag`, which would have flipped consume on every shape
  tweak; shape moved to **ALT+drag** (and remains on the Tool Parameters Shape field). Toasts and
  the hint line updated in the same pass.

## 2026-08-09 (master) — OPPERF3: kernel perf round 3, 4 fixes — ✅ FIXED

Cumulative across all three rounds, measured in ONE harness against the same pre-sweep baseline:

| case | pre-sweep | **now** | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inset_region`, 64-face sel, 9216 f | 103.85 ms | **0.851 ms** | **122×** |
| `inset_region`, 64-face sel, 4096 f | 56.97 ms | **0.558 ms** | 102× |
| `extrude_region`, 1024-face sel | 113.11 ms | **1.088 ms** | 104× |
| `extrude_region`, 4096-face sel | 2041 ms | **120.8 ms** | 17× |
| boolean difference, 6144 f target | 411.85 ms | **205.4 ms** | 2.0× |
| `is_manifold()` @ 9216 f | 10.71 ms | **0.902 ms** | 11.9× |
| `count_folded_coplanar_pairs()` @ 9216 f | 2.14 ms | **0.198 ms** | 10.8× |

- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-MANIFOLDCHK** (`half_edge/validate.rs`): `is_manifold()` was ~400× `validate()`
  (10.7 ms @ 9216 f) and `post_boolean_polish` gates each of 5 steps on it. `manifold_check` used three
  `(u32,u32)`-keyed `HashMap`s, a `Vec`-per-vertex `by_source`, and allocated a FRESH `HashMap`
  union-find INSIDE the per-vertex loop (~9k allocations); `integrity()` added a `Vec`+`HashSet` per
  face. Both rewritten for flat `Vec`-by-id (CSR counting sort + one epoch-stamped reusable
  union-find + `face_vertices_into`). is_manifold 8.44 → 0.91 ms, integrity 1.34 → 0.067 ms (20×);
  ~20 ms → ~1.7 ms per boolean at the polish gate. Verified against a VERBATIM oracle over bowtie
  (2- and 3-fan), 3-faces-on-an-edge, slit, wire, loose-vertex and long-free-list meshes **plus 4000
  randomized-corruption fuzz rounds** — zero divergence in verdict or message. Error messages are now
  deterministic (lowest id first) instead of `HashMap`-order dependent. Check (a2) proven unreachable
  given (a1) — documented and KEPT, not dropped.
- ✅ FIXED — **DELFACES-NONDET + INSET-BATCH-DELETE + REDUNDANT-NOW(inset)** (`half_edge/euler.rs`,
  `half_edge/ops_inset.rs`): `delete_faces` iterated the caller's `HashSet` (reproduced: 4 processes,
  4 digests) — now frees in ascending id order; `delete_faces_region` was additionally picking a
  RANDOM replacement vertex-disk pointer from a `HashMap` iteration (that pointer is `vertex_fan`'s
  start), now lowest-live-id. 3 regression guards, all failing when reverted. Unblocked
  `inset_region` batching its deletes: **5.90 → 0.70 ms (8.5×)** with **ZERO id shifts** (full bincode
  digest incl. all three free-lists unchanged — `live` was already sorted). The collar
  snapshot/restore in `inset_recompute_normals_local` was MEASURED before deletion (engages on 4–22
  verts across six primitives, zero differed) then removed.
- ✅ FIXED — **OPSMISC-CREATEFACE** (`half_edge/ops_misc.rs`): the scouted free-list scans turned out
  to be irrelevant — measurement found `create_face` (= `create_face_no_normals` + a WHOLE-MESH
  `recompute_normals()`) being called once per face inside batch loops that already end with their
  own full pass, so Mirror was N full normal passes all but one of them overwritten. `flip_across`
  compounded it: a half-flipped mesh has inconsistent winding, so `vertex_fan`'s walk never finds its
  start and every region pass silently degraded to O(mesh). @9216 f: **Mirror 5777 → 8.42 ms (686×),
  mirrored_across 5760 → 7.59 (759×), Solidify 4020 → 4.54 (885×), flip_across 4198 → 1.19 (3500×),
  connect_path 55 → 7.9**. Extracted `flip_face_winding()`; converted the 14 free-list scans; declined
  the remaining accessor conversions with the ceiling measured (0.26 ms of 15–40 ms ops — noise).
- ✅ FIXED — **FOLDPAIRS + FREELIST-SWEEP(ops_dissolve)** (`half_edge/ops_dissolve.rs`):
  `folded_coplanar_pairs_dbg` AND `limited_dissolve`'s candidate scan each called the allocating
  `compute_face_normal` twice per edge and re-derived every face normal once per INCIDENT edge; both
  now cache the fully-processed normal once per face (caching the composite, not the raw Newell —
  re-normalising an already-unit `Vec3` is not the f32 identity). All 15 free-list scans converted,
  both deliberate "free-list OR `half_edge == NO_EDGE`" sites keeping their OR. fold-pairs 2.08 →
  0.21 ms, `merge_vertices_to` 11.67 → 1.10 ms, `limited_dissolve` 52.6 → 8.5 ms. Verified by
  reimplementing the OLD algorithm in-process as a seed-free oracle (6 real fold pairs exercised;
  no natural fixture produces one, so two were hand-built) + 375 baseline-stable digest fields across
  3×3 runs.

**OPEN after round 3 — ranked:**

  agents: the boolean kernel, `extrude_region_volume`, `delete_faces`, `delete_faces_region`,
  `to_sphere`, `bevel_edges_ex`, `limited_dissolve`, `dissolve_*_region`, `dissolve_vertex`,

  `mesh_ops/mod.rs:1069` documents that edit ops now gate on `integrity()` only. The slit fixture was

- **FREELIST-SWEEP remainder**: ~11 open-coded `free_*.contains()` sites left (`ops_loop_cut` 4,

- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-FREELIST** (`half_edge/types.rs`, `half_edge/alloc.rs`): `is_edge_live` /
  `is_face_live` / `is_vert_live` — documented as "the canonical predicate every consumer MUST use",
  131 call sites — were `Vec::contains`, i.e. a LINEAR SCAN, making every kernel liveness sweep
  O(HE × free_len) and bulk delete O(N²). Added a `#[serde(skip)]` `FreeBitset` mirror maintained by
  the `alloc_*` / `free_*` chokepoints. **Deriving liveness from the canonical dead state was
  evaluated and REJECTED as unsound**: a live LOOSE vertex carries `half_edge == NO_EDGE`, exactly
  what a freed one carries, and that is a ratified invariant (`validate.rs:112` and `:182` both
  comment "loose … allowed, not corruption"); separately `euler.rs:420` allocates LIVE half-edges
  carrying the exact canonical dead tuple and patches them later. A hand-written `Deserialize` over a
  renamed wire mirror rebuilds the index so a loaded mesh can never be stale, and `contains` falls
  back to the linear scan on any cardinality mismatch so the mirror cannot lie. **On-disk shape
  byte-identical, verified independently by the coordinator in BOTH directions**: the committed
  golden blob (written by pre-change code) decodes and re-encodes to the same 1384 bytes, a mesh with
  a non-empty free list round-trips at 912 bytes, and post-load id allocation matches in-memory
  allocation. Full-mesh liveness sweep 5.50 → 0.037 ms @ 9216 f (149×).
- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-DELFACE** (`half_edge/euler.rs`): `delete_face` ran one FULL half-edge scan per
  corner vertex to repair stale `vertex.half_edge` pointers, with a NESTED `free_edges.contains`.
  Replaced with a single ascending pass resolving every stale corner at once, early-exiting when the
  last is answered — keeping the identical "lowest live id sourced at v, else NO_EDGE" choice.
  **Fan circulation was evaluated and REJECTED**: the required answer is a GLOBAL minimum and a vertex
  can carry several disjoint fans (booleans produce them, `validate()` tolerates them,
  `is_manifold()` check (d) exists to detect them), so a fan-derived pick would silently differ on
  exactly those meshes. 13.7× (65.3 → 4.8 ms); a single delete against a long free list 77×
  (5763 → 75 µs). Absorbed two duplicate copies of the same repair.
- ✅ FIXED — **NORMREGION (CORRECTNESS)** (`half_edge/normals.rs`): `recompute_normals_region`
  weighted every one-ring collar face by a hardcoded `area = 1.0`, under a comment describing an area
  derivation that was never written. All 11 callers (both grab paths, bevel, loop cut, 5× extrude,
  inset) therefore wrote vertex normals that a full `recompute_normals()` disagrees with — up to
  0.76 of normal-vector length (~50°) on curved geometry. Reached users via `to_mesh` →
  `export_node_obj` → OBJ `vn` lines and via inheritance by newly created vertices; the viewport was
  NOT affected (`to_raster_data` builds per-corner normals from face geometry). Found INDEPENDENTLY
  by two agents in different files. Fixed structurally — the region pass now shares the full pass's
  `weighted_face_terms_at` + `accumulate_weighted` kernel over real Newell areas, so the two can no
  longer drift. Region-vs-full write-set delta now **0.000000** on plane/box/uv-sphere/torus/
  cylinder/cone.
- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-FLIPFACE** (`half_edge/ops_misc.rs`): `flip_face` ended in a full-mesh
  `recompute_normals()` (0.166 ms/call at 4096 f, versus 0.210 ms for an entire full pass), and
  `extrude_region_volume` calls it once per region face. Now region-bounded: 0.0042 ms/call, **40×**,
  and per-call cost no longer grows with the mesh. This is what took the 4096-face-selection extrude
  from 772 ms to 115 ms.
- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-BOOL-B4** (`mesh_boolean_manifold.rs`): `re_dissolve_soup` passed its one material
  source as BOTH operands (double sample scan); `collapse_epsilon_debris` recomputed the caller's fold
  count; the sliver gate called `is_edge_manifold` twice (`A && B` where `A ⇒ B`); `min_edge_length`
  was recomputed per candidate; `resolve_overused_edges` built a dead second `BTreeMap` over every
  face corner on all 64 rounds, read by nothing but a `let _ = (…)` keep-alive (leftover scaffolding
  from a reverted attempt); and `halfedge_to_manifold` / the sliver scan used allocating accessors
  where `_into` exists. All provably output-identical (6 fixtures confirmed deterministic first, then
  digest-compared). 6144-face boolean 351 → 326 ms in isolation; 96-face 13.1 → 7.9 ms.

**OPEN after round 2:**

- ❗ **FL4LOAD (P1, NOT from this work): 5 app tests fail to load committed `.fl4` fixtures** —
  `dc_baseline::dc_gate0_committed_ref_fl4_loads_unchanged` plus 4 in `project::tests`, all
  `"Deserialize error: invalid u8 while decoding bool, expected 0 or 1, found 63"`. Diagnostic
  signature: `dc_gate0_ref_scene_roundtrip` PASSES while the committed-file gate FAILS — the code
  reads what it writes but no longer matches disk, i.e. a serialized-shape change in the working

  (`app/src/project/{io,mod,tests}.rs`, `project_load.rs`, `project_save.rs`, `dc_baseline.rs`) was
  last modified at 10:41, BEFORE any agent ran. Most likely the in-flight SMOOTHMASK work (new
  `FL4PSMTH` tail section + `#[serde(skip)]` fields on `PolyModifier` / `ProjectFile`). NOTE: the
  definitive stash-isolation test was blocked by a permission rule, so this is strong evidence, not
  a bisected proof.
- **DELFACES-NONDET**: `delete_faces` nondeterminism is now REPRODUCED, not theoretical — identical
  code on identical input produced three different mesh digests, and two pre-change baseline runs
  also differed. Its `HashSet<FaceId>` parameter decides free-list order and therefore all subsequent
  id allocation. This is the 4th confirmed instance of the HASHITER class (with the boolean,
  `extrude_region_volume`, and `delete_faces` itself).
- **INSET-BATCH-DELETE**: `inset_region` issues N separate `delete_face` calls; the same 64 through
  `delete_faces(&set)` measured **0.187 ms vs 4.78 ms (25×)**, which would take inset to ~0.7 ms.
  Gated on DELFACES-NONDET above — `delete_faces` is not a drop-in, it changes free-list order.
- **BOOL-MULTIMAT**: the multi-material nearest-face search is now the largest single item in the
  boolean, **65.6 ms of 326 ms**. Two agents independently declined to index it: `sample_score`
  branches on plane distance when coplanar and centroid distance + 10.0 otherwise, so it is not a
  metric — an index needs two searches plus exact reproduction of first-wins on equal floats.
- **FOLDPAIRS**: `folded_coplanar_pairs_dbg` (`ops_dissolve.rs:781`) calls the ALLOCATING
  `compute_face_normal` twice per undirected edge and `manifold_boolean` runs it 6–10× per boolean;
  ~10 ms/boolean recoverable by the mechanical `_into` swap. Same for `mesh_signed_volume`
  (`mesh_boolean/mod.rs`), ~8 calls/boolean.
- **FREELIST-SWEEP**: 45 open-coded `free_*.contains()` sites remain (`ops_dissolve` 15, `ops_misc` 14,
  `validate` 5, `ops_loop_cut` 4, `ops_extrude` 4, `builders` 3), plus **23 hoisted `HashSet` /
  `free_mask` workarounds** that existed purely to dodge the old linear scan and are now SLOWER than
  the O(1) predicate they were avoiding. Mechanical cleanup.
- **REDUNDANT-NOW**: `ops_inset.rs::inset_recompute_normals_local`'s collar snapshot/restore and
