## 2026-08-09 (master) — OPPERF: boolean / extrude / inset perf sweep, 6 fixes — ✅ FIXED

Owner asked whether boolean, extrude and inset could be faster. Measured first (temporary probes
against the public API, `--profile fast-release`), then six fixes landed by six agents under strict
one-file-each ownership. **Every fix is pure perf: output identity was proven empirically per fix,
not argued.** Final integrated numbers, measured in ONE harness against the pre-sweep baseline:

| case | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extrude_region`, 64-face sel, 9216 f mesh | 19.94 ms | 0.95 ms | 21× |
| `extrude_region`, 1024-face sel, 4096 f mesh | 113.11 ms | 1.17 ms | 96× |
| `inset_region`, 64-face sel, 9216 f mesh | 103.85 ms | 50.41 ms | 2.1× |
| inset **Individual**, 64 faces, 4096 f mesh | 68.25 ms | 3.69 ms | 18.5× |
| boolean difference, 6144 f target | 411.85 ms | 226.87 ms | 1.8× |

- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-BOOL-PROV**: `collect_provenance` classified every result face against EVERY
  fan-triangle of both operands with a linear `.any()` — O(F_out × (T_a+T_b)), 176 ms of a 470 ms
  6144-face boolean — and `mesh_boolean` was `mesh_boolean_with_provenance(..).map(|(m,_)| m)`, so
  callers that DISCARD provenance paid in full (the live knife twice per cut). Both entry points now
  share one `boolean_impl(.., want_provenance)`; the surface test goes through a BVH candidate filter
  reusing `bvh::build_bvh` (provenance pass 176 → 8 ms). Duplicate private `point_tri_distance`
  collapsed into the public `classify::point_triangle_dist_sq`. Identity: 321 results across 4
  densities × 4 cutter sizes × 7 placements (incl. coplanar/flush contact) × 3 ops bit-matched the
  original linear classifier. `core_math/src/mesh_boolean/mod.rs`.
- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-BOOL-MATXFER**: boolean material transfer was O(F_out × (F_a+F_b))
  unconditionally (64 ms of that same boolean). Added a provably-equivalent single-material fast path
  (64.2 → 0.7 ms, ~92×) — deliberately NOT "assign and return", which diverges from the min-search on
  NaN/overflow coordinates where `best_score` never beats `f32::MAX`; it scans to the first winner so
  equivalence is unconditional. Per-face `Vec` allocs removed via `face_vertices_into` /
  `compute_face_normal_into`. Multi-material scoring path left bit-identical, gated by two new oracle
  tests using a frozen copy of the old search. `core_math/src/mesh_boolean_manifold.rs`.
- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-BOOL-MERGE**: `greedy_merge_region_impl` (Mesh Cleanup / `merge_coplanar`) was
  O(K² log K) — sort key recomputed INSIDE the comparator, and both adjacency maps rebuilt as
  BTreeMap/BTreeSet after every single merge. Now flat sorted vecs + one key computation per candidate
  + an exactly-invalidated key cache: K=4608 region 15.2 s → 1.48 s (~10×). Identity proven by a
  differential test against a verbatim copy of the old implementation over 240 randomised
  annulus/T-pin/tie-forcing soups in 3 preserve states. `core_math/src/mesh_boolean/rebuild.rs`.
- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-EXTRUDE-REGION**: `extrude_region` was O(region_verts × mesh_faces) with a heap
  alloc per inner step — cost scaled with the WHOLE mesh for a constant selection. Compounding it, the
  determinism fix had shadowed the `faces: &HashSet` parameter with `faces_sorted: Vec`, silently
  turning every `faces.contains()` into a linear scan. Now one pass over the mesh's faces + O(1)
  membership (sorted Vec still drives all iteration, so allocation order is byte-identical) +
  prebuilt half-edge lookup maps replacing three per-element full-HE rescans + local
  `recompute_normals_region`. A 64-face `extrude_region` is now 0.53 ms vs 0.58 ms for 64 individual
  `extrude_face` calls — the 14× inversion is gone. Also **fixed a nondeterminism**:
  `extrude_region_volume` iterated a `HashSet<FaceId>` to allocate cap faces, so its output id order
  differed every process run. `core_math/src/half_edge/ops_extrude.rs`.
- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-INSET-CREATEFACE**: `inset_region` cost scaled with the whole mesh on a constant
  selection because `create_face` (`euler.rs:374`) runs a FULL-MESH `recompute_normals()` per created
  face — ~100 of them for a 64-face inset. Converted to `create_face_no_normals` + one local pass.
  Individual mode 168 → 1.5 ms (113×). Note `recompute_normals_region` is NOT bit-identical to the
  full pass — three gaps found and closed in a local helper (created faces the `vertex_fan` walk
  cannot reach on a checkerboard selection keeping a `Vec3::Y` placeholder; the one-ring collar it
  rewrites with wrong weights; a seed vertex with no incident live face on a pinched region). Identity
  proven over 46 configurations plus cross-binary digests. `core_math/src/half_edge/ops_inset.rs`.
- ✅ FIXED — **PERF-EXTRUDE-DRAG**: `poly_extrude_build_topology`'s Individual branch deduped
  `vert_normals` with a linear scan of a Vec growing across every selected face — O(N²) in total new
  verts; now a `HashMap` built inline with identical last-write-wins values (and deterministic output
  order, where it was `HashMap::into_iter()` order before). Per-drag-frame churn cut in
  `poly_update_extrude_drag`: redundant `face_normals` clone dropped, per-cap-face `face_vertices`
  allocations replaced with a reused `face_vertices_into` buffer in the centroid walk,
  `poly_extrude_apply_delta` and `poly_extrude_flatten_caps`.
  `app/src/poly_drag_tools/extrude_drag.rs`.

**OPEN — found during the sweep, deliberately not fixed (each needs its own task):**

- ❗ **BOOLNONDET (P1): the boolean is nondeterministic run-to-run.** Same input, same process,
  5 repeats: the result's vertex ORDER differs every run, and on one case the vertex COUNT flips
  (106 v vs 107 v). Reproduced independently by the coordinator across two processes; input-dependent
  (CC levels 0/1/3 stable, level 2 not), which is why it hid. The `mesh_boolean/mod.rs:21-26`
  DETERMINISM banner documents this exact symptom as already-fixed — the BTreeMap conversion covered
  the coplanar-merge/region-trace passes, but the default kernel is now Manifold and its weld path is
  not covered. Consequences: a `.fl4` reload can differ from the session that saved it, position-keyed
  Smart Select tags can land differently, and level-2-class oracle tests pass partly by luck.
- ❗ **NORMREGION: `recompute_normals_region` weights faces outside its dirty set with a hardcoded
  `area = 1.0`** (`normals.rs:622`) — and the comment above it describes deriving area from normal-length
  history, an implementation that was never written. Found INDEPENDENTLY by two agents in different
  files. 11 call sites incl. both grab paths (`transform_drag.rs:383/418`), bevel, loop cut, extrude,
  inset — wherever the collar's normals genuinely change they are computed with fake weights. Bounded
  blast radius: the viewport is unaffected (`to_raster_data` builds per-corner normals from face
  geometry), but `to_mesh` → `export_node_obj` → `export_obj` writes `HVertex.normal` as OBJ `vn`
  lines, and new verts inherit it. Fix: use the real Newell area, which also deletes the need for
  inset's snapshot workaround.
- **DELFACE: `delete_face`'s `repoint_vert_disk_if_stale` (`euler.rs:161`) is now 99.5% of what
  remains in `inset_region`** (54.00 of 54.25 ms at 9216 f) — a full `0..half_edges.len()` scan with a
  nested `free_edges.contains()` per corner. The batch `delete_faces` is NOT a drop-in: it iterates a
  `HashSet`, making free-list and therefore id allocation order nondeterministic.
- **FLIPFACE: `flip_face` (`ops_misc.rs:1487`) ends with a full-mesh `recompute_normals()`** and
  `extrude_region_volume` calls it once per region face — 645 ms of the 865 ms remaining in the
  4096-face-selection extrude. Same defect class as `create_face`.
- **CREATEFACE: do NOT blanket-strip `recompute_normals()` from `create_face`** — every caller depends
  on it for correctness today, and each needs its own seed and its own answer to the three gaps found
  in PERF-INSET-CREATEFACE. Audit callers individually (bevel, dissolve, mirror/symmetrize, boolean
  rebuild).
- **HASHITER (class): three independent instances of `HashSet` iteration driving allocation/topology
  order found in one day** — the boolean, `extrude_region_volume` (fixed), and `delete_faces`. Worth a
  systematic sweep rather than three one-off fixes.
- **CLEANUPGATE**: `cleanup_mesh_with` still has no face-count gate (unlike the boolean's `<= 2048`).
  ~10× cheaper now but still quadratic in region size. Owner decision — a gate would silently refuse
  to clean big meshes.
- **BOOLDUPSAMPLE**: `mesh_boolean_manifold.rs:602` passes the same mesh as BOTH operands to
  `transfer_materials_from_operands`, collecting every sample twice for zero information. One-line
  dedup, provably output-identical.
- **INSETLEAK**: `inset_region` leaks a vertex on pinched selections (`map.insert` discards the first
  allocation when a boundary vertex ends two boundary edges). Preserved bit-for-bit by the perf fix;
  the clean fix is `entry().or_insert_with()`, which changes vertex counts so it needs its own task.
- **INSETMAT**: `inset_region` drops per-face materials (deletes the region's faces, recreates at
  `material_id: 0`) — the exact defect `create_face_no_normals_with_material` exists to prevent.
  Pre-existing, preserved.
- **BENCHFLAKY**: `bench_display_mesh_ops::prefix_cache_actually_reuses_the_unchanged_prefix` is an
  `assert!(warm < cold)` wall-clock assertion — passes alone, fails when the full suite runs its
  binaries in parallel. Flaky by construction.

Gates: `cargo check -p app --profile fast-release` clean; `cargo test -p core_math` 1023 passed /
3 failed — the same 3 that failed before the sweep (`directed_loop_crosses_pole_straight`,
`apply_in_place_refusal_leaves_mesh_untouched`, `clean_mesh_still_refuses_slit_creating_dissolve`),
none of them touched by it. NOTE: dev/release profiles cannot build in this environment —
`manifold-csg-sys` needs `cmake`, which is not installed; only `--profile fast-release` works.

## 2026-08-09 (master) — SMOOTHMASKFAIL: "Marked polygons" channel does nothing / masks the wrong faces — 🔴 OPEN (logged, NOT fixed — owner: "do not fix now just log it as a bug for later")

Owner report: *"i try this Marked polygons: did not work, i think remesh modifier if killing group"*.
Hypothesis is **CORRECT about the symptom, and the mechanism is worth stating precisely** — plus
there is a SECOND, independent cause that bites even with no Remesh in the stack. Verified by code
reading, not yet by a repro test (no test was written — this entry is the log, per the owner).

### A. Authored marks cannot cross a Remesh — 🔴 OPEN (design gap, known and flagged at ship)

**The group is NOT killed.** `cache.poly_custom_data` is keyed per node and describes the **base**
mesh, which the non-destructive stack never mutates — the polygroup is still there, still assigned,
still visible in the group overlay. What fails is the *lookup bridge*.

`poly_authored_channels(nid, base)` keys the table by quantized FACE CENTROID off the **base** mesh
(`AuthoredChannels::face_key`, 1e-5). The Smooth arm then looks that table up against `result` —
the mesh **as it stands at that stack slot**. With Remesh above it, `result` came out of
`surface_nets_placed` + QEF placement on a voxel lattice (`poly/remesh.rs:93`): every vertex is
newly generated, and Project-to-surface snaps onto the source **surface**, never onto original
vertex positions. New quads' centroids bear no relation to the old faces'. So every lookup misses,
`group_of_face` returns 0, the mask is all-zero, and `smooth_laplacian_masked` is a strict no-op —
the modifier appears dead.

Same failure applies to the **Edge weight** channel and to `op_created` Smart Select tags across a
Remesh; the class is "position keying cannot bridge an op that regenerates every position".

**Fix direction (already the standing next step):** transfer the channel through the remesh by
closest-point onto the PRE-remesh surface — `io_bridge::mesh_to_sdf::project_points_to_mesh` is
already in the tree and already used by Project-to-surface. Sample the base mesh's authored value at
each remeshed element's closest point instead of requiring an exact position match. This is the same
primitive a painted weight map needs, so build it once.

### B. `group_id` defaults to 0 = "ungrouped", so a fresh Polygroup channel masks the COMPLEMENT — 🔴 OPEN (regression introduced by SMOOTHAUTH, same day)

Independent of Remesh, and arguably the worse of the two because it produces a confidently WRONG
result rather than a visibly dead one.

`GeometryChannel::group_id` defaults to `0`, and `AuthoredChannels::group_of_face` returns
`unwrap_or(0)` for any face with no authored group. The Polygroup arm tests
`group_of_face(..) == self.group_id`, so at the default `0 == 0` matches **every UNGROUPED face** —
the exact complement of what the user marked. Selecting "Polygroup" from the kind dropdown sets only
`ch.kind`; `group_id` stays 0 until the user opens the group combo and clicks an entry, which
nothing prompts them to do (the combo's own label reads a bare "Group 0").

**Why the gate missed it:** `polygroup_channel_masks_the_smooth_modifier` sets `group_id: 1`
explicitly, so it exercises the working path and never the default one. A test that constructs a
channel the way the UI constructs it would have caught this.

**Fix direction:** on switching the kind to `Polygroup`, default `group_id` to the body's first
authored group (and show "no group selected" when there is none) — and/or give "ungrouped" its own
explicit sentinel so `0` cannot silently mean "match everything unmarked". Add a default-state test
alongside the existing one.

## 2026-08-09 (master) — SMOOTHAUTH: masked Smooth could not use AUTHORED marks (weighted edges / marked polygons) — ✅ ADDED

- ✅ ADDED 2026-08-09 — owner: *"the smooth option still need work i need to be able to use weighted
  edges, or mark specific polygone"*. SMOOTHMASK (below) shipped only PROCEDURAL channels — rules
  derived from the geometry in front of them. Neither of the two things the owner actually marks by
  hand could drive the mask. Two gaps, and they were not the same gap:
  - **Polygroups** were fully authorable already (`poly_assign_selection_to_new_group`, Group work
    mode, colour viz) — nothing read them as a modifier filter.
  - **Edge weights** were NOT authorable at all. `CustomData.crease` has persisted (`PolyLayerRecord`)
    and survived rebuilds (`remap_by_position`) since the sidecar landed, and dissolve / Mesh Cleanup
    already treat a weighted edge as protected — but **nothing in the app ever WROTE one**, so the
    column could only ever arrive from a file. Grep for a writer found tests and load, nothing else.
  Delivered:
  - **`AuthoredChannels`** (`core_math/src/geometry_channel.rs`) — polygroup-by-face-centroid and
    weight-by-undirected-edge tables, re-keyed by QUANTIZED POSITION at the same `PRESERVE_Q` = 1e5
    tolerance `remap_by_position` uses. Id keying would have been a silent wrong-geometry bug: every
    id dies in the stack (subdivide/bevel/boolean/remesh renumber, most rebuild from scratch), so
    `groups[FaceId]` on an intermediate mesh reads whatever face landed at that index.
  - **`GeoChannelKind::Polygroup` + `EdgeWeight`** (append-only, indices 8/9). `EdgeWeight` is
    **CONTINUOUS**: the authored 0..1 value becomes the mask strength directly, so a 0.5 edge is
    half-smoothed. Feather still applies but descends FROM the authored value (`seed` array), so
    dilation can only ever soften a painted weight, never amplify it — and the Falloff slider hides
    itself for a continuous channel, because the user already painted the ramp.
  - **FAIL-CLOSED**: an authored channel with no tables threaded in matches NOTHING, never
    everything. The opposite default would silently smooth a whole body the moment a group was
    deleted. Gated by `authored_channels_match_nothing_without_the_tables` and by the control half
    of the end-to-end test.
  - **`poly_set_edge_weight`** (`poly_groups.rs`) + a "Set Edge Weight" preset submenu — the missing
    authoring half. `EdgeKey` is canonical-undirected, so weighting either half-edge weights the
    pair once. `w <= 0` clears rather than storing 0.0 (a weightless-but-authored edge is a
    different thing from an unweighted one).
  - **Plumbing**: `poly_authored_channels` builds the tables off the BASE mesh; threaded through
    `apply_poly_modifiers_tagged` → `apply_one_poly_modifier` beside the existing `op_created` tags.
    `poly_stack_needs_tagged_eval` now also fires for authored channels — a reused prefix would hand
    the modifier an empty table (same rule, same reason as Smart Select). Select-by-Channel got the
    `_auth` variants too, or the two new kinds would silently select nothing.
  - **Display-cache key**: authored group/weight data folded into `stack_key` when a modifier reads
    it, and both authoring paths now call `poly_request_display_sync`. Without this, marking a group
    changes neither the mesh signature nor any modifier parameter — the exact stale-display trap the
    Smart Select tags hit on 2026-08-05.
  - **Persistence**: `group_id` / `weight_min` / `weight_max` are `#[serde(skip)]` on
    `GeometryChannel` and ride the `FL4PSMTH` record. `GeometryChannel` is serialized INSIDE
    `PolyModifier` in the blob, so a plain field there shifts every following byte and corrupts any
    `.fl4` that already stored a channel. The edge weights themselves need nothing new — `crease`
    already rides the in-blob `poly_layers`.
  Gates: `geometry_channel` 14/14 (4 new), `polygroup_channel_masks_the_smooth_modifier` (end-to-end
  through the real stack: marked faces move, every other vertex is asserted bit-identical, and the
  no-authored-data control is a strict no-op), `poly_smooth_falloff_round_trip` extended with the
  channel params, `poly_smooth_parity` 6/6, `serde_golden` 3/3, `cargo build -p app` clean.
  **Still open (unchanged from below):** post-Remesh, authored marks do not survive — every position
  moved, so position keying finds no match. Channel TRANSFER through the remesh via closest-point on
  the pre-remesh surface is still the missing piece, and it is now also what a painted weight map
  would need.

## 2026-08-09 (master) — SMOOTHMASK: Smooth (Laplacian) modifier had no way to control WHERE it smooths — ✅ ADDED

- ✅ ADDED 2026-08-09 — owner: *"the smooth modifier i need way to control where the smooth appear …
  can we still use underlying geo as selection to remove effect, we could use channel info, or angle
  base"*. The modifier exposed only Iterations + Factor and relaxed **every** vertex uniformly
  (`smooth_laplacian`), so a post-Remesh cleanup pass melted the features it was meant to keep.
  `PolyModifier.geo_channel` (the Modo-style filter: tris/quads/n-gons/side-count/material/edge-length/
  **edge dihedral angle** + invert) already existed, was already serialized, and was already in the
  display-cache stack hash — but **only Bevel and Inset read it**; Smooth's apply arm was a bare
  kernel call. Wired it through:
  - **`GeometryChannel::vertex_weights(mesh, feather_rings)`** (`core_math/src/geometry_channel.rs`) —
    turns a FACE/EDGE channel into a per-vertex `0..=1` strength mask. Edge channels seed from the
    matched edges' endpoints, face channels from the matched faces' corners, then a BFS dilation over
    the **same face-ring adjacency the Laplacian itself averages over** ramps the weight down across
    `feather_rings`. The feather is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a binary mask leaves a visible ridge
    exactly on the channel boundary (one row fully relaxed, its neighbour fully pinned). Returns
    `None` for the `All` channel so unfiltered stacks take the untouched fast path.
  - **`HalfEdgeMesh::smooth_laplacian_masked(iters, factor, Option<&[f32]>)`** (`half_edge/ops_misc.rs`)
    — `smooth_jacobi_pass` scales `f` per vertex. A pinned vertex still CONTRIBUTES to its neighbours'
    averages (it is masked out of the write, not out of the stencil), which is what keeps the masked
    boundary continuous instead of cracking. `mask = None` is the literal pre-existing arithmetic
    (`f`, not `f * 1.0`) — `poly_smooth_parity.rs`'s exact-`f32` gate stays green.
  - **`smooth_falloff: u32`** on `PolyModifier`, `#[serde(skip)]` + the **NEW `FL4PSMTH` tail section**
    (append-newest-last, after `FL4PMODF`), reattached by (node_id, modifier index). NOT a field added
    to the existing `PolyModFlagRecord` even though that record exists for exactly this class of state:
    `load_binary` propagates a section decode error with `?`, so widening that record would not degrade
    to "lose that section" — it would fail the ENTIRE load for any `.fl4` already carrying an
    `FL4PMODF` from an older build. Records emit only when the modifier has BOTH a channel and a
    non-default falloff → files stay byte-identical when unused (pinned by the test).
  - **UI** (`properties_poly.rs`): channel picker + Falloff slider (shown only when a channel is set),
    plus a Factor hover note — on a quad mesh (anything out of Remesh) the vertex adjacency is
    bipartite, so the checkerboard mode is damped by `|1 − 2·factor|`: at 0.5 it dies in one pass, at
    **1.0 it never decays at all** and extra iterations only shrink volume. `smooth_falloff` added to
    `hash_modifier_stack_into` (an unhashed field is a field the user cannot edit — the Pipe trap).
  Gates: `geometry_channel` 9/9, `smooth_laplacian` 3/3 (incl. a new masked test: all-ones ==
  unmasked bit-for-bit, all-zero == strict no-op, weight-0 pins while neighbours are pulled toward it),
  `poly_smooth_parity` 6/6, `serde_golden` 3/3, `poly_smooth_falloff_round_trip` green,
  `cargo build -p app` clean.
  **KNOWN GAP (by design, documented for the next step):** right after a Voxel Remesh, most channels
  are inert — the output is uniform quads (tris/quads/n-gons/side-count match all-or-nothing), material
  ids do not survive, and polygroups / `op_created` tags cannot be carried by `remap_by_position`
  because every position moved. EdgeAngle *does* survive but is misleading there: lattice terracing has
  the same dihedral signature as a real corner, so an angle mask protects the stair-steps the user is
  trying to remove. The fix is channel TRANSFER through the remesh via closest-point on the pre-remesh
  surface (`project_points_to_mesh` already exists and is already used by Project-to-surface) — that
  one piece is what makes every other channel, and a painted weight map, usable post-Remesh.

## 2026-08-08 (master) — REMESHLIVE: poly Voxel Remesh modifier froze the UI seconds per slider tick — ✅ FIXED (~135× live-edit)

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-08 — owner: *"how can we make the remesh modifier more clean, and faster live edit"*.
  Measured baseline (release, this machine): ONE resolution-slider tick at res 128 on a 5k-tri body
  = **~10.4s** on the main thread. Four independent causes, each fixed at its layer:
  1. **Mesh→SDF sampled an exact Euclidean distance at every lattice cell** (`region_mesh_to_sdf`,
     O(res³ × tris) — 5.1s at 128³/5k tris) even though `write_region_from_sdf` saturates
     everything beyond |d| ≥ w/2 — ~85–98% of the work computed then clamped away. NEW
     **`region_mesh_to_sdf_band`** (`io_bridge/src/mesh_to_sdf.rs`): triangles scatter exact
     signed distance into their band-dilated AABB cells (parallel per z-plane, same
     `closest_on_tri` + first-wins tie-break as the brute path → bit-identical in band); far
     field classified by span-based 6-conn flood from the region border (contract: border in
     air — remesh's padding guarantees it). 5.1s → **35ms**; 256³/20k → 75s → **242ms**.
     Golden gate `io_bridge/tests/band_sdf_golden.rs`: bit-identical densities vs the full
     sampler (cube/brute + sphere/hash + sub-region), enclosed-pocket semantics pinned.
     Post-review hardening: air-walk flood (walks in-band positive cells; unreached air
     flips solid) so sealed voids fill with NO phantom inner crossing and narrow throats
     stay open; border-in-solid fails closed (None); remesh enforces a structural ≥2-cell
     air margin independent of the padding slider; AABB pre-cull + deferred sqrt (final:
     5k/128³ = 17.9ms, 20k/256³ = 130ms). DELIBERATE divergence: sealed interior voids now
     FILL instead of remeshing a phantom inner shell, and open meshes remesh as a thin
     crust instead of a solidified half-space — the Blender/3D-Coat voxel-remesh semantics
     (documented in remesh.rs + the sampler contract; flagged for owner sign-off).
  2. **The Modifiers panel ran the whole stack a SECOND time per edit** for its before→after
     vert/face card stats (`properties_poly.rs` "Gate 2") — a full voxel remesh per slider tick,
     memoized single-slot only. Now reads per-slot counts off the **prefix ladder** the display
     sync already built (`poly_prefix_slot_stats`, `mesh_sync.rs`); cold ladders are built via
     the SAME `apply_poly_modifiers_cached` the display path uses; only tagged
     Smart-Bevel/Cleanup stacks (which never get a ladder) still walk manually
     (`poly_mod_stats_uncached`). Tagged-stack detection extracted to ONE predicate
     (`poly_stack_needs_tagged_eval`) shared with `apply_poly_modifiers_cached`.
  3. **`VoxelGrid::surface_nets` was serial** (37.6ms at 128³) while the sculpt path's chunk
     mesher was parallel. Internals rewritten as rayon z-slab passes (vertices + quads),
     **bit-identical output** — serial body retained `#[cfg(test)]` as the oracle, gated by
     `surface_nets_parallel_matches_serial_reference` (sphere+blob+LCG-speckle grids, both
     smooth modes). 42.4ms → **9.5ms** smooth.
  4. **`from_quads`/`from_triangles` twin-linking** used SipHash on tuple keys + a heap-alloc'd
     Vec per face: packed-u64 keys + splitmix64 hasher + capacity reservations + stack arrays
     (`half_edge/builders.rs`, construction internals ONLY — serialized shape untouched).
- Net: ~10.4s/tick → **~70ms/tick at 128** through the PRODUCTION dispatch
  (`bench_remesh_slider_scrub`, app path: 32→4.3ms, 64→15ms, 96→37ms, 128→70ms, 192→190ms,
  256→389ms).
- **RESOLUTION UNLOCKED 128 → 256** (owner: "128 too low"): `REMESH_RES_MAX = 256`, UI slider
  derives from the constants. Two supporting changes: (a) `VoxelGrid::new_empty_dense` — the
  transient remesh grid stays DENSE above `SPARSE_RES_THRESHOLD` (brick-indirected reads made
  the 256³ extract ~1.5× slower for zero benefit on a grid freed at end of eval; 585→389ms);
  (b) top-range scrub deferral (`REMESH_LIVE_SCRUB_MAX = 128`): dragging the Resolution
  slider above 128 shows the value live but commits + re-evaluates on RELEASE (a per-notch
  eval at 256 is ~400ms = frozen drag); ≤128 stays fully live per notch. Never a draft mesh —
  display always shows committed geometry. ⚠ NEEDS A HANDS-ON DRAG TEST (headless can't
  drag a slider): drag above 128 → value tracks pointer, mesh updates on release.
- **V1 INCREMENTAL REMESH SHIPPED** (owner 2026-08-08: "only remesh what changing" → "v1"):
  a live edit under an active Remesh now resamples only the DIRTY REGION instead of the
  whole lattice. Measured drag frame (16×16 plane fixture, `bench_remesh_incremental_drag`):
  128³ 38.1→**21.8ms**, 256³ 223.6→**120.7ms** — ~1.8×. (An earlier 4.4× figure was measured
  BEFORE the enclosure-reconcile fix below and was not correct; the mandatory whole-field
  seal is most of the remaining incremental cost. Cutting it further needs V2's incremental
  extract, not more sampler work.)
  Pieces: (a) `region_mesh_to_sdf_band_seeded` (io_bridge) — dirty-region band sampler whose
  sign flood seeds from the PREVIOUS grid's border signs via a `prev_air` closure (a dirty
  region's border legitimately cuts the solid; the full sampler's border-is-air contract
  cannot apply), golden-gated BIT-FOR-BIT vs a full resample
  (`seeded_region_splice_matches_full_resample`); band internals factored into shared
  helpers (`band_scatter`/`flood_air_reach`/`band_finalize`) — one implementation, two
  seeding policies. (b) `RemeshIncrCache` + `voxel_remesh_mesh_incremental` (remesh.rs):
  single-slot per-(body,slot) retained grid; input diff (positions vs snapshot) → dirty
  AABB from faces touching moved verts (old+new extents) → seeded resample →
  `write_region_from_sdf` → full extract. Wired ONLY in the display walk
  (`apply_poly_modifiers_cached`); stateless callers unchanged. (c) Lattice latch is
  EPISODE-SCOPED (InteractionRenderPolicy pattern): mid-episode cache fills give the
  lattice 1.25× headroom (the canonical structural fit leaves exactly 2 cells — zero room
  to drag) and mark `diverged`; `commit_episode` drops the cache and, when diverged, fires
  ONE `poly_force_display_resync` so committed/saved geometry never keeps a latched
  lattice; `cancel_episode` just drops. AABB-preserving nudges reuse the lattice everywhere
  and are BIT-IDENTICAL to stateless (gate `incremental_interior_nudge_is_bit_identical`);
  topology/param changes fall back statelessly (gates), dirty >50% of lattice bails to full.
- **Three defects found by the post-implementation multi-agent review, all fixed before
  landing** (the review paid for itself twice in two rounds):
  1. **ENCLOSURE IS GLOBAL, a local splice cannot see it** (high severity). Far-field sign
     comes from air-connectivity flooded from the lattice border, so an edit that SEALS a
     cavity leaves every far cell OUTSIDE the dirty region at its stale air sign → phantom
     inner shell — and because such an edit can be AABB-preserving it read as `exact`,
     `diverged == false`, and was never reconciled. Fix is two-sided and fail-closed: every
     incremental splice now runs `VoxelGrid::seal_enclosed_air` (whole-field span flood,
     grid-space twin of `band_finalize`) so seal-direction changes match stateless exactly;
     and because void filling is ONE-WAY, any field that ever contained a filled void is
     marked `had_enclosed_void` and permanently refuses the incremental path (a re-opened
     void can never be restored locally). Sampler stats plumbed via
     `region_mesh_to_sdf_band_stats`. Gate: `incremental_refuses_fields_with_sealed_voids`.
  2. **Single-slot cache dropped other bodies' divergence.** `episode_active` is global, so
     any second body evaluating mid-episode overwrote `poly_remesh_incr` and discarded the
     first body's `diverged` flag — that body kept a 25%-coarser latched lattice
     indefinitely (display early-outs never re-evaluate a matching key). Fix: divergence is
     recorded per body in `poly_remesh_diverged`, drained + resynced by BOTH
     `commit_episode` and `cancel_episode` (`poly_remesh_reconcile_diverged`).
  3. **My own border guard was too strict and refused valid meshes.** The fail-closed
     "in-band negative border cell ⇒ None" check fired on a plain cube: at an exact
     geometric tie (lattice point exactly `band` from a box corner) the pseudo-normal sign
     can pick either adjacent face, producing an isolated −band border cell. Replaced with a
     guard that cannot misfire — refuse only when the border has NO air at all (the flood
     would have no seed). Partial border crossings are already safe by construction:
     interior cells are not walkable so they cannot seed, meaning signs are never inverted;
     the only degradation is border-cut openings reading as sealed, which is exactly what
     the structural air margin exists to prevent. **Lesson worth keeping: a fail-closed
     guard written from a contract, not from measurement, can be stricter than reality —
     this one refused every cube until the fixture caught it.**
- **TIER-1 PERF PASS (same session, after the V1 review)** — measured, each gated:
  * **Tier 2.5 KILLED BY MEASUREMENT.** The idea "when a drag frame changes no topology,
    skip extraction and just reproject vertices" was quantified before being built
    (`measure_drag_topology_churn`): **0 of 12 frames** are topology-stable at any realistic
    drag speed (3–4/12 only at an unrealistic 0.1 voxel/frame). Do not build it. The SAME
    run makes V2 look far better than estimated: dirty 16³ chunks are **0.02–0.6%** of the
    grid (6–8 of 4096 at 256³), i.e. the drag frame does 100% of the extract work for ~0.2%
    of the actual change.
  * `write_region_from_sdf_ex(want_delta=false)` + Dense parallel z-plane write: the full
    write built one `(u32,f32)` undo entry per voxel (~134 MB at 256³) that the remesh path
    discards. **45.4 → 3.1 ms** at 256³ (15×). Sculpt callers keep the delta.
  * `surface_nets` skips whole unmasked 16³ blocks in BOTH passes via `surface_chunk_mask`
    (chunk-stepped, so the O(res³) walk is actually removed, not just tested per cell), and
    `relax_mesh`'s wide-stencil normal pass is now a rayon per-vertex map. **55.1 → 31.9 ms**.
    Still bit-identical (`surface_nets_parallel_matches_serial_reference`).
  * `to_raster_data` reserves both outputs from the live face count and reuses the per-face
    ring/point buffers (`face_vertices_into`) — it was running ~450k allocations on a 150k-quad
    extract. **42.1 → 24.5 ms**. Pure allocation removal; identical output.
  * Net 256³ full eval **220.6 → 138.7 ms**; app-path slider notch **388.7 → 231.5 ms**;
    incremental drag frame **120.7 → 85.3 ms** (128³: 21.8 → 14.4 ms).
- **NEXT TARGETS, quantified** (do not re-derive): `seal_enclosed_air` **46 ms** at 256³ — the
  designed fix is a coarse (8³-block) pre-flood that bulk-clears fully-air blocks and seeds
  the fine flood only at block-boundary frontiers; `from_mesh` **33 ms**; `surface_nets`
  **32 ms** still ~2× off `object_display_mesh_chunked`'s 14.5 ms, and the gap is the
  `cell_vert` scratch array (res³ × u32 = **66 MB** memset per call) — needs a per-live-chunk
  sparse allocation. Then V2.
- ⚠ ENVIRONMENT (not a code defect): `cargo build -p app` in the DEBUG profile now fails with
  `manifold-csg-sys: failed to run cmake configure: program not found` — **cmake is not on
  PATH** in this shell (`where cmake` → not found; absent from Program Files and the VS2022

- NOT touched (flagged for follow-up): `recompute_normals` (now the largest rebuild cost),

## 2026-08-08 (master) — KNIFEUNBEVELWIND: Unbevel refused every knife-rect corner round — a winding heuristic vetoed a correct collapse — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-08 — owner: *"i still cant unbevel the bevel from rect knife cut, we could add
  an edge case or function in unbevel — just rail vertex to one shared point, do that for each
  ring edge in the bevel, now you have perfect 90 degrees, and since you refind the starting edge
  you can reapply bevel to change segment and roundness."*
- **The requested algorithm already existed.** `core_math/src/unbevel.rs` reverse math does
  exactly that (rails, profile arcs, `solve_sharp_point`). It was being vetoed one line before
  the finish, so no new code path was needed.
- Root cause (`unbevel.rs`): the rebuild ended with "flip any face whose normal points away from
  the mesh centroid" before `from_polygons`. That is valid only on a STAR-SHAPED solid. A knife
  rect cut is the canonical counter-example — the body centroid lands **inside the hole**, so
  every wall of the hole points back at it and the whole hole was reversed. `is_manifold()` then
  reported *"directed edge 35->36 used by 2 faces (same winding)"* and the gate turned that into
  a flat "Unbevel: reverse math refused" — on a collapse whose counts were already **exactly
  right** (48v/28f → 40v/24f: ten arc verts merged to two, four arc quads gone).
  **Fix: deleted the heuristic. Winding is INHERITED, never re-derived** — every ring is copied
  off the input mesh by `face_vertices` and already carries its consistent orientation; merging
  vertices cannot reverse a loop. Same family as BEVEL.md §11 2026-07-18 (centroid inward
  sign-fix is wrong on concave faces).
- Second defect, the app path (`unbevel_from_edges`, which is what Ctrl+Alt+B uses with an edge
  selection): seeding "every face touching a selected edge" drags in the strip's flanking walls
  (each shares a rail), so the component grew sideways and refused. Added a second seed tried on
  refusal — **`crossed`**: only faces the selection SPANS (≥2 selected edges non-adjacent in the
  face ring). Touching a face is not being part of it.
- ⚠ KNOWN LIMIT (documented, not hidden): selecting the arc's RIM CHORDS still refuses — they
  bound the flat face as much as the strip, so they do not identify a strip. Select the strip
  faces, or its cross edges.
- Method worth reusing: build the owner's shape headlessly through the REAL app path
  (`poly_knife_shape_release`), then mechanically tag every `return None` in the kernel with its
  line number. One run named the exact bail; printing the manifold error string named the defect.
- Gates: `knife_rect_corner_round_unbevels_to_a_sharp_90_degree_corner` (full round-trip: cut →
  rounded with no vertex at the sharp point → unbevel → −8v/−4f, corner recovered at the true
  (0.5,0.5), recovered edge measured **90.0°** → re-bevel at 7 segments takes), and
  `unbevel_works_from_the_corner_strips_own_edge_selection`. core_math 1013 pass; app 652 pass
  (4 pre-existing unrelated failures, verified identical without the change).

## 2026-08-08 (master) — KNIFEOPENSUB: knife subtract refused on open meshes (a plane could not be cut) — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-08 — owner: *"can we make the boolean work on an open mesh, it would be useful also
  when you use the knife tool on a simple plane."* Subtract toasted "Knife subtract needs a closed
  mesh — this one has open edges (use Slice)" and did nothing.
- **The honest framing:** a SOLID boolean on a surface is not a missing feature, it is undefined —
  Manifold needs a watertight operand and a surface has no interior, so Difference has no answer.
  The operation the user wants is well defined though: scribe the outline, drop the enclosed faces.
  The scribe is pure surface topology and **already worked on open meshes** (probe: 2×2 quad +
  closed rect → v=9/f=3, the enclosed rect already its own face) — only the solid path refused.
- Fix (`app/src/poly_knife.rs`): `poly_knife_free_boolean` checks `boundary_half_edge_count > 0` and
  routes to `poly_knife_free_slice_commit` with the new `SliceEnclosed::Remove(rings)` — handing it
  the very polygons the prism would have been extruded from, so open and closed meshes cut the
  identical silhouette (projected along the drawing-plane normal, the prism's own axis). Closed
  bodies are untouched and keep the true solid boolean. Covers the closed-loop AND the open-line
  side-pick branch. Guard: a cookie-cut that would eat every face refuses (fails closed — the scribe
  still committed).
- ⚠ TRAP (cost one wrong implementation, logged in KNIFE.md §7): **centroid is not an interior test.**
  The scribe leaves the surviving OUTER region as concave n-gons whose centroids land INSIDE the loop
  — on a plane all three read as enclosed and the whole surface would have been deleted. The rule is
  every VERTEX inside-or-on the ring, and "on" must count as in (after a scribe every enclosed-region
  vertex lies exactly on the ring, where a crossing-number test coin-flips).
- Gates: `closed_loop_subtract_punches_a_hole_in_an_open_plane` (area 4.0 → 3.0, outer extent
  untouched, boundary 4 → 8 = rim + hole), `open_mesh_subtract_never_consumes_the_whole_surface`,
  `closed_body_still_takes_the_solid_boolean_path`. 39 knife + 14 slice green; app 650/654 (4
  pre-existing unrelated failures).

## 2026-08-08 (master) — KNIFERECTROUND: rectangular knife stopped beveling corners (regression from the Unbevel "fix") — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-08 — **"the rectangular knife no longer bevels corners — this is not a
  proper fix"**, plus the owner's own bisect: *"the bevel point cut works on the right click,
  on the release of drag should be same thing."* An earlier same-day change tried to make
  Ctrl+Alt+B (Unbevel) reverse a knife-rect corner round by changing what the CUT PRODUCES:
  `poly_knife_shape_release` / `poly_knife_slice_through_now` overwrote `knife_points` with the
  sharp 4-corner ring, cut that, then ran `bevel_op::bevel_vertices_offset` on the matched
  corner verts and pushed a `PolyBevelHistory`. RMB/Enter (`poly_knife_free_confirm`) was left
  cutting the arc ring — **two paths for one operation**, and the release path's round was
  either invisible or absent.
- Root cause (full autopsy in `docs/planning/poly/BEVEL.md` §6): a knife corner round is a
  property of the cut POLYLINE, not a 3D bevel strip. On the SLICE path the four corner verts
  are coplanar, so the vertex bevel inserts a coplanar (invisible) facet; on the SUBTRACT path
  it chamfers only the rim it matched while the hole stays square through its depth. Corner
  matching was nearest-vert within `radius * 4.0` measured in DRAWING-PLANE space against verts
  that live on the mesh surface — when the press misses a face the plane sits at the body's
  bounds centre and nothing matches. All five failure branches `return`ed silently with **no
  toast**, so the tool simply looked like it had lost the feature.
- Fix (`app/src/poly_knife.rs`): release and S cut `knife_points` untouched — the same rounded
  ring RMB/Enter cuts. Deleted `poly_knife_bake_rect_corner_bevels`,
  `knife_rect_pending_corner_bevel`, `knife_closed_rings_from_corners` (185 lines).
- Gate: `rect_release_cuts_the_same_rounded_corners_as_rmb_confirm` — release and RMB must land
  the same `content_signature`, and the round must add geometry over a sharp cut. **Verified RED
  on the pre-fix tree** (release v=184/f=138 vs RMB v=64/f=36), green after. 36/36 knife tests.
- ⚠️ ALSO FOUND — **the `app` test binary did not COMPILE at HEAD.** The deleted
  `rect_corner_bevel_bake_is_unbevelable` formatted `app_types::ActiveTool` with `{:?}` and
  `ActiveTool` has no `Debug`, so `cargo test -p app` had been failing to build; that change was
  never test-run. Now 645/650, with 5 pre-existing unrelated failures
  (`dc_gate0_committed_ref_fl4_loads_unchanged`, `diag_modifier_audit`,
  `test_020_intrude_boundary_and_ctrl_x`, `test_021_along_normals_inward_keeps_planar_walls`,
  `intrude_owner_fixtures_pinned` — confirmed identical on the pre-fix tree).
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-08 (same day) — **Unbevel (Ctrl+Alt+B) on a knife-rect corner round.** Neither
  of the two options above was needed — see KNIFEUNBEVELWIND below.

## 2026-08-08 (master) — BOOLEAN LOCALITY: post-boolean polish wiped untouched topology (386v grid cube → 10v; scribed slices deleted) — ✅ FIXED

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-08 — **BOOL-LOCALITY: `post_boolean_polish` was preserve-blind — its
  `limited_dissolve(12°, None, None)` (rebuild.rs, the one admitted inconsistency) selected
  every zero-dihedral edge ANYWHERE on the mesh; the region merge + valence sweep then ate
  entire untouched lattices and knife-scribed coplanar edges.** Owner: "the knife subtract
  must not delete an applied slice" / "this needs to be localised". BEVEL.md §11 2026-08-08c
  numbers reproduced exactly (grid_cube(8) − partial-edge 45° wedge: 386v → 10-14v). The
  box-vs-wedge asymmetry that hid it: a mid-face notch makes the coplanar region an annulus
  → region merge refuses → batch aborts → lattice survives BY ACCIDENT (which is why the
  2026-08-08 KNIFECLEAN-GLOBAL entry's box-notch repro declared the boolean "NOT guilty" —
  its cutter shape missed the defect; the wedge class proves it). Upstream Manifold kernel
  verified INNOCENT (raw output keeps the lattice, v=363/f=354).
- Fix (core_math/src/mesh_boolean/rebuild.rs, mesh_boolean_manifold.rs — kernel-only):
  (1) polish step A passes a protect set resolved from the thread-local PRESERVE_EDGES
  (flat at-risk edges only); (2) `dissolve_coplanar_edges_iter` + `dissolve_valence3_
  collinear_tjunc` gain preserve skips; (3) belt-and-suspenders acceptance gates — every
  polish step and the manifold-wrap accepts refuse any candidate that DELETED a preserved
  input vertex (`preserved_vert_count`), killing the class for future preserve-blind passes;
  (4) coarse-weld hardening: a cluster mixing a preserved and a cut vertex keeps the INPUT
  position (was first-seen-wins, silently de-protecting verts near the cut); (5) NEW seam
  exemption `SEAM_VERTS`: input verts lying ON the other operand's surface are contact

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **KNIFESLICE-ORDINAL: through-slice layers were keyed by raw depth
  ordinal (`hits[li]`), not by surface identity.** Any densify sample whose ray grazed a
  silhouette or clipped an extra surface had a different hit count, shifting every deeper hit
  up one slot for that sample only — layer 1 mixed back faces of one sample with mid faces of
  the next, the scribed polyline jumped between shells, and `knife_result_is_sound` correctly
  vetoed the corrupted result ("that path can't cut cleanly here"). Fix: layers are now keyed

  (`build_shell_layers`, `knife_face_shell_ids`, `knife_surface_hits_shelled` in
  `poly_knife.rs`); each layer carries a front flag so entry surfaces scribe along the view
  and exit surfaces against it. `deep_scribe` now checks the whole layer tail, not just
  layers[1].

  `collapse_collinear_pins` + `purge_degenerate_faces` after the cut, but the preview clone

  (largest false-fail class). `try_cut` now runs the same heal on the clone before
  `knife_result_is_sound`.
- Addendum (verified headless 2026-08-08): silhouette walls are now closed deterministically —
  a face whose ring gained exactly two non-adjacent cut verts is split via the ID-preserving

  (+4v/+4f exact), `s_through_slice_two_cubes_cuts_each_shell_independently` (+8v/+8f, shells

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Loop Cut RMB-confirm ALSO opened the context menu — ✅ FIXED

## 2026-08-07 (master) — SELECTION "fails often" (vert/edge pick misses + wrong element) — ✅ FIXED (class)

Owner: "my selection fails often — compare with the Blender oracle, just the tech under the
hood." Root-cause comparison against Blender's `view3d_select.cc` + select engine found the
structural divergence: our select buffer held ONLY face ids, so vert/edge visibility was
INFERRED ("does a nearby pixel show an incident face?") — silhouette false-culls (miss →
selection cleared) and behind-surface false-passes (wrong vert zoomed out); plus the buffer
was settle-gated + async, so for several frames after every orbit/edit a DIFFERENT algorithm
(single CPU ray + `distance*0.02` bias) answered — same click, different result.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **PICKELEMID: per-element ID select buffer (Blender's actual
  architecture).** Two passes in `poly_pick.wgsl`: (1) faces + id-0 occluder bodies, depth
  tested/written; (2) edges (lines) + verts (points) with NO depth attachment, discarding
  only when the fragment is behind the **3×3 window MAX** of the pass-1 face depth. Tagged
  ids throughout (`PICK_TAG_VERT/EDGE/FACE | idx+1`, `poly_select_gpu.rs`).
  **First attempt used hardware depth bias and was WRONG** (owner screenshot: ~half a
  sphere's vert markers missing) — slope-scaled bias derives from the primitive being
  drawn, and a POINT has zero slope, so verts carried only a ULP constant against the
  face's real per-pixel depth gradient and lost the race at random. The window max
  expresses the neighbor slope exactly: coplanar own-face ties pass, silhouettes pass
  (a neighbor is background 1.0), real occluders fail. No tunable constant, no backend
  dependence. Visibility everywhere is now the element's OWN id — exact,
  no inference. The 2026-08-06 edge tiers T1-T3 (incident-face probe / endpoint fans /
  cursor-ray rescue) are DELETED with their cause; the CPU ray+bias path survives only as
  the pending-buffer fallback. Consumers updated: `pick.rs` hover gates, `paint.rs`
  paint/region tests (face test accepts the face's rim edge/vert ids — boundary samples now
  land on rim pixels), `draw_poly.rs` overlay occlusion (6 sites), `poly_face_visible_at_screen`.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **PICKSYNC: click-time synchronous buffer refresh.** A pointer press
  in a poly edit sub-mode refreshes a stale buffer BLOCKING in `poll_background_tasks`
  (Frame Ordering respected; one blocking render per click, never per frame) — Blender
  renders its select buffer inside the pick operator for the same reason. The
  stale-window nondeterminism class is gone.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **SELEDGEMOTION: selected-edge highlight showed BACK edges while the
  camera moved.** Owner: "when I zoom out and all edges are selected, during the movement I see
  the back edges — highlight should stay consistent." Root cause: the egui highlight has no
  depth test of its own, so it borrowed the face-ID pick buffer, which by design only refreshes
  once the camera SETTLES; mid-orbit there is no buffer and the documented fallback is
  "no depth info => draw" (itself the fix for the opposite bug, highlights vanishing). A CPU
  overlay simply cannot answer an occlusion question only the depth buffer knows.
  **Fix:** selected + hovered edge highlights MOVED to the depth-tested GPU line batch
  (`overlay_lines.rs::append_poly_selected_edges`), the same pass that already draws the edit
  wire against the live G-buffer depth every frame — nothing to go stale, correct during motion.
  X-Ray keeps working because the batch itself routes to the always-on-top pass. The egui edge
  block is DELETED (not disabled) along with both of its guess-based fallbacks.
  KNOWN, unchanged: the VERTEX marker overlay is still egui and still uses a facing-based
  fallback while the pick buffer settles — same class, not yet moved (no GPU point overlay pass).
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-10 — **SELEDGEMOTION regression: edge highlight vanished / felt “back”.**
  Owner: "the edge highlight bug came back." Cause: `append_poly_selected_edges` was nested
  *inside* `append_poly_edit_wire`, which early-returns when `show_poly_overlays` is false
  (or master overlays off). Selection highlight then never entered the GPU batch — same class
  as “highlight does not render even if the edge gets selected.” Fingerprint early-exit also
  skipped rebuilds when only edge selection was live (no edit cage). **Fix:** emit edge
  selection via `append_poly_selected_edges_for_active` from `build_overlay_lines` independently
  of the edit-cage gate; fingerprint treats `edge_hilite` as a body-walk consumer. Depth-test
  / X-Ray routing unchanged (still SELEDGEMOTION GPU path).
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **PICKOCCLUDE: other visible poly bodies now occlude vert/edge picks**
  (drawn as id-0 depth occluders in the pick pass). KNOWN GAP (unchanged from before,
  documented): SDF / voxel bodies still do not occlude poly sub-element picks.


## 2026-08-07 (master) — SELECTION HIGHLIGHT vanishes on orbit — ✅ FIXED

Owner, reported twice: (1) "a selected EDGE on the top of a box shows no highlight while the
other three edges of the same face are highlighted"; (2) "selected FACES inside a cut notch
show their green from one angle and lose it from another." Owner directive: "check under the
hood Blender code to see how they do highlight."

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **SELHILITEFACING: poly selection highlight was culled by
  `dot(normal, view)`, not by depth.** Three independent facing tests, each dropping the WHOLE
  element the moment its normal tipped ~87° off the view direction — while it was still plainly
  on screen:
  - `overlay_faces.rs:111` — GPU face-fill emit (`n_world.dot(cam_fwd) > 0.05` → `continue`)
  - `draw_poly.rs:537` — egui selected-face fill + outline (same predicate via `faces_away`)
  - `draw_poly.rs:618-629` — selected EDGE, using the AVERAGE of the two adjacent face normals.
    This is the owner's case 1 by construction: a box top edge's neighbours are the top (+Y)
    and a side (+X), so the average is a 45° diagonal; from a 3/4 view exactly ONE of the four
    symmetric top edges has its diagonal past the camera and is silently dropped.
  Direct violation of the standing project rule **"facing is NOT occlusion"**
  (`feedback_facing_is_not_occlusion`). **Fix:** all three deleted. Occlusion is the depth test
  that already existed — `face_overlay.wgsl::scene_visible()` (G-buffer depth sample) for the
  fill, the face-ID pick buffer for edges/outlines. "Show backfaces" now folds into the X-RAY
  flag, which is the only honest way to reveal a surface facing away.
  **Blender parity:** `overlay_edit_mesh` never does a facing test — it rasterizes the overlay
  and calls `test_occlusion()` against the scene depth texture, plus an X-Ray toggle.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **SELHILITEBIAS: coplanar depth bias ran along the FACE NORMAL.**
  `overlay_faces.rs` emitted `lp + face_n * 2.5e-4`, which assumes the normal points at the
  camera. Boolean notch walls point INWARD and bevel/dissolve can flip winding, so for exactly
  the owner's case-2 faces the "bias" pushed the fill *into* the solid and `scene_visible()`
  discarded it. **Fix:** bias moved to `face_overlay.wgsl::vs_main` as a clip-space
  `NDC_OFFSET` (`clip.z -= NDC_OFFSET * clip.w`) — Blender's `ndc_offset`, no normal
  dependency, constant in window depth at any zoom. Also keeps the emitted vertex list
  camera-independent so `overlay_faces_fingerprint` still caches across orbit frames.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **SELHILITEPROBE: edge/outline occlusion probed a single midpoint and
  fell back to an on-rim CPU test.** Two structural faults, both measured:
  - The probe point was the segment MIDPOINT, which lies exactly on the shared rim of both
    adjacent faces — the documented boundary trap (`point_in_face_3d` reads on-rim points as
    OUTSIDE), so the CPU fallback answers "hidden" for edges obviously in front.
  - When the face-ID buffer was absent (it refreshes only after camera AND mesh settle, i.e.
    for a frame or two after every orbit step) the code fell back to that unreliable CPU test
    and hid the selection.
  **Fix:** probe at t=0.2/0.5/0.8 ALONG the segment (two samples land in face interiors, not
  on the rim) with the wider `any_near_r(.., 3, ..)` edge radius the pick buffer documents;
  and when there is NO depth information, DRAW. A highlight briefly drawing through the mesh
  is cosmetic; a highlight that disappears is the P0 ("Selection must ALWAYS work").

- ✅ NEW — **`AZRA_SELDIAG` harness (`app/src/seldiag.rs`).** Self-driving verification:
  creates a poly box, cuts a real recess (inset + negative depth), selects the notch floor +
  all four inward-facing walls, then the four top rim edges, and sweeps a full 8-step yaw orbit
  capturing a screenshot per pose. `AZRA_SELDIAG_XRAY=1` opens the X-ray escape,
  `AZRA_SELDIAG_TRACE=1` prints per-frame counts. Because the screenshot copies the GPU
  viewport TEXTURE, egui-painted overlays never appear in a shot — so the harness also counts
  `EDGES_PAINTED` at the exact `line_segment` call that strokes a selected edge.
  **Measured verdict (5 faces + 4 rim edges selected, Visible-Only ON, backfaces OFF):**
  | | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `overlay_face_verts` (5 faces = 30) | **12** at every angle | **30** at every angle |
  | `EDGES_PAINTED` (4 selected) | 2–3 depending on yaw | **4** at every yaw |
  Before-screenshots reproduce the owner's report exactly: ONE notch wall is green and WHICH
  ONE changes as the camera orbits (yaw 45 → right wall, yaw 225 → left wall), floor not green
  at all. After: floor + all four walls green at all 8 angles.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Multi-agent review: Material · Poly · PBR · Render

Source: 4 parallel explore agents (material / poly modeling / PBR shading / rendering
pipeline), 2026-08-07. **REVIEW ONLY — no fixes applied in that session.** Confirmed
code findings preferred. Cross-refs existing OPEN entries where already filed.

**Note:** Earlier Progressive-PBR backlog OPEN items in this file (CSM gate, probe
sub-rect/HZB, C1/C2 energy, lazy pbr_accum, idle ladder 8192) were largely addressed
by `PBR_REFINE_HARDENING_PLAN.md` Phases A–E (SHIPPED). Residual energy / gate issues
from the multi-agent pass are listed under **PBR** below.

### Must-fix (cross-domain)

- ⬜ OPEN — **GPUCULLOOB: D1 instance cull indexes `batch_meta[u32::MAX]` for special
  draw kinds (default cull ON).** `raster_gbuffer` marks SDF/voxel/CLUSTERED with
  `batch = u32::MAX` ("never drawn through cull") but still dispatches one thread per
  draw; `instance_cull.wgsl` `cs_frustum_cull` / late path has **no** `batch == MAX`
  skip → GPU OOB / corruption / device loss when any non-MESH draw is present.
  `dbg_gpu_cull` / `dbg_hzb` default **true** (`types_render.rs`).
  **Fix:** skip `cm.batch == 0xffffffffu` in cull shaders (or exclude specials from
  `n_instances`). Severity Critical. Confidence confirmed.

- ⬜ OPEN — **PTALBEDOPACK: path-trace albedo samples with `amap_pack & 1u`.**
  `pathtrace_tri_entry.wgsl` (~2636–2641, ~1947–1949) strips HP (bit 10), blend
  (5–9), rot (12–17), Sphere/Cyl/Planar (2–4). Hybrid uses full pack via
  `sample_mat_proj_hp` (`gbuffer.wgsl`). Rough/metal PT paths pass full pack;
  albedo alone is masked → Hybrid vs PT diverge on any non-trivial albedo map.
  Severity Critical. Confidence high.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **KNIFECIRCLESLIT / closed knife** — closed interior loop now
  routes to `split_poly_closed_loop` (disc + two annulus halves), not `split_poly_slit`.
  Single-face closed loops (incl. the multi-cell suite's single-cell case) now truly
  separate the enclosed region. See the *CIRCLE knife leaves a segment* section.

- ⬜ OPEN — **SSGIPROBEDBL: SSGI + light probe double ambient when no HDRI.**
  Deferred adds probe ambient with `env_width==0` (`deferred_entry.wgsl` ~1223–1228);

## 2026-08-07 (master) — BRIDGE does not work on a MULTI-SELECTION

Owner: "look at the bridge code — I feel it does not work on multi select and it needs to."

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **BRIDGEMULTI: bridge refused any selection that was not EXACTLY two
  loops / EXACTLY two faces, so a 3+ loop selection silently no-opped.** Three give-up points,
  all of them a literal `== 2`:
  * `core_math/src/half_edge/ops_misc.rs` `bridge_edge_selection` — `if rings.len() != 2 { return
    Vec::new(); }`. `edge_loop_rings` already returned N rings correctly; the wrapper threw N-2 away.
  * `app/src/poly/bridge.rs:70` — the app repeated the same `rings.len() != 2` refusal in its
    manifold preview, so even a fixed kernel would still have been unreachable from the tool.
  * `app/src/poly/bridge.rs:27` — the FACE path gated on `sel_faces.len() == 2`.
  **Fix:** new `bridge_ring_chain` orders N rings by proximity (`order_loop_chain`, Blender's
  `BM_mesh_edgeloops_calc_order`) and bridges consecutive pairs → **N-1 bridges in one
  invocation**. `bridge_edge_selection` and the new `bridge_faces_multi` both route through it;
  `bridge_faces` is now a two-face wrapper over `bridge_faces_multi` (ONE implementation).
  `bridge_ring_pair` is the single place that chooses equal-strip vs unequal-fan.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **BRIDGEFAN: `bridge_unequal_loops` emitted OVERLAPPING faces on any span
  covering more than one long-ring edge.** It built a quad SPANNING the whole arc
  (`[s0,s1,l_to,l_from]`, skipping the interior long verts) and THEN fanned triangles over that
  same arc. `validate()` passed, so it shipped; the mesh was wildly non-manifold. Measured on a
  6/8/4 chain: 40 boundary half-edges where Blender has 10. Now a single non-overlapping tiling
  (`nl + ns` triangles), which matches the Blender oracle's face count exactly.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **BRIDGERAND (data corruption): `edge_loop_rings` was NONDETERMINISTIC.**
  `nav.rs::edge_loop_rings` iterated the `edges` **HashSet** straight into
  `geom.entry().or_insert()`, so which of a half-edge / its twin won — each ring's ORIENTATION —
  depended on hash iteration order; `adj` was built from `geom.values()` with unsorted neighbour
  lists, randomising the walk direction too. Ring orientation decides the winding `bridge_loops`
  picks, so **the same selection bridged differently run to run.** The app previews on a clone,
  gates on `is_manifold()`, then re-runs on the real mesh — two rolls of the same dice.
  `AZRA_BRIDGEDIAG=edges2`, 5 identical runs: **4 silent refusals + 1 committed NON-MANIFOLD
  mesh** that would have been saved to the `.fl4`. Invisible to unit tests (a unit test runs the
  op once). Fixed by sorting ids/keys/neighbours. Test:
  `edge_loop_rings_is_deterministic_across_runs`. CLAUDE.md already warned: "HashMap iteration =
  random order. Sort when order matters."

- ⬜ BY DESIGN (documented, not a defect) — **EDGE-mode bridging of N > 2 rims refuses.** Chaining
  N rings that each already bound a face gives interior rings 3 faces/edge. Blender ships that
  non-manifold result (oracle: `nonmanifold_edges` = 8 for 3 rings, 16 for 4); AZRA refuses it per
  the no-non-manifold rule and now toasts a reason instead of silently falling through to the
  legacy quad fabrication. **FACE mode is the manifold-clean N-loop path** (it deletes the caps
  first) and works for any N. Do not fix by dropping the manifold gate — see BRIDGE.md §3b.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **BRIDGECHAINWIND: the second bridge of a chain reused directed edges.**
  The reverse/rotate alignment search minimised distance only; but a chained bridge receives a
  long ring whose half-edges were ALREADY created by the previous bridge, and reversing the ring
  is exactly what flips their direction. The reverse choice must satisfy the twin constraint
  FIRST and minimise distance only among surviving orientations.

  **Blender oracle:** `docs/planning/poly/bridge_multi_ref.py` (Blender 4.5, `--factory-startup`).
  N loops → chain of N-1 bridges, ordered by proximity, **island-agnostic** (`two_islands_wire`
  gives a census byte-identical to `four_wire_rings`), and adding **no vertices**.
  **App-path harness:** `AZRA_BRIDGEDIAG=<mode> cargo run -p app` (`app/src/bridgediag.rs`) drives
  the real `poly_bridge()` entry on a real selection. Tests: `bridge_ring_chain_*` in
  `core_math/src/half_edge/tests.rs`.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — BOOLEAN materials + Boolean tool properties (cutter-material policy)

Owner: "Doing a boolean, it should pick up the material. Boolean needs their own tool properties,
so after a boolean, if the user wants to toggle 'no material' I could — even though this operation
is destructive."

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **BOOLMAT: the boolean's material result depended on which kernel ran,
  and the edit-mode island cutter lost its materials before the kernel even saw it.**
  * Legacy BSP kernel (`AZRA_BSP_BOOLEAN=1`): **24/24 result faces at material 0** — total loss
    (`from_polygons` stamps 0). Default Manifold kernel already repaired it internally
    (`transfer_materials_from_operands`), so the defect was invisible on the default path.
  * `app/src/poly/boolean.rs::mesh_from_faces` (edit-mode island cutter extraction) rebuilt
    through `from_polygons` and dropped every material BEFORE the boolean ran — fixed in place
    with the `merge_mesh_list` snapshot/restore carry.
  * Fix: `app/src/poly/bool_material.rs` assigns each result face the material of the input face
    whose SURFACE it lies on — operand from the existing `BoolProvenance`, face-within-operand by
    nearest point-to-triangle. App layer only; `core_math/src/mesh_boolean/` untouched.
- ✅ DONE 2026-08-07 — **BOOLPROPS: the Boolean had no tool properties at all.** New
  `Last · Boolean <op>` redo panel (Tool Parameters dock + legacy float), same lifecycle as
  `PolyToSphereAdjust`, with a 3-way cutter-material policy: **Cutter material** (default,
  Blender parity) / **Target material** / **No material**. Sticky in `ui.bool_cutter_material`.
- ✅ DONE 2026-08-07 — **BOOLMATREDO: the choice is adjustable AFTER the destructive op, honestly.**
  The kernel is never re-run. Each result face stores BOTH candidates
  (`FaceMatPlan { own, inherit, from_cutter }`), so flipping the policy is a pure re-stamp of
  `face.material_id` — reversible, geometry untouched. The panel FAILS CLOSED: if a later op
  rebuilt the mesh so the plan no longer indexes it, the panel drops instead of stamping
  materials onto strangers.
- Coverage: `app/src/poly/bool_material.rs` (kernel-level, all 3 policies) +
  `app/src/poly/diag_bool_material.rs` (4 APP-PATH tests through the real
  `poly_boolean_execute` X-pie entry, materials read off the INSTALLED scene-graph mesh,
  incl. flip-and-flip-back reversibility). Green on BOTH kernels.
- Doc: `docs/planning/poly/MATERIAL_PRESERVATION.md` §6.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Per-face MATERIAL LOSS class (Ctrl+X dissolve, Alt+X symmetrize)

Owner: "Dissolving edge (Ctrl+X) removes material" and "Symmetrize (Alt+X): I lose my material
that is assigned; it should symmetrize material by default."

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **MATLOSSCLASS: face-allocating constructors hardcode
  `material_id: 0`, so every op that REBUILDS geometry repaints the body with the default
  material.** Two allocators, not one:
  * `HalfEdgeMesh::from_polygons` (`core_math/src/half_edge/builders.rs`) — the already-known
    half (knife / boolean / bevel each fixed it locally, one call site at a time).
  * `HalfEdgeMesh::create_face` / `create_face_no_normals` (`core_math/src/half_edge/euler.rs`) —
    the half that had NOT been found, and the one the owner's Ctrl+X actually hits.
  **Ctrl+X root cause:** `dissolve_edges_region` → `dissolve_faces_region_gated` →
  `dissolve_one_region` (`ops_dissolve.rs`) DELETES the region's faces and rebuilds ONE merged
  n-gon with `create_face` → material 0. (`dissolve_edge`, the two-face merge, was never
  affected — it keeps `face_a` and its material.)
  **Alt+X root cause:** `symmetrize` → `mirrored_across`, and `mirrored`/`mirrored_single_axis`
  (`ops_misc.rs`), rebuild the WHOLE mesh face-by-face through `create_face` → the kept half AND
  the mirrored half both come back as material 0.
  **Fix — the class, at the source (all additive; no signature, behaviour or serialized shape
  changed):** new `from_polygons_with_materials` / `from_quads_with_materials` /
  `create_face_with_material` / `create_face_no_normals_with_material`; the existing entry points
  now delegate with an empty material slice, so every current caller is bit-identical. Materials
  are stamped AT ALLOCATION TIME, indexed by INPUT index — `from_polygons` skips rings shorter
  than 3, so a naive post-pass over output `FaceId`s would drift and paint faces with a
  NEIGHBOUR's material (worse than the default it replaces). Converted: `dissolve_one_region`
  (merged n-gon takes the lowest live `FaceId`'s material — deterministic, `comp` is a HashSet;
  Blender `BM_faces_join` likewise takes an example face), `mirrored_single_axis` /
  `mirrored_across` (each mirrored face carries ITS SOURCE face's material — "symmetrize material
  by default"), plus three more instances of the same class found in the audit:
  `faces_as_new_mesh` (Separate by Selection), `poke_faces`, `subdivide_faces`,
  `subdivide_catmull_clark`.
  **Tests:** `core_math/src/half_edge/tests_materials.rs` (17, kernel, exact ids incl. an
  index-drift guard) + `app/src/poly/diag_material_class.rs` (4, APP PATH — headless `AzraApp`,
  distinct materials, real `poly_dissolve()` / `poly_symmetrize_op()` entries, materials read
  back off the INSTALLED scene-graph mesh). All assert EXACT ids: "not zero" would pass for a fix
  that floods one material over the whole body.
  **Manual test:** poly body, assign material A to some faces and B to others → select an interior
  edge, Ctrl+X → merged n-gon keeps A (not default grey); Alt+X symmetrize → the mirrored half
  shows the same materials as the source half.
- ⬜ OPEN (audited, NOT fixed — deliberate) — `HalfEdgeMesh::bevel_edges_ex` (`ops_misc.rs`)
  rebuilds via `from_polygons` and loses materials. It is DEAD for users: superseded by
  `core_math/src/bevel_op/` (which handles materials), referenced only from `half_edge/tests.rs`.
  Fix it only if it is ever revived.
- ⬜ OPEN (audited, NOT this class) — new-geometry `create_face` sites (`bridge_loops`,
  `grid_fill`, `rip_fill_edge`, `solidify` inner shell) give brand-new faces material 0. Blender
  gives them the ACTIVE/adjacent face's material. Separate parity item, not a regression.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — CIRCLE knife leaves a segment instead of a cut

Owner: "KNIFE CIRCLE FAIL TO DO, GOT SEGMENT AFTER CUT" (repro `Desktop/KNIFE CIRCLE CUT FAIL.fl4`).

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 —
  **KNIFECIRCLESLIT: a CLOSED interior loop is emitted as a slit spur, never a face
  division** (`core_math/src/knife.rs:722-739`, the anchor-less branch of
  `knife_cut_screen`). A circle drawn wholly inside one face crosses no edge and snaps to no
  vertex, so the chain has NO Bound anchors. `nearest(head)` and `nearest(tail)` then resolve
  to the SAME ring vertex — the loop's head and tail are the same point, because
  `poly_knife_shape_rebuild` (`app/src/poly_knife.rs:1209`) repeats the first sample as the
  last so `knife_free_is_closed()` reads closure — and the `(Some(a), _)` fallback arm calls
  `split_poly_slit`. `closed` is a parameter of `knife_cut_screen` but the anchor-less branch
  never reads it: there is NO closed-loop case at all.
  **Evidence** (`app/src/project/diag_circle_knife.rs`, new): the owner's box is v=67 f=29,
  `validate()` OK, `is_manifold()` = *"degenerate face 0: repeated vertex 65"*, arity
  `{4:22, 5:1, 8:1, 9:2, 11:2, 47:1}`. Face 0's 47-ring has 28 unique verts: box corners
  v1..v8, bridge v8→v48, the 19-sample circle v48..v66, then the SAME circle walked backwards
  v65..v48, back to v8. A spur. Zero boundary edges, zero wire edges, zero orphan verts, zero
  slivers, zero valence-2 pins — the stray "segments" the owner sees ARE the spur. Also
  1 coincident vertex cluster `[v48, v66]` (the duplicated closing sample).
  **Blender oracle** (`docs/planning/poly/circle_knife_oracle.py`, new; cylinder r=0.35
  DIFFERENCE box ±1, solver EXACT): nv=40 nf=24 ne=64, non_manifold=0, boundary=0, wire=0,
  orphan=0, coincident=0, **pinched_faces=0**, arity `{4:20, 7:2, 17:2}`. Blender splits the
  resulting ANNULUS into two SIMPLE polygons (7 + 17 = 4 ring corners + 16 loop verts + 4
  bridge duplicates) — never a keyhole ring, never a spur.
  **Proposed fix**: `split_poly_closed_loop()` in `knife.rs` — inner disc + two annulus
  halves bridged at two non-crossing (ring, loop) pairs, with the plane GATE from §3 and the
  midpoint-visibility filter already used by the anchor-less chord. Patch text in
  `docs/planning/poly/KNIFE.md` §5.5. Target topology PROVEN legal in our kernel by
  `core_math/tests/knife_circle_annulus.rs` (2 tests, green): the annulus split rebuilds
  through `from_polygons` manifold with 0 pinched / 0 boundary, and the slit form is asserted
  non-manifold so the class stays locked.
- NEW HARNESS — `AZRA_KNIFEDIAG=circle` (`visdiff.rs`), alongside `rect`: real input path
  press(centre) → drag(radius) → release, then censuses pinched rings and prints
  `VERDICT(circle)`.

**FIX LANDED 2026-08-07** — `split_poly_closed_loop()` implemented in `core_math/src/knife.rs`
beside `split_poly_slit`, called from the anchor-less branch before the `nearest(head)/nearest(tail)`
chord logic when `closed` and the chain's head/tail close the ring. Carrier face is plane-GATED
(§3), bridges are midpoint-visibility filtered, the loop is re-wound to the parent ring via Newell,
and the parent material is propagated to both new faces.
**Before → after, through the REAL app path** (new test
`poly_knife.rs::s_circle_inside_one_face_divides_it_and_never_pinches`, 16-gon inside a cube face):
BEFORE = 2 pinched rings `[25..41, 40..25, 3,2,5,4,3]` and `[0,8..24, 23..8, 0,7,6,1]` — the circle
walked out and back, the face never divided (the owner's exact signature). AFTER = pinched 0,
boundary 0, the front sheet 1 → 3 faces (disc + two annulus halves).
**Harness:** `AZRA_KNIFEDIAG=circle` at its old 3-segment default never reached this branch
(needs `inter.len() >= 4`) — it was measuring the anchored-chord path, which is why it read
CUT COMMITTED either way. It now defaults to a 16-segment circle (`AZRA_KNIFEDIAG_SEGS`) and prints
`VERDICT(circle): CUT COMMITTED`, v=40 f=24 pinched=0 manifold=true — **the same nv/nf as Blender's
oracle** (`nv=40 nf=24 ne=64`, boundary/wire/orphan/coincident/pinched all 0). Bridge placement
differs from Blender's, so the arity histogram differs (ours 14+10 / 5+19 vs `{4:20,7:2,17:2}`);
every census invariant matches.
**Tests:** `knife_circle_annulus` 2 → 4 (added flat-quad and solid-box REAL-code-path cases; both
fail with the new branch disabled). `knife_stress_closedloop::closed_interior_single_face_splits_ngon`
updated from +1 face (chord) to +2 (disc + halves) — its own comment already flagged the chord as
"does not truly CLOSE". Green: `app poly_knife` 28, `core_math knife` 20, all 6 stress suites.
**Also:** the slice commit gate (`poly_knife.rs`) moved from bare `validate().is_ok()` to
`knife_result_is_sound()` — validate + no vertex 3+ times on a ring + no zero-length edge + edge
multiplicity. Deliberately narrower than `is_manifold()`, which would reject every legitimate knife
slit (`integrity()` flags ANY repeated ring vertex). Rationale + known limit in KNIFE.md §3.
  `AZRA_KNIFEDIAG_RECT=<frac>` sizes the radius (keep ≤0.035 — see the sizing note).
- NOTE / TRAP — do **not** "fix" this by dropping the duplicated closing point in
  `poly_knife_shape_rebuild`: `knife_free_is_closed()` decides closure from first↔last
  distance, so removing it makes the circle read as an OPEN line and take the SUBTRACT path.
  The duplicate must be dropped inside the kernel's closed-loop case instead.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Geo stays decimated after deleting the modifier + Tab-in-Knife

Owner: "I put a triangulate decimation modifier, delete it and now all the geo I created
was decimated; the mesh to SDF no longer work; Tab in knife needs to open the selection
on the same first trigger."

- ✅ FIXED — **Deleting a modifier can leave the OLD (decimated) solid on screen forever**
  (`poly/mesh_sync.rs` hot + arc early-outs). Root cause: the early-outs treated a
  `poly_display_cache` key match as proof the GPU buffer holds that content — but
  `poly_cached_display_mesh` (called every frame by `draw_selection.rs:613` /
  `overlay_lines.rs:533`) stamps exactly that key WITHOUT uploading (its own doc says
  so). Any DEFERRED resync (undo/redo of a stack edit, pipe editor's
  `poly_request_display_sync`, the one-body-per-frame `poly_drain_display_dirty`
  requeue) lets an overlay stamp the post-removal key between queue and drain → the
  drain's sync early-outs → no upload, no LOD invalidate, no MESH dirty → stale

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Modifier wire: triangulated look + Object-mode leak

- ✅ FIXED — **"Bevel modifier … the wire frame is looking very bad, it triangulated —
  just use the same wire frame from edit"**: the mesh was never triangulated (owner's
  own card read `24v 26f` = a correct 6 quads + 12 strips + 8 corner-tris bevel). The
  WIRE was: `want_gpu_wire` (raster_gbuffer) runs `fs_gbuffer_wire`, a
  **POLYGON_MODE_LINE pass over the TRIANGLE stream**, so it can only ever draw
  triangle edges — every quad shows its tessellation diagonal. That is the right (and
  only possible) wire for a DC/voxel mesh — a genuine triangle soup with no authored
  topology, hence "DC wire" — but a poly body HAS real quad/n-gon topology and an exact
  edge wire already exists (`collect_poly_local_edges` on the half-edge mesh → line
  overlay), which is what Edit mode has always drawn. Fix: poly bodies are EXCLUDED
  from the GPU triangle-edge pass (skip by mesh-cache id); their object/modifier-result
  wire routes through the same real-edge path as edit (`poly_append_display_wire` →
  display mesh). One wire, real edges, both modes — literally the owner's ask.
  LESSON: a hardware line-mode pass over triangles is not a wireframe of the model;
  it is a wireframe of the tessellation.
- ✅ FIXED — **"In object mode the wire frame from modifier is showing; no wireframe
  default in object mode"**: the modifier card's ▦ result-wire button flipped the
  GLOBAL `render.wire_overlay_enabled` (the user's Shift+Z viewport overlay) — so
  enabling modifier feedback silently turned the viewport-wide wireframe on and it
  followed the user back into Object mode. Two features were sharing one flag. Fix:
  the button owns `ui.poly_mod_result_wire` (runtime-only, never serialized); the
  global stays the user's explicit overlay. The modifier-wire block is already
  Edit-mode-only, so Object mode is clean by default again. Added to
  `overlay_fingerprint` so the cached segment list rebuilds when it toggles.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Knife slice "always fails to do a proper cut"

- ✅ FIXED — **Free-knife S slice double-cuts hidden faces**: `knife_apply_slice_layers`
  ran the front pass with `through=true` (chording every hidden face) AND then scribed
  those same faces exactly from the deeper layers — two cuts per hidden face at
  densify-quantized offsets. Straight box slice came out +7v/+3f: duplicate ring verts
  0.01 apart on every silhouette edge, one face never divided, and a mis-bound vertex
  INSIDE the box volume. Fix: chord only when no deeper layer exists (`deep_scribe`).
- ✅ FIXED — **Knife engine: crossings materialise duplicate verts** (`knife.rs`): the
  per-edge merge used edge-PARAM epsilon `VEND=1e-3`, which neither absorbs the densify
  chord error (~1% of diag, scales with sample step not edge) nor composes across
  passes (the same crossing re-expressed on an already-split segment sits >VEND away in
  param). Fix: 3D vertex snap at ~1% mesh diag — a crossing near an existing vertex on
  its edge (endpoint / previous split / earlier-pass split / near-edge densify snap)
  reuses it. All 66 knife tests green (incl. U-turn multicross); box slice now a clean
  +4-face ring, zero duplicates, zero interior verts.
- ✅ FIXED — **Classic surface knife S DELETES faces** (was OPEN P1): three stacked
  causes. (a) The run walk paired cut nodes by raw path order, so a HIDDEN
  through-crossing interleaved into the visible chain and stole the tail-slit anchor —
  now nodes chain by FACE CONNECTIVITY (hidden crossings form their own depth-sheet
  chain). (b) `split_poly_slit` bound the resulting cross-face spur via footprint
  winding with plane distance only ranking candidates — now a hard plane GATE (>2% of
  face diameter rejects). (c) The actual face-eater: `purge_degenerate_faces`
  (2026-08-06 digon rule) treated ANY repeated ring vertex as degenerate — but a knife
  slit ring revisits its anchor BY DESIGN, so every slit-carrying face was silently
  deleted on the classic commit; narrowed to <3 unique corners / zero-length
  (adjacent-repeat) edge. Verified: classic two-face S now = two slits, f 6→6,
  validate ok (Blender parity, KNIFE.md §1); free personality unchanged (+4-face
  ring); 26 app + 45 kernel/stress knife tests green. New regression test
  `s_classic_two_face_clicks_never_deletes_faces` — the classic personality's first
  app-path S coverage.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Material system: bincode field trap LIVE + bump high-precision guess
