  by the pinned intrude fixtures). Fix = the documented pattern: fields are now
  `#[serde(skip)]` (wire shape restored to pre-rot), persistence rides FL4MATX2
  record bits 10-15 (`MATX2_PROJ_ROT_SHIFT`, green_dx-style) for the data
  channels; albedo-channel rotation is not persisted yet (no albedo record).
  ⚠ Files SAVED during the broken window (hours, 2026-08-07) carry 3 extra
  bytes per material and may not load back — re-save from a session that still
  has the scene open if one exists.
- ✅ FIXED — **"bump maps look weird on ALL materials"** (owner): the load path
  FORCED `high_precision = true` for every Bump/Displacement channel record
  (`matches!(kind, ...)` — its own comment said the pixels are 8-bit). Bit 10
  set → the shader reconstructs 16-bit from `tex_id` and `tex_id+1`, and slot+1
  is an UNRELATED neighboring map — every loaded 8-bit bump decoded its own map
  as high bytes + a stranger's map as low bytes. Fix: persist the REAL flag
  (record bit 9, `MATX2_PROJ_HIGH_PREC_BIT`); zero = 8-bit = old-save behavior;
  genuine 16-bit maps saved by older builds degrade to their hi plane
  (quantized), never to cross-map garbage.

  not emissive"**: the whole chain reads wired (scanner tags emission/emissive →

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Probe wall smudges + GTAO crease streaks under accumulation

- ✅ FIXED — **"weird artifact" (owner screenshot: warm/blue smudge bands + corner
  flare on flat room walls)**: PROBE reflections in their ugliest regime — proof
  the probe bakes and serves, sampled wrong twice. (1) `probe_sample`'s
  mip-by-roughness ran to the 2×2 face-average level, but the mip chain is
  PER-FACE box reduce with no cross-face filtering — the last levels converge to
  each face's own average (warm ceiling face, blue floor face), and cube-sampling
  them paints FACE-SEAM bands wherever reflection directions cross a face edge
  (the crossing flare = a 3-face corner). `probe_max_sample_mip` now stops at the
  8×8 level (`log2(N)−3`). (2) No roughness fade: near-matte walls got the probe
  swap at full envelope weight. `probe_sample` now fades alpha over
  rough ∈ [SSR_ROUGH_MAX, 0.95] — deferred's smooth IBL + the SH light probe own
  that regime. LESSON: never cube-sample per-face-reduced mips near the face-
  average end; clamp to a level with intra-face structure.
- ✅ FIXED — **"occlusion feels weird too" (owner screenshot: dark streaks hanging
  from the wall–ceiling crease)**: the RT-penumbra-dots defect class, in GTAO.
  While accumulating, the IGN frame term was a DIAGONAL SHIFT of the noise field
  (`px + frame·5.588238`) feeding BOTH the slice azimuth and the step offset —
  two stochastic dimensions walking one correlated 1D path, and a poor per-pixel
  sequence besides. Converged AO landed on per-pixel-different structured values;
  steep AO gradients (creases) show it as permanent streaks. Fix (ssao.wgsl):
  `ign()` is purely spatial again; GTAO's rot/jitter advance decorrelated R2
  fractions (0.7548777 / 0.5698403) from INDEPENDENT per-pixel phases; SSAO's
  spiral rotation (its only stochastic dim) advances a golden-ratio sequence from
  its phase. `frame_jitter == 0` paths are bit-identical to the static pattern.
  RULE OF THE DAY (3rd instance): every stochastic pass joining the refine
  accumulator needs per-pixel-phased, per-dimension-decorrelated sequences —
  audit remaining accumulator inputs (SSR hash ✓ frame-term, SSGI ✓ R2 2D,
  RT disc ✓ fixed, GTAO/SSAO ✓ fixed, sun-cone ✓ R3 pair).
- Tests: app build green, render 100/100, graphics 84/84.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Progressive PBR leaks a 20 Hz repaint pump into Matcap

- ✅ FIXED — **"Matcap was fast; after visiting PBR progressive and switching back,
  Matcap is now slow"**: the refine block's RT-residency wait
  (`!rt_sun_ready → request_repaint_after(50ms)`) ran whenever
  `pbr_progressive_enabled`, with NO shading-mode gate. Outside Pbr/Lit the TLAS
  is rightly never built (`rt_shadows_active()` excludes those modes), so
  `rt_sun_ready` could never become true — the pump repainted the full frame at
  20 Hz forever while the user sat in Matcap. Fix: the wait-pump (and
  eligibility) now require `mode_ok` (Pbr|Lit + Hybrid) first — refine outside
  those modes is a zero-cost no-op. The settings status line also says
  "refine: inactive in this shading mode" instead of a forever-stuck
  "preparing ray pipelines…". LESSON: any wait-loop pump must be gated on the
  same prerequisites as the thing it waits for, or an unreachable condition
  becomes a busy-wait.
- ✅ FIXED — **"the refinement number makes the UI glitch"**: the live frame count
  changed the status label's width every frame, toggling the text between 1 and
  2 wrapped lines → the settings panel reflowed at 60 Hz. Now width-stable:
  counts ≥1000 display as a rounded "1.5k" (text changes every ~100 frames), the
  line is short enough to never wrap, and the restart-reason diagnosis moved to
  hover. LESSON: never put per-frame-changing text in a wrapping label — quantize
  the display or fix the width.
- ✅ FIXED — **Refine auto-sun deadlock: progressive refine never started at all**
  (found by the AZRA_MATCAP_DIAG harness: N stayed 0 through an entire idle Pbr
  phase): `rt_sun_ready` requires `rt_shadow_pipeline`, but the poll warm
  (app_poll.rs) compiled it only when the MANUAL `render.rt_shadows` toggle was
  on, and the render-path `ensure_rt_shadow_pipeline` fallback sits inside
  `if rt_active`, which needs `pbr_accumulate_this_frame` — which needs
  `rt_sun_ready`. Circular: with the toggle off (default), auto sun waited on a
  pipeline nobody would ever compile and refine never engaged. Fix: the poll
  warm now keys on `rt_shadows_active()` — the SAME canonical predicate that
  keeps the accel resident — so every consumer that wants rays also warms the
  pipeline. Verified: refine reaches N=105+ in the harness. LESSON: readiness
  checks and the warm-up that satisfies them must share one predicate.
- ✅ FIXED — **Per-frame `ViewportCommand::Title` = permanent full-rate busy loop
  in EVERY mode** (the real bulk of "Matcap got slow", and the long-standing
  idle floor): app_update.rs sent the window title unconditionally each frame,
  and egui's `send_viewport_cmd` requests an IMMEDIATE repaint — so every frame
  scheduled the next, ~300 fps forever, pinned by `ctx.repaint_causes()`
  (egui context.rs:3532 = send_viewport_cmd_to). Fix: cache
  `last_window_title` (ProjectState) and send only on change. Verified: the
  cause disappears from repaint_causes; idle cadence drops to the throttled
  compile-wait pumps only. LESSON: `send_viewport_cmd` is repaint-triggering —
  never call it unconditionally per frame; diff first.
- NEW HARNESS — **AZRA_MATCAP_DIAG=1** (visdiff.rs): self-driving repro for
  "mode X still renders after visiting mode Y" spin bugs — Pbr+progressive
  warm-up → MatCap switch → passive trailing-5s cadence verdict with
  `ctx.repaint_causes()` attribution per frame (only a 1 Hz heartbeat of its
  own, so any faster cadence is the app's). AZRA_SCOREBOARD=1 adds the
  [IDLE_SPIN] pending-work reason.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Permanent dots in converged penumbras + Auto Light Probe v1

- ✅ FIXED — **"why do I see those dots, I thought we added denoise on cast shadow"**
  (owner screenshot: stipple in a CONVERGED wide penumbra that never averages
  out): in the refine 1-ray disc sampler, BOTH the angle and the radius fraction
  advanced from the same `frame_index` (angle += golden angle, radius = golden-
  ratio sequence) — perfectly correlated, so each pixel integrated a thin
  phase-rotated 1D SPIRAL through the light disc instead of the full 2D disc.
  Different pixels → different spirals → slightly different converged means =
  permanent per-pixel stipple. No denoiser can help: the values are *converged*,
  just to the wrong per-pixel answers. **Fix (rt_shadow_entry.wgsl): while
  accumulating, angle and radius advance DECORRELATED R2 fractions (0.7548777 /
  0.5698403) with INDEPENDENT per-pixel IGN phases in both dimensions** — every
  pixel now covers the same full disc and converges to the same smooth penumbra.
  The non-refining path is bit-identical to before. LESSON: a 1-sample-per-frame
  accumulator needs a genuinely 2D low-discrepancy sequence per pixel; driving
  two dimensions from one counter collapses the sample set to a 1D curve.
- ✅ SHIPPED — **Auto Light Probe v1** (owner: "the auto probe should auto place
  light probe"): the auto reflection probe's bake now doubles as a LIGHT probe.
  On each completed bake round, `probe_sh_project` (probe.wgsl, one tiny
  dispatch) projects the cube's 8×8 mip into SH9 irradiance coefficients
  (per-texel solid-angle weights, Ramamoorthi eval); deferred consumes them at
  new binding 51 (bgl.rs single source) as the diffuse ambient: with no HDRI the
  flat gray ambient gains real directional bounce (sunlit floor tints walls,
  point-lit rooms get colored fill); with an HDRI the diffuse IBL BLENDS toward
  the probe (the probe sees the walls that occlude the sky — the HDRI SH assumes
  no scene). Never both terms (ambient double-count class). AO-occluded, bent-
  normal aware, both PBR and Lit branches. CPU owns strength ([9].x written per
  frame — toggle acts instantly), GPU owns coefficients + valid flag; zeroed
  buffer = structurally inert. UI: "Auto Light Probe" + "Bounce Strength" under
  the probe group; both hashed into the refine sig. Same auto placement, zero
  authoring — per the owner's standing "never place probes by hand" directive.
- Tests: graphics 84/84, render 100/100, app build green.

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Soft-shadow leak ROOT CAUSE (horizon clip) + SSGI denoiser + refine reflections

- ✅ FIXED — **"still leaking at 20% softness"** (owner screenshot: whole wall washed
  with stipple): the true mechanism, third and final — wide sun cones sample rays
  near the receiver's HORIZON, which graze along the receiver's own thin geometry;
  grazing any-hit tests against thin triangles miss on precision and report
  "clear", washing entire walls with false light proportional to cone width.
  **Fix: horizon clipping in the RT disc loop** — a sample below the receiver's
  tangent plane is self-occluded BY DEFINITION (that part of the light disc is
  behind the surface) and now counts as occluded WITHOUT tracing. Physically
  correct, leak-proof at any cone angle, and slightly cheaper.
- ✅ SHIPPED — **SSGI denoiser** (owner "we do not have the denoiser"; the review's
  Gate-4 spatial arm): normal edge-stopping added to the bilateral blur (the
  depth-only guide blurred straight across creases — muddy corners), and the blur
  reach now TIGHTENS as the accumulator converges (2.5σ → 0.8σ as 1/√N) so the
  converged mean is sharp — the accumulator replaces spatial filtering over time.
  Plus: GI rays ×2 while accumulating (idle budget — halves frames-to-clean after
  restarts) and R2 per-frame IGN offsets instead of the diagonal slide (the
  "marching pattern" the owner read as broken).

## 2026-08-07 (master) — REGRESSION: refining killed ALL shadows; leak-proof sun never engaged; ladder oscillated ("still flicker")

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **"NO MORE SELF SHADOWING, NO CAST SHADOW — THIS IS REGRESSION"
  + "THE LEAK PROOF DO NOT WORK" + "STILL FLICKER"** (owner, point-lit room scene).
  Three symptoms, two root causes:
  1. **The blunt suppression flag.** Phase 2b OR'd `pbr_accumulate_this_frame` into
     `gu.interaction_no_shadows` to silence the analytical SDF sun smear while
     refining — but that flag also kills point/spot SDF soft shadows (the ONLY
     shadow path for non-RT point lights), contact shadows, AND gates the RT sun
     swap itself. Net effect while refining: point-lit scenes converged to a
     shadowless image (the regression), and Leak-Proof Sun could never fire (its
     swap requires the very flag the refine path was setting). FIX: the refine
     suppression moved to a surgical channel — **post_flags bit 512** — set ONLY
     when the RT sun swap is actually live (accumulating + toggle + rt_shadows_on
     already proving pipeline/TLAS residency). The bit silences ONLY the analytical
     sun/AO recompute and doubles as the swap key on BOTH sides (ray pass +
     deferred PBR/Lit), so they can never disagree; point/contact/CSM shadows stay
     alive while refining. Probe faces use the same scheme (point soft shadows now
     LIVE in reflections — better than the v1 note).
  2. **The ladder oscillator.** An audit fix stepped `pbr_refine_shadow_boost` back
     to 0 inside the reset branch while the boost was hashed into the refine sig —
     a 2-cycle feedback loop: N reaches 32 → boost climbs → sig changes → reset →
     step-down → sig changes → reset → climb... N could never pass ~33; shadow maps
     recreated in a loop and FXAA pulsed at the N=8 boundary ("still flicker").
     FIX: the boost is OUT of the sig; a ladder climb explicitly restarts
     accumulation at the single place the level changes (fires at most twice per
     idle session); content resets KEEP the boosted maps; only interaction
     (!eligible) restores the base.
- Tests: graphics 84/84, render 100/100, build green. Manual: point-lit room —
  shadows present interactively AND while refining (converging, not vanishing);
  sun scene with thin walls — leak-free after ~1s idle (the swap now actually
  engages); N climbs past 32/128 with exactly two ladder restarts (verify with
  AZRA_REFINE_LOG=1 — no recurring resets).

## 2026-08-07 (master) — Light leaking through thin walls (owner corridor screenshot)

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-07 — **"can we fix light leaking — usually we need to put walls
  thicker but this is very artistically restrictive, can we automate the fix"**
  (owner corridor screenshot: light bleeding through/around thin walls, smudged
  shadow gradients). Root cause is structural to shadow MAPS: the anti-acne bias
  (normal offset + slope bias, scaled by cascade texel size) passes light through
  any wall thinner than the bias in world units — thickening walls just out-runs
  the bias by hand. **Automated fix (Progressive Refine Phase 2c): while the
  accumulator averages, the sun's shadows are RAY-TRACED against the triangle scene
  (rays need zero bias — a paper-thin wall blocks exactly), jittered through the
  "Sun Softness (idle)" cone with per-frame radius jitter, converged by the 1/N
  accumulator.** No per-light setup: the refine bit (post_flags 256) auto-enables
  the sun in the existing RT-shadow ray pass (`RtShadowParams.sun_tan`), the
  deferred sun swap + contact-shadow suppression gained the same arm, and the PT
  accel stays resident whenever the new "Leak-Proof Sun Shadows" toggle (default
  ON, under Progressive Refine) is armed. Interactive frames keep fast CSM.
- **Two pre-existing RT-sun gaps fixed:** `any_rt_soft_light()` excluded
  directionals (stale doc — a sun-only scene with an authored Source Radius
  silently collapsed to the hard center ray, no penumbra/denoise); the Lit
  early-return branch never applied the 2026-07-28 sun RT swap (full builds kept
  CSM in Lit while PBR traced).

  BIT-IDENTICAL with the extended params (proves the auto-sun arms are inert when
  off); render 100/100; build green. Manual: the corridor scene, Progressive
  Refine ON, idle 2s — no light through walls at any thickness; Sun Softness
  drives physical penumbra width.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — shadow bias is now three LIVE SLIDERS (and the units trap behind them)

- ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-06. After three hand-picked bias constants each shipped a visible artifact,
  the constants were replaced with live controls: **Render Settings → Sun Shadows → "Shadow Bias
  (tuning)"** — Normal Offset / Depth Bias / Slope Bias, all in TEXELS, plus Reset.
- **The distinction the sliders encode** (and the thing three attempts got wrong): the normal
  offset moves the sample POSITION, so it slides the shadow boundary along the surface
  (peter-panning) — that was the owner's "not landing in the right position". The depth biases
  shift the compared DEPTH instead, killing acne WITHOUT moving the boundary. Tune Normal Offset
  down first, then clear the exposed acne with Depth/Slope.
- All three ride unused padding lanes (`params.w`, `texel_world.w`, `cascade_splits.w`) — uniform
  size, layout, and bind groups unchanged (`shadow_bias_rides_padding_lanes`).
- **Units trap, caught in adversarial review BEFORE the owner tuned anything.** The depth sliders
  first shipped in raw light-clip NDC z. `compute_cascade_vps` builds
  `orthographic_rh(.., -r, 50+r)`, i.e. ~50 world units of caster headroom, so receivers occupy a
  band only `2r/(50+2r)` ≈ 0.03 NDC wide on a small scene: the entire useful travel sat in the
  first ~1% of a 400-step slider, making it read as binary. Fixed by denominating both in TEXELS
  and converting in `sample_shadow_cascade`. That also makes the values resolution- and
  scene-independent, matching the rule the file already stated for the normal offset.
- The conversion recovers the cascade depth range **from the matrix** —
  `1/|row2(cascade_vp).xyz|`, exact because glam's `orthographic_rh` puts `1/(near-far)` in the z
  row and the view rows are unit-length — rather than repeating the literal 50, so changing the
  headroom cannot silently desync the shader.
- **Gates:** `cascade_depth_range_is_recoverable_from_the_matrix` pins that identity AND bounds
  full slider travel to <5% of the receiver band (the tunability property that actually failed);
  `shadow_bias_defaults_are_neutral` + `shadow_bias_defaults_agree_across_crates` pin the defaults
  to the pre-slider image (the two default sites are in crates with no dependency edge either way).
- A discarded over-claim, kept so it is not re-attempted: the first version of that test also
  asserted the 50-unit headroom always dominates the band. **It does not** — cascade 1 of a far=40
  scene measures 0.51 — and the claim was never needed, since the conversion is exact at any ratio.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — "8K shadow map" was actually 1024² (the cap is not the resolution)

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 (UI honesty) — owner set **"Idle shadow cap" = 8192** and judged the
  viewport as an 8K shadow map. It was not. Two DIFFERENT settings:
  - `shadow_map_resolution` — the real per-cascade map size. **Defaults to 1024.**
  - `pbr_refine_shadow_res_cap` ("Idle shadow cap") — a CEILING on the progressive-refine idle
    ladder only.
- `app_poll.rs:288-291`: `effective = if boost == 0 { base } else { (base << boost).min(cap) }`,
  with `boost = pbr_refine_shadow_boost.min(2)`. So on the default base the viewport ran at
  **1024² whenever anything moved** and **4096² at best when fully idle** — and the 8192 cap was
  **unreachable**, since `1024 << 2 = 4096`. Every shadow-quality judgement in this session was
  made against a 1K/4K map while believing it was 8K.
- **Fix (UI, not behaviour).** The cap row now prints `→ actual: {base}² moving · {ladder_top}²
  idle`, mirroring poll's exact arithmetic, and the hover says the cap cannot raise sharpness.
  Behaviour deliberately unchanged: silently promoting the base on cap selection would allocate
  768 MB of VRAM from a control that never claimed to.
- **Owner action:** raise **"Shadow Map Resolution"** (Sun Shadows section) — that is the sharpness
  control. 8192² = 768 MB across 3 cascades.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — shadow acne at grazing light angles (comb-tooth terminator)

- ⛔ **REVERTED 2026-08-06, same day. The "fix" below was a visual REGRESSION** (owner: "WORST").
  Slope-scaling the NORMAL offset moves the sample POSITION by up to 5 texels on near-edge-on
  faces, which smears the lookup into a soft gradient across the face — worse than the acne it
  targeted. Reverted to the flat `pcf_radius + 1`. Guard `shadow_normal_offset_is_not_slope_scaled`
  now asserts the slope scale stays OUT so the dead end is not re-derived. Grazing-angle depth
  slope belongs on the shadow pipeline's `DepthBiasState`, which does not move the sample point.
- **Still open:** the underlying comb-tooth acne. Note it was diagnosed against what was believed
  to be an 8K map but was 1024² (see the entry above) — re-triage at a real 8192² base BEFORE
  attempting another bias change, because texel size is the dominant term.
- Original (now-reverted) analysis retained below for provenance:
- ~~✅ FIXED~~ 2026-08-06 — owner repro: **`docs/planning/render/repro/shadow-acne.fl4`** (their
  `Desktop/SHADOW.fl4`). Symptom: a dark band with a regular vertical comb/sawtooth boundary on a
  face nearly edge-on to the sun.
- **Root cause.** `normal_offset_texels()` returned a flat `pcf_radius + 1` TEXELS. That covers
  texel quantization for a surface facing the light, but the depth a single shadow texel spans
  grows as **tan(theta)** between the surface and the light, so at grazing angles the offset stops
  covering it and the depth comparison flips back and forth across texels — the comb teeth.
- **Why it surfaced now, honestly:** the offset is texel-SCALED, and the cascade-fit fix earlier
  the same day shrank `texel_world` ~6x. The bias shrank with it. The acne was latent; tightening
  the cascades exposed it. Sharper shadows and more acne are the same coin.
- **Fix.** Slope-scaled normal offset: `base * (1 + min(tan(theta), 4))`, with the sun direction
  carried in the previously-unused `ShadowData.flags.yzw`. The `min(.., 4)` bound is load-bearing —
  tan diverges as the surface goes edge-on and an unbounded offset would detach the shadow
  entirely (peter-panning). Scaling only at grazing angles means faces pointing at the light keep
  their tight contact.
- **Gate: PARTIAL and labelled as such.** `shadow_bias_is_slope_scaled` was a shader-TEXT guard
  against silent removal. The real gate — a readback with the sun near-parallel to a probed
  surface — is **OWED**: `run_sun_harness`'s probe set assumes the default up/+x/-z sun and cannot
  simply be re-pointed, so it needs its own probes. Recorded rather than left implicit.
- **Lesson (the reason the text guard was not enough).** A text guard proves the code is PRESENT,
  never that it HELPS. It passed green while the change made the render worse. Any future bias
  work here needs the readback gate first, not after.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — viewport rendered BELOW native resolution at any display scale >100%

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — the render target was sized from the egui rect, which is in **POINTS**
  (`viewport_render.rs:181`), and `pixels_per_point` never appeared in the render path. At Windows
  150% scaling the whole viewport rendered at **44% of native pixels** and was bilinearly stretched
  back up. Every image-quality judgement — shadow edges, wire AA, SSGI grain — was being made
  through that upscale. (Previously logged open at COMPLETE_BUG_TRACKER.md:75-79.)
- **Fix.** `px_scale = pixels_per_point * resolution_scale`, applied at the sizing site and
  deliberately BEFORE the ≥2px hysteresis gate: that gate compares against `gpu.texture_size` in
  physical texels, so a points-vs-texels comparison would differ by the DPI factor every frame and
  spin `mark_dirty(RENDER)` forever.
- **`resolution_scale` was DEAD** — written to the save file and read back, but never consulted by
  the render path (the generic upsample pass is disabled at `:211`). It is now the user's cost
  control, riding on top of the DPI factor.
- **Shipped in the same commit because they regress together:** every pixel-unit width is authored
  in POINTS but consumed as TARGET TEXELS, so a 1.5x target silently renders them at 67% apparent
  size — and the same sliders drive egui strokes measured in points, so the GPU wire and the egui
  overlay drawn on top of it would visibly disagree. Scaled: `LineInstance.width` (via a new
  `dpi_scale` in `LineParams.viewport.w`), `sel_rim_power`, `dc_wire_px`. **The AA feather is
  deliberately NOT scaled** — it is a one-target-texel coverage ramp, correct at any resolution.
- **Cost, measured by the audit:** viewport VRAM 550 MiB → 859 MiB at 125%, → **1237 MiB at 150%**
  (+687 MiB). A 4K panel at 150% goes 696 MiB → 1566 MiB.
- **Two follow-ups that pay for it, NOT done here:** (1) path-trace scratch (90 B/px = **32% of all
  viewport VRAM**) is allocated unconditionally in every shading mode, resident even in PBR/Lit
  where PT never dispatches — gating it on `shading_mode == PathTrace` frees ~400 MiB at 150%,
  covering ~58% of the DPI delta; (2) the VRAM HUD under-reports (~206 MiB shown against ~550 MiB
  real at 1080p) — fix the accounting or this change is unmeasurable and a regression invisible.
- **Verified safe by audit, no change needed:** click-to-select (P0) — `pick_node_at` renders its
  OWN pass into its OWN texture with its OWN camera and never samples the display G-buffer, so it
  is self-consistent at any resolution; `cam_ray` and every gizmo/poly ray helper normalise to NDC;
  the Phase-C cursor readback and the AI beauty region already normalise to UV and re-multiply by
  live texture dims; overlay line/face passes are world-space `view_proj`.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — Progressive Refine: converged shadows were NOT accurate (owner screenshot)

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **"THIS IS THE BEST QUALITY OF THE PROGRESSIVE REFINEMENT — WE
  HAVE A PROBLEM, WE NEED TO MAKE SURE SHADOWS ARE ACCURATE"** (owner screenshot: two
  white blocks, directional dark smears down lit faces + light leaks at contacts in
  the fully converged image). Two refined-frame smear sources (on top of the cascade
  far-plane fit fixed in the entry below, which starved texel density generally):
  1. The deferred **analytical SDF soft-shadow march runs while idle** (it is only
     suppressed during interaction) and samples the SDF FIELD, not the baked DC mesh
     actually displayed — field inflation self-shadows convex edges (the dark
     gradients under lit top edges) and misregisters cast shadows; the accumulator
     faithfully averaged that smear.
  2. The Phase-2 **PCF tap rotation** swept the square tap pattern through a ~1.41×
     annulus — it widened the fixed blur without ever producing a geometric penumbra.
- **Fix (Phase 2b): refined frames get occlusion from ONE accurate source.** Each
  idle frame renders the CSM cascades from a sun direction jittered inside a small
  cone — new **"Sun Softness (idle)"** slider (0–5°, default 1°; real sun ≈ 0.5°) —
  so the 1/N average converges to the physical area-light penumbra of the geometry
  actually rasterized into the maps: wide far from contact, razor-sharp at contact.
  The analytical soft_shadow/calc_ao duplicate is suppressed on refined frames
  (scoped decision on the known "two occlusion systems coexist" item; interactive
  and non-refining behavior unchanged). Tap rotation retired (shader capability
  kept, uniform fed 0). Shading keeps the un-jittered sun — no specular shimmer.
- **If any smear remains in the converged image after this, it is GTAO** (the third
  contributor, now converging to its true integral) — verify by toggling SSAO off;
  that would be a GTAO-quality task, not a shadow task.
- Tests: render 96/96, graphics 83/83, build green. Manual: same two-block scene,
  Progressive Refine ON, let it settle — smears gone, penumbrae widen with distance
  from contact and harden at contact; Sun Softness 0 gives converged hard shadows.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — shadow cascades fitted to a 500-unit far plane, not to the scene

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **owner: "WHY MY SHADOW ARE THAT UGLY ON A 8K SHADOW MAP ON A SIMPLE
  CUBE"**. 8192 was genuinely applied — verified end to end, no silent fallback, and `params.x`
  cannot disagree with the bound texture. The resolution was never the problem.
- **Root cause.** `app/src/raster_gbuffer.rs:830` computes the CAMERA render far plane as
  `(camera.distance * 20.0).max(500.0)` and handed that same value to
  `ShadowMapSystem::update_cascades`. The `.max(500.0)` floor dominates every normally framed
  scene, so cascade 0 covered the first 8% of **500 world units** — a **168-unit-wide ortho box**
  for a 2-unit cube. At 8192 that is a **0.0206 world-unit (2 cm) texel**, ≈**4.9 screen pixels**
  at camera distance 3 on a 1440p viewport: the reported staircase.
- **Why raising the slider could never work.** `z_split = 0.08 * far` is pinned at 40 units by the
  500 floor while the subject grows on screen, so texels-per-pixel degrades as **1/distance** —
  the closer you inspect, the worse it gets. 1:1 texels at 3 units would have needed a **40,387²**
  map, 5x past `max_texture_dimension_2d`. Crisp close-up shadows were unreachable at ANY
  supported resolution.
- **Fix.** The cascade far plane is now derived from the furthest shadow CASTER along the view
  axis, using `structural_world_aabb` — the same per-instance world AABB set the GPU culler uses,
  so "what casts" and "what is fitted" cannot drift apart. 5% + 1 unit of slack, clamped to the
  render far plane, falling back to the old value when nothing casts.
- **Second, coupled fix — the split fractions.** `CASCADE_SPLITS = [0, 0.08, 0.3, 1.0]` was
  hand-tuned for the 500-unit far plane. Once the far plane became scene-fitted, 8% of a ~17-unit
  range put cascade 0 entirely in FRONT of the subject and pushed a cube at 3 units into the
  coarser cascade 1. Replaced by `cascade_split_fractions()` — near/far-relative PSSM practical
  splits (λ=0.85). Fixed fractions cannot serve both a 500-unit and a 17-unit range.
- **Measured** (`cascade_fit_gives_subpixel_shadow_texels`), stated in SCREEN PIXELS PER SHADOW
  TEXEL at the cascade that actually serves the subject (2-unit cube inspected from 3 units,
  1440p, fov 90):

  | map | old (500-unit fit) | new (scene fit + PSSM splits) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1024 | 0.109 world / **26.0 px** | 0.0173 world / **4.2 px** |
  | 8192 | 0.0136 world / **3.3 px** | 0.0022 world / **0.52 px** |

  **At 8192 a shadow texel is now SUB-PIXEL (0.52 px) where it used to span 3.3 px** — that is
  the difference between a crisp edge and the reported staircase. 6.3x tighter at equal
  resolution, and 1024 is now usable for close-up work.
- **Two measurement traps hit while writing the gate, both corrected:** (1) it first asserted on
  cascade 0, but tightening the far plane MOVES the splits and the subject changed cascade — it
  was measuring a cascade that was not in use, which inflated the claimed win to 28x; (2) it then
  compared ACROSS resolutions ("1024 beats old 8K"), which is rhetoric rather than a gate. It now
  compares like-for-like at each resolution and asserts the sub-pixel property directly.
- **Two pre-existing tests encoded the old fixed splits** and failed for the right reason:
  `cascade_depth_maps_into_unit_range` hardcoded `[0.0, 0.08, 0.3]` (reporting a false invariant
  break) and `texel_world_size_sane` asserted magnitude windows derived from them. Both now use
  the production splitter / assert invariants.
- **Exonerated, verified:** the comparison sampler (a real `sampler_comparison` with hardware 2x2
  bilinear compare), texel snapping / cascade stabilization (textbook-correct, pinned by
  `texel_snapping_is_stable`), and the whole resolution plumbing chain.
- **Still open, found alongside:** (1) cascades 1 and 2 hold only empty air in a normal scene yet
  consume 512 of 768 MiB at 8192 and re-render the scene twice per frame; (2) no cascade blending
  — a hard switch at the split leaves a seam where texel size jumps 1.64x; (3) the resolution
  slider is silently also the peter-panning control (normal-offset bias derives from texel size:
  3.1 cm at 8192, 24.7 cm at 1024); (4) `stress_test/demo_scene.rs:1014` hard-writes
  `shadow_map_resolution = 2048`, stomping the owner's choice; (5) `CASCADE_SPLITS` is a linear
  split — log/practical would tighten cascade 0 further still.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — Progressive Refine (PBR viewport) Phase 2

- ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-06 — **the "slowly increasing shadow resolution, better raytrace,
  better reflection ray" half of the owner's progressive-rendering request.** All
  frame terms are gated on the Phase-1 accumulate verdict (static values otherwise —
  interactive path bit-identical): shadow PCF taps rotate per frame (golden-angle,
  `ShadowUniforms.params.z`) so penumbras converge to a filled disc; shadow maps
  step 2×/4× above the user's base at accumulation milestones N=32/N=128 (capped by
  the new "Idle shadow cap" setting, applied via `set_resolution` in poll, base
  restored the moment interaction starts); SSAO/GTAO's IGN rotation animates
  (`SsaoParams.frame_jitter`) so AO converges to the true hemisphere integral; SSR
  gains a per-frame hash offset + a doubled march budget while idle; RT-shadow
  temporal switches from the fixed 0.9 EMA to count-weighted 1 − 1/N (true running
  mean) while accumulating. Cascade fitting now reads the un-jittered camera so
  texel snapping stays stable under the Phase-1 sub-pixel jitter.
- Tests: render 95/95 green (incl. the real-GPU shadow/SSAO/curvature harnesses with
  the extended `update_cascades`/`SsaoParams` signatures), graphics 83/83 green.
  Manual scenario: sun + soft shadows on a prop, enable Progressive Refine, let the
  camera sit — the penumbra fills in smoothly and sharpens as the ladder steps;
  orbiting instantly restores the interactive resolution and look.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — Progressive Refine (PBR viewport) Phase 1

- ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-06 — **owner feature request: "progressive rendering for the PBR
  viewport … like a path tracer but on PBR tech, quality to infinite."** Phase 1 of
  `docs/planning/render/PROGRESSIVE_PBR_PLAN.md`: while the camera is idle in PBR/Lit
  Hybrid, every frame renders with R2 sub-pixel camera jitter and `pass_tonemap`
  folds the fully composited HDR into a 1/N running mean (`pbr_accum`, post_flags
  bit 256, bindings 63/64) — edge aliasing converges toward supersampled reference;
  FXAA auto-skips at N ≥ 8. Interaction frames are bit-identical to the legacy
  pipeline (jitter zero, bit off); at N = 4096 repaints stop (idle GPU quiet) while
  the frozen average keeps displaying. Reset discipline follows the PT rule
  (camera epsilon + curated content/quality signature, NEVER blanket is_dirty).
  Jitter is applied to the raster proj AND subtracted in every GpuUniforms
  `camera_ray()`; overlays (wire/face) draw from a new un-jittered camera buffer so
  they don't shimmer. Setting: **"Progressive Refine"**, default OFF, next to
  FXAA/Wireframe AA in both settings panels (runtime-only, save format untouched).
- **Known Phase-1 limits (by design, documented in the plan):** floor-grid lines
  (raymarch_lite) don't participate in the AA convergence; time-animated VFX in HDR
  would smear into the average (extend the reset signature if VFX gain animation);
  SSAO/SSR keep their static per-pixel patterns until Phase 2 adds their frame terms.
- Tests: full graphics suite green (Naga parse over the edited sdf_shared/
  post_process + the tonemap GPU test whose BGL mirror was extended 63/64), full
  render suite green. Manual scenario: enable Progressive Refine in Render Settings →
  Anti-aliasing, let the camera sit — edges visibly smooth over ~1s; orbiting snaps
  back to the normal interactive image instantly.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — Drag-drop material "looks broken" (owner report, Bricks038 on a plane)

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **Speckled/noisy material at distance & grazing angles.** The material
  texture array had `mip_level_count: 1` and every shader sample was `textureSampleLevel(…, 0.0)`
  — no minification story at all, so a 1K map on a ground plane aliased into per-pixel noise, and
  the Bump path's `dpdx/dpdy` of that aliased height turned it into black-speckle chaos.
  Fix: full mip chain on `material_tex_array` (`material_textures.rs` — descriptor counts levels,
  `write_layer` generates + uploads the chain via a linear-space sRGB-correct box filter, both
  capacity-grow copies move every level), plus real LOD selection in the samplers
  (`gbuffer.wgsl`/`shadow.wgsl` `mat_lod()` from `var<private>` texel footprints set in uniform
  control flow at the top of `fs_gbuffer`; vertex/shadow/probe contexts stay at mip 0 by
  construction). Tests: `mip_count_matches_wgpu_rule`, `downsample_preserves_solid_color_every_byte`,
  `downsample_averages_in_linear_space`; all 95 render tests (drift guard, naga, GPU probes) green.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **"Normal looks inverted"** (Bricks038 ships `NormalGL`). The whiteout
  triplanar read green as +v, and this pipeline samples v DOWN the image — i.e. AZRA implemented
  the DirectX convention, inverting every OpenGL-convention map (all of ambientCG). Fix: per-map
  convention flag `TexMap::green_dx` (`#[serde(skip)]` — bincode field-trap; persists via bit 8 of
  the FL4MATX2 record's projection word, zero = OpenGL = correct for old saves), GPU bit 11 of the
  packed projection word, green flip in `gbuffer.wgsl::sample_mat_triplanar_normal` AND the PT copy
  (`pathtrace_tri_entry.wgsl`). Auto-detect at import (`normal_green_is_dx`: filename markers
  NormalGL/NormalDX/_gl/_dx → else ORM-sibling ⇒ Unreal layout ⇒ DX → else OpenGL default) on both
  the library-drop worker and the file-picker path; manual override combo ("Green channel:
  OpenGL (Y+) / DirectX (Y−)") in the material panel's Normal row. Graph-BAKED normals keep DX
  (they were authored against the old read — render-identical). Probe fixtures pinned via the DX word.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **Packed ORM detected as "roughness"** — `detect_texture_role` matched the
  "roughness" substring of `…OcclusionRoughnessMetallic…`, so the whole pack landed in the
  roughness slot and the shader's `.r` sample read the OCCLUSION channel; metallic was lost.
  Fix: new `orm` role (checked before roughness), split at import — G → Roughness, B → Metallic
  (`decode_file_to_data_map_channel`); a dedicated Roughness/Metallic file still wins over the
  pack. Test: `packed_orm_wins_over_roughness_substring`.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **Poly plane unselectable in the viewport.** The object color-ID pick
  pipeline (`render/src/picking.rs`) culled back faces while the main raster is two-sided
  (`pipeline.rs` cull None + fragment normal flip) — a single-faced body wound away from the
  camera rendered fine but wrote nothing into the pick buffer. Fix: `cull_mode: None`, same rule
  (and same comment rationale) as the poly sub-element pick pass below it: pick visibility is
  decided by depth alone.
- ⚠️ OPEN (found during this fix — concurrent session's in-flight work, NOT this task) —
  **`LightData.ambient_color` / `ambient_from_hdr` added as IN-BLOB serde fields**
  (`core_math/src/scene_graph/node.rs`, uncommitted). `#[serde(default)]` does not protect
  bincode: 3 committed fixtures now fail `load_binary` with "failed to fill whole buffer"
  (`project::tests::intrude_owner_fixtures_pinned`, `test_020`, `test_021`) — every existing
  `.fl4` with lights will refuse to load. This is the documented field trap; the fields must ride
  a FL4 tail side-channel (the `FL4LTVOL` pattern), not the blob.
- OPEN (deliberate, minor) — AO maps (`_ao` role and the ORM `.r` channel) are detected but not
  imported: `PbrMaterial` has no occlusion slot yet. Adding one is a material-model feature, not a
  role-detection fix.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — Overlay wireframe aliased (not Blender-sharp)

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **"IN AZRA THE WIRE FRAME IS NOT AS SHARP, MORE ALIASING"** (owner,
  vs Blender). The GPU wire pass (`render/src/line_overlay.wgsl`) drew each edge as a
  hard-edged screen-space quad at 1spp with flat alpha — no MSAA, no coverage falloff — and
  it draws AFTER FXAA, so scene AA never touched it. Blender's overlay engine antialiases
  wires analytically (per-pixel line direction+distance into a line-data texture
  → fullscreen resolve, `overlay_antialiasing.bsl.hh`); we now do the single-pass variant:
  the quad is expanded by a 1px feather ring + round-cap endpoint extensions, and the
  fragment shader converts exact distance-to-segment into a 1px coverage ramp multiplied
  into alpha (screen-linear `@interpolate(linear)` varyings — perspective interpolation
  would bow the ramp). The cap extension also mends the notch two adjacent edges left at a
  shared vertex (butt caps meeting at an angle). Covers edit wire, object wire overlay,
  modifier wires and X-ray in one place (shared shader).
- **Perf setting (owner-requested):** `render.wire_aa_enabled` — default ON, toggle
  "Wireframe AA" next to FXAA in both settings panels (`ui2/shell/render_settings.rs`,
  `properties_render.rs`). Off = zero quad expansion = the exact legacy pipeline for
  low-end GPUs. Runtime-only; deliberately NOT in the bincode ProjectFile (save-format
  red line).
- Tests (`render/src/line_overlay.rs`, real-GPU): new
  `wire_aa_edge_row_is_partial_and_off_is_binary` — a 5px line's edge row measures ~0.5
  coverage with AA on, empty outside the ramp, and AA off reproduces the legacy binary
  quad exactly. All pre-existing occlusion/coplanar/X-ray tests pass with AA on.
- **Still open (separate task):** the viewport target is sized from the egui rect in
  *points* (`viewport_render.rs:181`) and linearly stretched to physical pixels — at
  Windows 125%/150% display scale the whole viewport (wires included) renders below
  native resolution. Fixing it is a G-buffer-wide resolution change (~1.5–2× pixel count)
  and needs its own perf assessment.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — G-buffer depth convention diverged in ORTHOGRAPHIC views

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **every screen-space effect was silently wrong in orthographic views.**
  Found while grounding `docs/planning/render/SSGI_PLAN.md`; not reported by a user, because
  the symptom is "the effect quietly does nothing" rather than a visible artifact.
- **Root cause.** `render/src/gbuffer.wgsl` wrote `length(world_position - cam_pos)` into
  `gbuf_normal.w` with **no orthographic branch**, while every consumer reconstructs the
  world position as a **ray parameter** along `camera_ray()` (`p = origin + dir * t`).
  In perspective the two are identical — `camera_ray()` normalizes its direction from
  `cam_pos` — which is why this survived since the raster path was introduced. In ortho
  `camera_ray()` shifts the origin per-pixel and keeps `dir == forward`, so the parameter is
  `dot(rel, forward)`; the producer's Euclidean value exceeds it by `|rel| - dot(rel, forward)`,
  several world units at the screen edge.
- **Observed consequences (all ortho-only):**
  1. **SSR reflected nothing.** Its hit test `delta = ssr_metric(p) - sample_depth > 0`
     (`post_process.wgsl:368`) compares a forward-z metric against a Euclidean depth, so for a
     coincident surface `delta <= 0` always — the test could never fire.
  2. **SSAO/GTAO was internally inconsistent** — reconstructed `p` with the ray parameter
     (`ssao.wgsl:136`) but compared occluders with a Euclidean distance (`ssao.wgsl:173`),
     mis-occluding every off-axis pixel.
  3. **Deferred shading positions were wrong for raster pixels**, so point-light distance,
     attenuation and specular vectors were all off.
  4. Three temporal passes had already been *defensively disabled* in ortho because of this —
     `rt_shadow_temporal.wgsl` even named it: *"ortho (gbuffer .w is eye-distance, not
     along-ray)"*.
- **Fix.** `gbuf_depth()` in `render/src/gbuffer.wgsl` — one helper, used by both `fs_gbuffer`
  and `fs_gbuffer_wire`, branching on `cam_pos.w > 0` exactly like `ssr_metric()`. The camera
  forward is derived from the view matrix (`look_at_rh` stores `-forward` in the third row),
  so `CameraUniforms` is unchanged. `ssao.wgsl:173` updated to the same metric. The convention
  is now stated once, authoritatively, in the `gbuffer_format` contract block
  (`graphics/src/lib.rs`), whose old text — *"w = march distance t"* next to a producer writing
  world distance — is where the ambiguity was written down. That header also named two writers
  deleted 2026-07-14; corrected to the three real ones.
- **Perspective is bit-unchanged by construction** and all 93 pre-existing `render` tests passed
  unmodified.
- **Still open, deliberately NOT changed:** the three ortho guards in `pt_reproject.wgsl`,
  `pt_restir_reproject.wgsl` and `rt_shadow_temporal.wgsl` stay, because their
  `world_to_prev_screen` / `world_to_prev_lighting` helpers are still perspective-only (they
  divide by forward-z with `fov_scale`, no ortho branch). Their comments were updated so the
  next reader does not lift them for the now-fixed reason. Lifting them requires giving those
  helpers an ortho branch first.
- Test: `gbuffer_depth_is_ray_parameter_in_both_projections` (`render/src/ssao.rs`) — renders
  the real raster G-buffer in both projections, reconstructs the probe pixel's ray exactly as
  `camera_ray()` does, intersects the floor, and asserts the written depth equals that ray
  parameter. Ortho probe reads **5.6953** vs ray parameter **5.6956** (Euclidean would be
  **6.7505**). Sabotage-verified: reverting the ortho branch makes it fail.

## 2026-10-12 — Crash entering half-resolution interaction

- Confirmed panic in `viewport_render.rs`: `Half-res switch during active episode: false -> true`. The subsequent GPU `Dropped` event was shutdown after the panic, not evidence of a preceding GPU fault.
- Root cause: episode start updated the latched resolution but left its diagnostic baseline from the previous episode. PathTrace enters half resolution immediately, so the lite/fallback dispatch misclassified the legitimate start transition as a mid-episode change.
- Fixed: one `InteractionEpisode::begin` operation initializes pipeline and resolution latches together with both diagnostic baselines before marking the episode active. Genuine mid-episode assertion checks remain intact; an active episode cannot be relatched.
- Validation: app build succeeds; two lifecycle regressions pass. Automated PathTrace/orbit startup reached real render dispatch and exited cleanly without the assertion. This is not a long-duration native interaction stress test.

## 2026-10-12 — Real polygon Curvature node, automatic GPU cache

- Implemented in the owner-approved current version: Curvature reads real post-modifier mesh edges through a GPU BVH/surface atlas, not a synthetic field or interpolated corner constant. All twelve coarse cube edges respond; coplanar subdivision and triangulation seams stay flat.
- Parameter-only edits reuse surface measurements, graph pipelines and texture slots. Bounded scheduler work and a 128 MiB surface budget avoid unbounded per-frame discovery, compilation and geometry rebuilding. Shared materials retain object-specific output atlases.
- Corrected integration dependencies: raster cached draws and converged PT invalidate on publication/removal; PT carries real mesh UVs and color precision. Derived atlas meshes are excluded from saves through scene-graph ownership, independently of GPU lifetime.
- Validation: actual GPU raster pixels, default radius, intermediate falloff, PT atlas lookup, geometry/cache reuse and source-mesh save roundtrip pass. Material GPU tests 20/20, graphics 76/76, render 96/96, height/normal regressions 2/2. Native interaction verification remains owner-operated.
- Scope limits are explicit in `docs/planning/render/MESH_CURVATURE_PLAN.md`; unsupported graph/UV combinations fail closed. Three full core-math failures outside curvature remain unchanged.

## 2026-10-11 — Shader node fields and bump-strength discoverability

- Implemented: node-local font, interaction height and padding now fit the fixed socket rows instead of inheriting oversized shell controls. Vector fields have room for all three components.
- Implemented: Master Material displays the existing Bump Strength control directly beneath Height. Socket IDs and saved graph data are unchanged; wire anchors and map-resolution placement use the same visual-row mapping.
- Validation: node-editor tests pass, including large-shell-font and unique socket-row regressions. Executable replaced in the same checkout; owner performs native visual verification.

## 2026-10-11 — Node masks, connected bump strength and value resets

- ✅ FIXED — Mask: generated float and vector outputs now read the node's authored Mask default as a GPU parameter instead of hard-coding 1.0. Wired masks still evaluate their upstream graph.
- ✅ FIXED — Connected Bump Strength: height gradients and the strength field are evaluated separately, at their proper sample positions. Spatial strength is resolved into the existing resident GPU normal-map channel; the height channel is not also applied as bump. Scalar strength retains the existing height-map path. CPU fallback shares the height-to-normal sampler and surface-gradient math, including an existing Normal input.
- ✅ FIXED — Reset controls: each editable socket has a reset button; Reset Values restores selected nodes' numeric/color controls, including noise levels and projection offsets, without deleting connections or changing operation types. Changes return the existing editor undo snapshot.
- Tests: actual GPU mask and spatial-strength output changes preserve pipeline count and texture generation; CPU spatial strength and channel ownership pass; reset simulation preserves wires and returns pre-reset values for undo. Native testing remains owner-operated.

## 2026-08-06 (master) — test-021: Extrude Along Normals inward = very crooked geo

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-06 — **"THE EXTRUDE ALONG NORMAL, WHEN USE INSIDE GIVE VERY CROOKED GEO"**
  (owner TEST-021.fl4). Along Normals did a *region* extrude then slid every cap vertex along
  a *blend* of incident face normals. On a multi-face non-planar selection that shears every
  wall and warps every cap into a non-planar n-gon — worst when dragging inward.
- **Fix:** Along Normals = Blender Alt+E individual: each selected face is `extrude_face`'d
  on its own and every cap vert of that face slides along **that face's** normal (no blend).
  Caps stay planar, walls stay planar quads. Adjacent selected faces get independent shells
  (double wall on the shared edge), matching Blender individual.
- Region mode (plain E) unchanged. Mid-drag N toggle still uses frozen blend when starting
  from region (only Along Normals *start* takes the individual path).
- Fixture: `docs/planning/poly/repro/test-021.fl4`. Test:
  `test_021_along_normals_inward_keeps_planar_walls`.

## 2026-08-05 (master) — slice produced geometry OUTSIDE the mesh (regression, same day)

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-05 — **"slice produce geo outside of the target mesh to slice"** (owner
  screenshot: a cube with two triangular flaps hanging off the top and bottom after a free-knife
  slice). Introduced HOURS EARLIER by the poly_3d fix below — an own goal, and a good argument
  for the app-path gate that now exists.
- **Root cause, and it is not really about the knife:** `point_in_polygon_3d` is a
  sum-of-signed-angles winding test whose own doc says "`p` is assumed near the polygon plane".
  Nothing ENFORCED it. The test reads INSIDE anywhere in a face's infinite PRISM, at any height
  — a point floating a unit above a cube's top face is "interior" to it. The free knife draws on
  a plane captured through the BODY CENTRE, so every path point past the silhouette sits inside
  the top or bottom face's prism, became a real cut vertex out in space, and its edges rendered
  as flaps. The precondition is now structural: a point further than the mesh-scaled tolerance
  from a face's plane is not interior to it.
- ⚠️ Third entry in the `point_in_face_3d` trap family (see the boundary/on-rim trap that shipped
  two bugs in one day). The shape of it is always the same: this predicate is used as if it were
  a containment test on a surface, and it is not — it is a winding test with an unstated
  precondition. Anywhere else it is called, check what guarantees the caller has about the plane.

## 2026-08-05 (master) — free-knife `S` slice failed on any path with interior points

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-05 — **"this slice pressing s fail"** (owner screenshot: a free-knife line
  entering a quad from below and stopping INSIDE it; `S` reported "nothing to cut").
  `poly_knife_free_slice_commit` passed `poly_3d = None` to `knife_cut_screen`, which is the
  engine's documented switch for "crossing-only behaviour". Consequences:
  - a path that ENDS inside a face produced **nothing** — one boundary crossing with nothing
    to connect it to (the screenshot);
  - a path that crossed in AND out had its interior bends **ignored**, cutting a straight
    chord instead of the drawn zig-zag.
- ℹ️ The cut engine supported both cases the whole time (`knife_dangling_into_ngon_slits`),
  and the CLASSIC knife passes `Some(&local_pts)`. Only the free/alt slice withheld them —
  which is why every core_math knife test stayed green while the feature was broken. App-path
  gates added (three), two of which fail on the old code.
- ⚠️ The reason it could not simply pass its own points: the free knife's points live on the
  frozen DRAWING PLANE, not on the surface, so handing them over raw would classify every one
  as off-surface and SEVER the path. Each is now resolved onto the mesh along the captured
  view direction — the same thing this personality already means by "the cut extrudes along
  the captured view". A point whose ray misses the mesh stays off-surface on purpose (the
  engine reads it as a path break, correct for a line leaving the silhouette).
- ⚠️ STILL OPEN, owner decision: `S` deliberately does NOT commit the rubber-band point under
  the cursor, so the cut stops at the last CLICKED point even though the screen shows the band
  running past it (in the screenshot, out the right-hand side). With this fix the drawn part
  now cuts; whether `S` should also take the pending point is a behaviour question, not a bug.
- ⚠️ UNRELATED, seen in the owner's log: one frame spent **693.9 ms** in overlays, all of it
  `library` (`[Overlays] 693.9ms = ... library 693.9 (thumbs 0.0)`), with a second at 150 ms.
  Not investigated.

## 2026-08-05 (master) — mesh cleanup destroyed the tag system

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-05 — **"mesh clean up we have some mesh clean up operation that break the
  tag systeme, usaly all edge that are tag to bevel are important so mesh clean up should
  never touch it"** (owner). Two separate defects, both closed:
  - **The sidecar was DELETED wholesale.** `poly_mesh_cleanup_now` ran
    `poly_custom_data.remove(&nid)` after the rebuild, so one Mesh Cleanup erased every Smart
    Select tag, Mark Sharp, UV, seam, crease and polygroup on the body. It now carries the
    sidecar through by `remap_by_position` — the same carry the boolean, bevel and inset
    already used. Cleanup was the one rebuild op that never got it.
  - **Cleanup removed tagged edges.** Mesh Cleanup and Limited Dissolve merged/dissolved by
    flatness alone. Both now take a protected set built from the four authored layers
    (`op_created`, `sharp`, `seam`, `crease > 0`), and a protected edge is never removed.
- ⚠️ NON-OBVIOUS, worth remembering: excluding a protected edge from the dissolve CANDIDATE
  list is **not** enough. `dissolve_edges_region` merges each connected component of faces
  into ONE n-gon, and an n-gon has no interior edges — so a protected edge whose two faces
  reach each other by any other dissolvable path is swallowed regardless. On a flat grid
  every face is one component, which is how the first attempt was caught. Protection has to
  hold the two FACES. `merge_coplanar` does not have this hole (it consults the preserve set
  again when dissolving a region's internal edges).
- ℹ️ Enforcement rides the thread-local preserve set the boolean already seeds
  (`rebuild::set_preserve_explicit`), so `merge_coplanar` and the valence-2 sweep needed no
  per-pass plumbing. Fold repair is unaffected by protection — cleanup still fixes the
  zero-thickness flaps it exists to fix.
- ℹ️ **Known inconsistency, deliberately NOT changed here:** the boolean's own
  `post_boolean_polish` limited-dissolve does not consult that preserve set, so it can still
  dissolve input edges the other passes are told to keep. It is oracle-tuned face-for-face
  against Blender; changing it belongs in its own task with the oracle in hand, not as a side
  effect of this one.
- ⚠️ UNRELATED FLAKE observed while verifying: `bench_display_mesh_ops::prefix_cache_actually_
  reuses_the_unchanged_prefix` passes and fails run-to-run on identical code (debug-build
  wall-clock comparison at ~0.3ms). Not caused by this work — it needs a floor or `#[ignore]`.

## 2026-08-04 (master) — boolean/intrude: three root causes closed in one day

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-04 (7607c0e) — **Same intrude gave different results per app launch**
  ("worked two commits ago", replay-vs-app divergence, v=53/55/57 on identical input).
  Root: `extrude_region` iterated HashSets while ALLOCATING vertices → randomly-ordered
  topology per process, and the exact boolean is input-order-sensitive. Fix: sorted
  iteration everywhere ids are allocated (faces, region verts, up_at walks). Fingerprint-
  verified identical across runs.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-04 (7607c0e) — **Full-pierce intrude refused although the kernel result
  was perfect** (owner test-05 "completely off the island"). Root: the volume sanity gate
  measured operands by raw mesh integral, which underestimates a cutter whose caps span a
  non-planar ring — a correct result sat 0.25% below the lower bound. Fix: the invariant
  now uses Manifold's resolved volumes (`Manifold::volume()`) inside `manifold_boolean`;
  the raw-integral gate applies to the legacy BSP path only. Also: prism depth clamped to
  the farthest exit; refused THROUGH-cut restores the pre-drag mesh + toast.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-04 — **The entire "fold debris / doubled sheets / epsilon slivers"
  class** (owner test-04, step_fail.json, knife_now.json — chased for days as a
  Merge-by-Distance gap). Root: `halfedge_to_manifold` FAN-triangulated every face; on a
  nonconvex ngon (the coplanar horseshoe face wrapping an intrude region) the fan emits
  overlapping triangles outside the polygon → self-intersecting input → kernel emits fold
  debris + ~1% wrong volume, while Blender EXACT on identical input is clean. Fix:
  ear-clip ngons at the Manifold input boundary. test-04 vol == Blender EXACT to 6
  decimals; all fixtures now all-ngon (tris=0), folds=0. Merge-by-Distance kernel op is
  no longer needed for this class.

## 2026-08-03 (master) — extrude intrude: seam vertex not welded when the region touches the rim

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-03 — **Intrude (pushed-in extrude) left a stacked sliver + unwelded seam
  vertex whenever the pushed region touched the solid's rim** (owner: "does not merge the
  vertex to the segment properly"). Root: the stacked-wall merge probed cap corners with a
  strict inside/outside test (`point_in_face_3d`); a cap vertex landing exactly ON the
  neighbor's boundary (the common case — region corner = solid corner) read as *outside* →
  "mixed" → wall skipped → double plane + T-seam. Fix: probes are three-state — strictly
  inside / ON the rim (neutral, scaled eps via `closest_on_seg_3d`) / strictly outside; only a
  genuine inside+outside mix (real overshoot) vetoes the merge. The merge also moved from the
  app layer into the kernel (`HalfEdgeMesh::merge_coplanar_extrude_walls`, ops_dissolve.rs) so
  it is unit-testable; app wrapper unchanged in behavior. Regression tests:
  `intrude_full_top_merges_all_four_walls` (cube → shorter box, 6f/8v),
  `intrude_partial_top_welds_seam_at_rim` (the owner's split-top bar, 8f/12v, no coincident
  verts, split vertex kept).

## 2026-08-03 (master) — knife cut across a CONCAVE face corrupts the rest of the mesh

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-03 — **Knife cut across a concave n-gon "breaks the other part": long sliver
  edges sprayed across faces after the cut.** First surfaced by the new extrude stacked-plane
  merge (a pushed-in cap leaves a notched CONCAVE face), but latent for any concave n-gon. Root:
  a straight cut crosses a concave face's boundary 4+×, and `knife_cut_screen` joins EVERY
  consecutive crossing pair; for the pair spanning the notch (midpoint outside the polygon),
  `find_soup_poly`'s unconditional fallback returned "any polygon carrying both anchors" and
  `split_poly_through` emitted a chord straight across the notch → self-intersecting ring →
  ear-clipper stall-fan slivers (`poly_mesh.rs` fan-on-stall). The dry-run gate (`validate()`
  only) is blind to it. Fix (knife.rs): fallback now accepted ONLY when the probe lies ON the
  carrier's boundary (scaled eps, `closest_on_seg_3d`) — genuinely-outside probes REFUSE the
  span (fail closed, arms still cut); anchorless-chord `nearest` filtered to ring vertices whose
  connecting segment stays inside the face (midpoint `poly_contains`). Regression test:
  `knife_concave_face_cut_never_chords_the_notch`.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-03 — **knife occlusion + surface-pick raycasts FAN-triangulated n-gons**
  (owner repro: "the second small cut broke the first cut's geo but only on one side"). On a
  CONCAVE face the fan claims phantom area over the notch AND misses real face area — so during
  a visible-only cut, hidden back-side crossings were kept/dropped wrongly → the hidden side
  got spurious/half cuts. Fix: both raycast sites (`knife.rs occluded`,
  `poly_knife.rs knife_surface_hit_at_screen`) now do ray∩face-PLANE + winding-number
  containment via shared `knife::point_in_polygon_3d` / `newell_normal` (world-space ring for
  the app pick — xform-safe). Fan closure `ray_tri` deleted. Regression test:
  `knife_visible_only_occlusion_sees_through_concave_notch` (notched front sheet with the fan-
  hostile ring start + back quad behind the hole: both must split).
- ⬜ OPEN — every knife cut wipes per-face materials: the engine rebuilds the WHOLE mesh via
  `from_polygons` (`knife.rs`), which allocates all faces `material_id: 0`. Multi-material body
  → single material after any cut. (Also loses stable element IDs — audit Gap already tracked.)
- ⬜ OPEN — knife commit gate too weak: dry-run checks `validate()` only (`poly_knife.rs`), which
  is blind to self-intersecting rings; `is_manifold()` is not consulted (slit spurs would need a
  carve-out). A stronger gate would turn any residual tangle into a clean refusal toast.

  not move the SOLID — it snapped into place only on the next viewport click.** SDF and poly
  alike (both draw through the instanced raster path). Root: since the D1 key-driven instance
  upload (`e724f19`: upload ⇔ structural rebuild ∨ camera plane-key change; the sampled
  content-hash that used to catch transform changes was deliberately removed), a transform
  write that marks only `RENDER` redraws with the CACHED structural draw list's OLD instance
  matrix. Every object-transform writer (gizmo apply, apply_transform resets, poly/NURBS/SDF
  properties panels — six sites, one identical pattern) marked RENDER only. Fix: new canonical
  `mark_transform_dirty()` (dirty.rs) = structural stream stale + `raster_upload_plane_key = 0`
  + `scene_modified` + RENDER; all six writers routed through it. Class rule: `mark_dirty(RENDER)`
  is NEVER sufficient for a transform write.

## 2026-08-02 (master) — owner live-modelling session: frozen surface, dead bevels, torn corner

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-02 (feat/perf-tribound) — **Selecting a dense poly body cost O(mesh) CPU every
  frame** (68 ms @3.1M tris selected, 70 ms in edit mode — PERF_TARGETS G1/S2 + G1/S4, the two
  standing ❌ rows vs Blender). Root: `overlay_faces_fingerprint` (overlay_faces.rs:180) hashed
  `mesh.content_signature()` — a full O(verts+edges) walk — every frame the body was selected,
  and the fingerprint ran BEFORE the work-mode early-outs so object mode and edit mode both paid
  it. The memo built to avoid O(mesh) per frame cost O(mesh) per frame to check. Fix: the same
  O(1) identity its sibling `overlay_lines::overlay_fingerprint` adopted 2026-07-31 (Arc ptr +
  `pt_stamp`). Selected @3.1M: 68 → **8.8 ms**; edit @3.1M: 70 → **9.1 ms**; @0.2M: 1.4/1.8 ms —
  both rows now beat Blender normalized (3.0–3.8 ms @1M). Repro harness committed:
  `AZRA_FULL_UI` / `AZRA_STRESS_SELECT` / `AZRA_STRESS_EDIT` + `[DREST]`/`[DISP]` scoreboard
  drill-down probes (the probes are what attributed the cost — keep them).

  unchanged_prefix` (bench_display_mesh_ops.rs:397) is a flaky timing assert: fails ~1-in-3 on
  0.02 ms noise in debug builds (0.34 vs 0.32 ms). Not a functional failure; needs a
  multi-iteration median or a ratio threshold instead of a single-sample compare.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-02 — **Poly surface did not update live** (extrude/grab drags, object move; wires
  moved while the SOLID stayed frozen). `update_chunk_verts_in_place` mirrored the NEW verts into
  `imported_persistent` BEFORE the upload ran, but `upload_pending` uses that map as the
  "what the GPU holds" baseline for `update_vertices_dirty_runs` → it diffed the new verts against
  themselves, found zero changed runs and wrote NOTHING. Ownership is now single-writer:
  `imported_persistent` means exactly what the GPU holds, written only by `upload_pending` after a
  successful upload. (`b055cf8` predecessor + `mesh_cache.rs`.)
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-02 — **Same class, second writer: BEVEL drag froze** (HUD width moved, surface
  didn't). `update_editable_mesh_ex` is a FULL REPLACE that also poisoned that baseline; a bevel at
  constant segments regenerates identical topology every frame, so the index count matched and the
  diff path ran. `full_replace_pending` now forces `update_raw` for a replace — a replacement can
  never be served by a diff against a baseline it just overwrote. (`b055cf8`.)
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-02 — **Bevel silently did NOTHING on extruded geometry** (`6012c68`).
  `geometry_collide_offset` applies the collapse form `(k+cosθ)/sinθ` to BOTH neighbours; for an
  IN-LINE neighbour (θ=180°, exactly what an extrude leaves when it splits an edge into collinear
  halves) sinθ≈−8.7e−8 → denom 1.14e7 → width limit 6.5e−8 → clamped to ZERO. A side only constrains
  collapse when its adjacent edge actually TURNS; the straight case is the slide-walk's job (already
  implemented). Oracle: Blender gives a full watertight fillet on the same input.

  edge and caps with ONE n-gon over `[arc…, slides]`; AZRA collapsed that to a single recessed centre
  and fanned to it (1 vertex where Blender has 3) → sliver fan. `partial_slides` implements the real
  rule at degree ≥ 5 (degree-3/4 keep the oracle-verified centre). Owner's captured mesh now matches
  Blender **26v/19f, watertight, vertex-exact** on all 6 hexagon points.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-08-02 — **Two selection highlights at once** (`338bafd`): the green silhouette rim PLUS
  a full-edge selection cage. The cage is gone; edit wire / modifier wire / shaded+wire display stay.
