## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (box-path pen-up relaxation traversed diagonal stroke unions)

- **SCULPT-BOX-RELEASE-UNION: box/CPU release polish, Auto Smooth, and Pinch relax used the global
  stroke AABB.** On a fast high-resolution diagonal this could allocate and traverse mostly untouched
  volume. Like the atlas finish path, these optional release passes now run only when the union is at
  most 4,194,304 voxels; the per-dab live edits remain authoritative for larger swept strokes.

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (atlas release read back unrelated bricks inside the stroke union)

- **SCULPT-ATLAS-EXACT-READBACK: the high-resolution pen-up path selected pool handles by the global
  stroke AABB.** A diagonal gesture could therefore copy unrelated surface bricks lying between its
  dabs. Release now reads the exact first-touch brick set already owned by the atlas Undo builder,
  with the prior region/full-arena path retained only as a recovery fallback.

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (voxel sculpt map errors blocked later GPU work forever)

- **SCULPT-MAP-ASYNC-FAILURE: both the GPU box-brush readback and asynchronous surface pick only
  signalled successful `map_async` callbacks.** An error therefore remained indistinguishable from
  Pending: the brush's single in-flight slot rejected every later batch, while the pick slot stopped
  refreshing the live atlas hit forever. Both paths now use the existing explicit
  `Pending`/`Ready`/`Failed` map state. A failed brush batch is released without calling
  `get_mapped_range`; a failed pick clears the stale hit and discards its staging buffer so the next
  frame recreates and retries it. Regression tests:
  `callback_result_has_distinct_pending_ready_and_failed_states`,
  `brush_readback_failure_is_settled_not_pending`, and
  `brush_collect_waits_only_at_explicit_lifecycle_barriers` passed 1/1 each; `cargo build -p app`
  passed in the isolated review target (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (relax recorded zero-effect voxels)

- **SCULPT-RELAX-ZERO-DELTA: `relax_region` recorded and rewrote every voxel in its AABB even when
  the neighbour average produced the same density.** Uniform regions therefore generated
  volume-sized, zero-effect undo bookkeeping. The relax pass now computes the final iso-preserving
  value first and skips both `StrokeRecorder::record` and `DensityStorage::set_idx` when the density
  delta is at most `1e-7`; an all-no-op relax also avoids dirtying the AABB. Regression test:
  `relax_region_uniform_density_records_no_delta`. This atomic fix does not replace the function's
  full-AABB snapshot with tiling; that remains a separate architecture task.

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (first sculpt dab synchronously compiled GPU pipelines)

- **SCULPT-FIRST-DAB-PIPELINES: `VoxelBrushGpu` was lazily constructed inside the live input path.**
  Its brush, gather, and scatter pipelines are now created with the rest of the GPU context, moving
  one-time shader compilation out of pen-down latency. `cargo build -p app` passes; the existing lazy
  guards remain as device-context recovery fallbacks.

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (atlas pen-up postprocess escaped undo and swept empty space)

- **SCULPT-ATLAS-POSTPROCESS-UNDO: atlas undo captured stamp bricks, then release polish/relax could
  modify every brick in the stroke's global AABB after the builder was finished.** A local finish pass
  is now capped at 4,194,304 voxels and its complete brick set is captured before undo finalisation.
  Longer swept strokes skip the volumetric finish pass instead of traversing their empty union. Undo's
  affected chunks are derived from exact captured bricks, not that union. Regression test:
  `atlas_undo_regions_follow_captured_bricks_not_their_global_union`.

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (atlas readback erased the final interpolator/deferred dabs)

- **SCULPT-ATLAS-RELEASE-TAIL: pen-up applied the interpolator tail and budget backlog to the stale
  CPU grid, then GPU atlas readback overwrote those edits.** Release now resolves fresh-tail dynamics,
  preserves deferred-before-fresh FIFO order, symmetry-expands once, materialises exact touched
  bricks, captures their first-touch GPU snapshots, and dispatches the bounded atlas batches before
  finalising the undo builder or reading the pool back. CPU-path release tails now receive the same
  symmetry expansion. Regression test: `release_tail_keeps_deferred_fifo_before_fresh_samples`.

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (far atlas dabs allocated their empty union as GPU scratch)

- **SCULPT-ATLAS-UNION-SCRATCH: one live atlas dispatch allocated both density and snapshot buffers
  for the global stamp union.** A fast diagonal stroke or an off-centre symmetry pair could span most
  of a 1024 cubed grid and request multi-gigabyte buffers. Atlas stamps are now greedily partitioned
  in original order whenever their union would exceed 4,194,304 voxels (16 MiB per scratch buffer),
  while exact per-stamp brick materialisation and first-touch undo capture remain shared. Regression
  test: `distant_atlas_stamps_are_split_before_union_scratch_explodes`.

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (symmetry multiplied work and strength outside the stamp budget)

- **SCULPT-SYMMETRY-BUDGET-PLANE: the frame budget counted primary dabs before symmetry, and dabs
  exactly on a mirror plane were duplicated.** XYZ could therefore dispatch eight times the stated
  budget and apply up to eight deposits at the origin. The primary FIFO budget now reserves the
  worst-case symmetry multiplier, while axis expansion skips points within half a voxel of their
  mirror plane. Regression test: `symmetry_respects_final_budget_and_does_not_duplicate_plane_dabs`.

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (stroke path latch survived pen-up)

- **SCULPT-STROKE-PATH-LATCH: `stroke_uses_atlas` remained `Some(false)` or `Some(true)` after normal,
  Move, and Smudge releases.** At high resolution, a completed box/Move interaction could therefore
  keep disabling the atlas overlay as though the stroke were still active. Every release route now
  restores the documented `None` idle state. Regression test:
  `release_clears_both_atlas_and_box_path_latches` 1/1 passed; `cargo build -p app` passed in an
  isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (512 cubed violated the Sculpt viewport ownership boundary)

- **SCULPT-VIEWPORT-512-BOUNDARY: sparse 512 cubed selected the raymarch overlay even though the
  project contract assigns raster display through 512 cubed and raymarch only above it.** The
  centralized gate now uses `res > 512`, preserving one display owner at the boundary. Regression
  test: `raster_owns_512_and_raymarch_owns_only_above_512` 1/1 passed; `cargo build -p app` passed in
  an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (atlas strokes targeted the stale CPU surface)

- **SCULPT-ATLAS-STALE-HIT: the closest-hit chooser allowed the pre-stroke CPU field to beat the live
  GPU atlas and then replaced the GPU normal with `grid.normal_at`.** Subtractive strokes therefore
  kept aiming at the old outer shell instead of following the carved relief. While `cpu_grid_stale`
  is true, only an on-ray live g-buffer hit is accepted (with its own normal); the existing stable-hit
  plane remains the miss fallback. Asynchronous previous-cursor picks are rejected when their lateral
  distance from the current ray exceeds the brush tolerance. Regression test:
  `stale_cpu_surface_cannot_override_live_atlas_hit_or_normal` 1/1 passed; `cargo build -p app` passed
  in an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (random alpha orientation restarted every frame)

- **SCULPT-TIP-RANDOM-FPS: `TipOrientation::Random` used the frame-local loop index.** The random
  alpha spin sequence restarted at zero on every input event, so identical dabs rotated differently
  when frames were partitioned differently. It now uses the same per-stroke seed and absolute dab
  cursor as brush dynamics. Regression test:
  `random_tip_orientation_is_independent_of_frame_partition` 1/1 passed; `cargo build -p app` passed
  in an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (pressure radius was frame-local instead of dab-local)

- **SCULPT-RADIUS-PRESSURE-BACKLOG: deferred and pen-up dabs inherited another frame's radius.**
  Pressure-to-radius was applied only to a frame-local scalar while `StrokeSample::radius_scale`
  remained 1.0, and Random Radius replaced that field outright. The resolved pressure scale now
  travels with every sample, interpolates along the path, survives FIFO deferral and `flush()`, and
  composes multiplicatively with Random Radius. All dispatch paths multiply the stable tool radius by
  that per-dab value. Regression tests: `interpolated_dabs_preserve_pressure_radius_scale` and
  `random_radius_composes_with_existing_dab_scale` passed; `cargo build -p app` passed in an isolated
  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (pen-up did not drain the final GPU box batch)

- **SCULPT-RELEASE-NOT-A-BARRIER: release inferred waiting from `stroke_active`, which stayed true
  until after undo commit.** A Pending final box batch could land on a later frame, outside the
  stroke's undo entry and after CPU tail edits. GPU collection now has explicit `PollOnly` and `Drain`
  policies: frame/input polling never blocks, while pen-up and grid resample drain before committing
  or replacing authoritative state. Regression test:
  `brush_collect_waits_only_at_explicit_lifecycle_barriers` 1/1 passed; `cargo build -p app` passed in
  an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (brush dynamics changed with frame partition)

- **SCULPT-DYNAMICS-FPS-SEED: every input frame restarted random dynamics from a new wall-clock seed.**
  Jitter, Scatter, Random Rotation, Random Strength, and Random Radius therefore changed when the
  same tablet gesture was divided across a different number of frames. Each stroke now owns one seed
  and an absolute primary-dab cursor; a frame starts at the corresponding point in the deterministic
  stream and advances it only for newly generated dabs. Deferred dabs remain fully resolved and do not
  consume the stream twice. Regression test: `brush_dynamics_are_independent_of_frame_partition` 1/1
  passed; `cargo build -p app` passed in an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (voxel Sculpt pen pressure applied twice)

- **SCULPT-PRESSURE-DOUBLE: pressure-to-strength produced `pressure²`, while radius-only routing still changed strength.**
  The input path first multiplied shared brush strength by stylus force, then stored the same force
  in `StrokeSample`; both CPU and GPU stamp producers multiplied those values again. Pressure is now
  read once and carried only as the per-dab strength factor, while pressure-to-radius remains an
  independent one-time radius scale. Smudge, which returns before stamp creation, receives the routed
  strength explicitly. Random Strength still composes with the per-dab factor. Regression tests cover
  linear strength composition and radius-only isolation. Gates: `cargo test -p app pressure_` 3/3 passed;
  `cargo build -p app` passed in an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (voxel Sculpt repainted forever while idle)

- **GPU voxel-mesh flush continuously re-armed `DirtyFlags::RENDER` with no mesh work.**
  `voxel_flush_dirty_chunks()` visits the GPU route every frame while a voxel sculpt exists, and
  `voxel_flush_gpu_async()` unconditionally marked RENDER even when there were no dirty chunks and
  no in-flight batch. That kept egui's repaint loop and the full-screen sculpt raymarch running at
  idle. The render gate now fires only when the flush consumed or resident-dispatched chunks,
  re-queued failed/stalled work, or still owns an in-flight batch that needs another poll. Atlas
  brush writes keep their existing direct RENDER invalidation, so live stroke feedback is unchanged.
  Regression test: `idle_flush_does_not_render_but_real_work_and_polling_do`. Gates: targeted test
  passed (1/1); `cargo build -p app` passed in an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (GPU atlas stroke materialized empty union bricks)

- **SCULPT-ATLAS-UNION-ALLOC: separated dabs allocated every sparse brick inside their combined AABB.**
  The atlas gather still needs a temporary union window, but the persistent CPU/GPU brick pool and
  first-touch undo snapshot now materialize only the sorted unique bricks intersected by actual dab
  AABBs. Diagonal or symmetry-separated dabs therefore leave the empty union corners implicit instead
  of permanently growing the pool, undo payload, upload work, and later raymarch occupancy. Duplicate
  brick ids are deduplicated inside `DensityStorage`, preserving deterministic first-touch undo even if
  callers overlap. This is the safe sparse-allocation slice; replacing the transient union gather with
  brick-local halo work remains a separate architecture task. Gates:
  `materialize_bricks_report_is_sparse_deterministic_and_undoable` 1/1 passed;
  `diagonal_stamp_regions_do_not_allocate_union_corners` 1/1 passed; `cargo build -p app` passed in an
  isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (budget-deferred sculpt dabs changed shape across frames)

- **SCULPT-DEFERRED-REDYNAMICS: every retry re-projected, re-oriented, and re-randomized a deferred dab.**
  Budget overflow was prepended before the per-dab surface, tip-orientation, projection, culling, and
  dynamics stages, even though those samples had already completed all of them in the prior frame.
  A busy frame could therefore move or rotate the same pending dab repeatedly, making an identical
  gesture produce a different stroke at different frame rates. Only freshly interpolated dabs now run
  through those stages; fully resolved deferred dabs are prepended afterwards and drained FIFO before
  newer work. Symmetry still expands only the dabs actually dispatched that frame. Regression test:
  `deferred_dabs_keep_their_resolved_shape_when_budget_spans_frames` 1/1 passed;
  `cargo build -p app` passed in an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (live voxel remesh blocked the UI on a slow GPU batch)

- **SCULPT-MESH-FRAME-WAIT: an async mesh readback forced `device.poll(Wait)` after three frames.**
  A valid large batch that needed more than three repaint frames synchronously blocked the sculpt/input
  thread until the GPU finished. After five frames the code also guessed that callbacks were lost,
  dropped the batch, and repeated its work. Mesh readback callbacks now record both completion and
  failure explicitly; polling stays non-blocking for any Pending duration, Ready batches collect, and
  only an actual map error re-queues the affected chunks. One-shot parity/debug helpers retain their
  intentional blocking barrier but now check the captured map result before reading. Regression test:
  `pending_ready_and_failed_are_distinct_without_frame_timeouts` 1/1 passed;
  `cargo build -p app` passed in an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (unmasked GPU strokes allocated a box-sized zero mask)

- **SCULPT-GPU-ZERO-MASK: every unmasked atlas batch allocated and uploaded a dense zero volume.**
  The atlas route cannot run while a protect-mask is active, yet it created a CPU `Vec<f32>` and GPU
  storage buffer covering the entire union box solely to satisfy binding 3. The normal GPU box route
  also built the same zero payload when the sculpt had no mask. `VoxelBrushGpu` now owns one persistent
  four-byte zero binding; the reclaimed `aabb_max.w` uniform bit tells WGSL whether the real box-local
  mask may be indexed. Real non-zero masks retain their full buffer and behavior, while unmasked box
  and atlas strokes allocate/upload neither the CPU nor GPU zero volume. Gates:
  `zero_or_missing_mask_uses_the_dummy_binding` 1/1 passed; `cargo test -p graphics` 61/61 passed,
  including the real GPU brush parity suite; `cargo build -p app` passed in an isolated
  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## FIXED - 2026-07-20 (GPU box backpressure silently dropped sculpt dabs)

- **SCULPT-BOX-DAB-DROP: samples generated while the prior box readback was Pending were discarded.**
  The async collector correctly avoided a mid-stroke Wait, but the dispatch guard only requested a
  repaint when the previous batch was still mapping; the already interpolated current samples then
  fell out of scope. Fast strokes therefore lost density exactly when the GPU was busiest. The resolved
  primary prefix is now re-queued at the front of the FIFO, ahead of any later budget overflow. Mirrored
  copies are deliberately excluded because symmetry regenerates them once when the primary batch really
  dispatches. Regression test: `gpu_backpressure_requeues_primary_fifo_without_symmetry_copies` 1/1
  passed; `cargo build -p app` passed in an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (pre-existing warnings only).

## 🔴 OPEN — 2026-07-30 (poly tool audit vs Blender — `docs/planning/poly/POLY_TOOL_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md`)

- 🔴 **P0 — Mirror modifier mirrors the WRONG AXIS.** `PolyModifier.mirror_axis: u8` has **two
  incompatible encodings live at once, with no translation layer**. The kernel reads it as an INDEX
  (`half_edge.rs:4060-4066`, `match axis { 0=>X, 1=>Y, _=>Z }`) and `mesh_sync.rs:233` passes it RAW.
  But the properties panel writes a BITMASK — three independent X/Y/Z checkboxes XOR-ing bits 1/2/4
  (`properties_poly.rs:352-357`). Verified at source 2026-07-30. Concrete mis-mapping:
  **tick X → value 1 → kernel mirrors Y**; tick Y → 2 → falls to `_` → mirrors Z; tick Z → 4 → `_` →
  Z (correct only by accident); tick X+Y → 3 → `_` → Z only. Multi-axis mirror is presented in the UI
  and is **not representable at all** — the field is an index. A second writer,
  `symmetry.rs:234` (`axis.min(2)`), correctly writes an index, so the two writers also disagree with
  each other. Fix must pick ONE encoding and convert at the boundary; if bitmask is chosen the kernel
  needs a real multi-axis path, not a `match`.
- 🔴 **P0 — Extrude does nothing in Vertex or Edge select mode.** `mesh.extrude_vertices_move` /
  `mesh.extrude_edges_move` have **no AZRA equivalent** (grep for `extrude_vertices` /
  `extrude_edges` / `extrude_vert` / `extrude_edge` = 0 hits). Pressing `E` outside Face mode arms
  `poly_tool = ExtrudeFace` (`key_dispatch.rs:18`) but the drag gate requires a non-empty FACE
  selection, so nothing happens. Verifier precision: the arming **persists**, so after switching to
  Face mode the still-armed tool fires on the next viewport click — latent, not merely inert. Drawing
  an edge profile and pulling it into a surface is a core box-modelling move.
- 🔴 **P1 — Spin is hardcoded to one preset.** The kernel takes steps/angle/merge, the app pins all
  three (`spin.rs:11` `SPIN_DEFAULT_STEPS=8`, `:12` `SPIN_DEFAULT_ANGLE=TAU`, `:91` `merge=true`) and
  there is no redo panel, so only an 8-segment full 360° revolve is reachable. Verifier downgraded
  blocker→major: it does work, the authoring surface is just a single fixed preset.
- 🔴 **P1 — Kernel ops that exist, are Blender-oracle-tested, and have NO user path:**
  `Dissolve Faces` (`dissolve_faces_region`, `half_edge.rs:3267`, oracle test at `:9282`),
  `Split Edge` (`half_edge.rs:925`, `PolyEdit::SplitEdge`), and the poly **CustomData layers**
  (seam / sharp / crease / vcrease, `poly_mesh.rs:390-398`). The expensive half is built; only the
  wiring is missing.
- 🔴 **P1 — No Boolean MODIFIER.** Booleans are destructive-only; there is no non-destructive stack
  entry, so a boolean cannot be re-tuned after the fact.
- 🔴 **P2 — Merge by Distance is partial**, and the Merge menu lacks At First / At Cursor / Collapse.
  Also absent: the whole **Clean Up** submenu (Degenerate Dissolve, Delete Loose, Fill Holes, Make
  Planar Faces), **Beautify Faces**, **Rotate Edge CW/CCW**, **Select All by Trait** (non-manifold /
  interior / loose — the diagnostic selections), and **Extrude Individual Faces**.
- ✅ **Not a bug (refuted by the verifier, recorded so it is not re-filed):** "no operator smooths just
  the selection". `poly_loop_relax` (`poly/loop_tools.rs:54`) does exactly that, reachable via
  `Ctrl+Alt+L` and a menu entry.


## ⏸ PARKED (owner-directed) / 🔴 OPEN — 2026-07-30 (Smart Mirror — multi-agent pillar review)

Owner 2026-07-30: *"the smart mirror is an old tool that never work really, we should rebuild it to be
an action for mirror in sdf — but not now, put it on hold."*

**Do NOT fix these two. The tool is scheduled for replacement**, and patching it would stabilise code
that is meant to be deleted. Both findings are accurate and are kept as the SPEC for the rebuild —
they are exactly what the replacement must not repeat. Full write-up:
`docs/planning/render/PILLAR_REVIEW_FINDINGS_2026-07-30.md` § "Smart Mirror — PARKED".

- ⏸ **PARKED** — Smart Mirror "Instance" writes a **negative prim scale**
  (`app/src/mirror_actions.rs:314`). `core_math/src/primitives.rs:882` evaluates
  `d * self.scale.x.min(self.scale.y).min(self.scale.z)`, so a negative component makes the distance
  negative and **inverts inside/outside** — the solid renders inside-out in the bake, the GPU eval and
  the outline at once. *Rebuild rule: a mirror is a reflected transform (or body-level `mirror_flags`,
  which already exists), NEVER a sign flip on scale.* Verified at source 2026-07-30.
- ⏸ **PARKED** — `create_mirror_instances` pushes to the **flat GPU cache without a graph write**
  (`app/src/mirror_actions.rs:321`: `s.scene.primitives.push(inst)`). Violates Mutation Discipline
  (graph is source of truth, `primitives` is a read-only cache), so the next `sync_flat_cache()`
  silently destroys the instances. *Rebuild rule: go through the graph + the Structural Mutation
  Checklist, inside a `transaction()`.* Verified at source 2026-07-30.
- 🔴 **OPEN — decision needed (NOT parked):** the broken path is **reachable today**.
  `app/src/input_keyboard.rs:223` routes `Alt+X` to the Symmetrize pie only when
  `active_poly_nid().is_some()`; the comment at `:222` says *"SDF Alt+X is NOT poly, so it falls
  through to Smart Mirror further down."* So on an **SDF body**, Alt+X still reaches the broken tool.
  Options: **(a)** fail closed — disable that route with a "Mirror is being rebuilt" toast (one line;
  the documented temporary guard CLAUDE.md's No-Hacks rule permits), or **(b)** leave it armed.
  Recommended (a). Deliberately not done as part of the review: "park the rebuild" and "leave a
  corruption path armed" are different decisions and only the first was made.

## ✅ FIXED / 🔴 OPEN — 2026-07-28 (GPU material bake P1 — `gpu_material_bake.rs`, `GPU_MATERIAL_BAKE_PLAN.md`)

New dispatcher `app/src/gpu_material_bake.rs::bake_material_maps_gpu_blocking` (test + manual-verify
only; production integration still needs the async cross-frame `MapState` fence, not yet wired).
Building and testing it against the CPU oracle surfaced 4 pre-existing bugs in code this task
depends on but did not itself introduce — none were previously caught because nothing before this
task compiled a REAL generated `NodeGraph::generate_wgsl()` graph standalone (the only prior
compile test, `shader_build.rs::validate_material_bake_shader`, uses a hand-written stub):

- ✅ **FIXED** — `NodeGraph::generate_wgsl()`'s Noise/Voronoi/BrickTexture codegen calls `hash31`
  but never defines it; assumed supplied by a host shader that (post 2026-07-14 analytical-path
  deletion) no longer exists. Fixed by injecting a WGSL translation of the CPU oracle's
  `node_graph_bake::hash31` in `build_material_bake_wgsl` (`graphics/src/shader_build.rs`) — NOT
  `sdf_prim_eval.wgsl`'s same-named-but-different hash (a first attempt used that one by name-match
  alone; it compiles and validates fine but is numerically wrong, the "shares the same wrong
  convention" trap — caught by the parity gate showing an unexplained ~14/255 albedo divergence,
  not a compile error).
- ✅ **FIXED** — `graph.rs:1013` (`compile_wgsl`'s Noise octaves default) formatted with `{:.0}`,
  emitting a bare integer literal (`"4"`) that fails naga type inference inside
  `clamp(4, 1.0, 64.0)`. Every unconnected Noise node hit this. Changed to `{:.4}` matching every
  sibling default on the same node.
- ✅ **FIXED** — `input_var_name` (used for `MatResult.color`/`.emission`, both `vec3<f32>`) never
  coerced a `Float`-typed source (e.g. a bare `Noise` node) into `vec3(...)`, even though
  `SocketType::compatible()` explicitly allows Float→Vec3/Color "so Noise→albedo... connections
  work like Blender". Every bare Noise→Albedo graph — the canonical procedural material — failed
  naga's `InvalidStoreTypes` validation. Fixed with a new `input_var_name_vec3_coerced` used at
  both `compile_wgsl` and `compile_per_prim_wgsl`'s color/emission sites.
  **NOT fixed (flagged, out of scope):** the reverse direction — a Color/Vec3 source into a
  Float-typed target (Roughness/Metallic/Opacity) — is the same bug class and not yet hit by any
  graph this task built or tested.
- ✅ **FIXED** — `material_bake.wgsl`'s `mb_scalar3` (roughness/metallic channel encode) wrote raw
  linear bytes with a comment claiming the CPU does the same ("NO sRGB curve"). False: the CPU
  `encode_data_scalar_rgba` DOES apply the sRGB LUT, because the material texture array those maps
  eventually load into is `Rgba8UnormSrgb` and hardware-decodes on sample — the pre-encode is what
  makes the round-trip cancel out. Measured before fix: mean |Δ| = 70/255 on a constant 0.35
  roughness (not fp32 noise — the exact signature of one side curving and the other not). Fixed by
  applying `mb_linear_to_srgb` in `mb_scalar3`, matching `encode_data_scalar_rgba` exactly.
  Post-fix: mean/max = 1.0/255 / 1/255.
- 🔴 **OPEN, not fixed** — after all of the above, `gpu_bake_matches_cpu_on_procedural_graph`
  still measures albedo max |Δ| = 14/255 (task bound: 8/255) on 57/12288 channel-samples (0.46%),
  while mean |Δ| = 0.58/255 (task bound: 2/255, so 3.4x margin). Diagnosed as fp32 hash chaos:
  `hash31`'s `n *= n+33.33; n *= n+n` amplifies a sub-ULP fp32 evaluation-order difference between
  rustc and Naga/the driver into a different lattice-corner GRADIENT VECTOR at isolated samples —
  not a formula bug (the fade curve, gradient table, and tile-wrap formula were verified
  textually/numerically identical between the two sides; a standalone f64 re-derivation of the full
  chain agrees exactly at hand-picked points). Bounded, non-systematic (excellent mean is the
  "averages toward zero" signature of fp noise, not a biased formula), inherent to comparing two
  independent fp32 compilers on a deliberately chaotic hash. Per instruction, tolerance was NOT
  loosened to force a pass — `gpu_bake_matches_cpu_on_procedural_graph`'s max-albedo assertion is
  left failing and documented in the test itself. Follow-up options (not done): a less chaotic
  hash, or widen tolerance with owner sign-off after independent confirmation this is fp noise and
  not a residual bug.

## ✅ FIXED 2026-07-23 (late) — LIVE-MATERIAL-FEEL — pixel-proven by the AZRA_VISDIFF harness

**The harness worked exactly as designed** (`app/src/visdiff.rs`, `AZRA_VISDIFF=<dir> cargo run -p app`
— app builds box + Noise→Albedo material, scrubs Scale, screenshots Hybrid+PT, exits; PIL pixel-diff).
Run 2 verdict: A(scale4)↔B1(scale20 live) **byte-identical** → live layer rendered NOTHING. Frame-stamped
material trace then showed noise `en=true amt=1` at shot time but `albedo=(1,1,1)` — apply_live's black
was being clobbered.

**Root cause #1 (the whole "no live feedback" saga):** `enqueue_material_node_graph_bake_quality`
set `m.albedo = Vec3::ONE` (wired-albedo white tint for the incoming map) in the SAME call chain
immediately after `apply_live_gpu_noise_material` wrote `albedo = color0` (black). Live layer became
`mix(white → white)` = mathematically invisible — in Hybrid AND PT. Also explains the owner clue
"in PT noise showed in roughness but never albedo": roughness0/1 = 0/1 survived, albedo mix was
white-on-white. **Fix:** enqueue leaves albedo/albedo_map alone while `noise_pattern.enabled` (live
layer owns them); the white tint moved to the ONE settle-handoff point (`apply_map_slot` Graph arm,
where the live layer is switched off). Post-fix harness: A↔B1 mean|diff| 0.00 → **1.44**, visible
scale-4 clouds / scale-20 grain in the shots, PT reacts live too (C↔D1 1.26).

**Root cause #2 (baked graph materials always too dark + settle "pop"):** the CPU graph bake wrote
LINEAR bytes (`v*255`) into the `Rgba8UnormSrgb` slot array → hardware sRGB decode darkened every
baked albedo/emission (0.5 → 0.21). Live preview computed linear → mid-gray; bake landed near-black.
**Fix:** `encode_srgb_color_rgba()` (material_textures.rs) at the bake write for albedo + emission
(file-loaded PNGs were already sRGB — untouched). Post-fix: B1↔B2 settle diff 3.69 → **1.21**, settled
tone matches live.

The harness is kept permanently (env-gated, zero cost in normal runs) as the materials regression rig.

## ✅ FIXED / OPTIMIZED — 2026-07-20 (triangle path-tracer correctness + hot-path audit)

- ✅ **PT scene membership was camera-dependent.** PathTrace frustum culling removed off-screen
  meshes that could still cast shadows, appear in reflections, or contribute GI, and camera motion
  could force full scene uploads. FIX: PT now assembles the canonical renderer instance set.
- ✅ **PT BLAS lifetime leaked deleted meshes and could resurrect late jobs.** Removal now advances
  the generation before eviction, stale async results are rejected, and ownership-based retention
  releases deleted meshes without evicting hidden/isolation-filtered bodies.
- ✅ **New/load project boundaries could alias saved mesh IDs to the previous scene's caches.** New
  and loaded projects now reset mesh/PT ownership, advance allocation past every serialized graph
  and sidecar ID, and restore mesh sidecars before fallback voxel regeneration (avoiding collisions,
  stale BLAS reuse, and duplicate voxel meshing).
- ✅ **Instancing multiplied geometry storage and singular transforms could poison/refit the scene.**
  Repeated `MeshCacheId` placements now share one vertex/triangle/BLAS slice. Computed inverse and
  normal matrices are finite-validated (small valid scales remain supported), and the refit layout
  signature tracks ordered unique traceable geometry IDs so repeated-instance count/order changes
  stay on the cheap refit path while validity or geometry-layout transitions force assembly.
- ✅ **Triangle traversal did unnecessary work and could drop deep-BVH branches.** Closest-hit now
  visits nearer children first; shadow queries use true early-exit any-hit traversal; redundant
  any-hit near-distance stacks are gone; BLAS stack capacity now covers the CPU builder's depth-48
  contract; uploaded node-count bounds remain clamped by fixed GPU-hang watchdog caps.
- ✅ **Per-hit light selection reserved a 256-float function-local table.** The shader keeps only a
  compact 16-bin prefix CDF and recomputes weights inside the chosen bin, reducing private storage
  pressure while preserving the exact discrete PDF.
- ✅ **Half-resolution upscale sampled the wrong guide/footprint at borders and odd viewport sizes.**
  Mapping now uses the real full/half ratio, clamps candidates after offsetting, matches the PT
  G-buffer coordinate rule, and sharpens around the depth-selected half texel.
- ✅ **Regression gates:** `cargo test -p render` 42 passed / 1 ignored benchmark; `cargo test -p
  graphics` 62 passed. The GPU occlusion oracle now covers internal TLAS + BLAS nodes and shared
  instances. The explicit release benchmark (1,711,250 triangles) measured 375.5–410.6 ms BLAS
  builds and 43.3–44.6 ms full assembly on this machine. `cargo check -p app` remains blocked by 17
  pre-existing committed-tree errors outside this slice (material-editor symbol and SDF snapshot
  tuple/API drift); no new error is from this fix.

## ✅ ADDED — 2026-07-18 (RT PROJECTED SHADOWS — Stage 0 + 1 + 2 (denoise/temporal) + 3 (soft penumbra); full doc: docs/planning/render/RT_SHADOWS_DESIGN.md)

- ✅ **Point/spot lights cast NO shadow from poly/voxel/imported/NURBS geometry (coverage hole, CLOSED — Stage 1, uncommitted worktree)** —
  the deferred point/spot shadow came only from `soft_shadow` marching `scene_sdf`, which holds
  analytical SDF prims ONLY → non-SDF casters cast zero point/spot shadow (asymmetric vs the sun's
  CSM, which shadows all body types). FIX: a new RT-shadow compute pass (`rt_shadow_entry.wgsl`,
  `build_rt_shadow_wgsl`) fires ONE hard occlusion ray per point/spot light against the triangle-PT
  BVH (all 5 body types) and writes a per-light RGBA16F visibility texture; the deferred PBR + Lit
  loops REPLACE `soft_shadow` with it when `config.rt_shadows_on` (repurposed `_pad_env0`, zero
  layout change). Sun stays CSM. **Stage 0 keystone:** `update_pt_accel` now keeps the PT accel
  resident outside PathTrace when the runtime-only `RenderSettings.rt_shadows` toggle is on (accel
  machinery reused verbatim; toggle NOT serialized → no save-format trap). The shared BVH traversal
  is a `// #region PT_TRAVERSAL` block in `pathtrace_tri_entry.wgsl`, extracted (not duplicated) —
  one traversal, one CPU oracle. World P reconstructed from gbuf_normal.w exactly as deferred does
  (NOT raster_depth/29, which is 0 on SDF-compute pixels); origin = P + n·PT_EPS. Vis texture full-res,
  gen-aligned with the G-buffer in the resize block; rt_shadow pipeline lazy + poll-warmed; deferred
  RT-swap OUTSIDE `#region SHADOW_AO` so df-LITE gets shadows too. Render-panel checkbox added.
  **Verify (GPU readback, real `render::pt_accel` scene + production BGL, `rt_shadow_gpu_test.rs`):**
  occluded probe 0.0000, clear probe 1.0000, WGSL-vs-`trace_scene_cpu` oracle 0/1024 mismatches,
  no-occluder scene fully lit, deterministic. Gates: `cargo build -p app`✓, `graphics` 53✓ (all Naga
  variants incl. df-full/df-lite/PT/rt_shadow), `render` 35✓, `app --bins` 243✓.
- ✅ **Stage 2 (denoise + temporal) + Stage 3 (soft contact-hardening penumbra) — the "RTX look", DONE 2026-07-18 (uncommitted worktree).**
  Stage 3: the single hard ray → **N rays over the light disc** (radius = `dist·tan(half-angle)`, ⊥ ldir),
  Vogel-spiral + per-pixel IGN rotation + per-frame temporal rotation; `vis = unoccluded/N` → physically
  contact-hardening penumbra. GLOBAL controls (runtime-only, save-format red line): `rt_shadow_softness`
  (0..1) + `rt_shadow_ray_samples` (1..16), carried by a dedicated `RtShadowParams` uniform (binding 25),
  NOT in the locked-624 B GpuUniforms. **softness 0 OR samples 1 → BIT-IDENTICAL to Stage 1** (readback
  anchor: 0 partial px + assert_eq vs the exact Stage-1 dispatch). Stage 2: NEW `rt_shadow_denoise.wgsl`
  (4-channel joint bilateral, pt_denoise approach) + `rt_shadow_temporal.wgsl` (pt_reproject gather-reproject,
  fixed-α=0.9 EMA — a per-pixel history count is impossible, all 4 RGBA carry lights). Chain: rt_shadow→A,
  spatial A→B, temporal (B + reprojected history C)→A, copy A→C; deferred reads A. RT chain RELOCATED above
  the L7 prev-normal copy so reprojection sees genuine prev-frame geometry (reuses `temporal_prev_normal_dist`
  + `temporal_prev_cam`); a dedicated `rt_shadow_history_valid` flag (false on resize/RT-off/interaction-skip)
  = no stale-history pop on orbit-resume. Textures B/C in the resize block (Frame Ordering); passes lazy-compiled
  only when penumbra active. **Verify (readback, real GPU):** anchor 0 partial px + byte-identical; penumbra
  band 110 px; contact hardening near-recv 10 px vs near-light 216 px; bilateral edge-preserve 0.902/0.201 (no

- ✅ **Stage 4 = DONE (2026-07-18, uncommitted worktree).** Per-light hybrid (Approach C proper): each point/spot
  light gained an **RT-enable toggle** + a **per-light soft Radius** (`core_math::scene_graph::LightRtShadow { enabled, radius }`
  on `LightData`, `#[serde(skip)]`). The GLOBAL toggle is now the master gate; when on, deferred (both PBR :757 + Lit :522

## ✅ FIXED / ADDED — 2026-07-18f (GTAO + bent normals — the flat IBL-lit surface fix; full doc: docs/planning/render/RENDERER_IBL.md §11)

- ✅ **White cube under a bright HDRI looks FLAT (FLATIBL — owner-observed)** — diffuse IBL
  (`env_sh_irradiance(normal)`) flooded every face with the same SH9 irradiance; the only
  occlusion (SSAO) was a scalar contact-darkening applied uniformly → NO directional occlusion,
  faces never darkened by how much environment they could SEE. FIX: GTAO (horizon-based AO,
  Jimenez 2016) computes an AO factor AND a **bent normal** (average unoccluded direction);
  deferred diffuse IBL now samples `env_sh_irradiance(bent_normal)` → real directional self-
  shading from the environment. Bent normal packed octahedral into the spare b,a of the existing
  binding-38 half-res texture (zero new G-buffer target / deferred binding / BGL churn); b=a=0
  sentinel → deferred falls back to the geometric normal (SSAO/off unchanged). Plus Jimenez
  multi-bounce on the diffuse ambient + roughness/N·V specular occlusion on the specular IBL.
  SSAO kept as a cheaper tier (shares module/resources/output; `AoMode` selects pipelines).
  Panel: AO checkbox + GTAO/SSAO quality radio (`use_gtao`, runtime-only, default GTAO). 17e
  ambient-only contract intact. Readback (real raster G-buffer, cube-over-floor): open floor AO
  0.990 / bent·Y 0.941; contact AO 0.469 / bent bends away (−0.658 < geo 0.000); two faces
  |Δbent| 0.660; deterministic. 0.162 ms @1080p half-res. Gates: app build clean, graphics 50,
  render 35 (+2 GTAO GPU tests), app --bins 240. UNCOMMITTED.

## ✅ FIXED / ADDED — 2026-07-18d (SSR quality pass; full doc: docs/planning/render/RENDERER_IBL.md §7)

- ✅ **SSR energy double-add + full-pixel overwrite (SSRENERGY)** — the composite was
  `mix(hdr, ssr.rgb, mask)`: raw reflected color REPLACED the whole shaded pixel (diffuse, sun
  specular, IBL specular all wiped), the IBL specular stayed underneath at partial mask (energy
  double-count), and it ran AFTER fog (reflections pasted over fog, invisible to bloom). FIX:
  pass_ssr outputs an energy-conserving DELTA `envelope × conf × (traced − IBL-specular)` using
  the EXACT deferred split-sum envelope (extracted ENV_BRDF region + LUT binding 39) and the
  EXACT deferred IBL term (extracted ENV region + env buffer binding 21); pass_tonemap adds it
  BEFORE bloom/fog. SSAO never touches it (specular ≠ ambient — 17e contract holds).
- ✅ **SSR world-step banding + soft contacts (SSRDDA)** — 32 × 0.4-unit fixed world steps
  over/undershoot in screen space (banding, missed thin geometry, mushy contacts). FIX:
  screen-space DDA (uniform pixel-space stepping between the projected segment endpoints,
  perspective-correct t interpolation, ≥2px stride, deterministic per-pixel jitter) + 4-iteration
  binary refinement at the crossing + adaptive thickness (base + per-step depth advance + 1% depth).
- ✅ **SSR hard cutoffs (SSRCUTOFF)** — hard gates `roughness > 0.6 || metallic < 0.15` (glossy
  dielectric floors got NO reflections) and a linear edge fade. FIX: envelope-luminance gate
  (any surface whose split-sum envelope carries energy marches — glossy dielectrics included),
  smooth roughness fade 0.45→0.7 (IBL takes over), smoothstep screen-border fade on the HIT uv,
  backface rejection (dot(sample_n, R) < 0 — also structurally kills self-hits), toward-camera
  fade, opacity-scaled confidence (transparent pixels no longer over-subtract).
- ✅ **SSR ignored roughness in the resolve (SSRBLUR)** — mirror-sharp reflections at every
  roughness. FIX: 4-tap cone blur around the refined hit, radius ∝ roughness × marched pixel
  distance (jittered by a deterministic per-pixel hash — no temporal noise, readback-proven
  deterministic).
- ✅ **Stale SSR composited over path tracing (SSRPTSTALE)** — post_flags bit 2 was set from
  `ssr_enabled` alone; in PT mode the SSR pass never dispatches, so tonemap composited a STALE
  ssr texture over the PT accumulation. FIX: bit 2 excluded when shading_mode == PathTrace.
- ✅ **post_process GpuUniforms copy silently truncated (PPUNIFORMLAYOUT)** — the module's local
  GpuUniforms copy skipped the LOD (512–575) and atlas (576–591) blocks, so any field appended
  after wp_color read the WRONG bytes (found live: ssr_intensity read foveated_enabled == 0 →
  all-zero SSR output, no validation error anywhere). FIX: copy completed to the full 624-byte
  layout + a structural guard in `validate_post_process_shader` (Naga-reflected WGSL struct span
  must equal `size_of::<GpuUniforms>()`) so a missing/extra field block fails the test suite.
- ➕ **SSR controls** — render panel: SSR Quality (16–96 DDA steps, uniform `ssr_max_steps`) +
  SSR Intensity (0–1, `ssr_intensity`). Runtime-only (save-format red line, env_rotation
  precedent). GpuUniforms 608 → 624 (appended tail; all other WGSL copies remain valid prefixes).
- ➕ **SSR headless readback proof** (`graphics/src/ssr_gpu_test.rs`, production module +
  mirrored production ssr_bgl wiring): red cube on a mirror floor — 93.5% of CPU-mirror-oracle
  pixels get confidence > 0 with red-dominant color, 0 false-confidence on 30,834 sky-floor
  pixels, background exactly vec4(0), delta non-negative with env off, byte-identical across
  dispatches. Perf: 0.18 ms/dispatch wall-clock at 1920×1080 / 48 steps on the RTX 4090 —
  full-res fits the ≤1.5 ms budget with ~8× headroom (no half-res needed).

## ✅ FIXED / ADDED — 2026-07-17 (poly modifier stack: the UI-lie — 5 of 8 modifiers silently dropped)

- ✅ **Array / Triangulate / Smooth / Decimate / Bevel poly modifiers silently no-op'd (the UI lied).**
  `apply_poly_modifiers` (`app/src/poly/mesh_sync.rs`) handled only Mirror/Subdivide/Solidify then
  `_ => {}` — so the other five `PolyModifierType` arms did NOTHING, even though `properties_poly.rs`
  ships selectable controls (count/offset/iterations/factor/angle/width/segments) for all of them and

  at all, with no signal to the user.

  - **Array** = Blender Array modifier (constant_offset_displace, no merge): `array_count` copies of the
    running stack result, copy i translated by `i * array_offset` (LOCAL units), concatenated via the
    shared `merge_meshes` + `transformed` (poly/boolean.rs). Blender-oracle IDENTITY on the size-2 cube
    count=3 offset (2,0,0): 24 verts / 18 faces, no weld — AZRA matches (from_polygons does not weld by
    position, so the seam duplicates are preserved exactly like Blender's merge-off default).
  - **Triangulate** = Blender Triangulate modifier: new `core_math::poly_mesh::triangulate_mesh` routes

## ✅ FIXED / ADDED — 2026-07-17 (feat: 3 Blender edit-mode ops + a split_face_between corruption fix)

- ✅ **`split_face_between` bowtied any INTERIOR face (real corruption bug).** The canonical face-split
  (`core_math::half_edge::split_face_between`, used by the knife and the new vert-connect) did
  `delete_face(f) + create_face ×2`, relying on `create_face`'s `vertex_fan`-based twin auto-pairing to
  re-link the freed boundary half-edges to the neighbours. On a face that SHARES an edge with another face
  the re-pair silently failed → the shared edge's twin was dropped → `is_manifold()` "2 disjoint fans
  (bowtie)". Reproduced on a 1×2 quad grid: a single diagonal split of one quad bowtied the shared vertex.
  **Fix:** rewrote it as a true ID-preserving Euler split — insert ONE diagonal half-edge pair, REUSE every
  existing boundary half-edge in place (twins to neighbours never touched), reuse `f` for one half + a new
  face for the other, both inheriting `material_id`. All knife stress tests stay green (they were passing on
  cuts that happened to dodge the fragile path); the new interior split now passes `validate()`+`is_manifold()`.
- ✅ **Poke Faces (Blender `bpy.ops.mesh.poke`).** Fan each selected face into a triangle fan from a new
  center vertex at Blender's DEFAULT `MEDIAN_WEIGHTED` center (each vertex weighted by its two incident edge
  lengths). Task premise said "bounds center" — **oracle-falsified**: a triangle centres at (0,0,-0.309017)
  not the centroid (0,0,-0.333), an irregular quad at (2.154508,0,0.523545) not (2.125,0,0.5); matched
  Blender exactly. `offset` pushes the center along the unit face normal. Kernel `poke_faces` +
  `PolyEdit::PokeFaces` + `poly_poke_faces` (Face mode, menu-only).
- ✅ **Connect Vertex Path (Blender `bpy.ops.mesh.vert_connect_path`, J).** Walk ordered verts, split each
  consecutive pair's shared face (the fixed `split_face_between`). Kernel `connect_vertices` +
  `connect_path_order` (reconstructs a walk from shared-face adjacency, since `PolySelection` is an unordered
  `HashSet`) + `PolyEdit::ConnectVertexPath` + `poly_connect_vertices` (Vertex mode). Keybind `ACT_POLY_CONNECT`
  = J, cleanly context-split from `ACT_CREATE_JOIN` (J) — the two dispatch in mutually-exclusive frame
  branches (`is_create()` vs poly normal-keyboard).
- ✅ **To Sphere (Blender `bpy.ops.transform.tosphere`).** Push each selected vertex toward a sphere
  (center = mean, radius = mean distance) by factor (default 1.0). Task formula confirmed exactly by oracle.
  Kernel `to_sphere` + `PolyEdit::ToSphere` + `poly_to_sphere` (Vertex mode, menu-only — Blender's Shift+Alt+S
  needs a modifier combo the keybind editor doesn't expose yet).
- **Gating:** Blender 4.5.1 headless oracles (`poke_ref.py`/`connect_ref.py`/`tosphere_ref.py`), matched by
  vertex identity (position multiset ± 1e-4) + face count. 15 new `core_math` tests; 537 lib GREEN (was 522),
  all knife stress suites GREEN, `cargo build -p app` clean. bincode: all 3 `PolyEdit` variants APPENDED at
  the enum END; no `HalfEdgeMesh` serialized-shape change.

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-17 (BUG: "bevel doesn't work when we have an open face")

- ✅ **Open-face bevel — the install guard wrongly rejected valid open-mesh bevels.** Owner report: bevel
  does nothing on a body with an open face. Two distinct findings (full write-up: `docs/planning/poly/BEVEL.md`
  §6 #25/#26, §8, §11):
  - **Boundary (open-face) edges are NOT beveled — and that is Blender-correct (NOT a bug).** Exhaustive
    Blender oracle (`docs/planning/poly/boundary_bevel_matrix.py`, **4.5 LTS + 5.0 agree**): a boundary-edge
    edge-bevel is IDENTITY (op FINISHED, no change) for a flat quad, a 3D open-box rim, the rim loop, and a
    hex-fan, across every offset type + seg 1/3; the raw `bmesh.ops.bevel` on a lone boundary edge CRASHES
    Blender. AZRA's STEP-0 skip already matches this. The task premise ("Blender bevels boundary edges") was
    oracle-falsified → documented as a dead-end, kept the skip. A pure-boundary selection now fires an honest
    toast so the no-op isn't silent.
  - **THE REAL BUG: `poly_bevel_regenerate`'s install guard used boundary EDGE count.** AZRA already bevels
    an INTERIOR edge of an OPEN mesh vertex-for-vertex to Blender (open box interior edge: seg1 nv=10/nf=6,
    seg3 nv=14/nf=8, 0.000000 vs oracle). But that legitimately reshapes the open rim → boundary EDGE count
    grows (4→5 / 4→7), and the old guard `manifold && boundary_edges <= orig` REJECTED it → "nothing happens
    on open faces." **Fix:** new pure/tested `core_math::bevel_op::bevel_result_installable(orig,new)` =
    `is_manifold()` (accepts clean OPEN meshes; stronger than the old `validate()` — catches non-manifold/
    bowtie tears) **AND `boundary_loop_count` not increased** (a tear opens a NEW hole = a new loop; a
    faithful open bevel keeps the loop count, only the edge count moves). Closed meshes unchanged (loops 0 ⇔
    0 boundary edges — no regression).
  - **Tests (`core_math`):** `boundary_edge_bevel_matches_blender_identity` (the 3 task cases = Blender
    identity), `interior_edge_on_open_mesh_matches_blender` (open-face fix lock, vertex-exact + loop-preserved),
    `bevel_install_guard_open_and_closed` (accepts closed+open, rejects synthetic tears), `boundary_loop_count_counts_holes`.
    58 bevel gates + 522 core_math lib GREEN, zero regression; `cargo build -p app` clean.

  with the stale maps still rendered. FIX (two structural pieces): (1) `ShadowUniforms.flags.x`
  = sun_enabled, derived from the SCENE GRAPH every frame (visible Directional exists) —
  `compute_shadow()` returns 1.0 without sampling when 0, cascade passes skipped; deletion,
  undo, visibility-toggle, load all covered with no event plumbing. (2) Raster pixels' baked
  factor is DIRECTIONAL SHADOW, not AO — deferred no longer multiplies ambient/IBL by it

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-17 (owner report: "PBR viewport surface is always black maybe because I don't have any material input" + analytical-material cleanup)

- ✅ **PBRBLACK — PBR viewport shaded every raster surface black (SDF worst-hit since the 2026-07-14
  analytical deletion made SDF raster-only).** ROOT CAUSE was the SHADOW MAP, not materials:
  `render/src/shadows.rs` passed raw light-view z coords (negative) as glam `orthographic_rh` near/far
  (which expects positive distances along -Z) → every caster/receiver mapped to NDC depth ≈2.6–3.6,
  casters clipped, receiver refs failed `LessEqual` vs cleared 1.0 → `compute_shadow()`=0 baked into
  gbuf_material.z → deferred PBR/Lit multiplied direct light AND ambient by 0 → black. Solid survived
  via its 0.55 floor (why "only PBR" looked broken). FIX: pure `compute_cascade_vps()` extraction +
  correct `(-max_ls.z, -min_ls.z)` near/far + near-expansion toward the light; regression test
  `cascade_depth_maps_into_unit_range` (render) proven to fail on the old code. Likely also the real
  driver behind VXSOLID's leftover "dark in PBR" and stale GEOBLACK-class reports.
- ✅ **SHADOWACNE — after PBRBLACK's cascade fix, shadows resolved but showed jagged sawtooth dark
  blobs creeping across lit faces (self-shadow acne + texel crawl) — 2026-07-17.** ROOT CAUSE (with
  numbers): the receiver anti-acne bias in `gbuffer.wgsl` was a FIXED `+ n * 0.03` world offset, tuned
  while `compute_shadow()` returned 0 everywhere (any bias "passed"). With `far = max(dist·20, 500)`
  the AABB-fit cascades have texel world-sizes ≈0.06 / 0.22 / 0.73 (c0/c1/c2, 1024² maps) — 0.03 is
  only 0.5 / 0.14 / 0.04 texels → massive acne; and the ortho box was refit to the light-space AABB
  every frame with no snapping → texel grid crawled under camera motion (the sawtooth). FIX
  (`render/src/shadows.rs` + `gbuffer.wgsl`): sphere-fit cascade extents (radius invariant under all
  rigid camera motion — texel size no longer pumps while orbiting), radius quantized (1/16 step) +
  slice center snapped to whole texels in the light rotation frame (sub-texel camera move → bit-
  identical cascade matrix, test-proven), per-cascade `texel_world` exported in `ShadowUniforms`, and
  the shader bias is now ADAPTIVE: `NORMAL_OFFSET_TEXELS (1.5) × texel_world[cascade]` (derived: 0.5
  texel PCF footprint + 1 texel caster depth quantization; slope handled by the existing hardware
  slope-scale bias on the shadow pipeline). Depth window now analytic (near −r, far 50+r — same
  50-unit caster headroom, D32F). Tests: `texel_world_size_sane`, `texel_snapping_is_stable` +
  existing `cascade_depth_maps_into_unit_range` all green (render 23/23).
- ✅ **SHADOWACNE-3 (2026-07-17c) — the residual smooth dark blob (object's own silhouette projected
  along the light dir, hugging the top-left corner) after the two fixes above: the LIGHT FRAME WAS
  UPSIDE-DOWN.** `LightConfig::direction()` returns the direction TOWARD the sun (el=55 → y=+0.82, up);
  `compute_cascade_vps` treated its parameter as the propagation direction (`eye = center − dir·50`) →

  underside. The 2 prior fixes' unit tests hand-wrote downward vectors, which is why they stayed green.

    with NO `sel_bit`, so the rim never runs for poly. Poly relies on the wireframe (Edit) + the CPU
    silhouette outline (Object). `SdfBody` (189/196) and `NurbsBody` (347) KEEP `sel_bit` — they have no
    wireframe and need the rim.
  - **Feature Dependency Audit — `sel_bit` proven rim-only (P0 selection safe).** `sel_bit` (material_idx
    bit 31) is DECODED only at `render/src/gbuffer.wgsl:394` into the flags channel; the material lookup
    (`gbuffer.wgsl:280`) MASKS it off (`& 0x3FFFFFFFu`) so it never affects shading; the deferred shader
    consumes the flag at EXACTLY one site — the rim (`deferred_entry.wgsl:660`). Click-to-select uses a
    SEPARATE picking pass (`app/src/raster_pick.rs`) that renders with `material_idx = node_id_u32`
    (lines 190/204/222) and reads the NodeId back — it never reads `sel_bit`. Dropping `sel_bit` for
    poly cannot break picking. Verified by reading the full picking path.
  - **Path B — CPU silhouette classification (Object mode).** `draw_node_selection_outlines`
    (`app/src/draw_selection.rs`) draws true silhouette EDGES for a poly body. The old test classified
    each adjacent face by the raw SIGN of `normal · toward-camera` (`> 0.0`) with ZERO dead-band. When
    the whole surface turns edge-on, a WIDE band of near-tangent faces all have facing ≈ 0; their signs
    flip on float noise → a huge region of edges all read as silhouette → the thick flaring band. **FIX
    (classification, NOT stroke width):** `face_front` now returns the SIGNED facing dot; an interior
    edge is a silhouette only when its two faces are DECISIVELY opposite — opposite sign AND
    `max(|facing_a|,|facing_b|) > 0.15` (~cos 81°). In a pure edge-on band both faces are within the
    dead-band → not silhouette → no flare. Genuine profile edges always have at least one solidly
    front/back neighbour → stable thin outline. Boundary edges (one face) are ALWAYS drawn — unchanged.
  - **Build:** `cargo build -p app` green (no shader/core_math change → no `cargo test -p graphics`/
    `core_math` needed; the deferred rim shader was NOT touched, only the CPU instance flag). No LNK1104.
  - **What the owner should now SEE:** Edit mode — poly shows the wireframe only, no rim, at every angle.
    Object mode — a selected poly shows a thin silhouette outline that STAYS thin and does not balloon
    when the surface turns edge-on. SDF/Nurbs selection rim is unchanged. Click-to-select still works.

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-16 (user report #4: "face subdivide does not work — nothing happens, no message")

- ✅ **BOTH `SubdivideFaces` (Ctrl+D, faces selected → linear) and `SubdivideCatmullClark` (nothing
  selected → smooth) were SILENTLY REFUSED by the app.** The menu/key path was fully wired
  (`menus.rs` Ctrl+D + context menu → `AppCommand::PolySubdivide` → `poly_subdivide` → `poly_op_batch`
  → `PolyEdit::…apply_in_place`). ROOT CAUSE (proven through the exact app path): `apply_in_place`
  (`mesh_ops/mod.rs:564`) runs the full `is_manifold()` integrity gate for snapshot-tier ops, and BOTH
  subdivide ops produced **NON-MANIFOLD** meshes, so `compute()` returned `Err(InvalidResult{"…bowtie"})`
  and the whole op was rolled back — no geometry change, no toast. The existing `subdivide.rs` unit
  tests stayed GREEN because they only called `validate()` (next/prev/twin) + `face_count`, NEVER
  `is_manifold()` — "tests pass, app refuses."
  - **Bug A — linear (`half_edge.rs::subdivide_faces`)**: re-tessellated only the SELECTED faces and kept
    unselected neighbours AS-IS. A boundary edge shared with an unselected neighbour got a midpoint on the
    subdivided side while the neighbour still spanned the full original edge → T-junction → bowtie. FIX:
    two-pass — pass 1 creates the midpoint for every edge of every selected face; pass 2 emits selected
    faces as center+N-quads AND inserts each split-edge midpoint into the unselected neighbour's vertex
    ring (neighbour → n-gon), so the mesh stays closed + manifold. This is the "Phase 5" T31537 fix the
    file's own SCOPE-GUARD comment deferred.
  - **Bug B — Catmull-Clark (`half_edge.rs::subdivide_catmull_clark`)**: the sub-quad assembly used the
    half-edge's DESTINATION vertex (`he(he_id).vertex`) while pairing it with the prev+cur edge points —
    which are the two edges incident to the SOURCE, not the destination. So each new vertex was joined to
    an edge point that does not touch it; shared-edge half-edges across faces did not line up → bowtie
    even on a plain cube (all-faces, no partial-selection excuse). FIX (one line): the corner vertex is
    the half-edge SOURCE (`he_source(he_id)`); both edge points then correctly touch it. CC of a cube is
    now manifold (26 verts: 8 corner v3 + 12 edge v4 + 6 face).
  - **Blender-oracle gated by VERTEX IDENTITY** (`bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges(use_grid_fill=True)` on a ±1
    cube). AZRA linear matches Blender's vertex multiset EXACTLY for single-face (13v), 2-adjacent (17v),
    L-shape/corner-triad (20v), and all-faces (26v, 24 quads). Blender additionally TRIANGULATES neighbours
    that get ≥2 adjacent cuts; AZRA keeps them as manifold n-gons — same vertices, different tessellation,
    both closed+manifold. CC: AZRA uses the TEXTBOOK Catmull-Clark stencils (corners ±5/9, edge points ±3/4,
    face points ±1); Blender/OpenSubdiv pulls further in (±0.5 / ±0.6096 / ±0.8395) via limit-converging
    weights. Both are valid manifold CC surfaces; the task's prose ("±7/9, face points at face centers")
    matched NEITHER. OpenSubdiv-exact CC weights are a **separate follow-up** (position-only; connectivity
    is now correct). This corrects the earlier note (see the Ctrl+X entry) that "subdivide-via-menu is a
    DIFFERENT path still to be diagnosed" — it is now diagnosed and fixed.
  - **Regression guard = REAL app path** (`mesh_ops/subdivide.rs` `apply_path_tests`): 6 tests via
    `PolyEdit::…apply_in_place`, each asserting `Ok(_)` + `is_manifold()` + vertex-identity vs the Blender
    oracle (linear: single/2-adjacent/L/all; CC: cube positions + a NON-cube irregular case proving CC is
    not cube-special-cased). RED-verified on base `65eb0905` (all 5 fail `InvalidResult{"…bowtie"}`, the

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-16 (`he_source` orphan-warning spam across the WHOLE delete/dissolve family)

- ✅ **Repeating `[WARN] he_source: no valid prev or twin for he HalfEdgeId(N)` during EVERY
  dissolve/delete action** (owner-reported; HalfEdgeId 13/19). Root cause was NOT a kernel loop-splice
  bug — the live relink already matches Blender `bmesh_kernel_join_face_kill_edge`. It was a **freed-slot
  dereference**, two-fold: (1) freed half-edge slots left in INCONSISTENT states — `dissolve_edge` zeroed
  next/prev/twin but `delete_face` / `delete_edge` / `collapse_self_loops` nulled only face+twin and left
  next/prev DANGLING at other freed ring members, so a dead slot was still walkable as if live; (2)
  consumers iterating `0..half_edges.len()` (`overlay_lines.rs:135` wire draw, `draw_selection.rs:304`
  silhouette) and stale selected/hovered ids (`draw_poly.rs:242/254`) called `he_source` on those dead
  slots every frame, hitting its no-prev/no-twin warn branch. `validate()`/`is_manifold()` never warned
  (both skip `free_edges`), so the mesh round-tripped — "sort of works but very buggy/noisy."
  FIX (class, not instance — mirrors the `free_face` chokepoint precedent above): **`free_edge(he)`** — the
  single edge-side chokepoint; zeroes the slot to ONE canonical dead state, idempotent. EVERY
  `free_edges.push` now routes through it (`delete_face`, `delete_edge`, `collapse_self_loops`,
  `dissolve_edge`) — grep-verified exactly one `free_edges.push` in the crate, inside `free_edge`.
  **`is_edge_live(he)`** — the canonical live predicate (`free_edges` is private; consumers could not check
  it). `he_source` now recognizes a freed/OOB slot and returns `VertexId(0)` SILENTLY; the warning fires
  ONLY for a genuine LIVE orphan (a real relink bug) — it means something again. `overlay_lines`,
  `draw_selection`, `draw_poly` skip non-live edges (no garbage origin lines from dead slots). This is
  Blender's "iterate LIVE pools only, freed elements unreachable by construction" guarantee, structural.
  Tests (RED verified — pre-fix `delete_face` → `freed he 0 has dangling prev HalfEdgeId(3)`):
  `freed_slots_canonical_after_delete_dissolve_family`, `zero_live_orphans_after_delete_dissolve_family`,
  `is_edge_live_recognizes_freed_slots`. Oracle-identity gate (Blender 4.5 `dd_family_ref.json`):
  `dissolve_delete_family_matches_blender_oracle_counts` + `dissolve_vertex_merged_ngon_by_identity` —
  dissolve/delete vert/edge/face + region all match Blender by (v, undirected-e, f) and by vertex identity.
  Also closed the audit's **gate asymmetry**: `local_rebuild_ops.rs::run_snapshot` now gates on
  `is_manifold()` (not just `validate()`), so the DissolveEdgeOp/DissolveFaceOp/DeleteFaceOp MeshOp path
  can't commit a validate()-passing-but-non-manifold pinch. Gates: `cargo test -p core_math` 488 passed /
  0 failed / 6 ignored; `cargo build -p app` clean. Red line held: zero change to `HalfEdgeMesh`
  serialized shape (the fix needs no new state).

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-16 (`delete_face` could double-free a face slot; no gate could see it)

- ✅ **`delete_face` FREED A FACE SLOT WITHOUT CHECKING IT WAS ALREADY FREE.**
  `half_edge.rs::delete_face` ran its detach loops and then pushed `f.0` onto `free_faces`
  unconditionally. Called twice on the same face it double-pushed the slot: `face_half_edges()` /
  `face_vertices()` both return empty for a freed face (`:401`, `:418` — `half_edge == NO_EDGE`), so
  the loops became silent no-ops but the push still landed. `alloc_face` (`:216`) pops the free list
  with **no dedup**, so the duplicated slot was then handed to two separate `create_face()` calls =>
  **two live faces sharing one FaceId, silently**. Its sibling `dissolve_face` has always opened with
  the corresponding self-guard (`if self.face(fid).half_edge == NO_EDGE { return; }`) — the asymmetry
  was the whole bug.
  **Worse than the `dissolve_edge` slit fixed the day before (`4014d60`): NO gate anywhere catches
  it.** `validate()` only walks next/prev/twin round-trips and `is_manifold()` only checks live-face
  invariants — a duplicated *free-list* entry violates neither, so the corruption ships silently past
  the boolean/undo-snapshot gates that `is_manifold()` guards.
  **Latent, not live — stated honestly:** all 10 current call sites are safe today, 6 by an explicit
  `if face(f).half_edge != NO_EDGE` check (`:1313`, `:1328`, `:1329`, `:1257`, `:2224`,
  `mesh_ops/mod.rs:467` + `local_rebuild_ops.rs:164`) and 4 by construction (`:831`, `:1537`, `:1790`,
  `:2486` — deduped index filters). No user-reachable repro exists on today's code. It survived purely
  on **external discipline**, which CLAUDE.md forbids ("No Bandaids" Q3 — *"Will the next dev need
  tribal knowledge to avoid breaking it? If yes, the fix is wrong — enforce correctness
  structurally"*). That the guard at `:1329` is already load-bearing proves the trap is live: on a slit
  edge `f1 == f2`, and only that check stops `delete_edge` from double-freeing one face today.
  FIX (class, not instance): a private **`free_face(fid) -> bool` chokepoint** next to `alloc_face`,
  idempotent by construction (refuses a slot already on the list). **All three** `free_faces` writers
  now route through it — `delete_face` (`:1305`), `dissolve_edge` (`:2134`), `dissolve_face`
  (`:2166`) — leaving exactly ONE `free_faces.push` in the crate (grep-verified, inside `free_face`
  itself). No future op can double-push, because there is no other way to push. `delete_face` also
  early-returns on an already-free slot, which is what keeps a redundant delete byte-identical rather
  than merely harmless. Chosen over mirroring `dissolve_face`'s per-site guard because the free-list
  push is the real chokepoint. **The count that decided it: of the 14 free-list pushes in the file
  pre-fix, 9 already carried a dedup guard and only 5 were raw — and 7 of those 9 hand-roll a literal
  `free_X.contains(..)` check** (`:1206`, `:1251`, `:1317`, `:1335`, `:1344`, `:2234`, `:2258`; the
  other 2 — `:2109`, `:2142` — lean on an upstream invariant instead). A guard that 9 of 14 sites
  independently re-derive is the architecture asking for it to live at the push, not at every call
  site. Post-fix the file has 12 pushes, exactly one of them `free_faces`.
  Test `delete_face_double_free_never_duplicates_a_slot` (`half_edge.rs`) proven **RED** on unfixed
  code (`free_faces double-pushed slot 0: [0, 0]`) then GREEN: asserts no duplicate slot, that the
  redundant delete is a total no-op, and that two `create_face()` calls return distinct FaceIds.
  Gates: `cargo test -p core_math` 483 passed / 0 failed / 6 ignored; `cargo build -p app` clean.
  Red line held: zero change to `HalfEdgeMesh`'s serialized shape (no new/retyped/reordered field —
  the fix needs no new state).

- ⬜ **`free_verts` still has no chokepoint.** `free_verts.push` at `merge_vertices` (`:1183`) is still raw

  (`:194`) pops with no dedup, so a duplicated slot yields two live vertices sharing one id. Fix =
  `free_vert()` chokepoint mirroring `free_face()`/`free_edge()`. Deferred: `merge_vertices` is tracked
  separately.

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-16 (a rebind to any of 51 keys was silently lost on restart)

- ✅ **REBINDING AN ACTION TO A KEY WITH NO DISPLAY GLYPH LOST THE BIND ON RESTART.**
  `keybindings.rs` carried TWO hand-maintained key tables: `key_display` (`:12`, `Key -> str`)
  ending in `_ => "?"`, and `key_from_str` (`:28`, `str -> Key`) ending in `_ => return None`.
  `to_json` (`:71`) built the PERSISTED spelling by calling `key_display` — a **display**
  function — so any key absent from the tables was written to `~/.azra/keybinds.json` as the
  literal `"?"`, which `key_from_str` could not read back. Rebind → save → restart → the bind was
  gone, with no error. **Exactly 51 of egui 0.29.1's 104 keys** were affected (measured, not
  estimated): `Insert`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Copy`, `Cut`, `Paste`, all 15 punctuation keys
  (`Plus`, `Minus`, `Equals`, `Comma`, `Period`, `Colon`, `Semicolon`, `Quote`, `Backtick`,
  `Backslash`, `Slash`, `Pipe`, `Questionmark`, `OpenBracket`, `CloseBracket`), and `F6`–`F35`.
  Every one is reachable by a real user: the rebind editor (`input_keyboard.rs:77`) accepts
  **whatever key `Event::Key` carries**, with no filter against the tables, and `set()`+`save()`
  accept it happily.
  **SEVERITY — deliberately NOT inflated.** This costs ONE preference, not data. It is priority
  rung 3 (a save/load regression), not rung 1. An early framing of this bug claimed the SHIPPED
  defaults `ACT_POLY_GROW_SEL => ctrl(Plus)` / `ACT_POLY_SHRINK_SEL => ctrl(Minus)` (`:436-437`)
  were being lost — **that was wrong and is recorded here so it is not re-derived**: `save()`
  (`:508`) only writes binds where `*current != dflt`, so defaults never reach the serializer and
  survive by never being written. Their "Ctrl+?" in the Shortcut Editor was purely cosmetic (the
  editor renders via `key_display`). Both halves verified.
  **ROOT CAUSE was not the missing entries** — adding `Plus`/`Minus`/`F6`-`F12` to both tables
  would have fixed today and left the next key to rot. The cause was (a) persistence being derived
  from a *display* function, and (b) two hand-maintained tables free to disagree. Worth noting the
  sentinel was **ambiguous, not merely lossy**: `Insert` and `PageUp` both spelled `"?"`, so the
  tempting "just add `"?" => Questionmark` to the parser" would have silently loaded all 51 back as
  the **wrong** key — strictly worse than dropping them.
  FIX: ONE table, two derived views. `KEY_ALIASES` (`:50`) is now the only hand-maintained key
  table (7 entries — AZRA's compact labels `Esc`/`Del`/`Bksp`/arrows, which are also the v2 on-disk
  spellings). `key_name` (`:62`) is the persisted spelling and delegates to egui's `Key::name()`,
  which is **total** (exhaustive match over `Key`, no fallback) and whose exact inverse is
  `Key::from_name()` — so an unspellable key is now *structurally impossible*, not caught at
  runtime; there is no sentinel left to emit. `key_display` (`:67`) is presentation-only and never
  reaches disk. `key_from_str` (`:76`) accepts an alias, else defers to `Key::from_name`. Display
  and parse now read the SAME table and share the SAME total fallback, so they cannot drift.
  A compile-time exhaustive match over `egui::Key` was considered and **rejected**: `Key` is not
  `#[non_exhaustive]` so it is *feasible*, but it would duplicate egui's own `name()` in 104 arms
  for zero benefit once the total fallback exists.
  **SAVE-FORMAT SAFETY:** `keybinds.json` is `serde_json`, not bincode (confirmed — `:517`
  `serde_json::to_string_pretty`), so the bincode append-only rule does not apply. Existing files
  still load: the v2 spellings that `Key::from_name` does NOT know (`Del`, `Bksp`, and the four
  `\u{2190}`-family arrows — egui uses `\u{23F6}`-family symbols and the long names) are exactly
  the `KEY_ALIASES` entries, which the parser tries FIRST. Proven by two tests that pass
  **identically on pre- and post-fix code**. `"version"` bumped 2 → 3 (`:563`) to record that the
  on-disk vocabulary changed; confirmed by grep that **nothing has ever read it back** (only
  occurrence is the write), and `load()` stays deliberately version-AGNOSTIC — it accepts both
  vocabularies unconditionally, which is more robust than branching on a number a hand-edited file
  could get wrong. Bump is a signal for a future migration, not a branch.
  **SUB-BUG CAUGHT DURING THE FIX — the fix itself nearly shipped a worse bug.** Deferring to
  `Key::from_name` blindly resurrects corruption: egui maps `"?"` → `Key::Questionmark`
  (`egui-0.29.1/src/data/key.rs:343`). Existing `keybinds.json` files written by the buggy build
  contain `"key": "?"` for whichever of the 51 keys the user picked, so those records would have
  silently loaded as a **Questionmark** bind — the wrong key, strictly worse than the drop users
  already lived with, and the exact failure mode this fix exists to prevent. `key_from_str` (`:76`)
  now rejects the bare `V2_LOSSY_SENTINEL` before any fallback, so a corrupt record drops to the
  action's default exactly as before. A genuine Questionmark bind is unaffected — it persists via
  `key_name` as `"Questionmark"`, a string the old writer could never emit, so a bare `"?"` on disk
  is unambiguously the sentinel. Proven RED first (`left: Some(Questionmark)`, right: `None`).
  **KNOWN, ACCEPTED:** new files spell keys canonically (`"Escape"`, not `"Esc"`), so an OLDER AZRA
  build reading a NEWER `keybinds.json` drops non-default binds on keys whose canonical name it
  lacks. Downgrade-only; costs one preference; the v3 marker records it.
  GATE: `cargo build -p app` green. `cargo test -p app_types` 11/11. 7 new tests proven RED on the
  unfixed source first (verbatim: `51 of 104 keys are lost on save/reload`,
  `rebinding grab to Insert is lost on restart`, `Insert and PageUp both spell as "?"`,
  `poly_grow_sel labels as "Ctrl+?"`) then GREEN. The round-trip tests iterate `egui::Key::ALL`
  rather than a hand-listed set, so a key added by a future egui upgrade is covered with no edit
  here — that is the ratchet against this class returning.
  MANUAL: Shortcut Editor (`End`) → rebind any action to `F6` → restart → bind is still `F6`
  (previously silently reverted to default). Grow/Shrink Selection now read `Ctrl+Plus` /
  `Ctrl+Minus` instead of `Ctrl+?`.

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-16 (poly op refusals were invisible, and partial batches lied)

- ✅ **A REFUSED POLY OP TOASTED SUCCESS AND THREW AWAY THE SELECTION.** `poly_op_batch`
  (`app/src/undo.rs:384`) returned a bare `bool` — `true` if **≥1** op applied — and dropped every
  `OpError` on the floor at `if let Ok(inv) = op.apply_in_place(m)` (`:397`). `OpError` has a
  `Display` impl (`core_math/src/mesh_ops/mod.rs:62`) and appeared **nowhere** in `app/src`
  (grep-confirmed: 0 occurrences). So a caller could not distinguish "all 5 dissolved" from "1 of 5
  dissolved", and all 13 sites did the same thing: toast unconditional success + clear the WHOLE
  sub-element selection — discarding the selection of elements that were never touched, so the user
  could not see or retry them. Repro (cube → 3 corner edges → Ctrl+X): mesh unchanged, toast said
  "Edges dissolved", selection gone. Commit `1d1fa56` (atomic `apply_in_place`) fixed the
  corruption and RAISED this bug's urgency — a refusal now leaves the mesh byte-identical, so the
  app confidently reported success for a provable no-op.
  FIX: `poly_op_batch`/`poly_op` return `PolyOpOutcome` (`app/src/poly/outcome.rs`) carrying the
  **refused ops themselves** + their `OpError`s — not a count. `PolyEdit::targets()`
  (`core_math/src/mesh_ops/mod.rs`) maps a refused op back to its exact element ids (valid across a
  refusal precisely because `apply_in_place` is atomic), so retention needs no positional zip
  against the caller's six different sort orders. ONE shared reporter, `poly_report_batch()`, does
  BOTH halves — honest message AND selection retention — so no caller can do one and forget the
  other; there is exactly one message builder, never a copy per site. `#[must_use]` on the outcome
  makes ignoring a refusal a compile warning (`extrude.rs:37` dropped the bool silently). All 13
  sites migrated. Counts are in ELEMENTS, not ops: a region op (`DissolveFaces{faces}`) covers N
  faces through one op, so counting ops would have reported "1 face dissolved" after dissolving
  five — the same class of lie. Three `targets()` contract tests added (`targets_tests.rs`).
  Blender oracle: our per-op partial model **matches** Blender (verified geometrically — it
  dissolves the applicable edges of a mixed selection and retains exactly the refused one's
  selection), so batch semantics were left alone; only reporting + retention changed.

- ✅ **POLY REDO: A REFUSED STEP STRANDED AN UNDOABLE-PROOF MUTATION.** `undo.rs:271` did
  `Err(e) => { eprintln!("[poly-redo] re-apply failed: {e}; step lost"); ok = false; break; }`.
  Two defects, same swallow class as above: (1) the failure was reported only to **stderr**, which
  no user sees; (2) worse — `ok=false` left `reverse_ops = None`, so the `if let Some(rev)` guard
  skipped and **NO undo entry was pushed**, while every op *before* the `break` had already mutated
  the live mesh. Net: applied mutations with no undo entry to reach them — an orphaned mutation and
  a history desync, not merely a "lost step".
  FIX: skip-and-continue like the forward path (safe for the same reason — atomicity), push the
  entry for whatever applied so every mutation stays Ctrl+Z-reachable, and toast the refusal
  (message half only — the redo path already clears all three poly selections wholesale, so there is
  nothing to retain).

- ✅ **FIXED 2026-07-16 — PARITY: 3 corner edges now SUCCEED (collapse to a tetrahedron), matching
