## ~~✅ FIXED — 2026-07-16 (Path Tracer Phase 0 — REVERTED, see above)~~
- ✅ **PT-B1 "PT mode shows nothing" — the PathTrace dispatch was UNREACHABLE.** `viewport_render.rs`
  hardcoded `unified_raster: true` and `resolve_render_mode`'s unified-raster arm sat ABOVE the
  PathTrace arm, so `RenderMode::PathTrace` could never be returned (deliberate — commit a718110).
  FIX: PathTrace arm moved above the guard. Safe because PT's shader build strips GBUF_BINDINGS —
  PT writes HDR only, never the G-buffer, so the fusion hazard (commit 4f1a30a) the guard exists
  for cannot occur; deferred (the G-buffer consumer) stays gated off in PT mode. The raster pass
  still runs underneath for GPU picking / overlay depth / denoiser normals.
- ✅ **PT-B2 "PT output never reached the screen."** PT set `skip_deferred_pp = true`, which skipped
  tonemap — the SOLE HDR→LDR writer — so the viewport kept displaying a stale LDR frame. FIX:
  `skip_deferred_pp` REMOVED entirely; the bloom→tonemap→FXAA chain now runs for every render mode,
  and the depth-tested overlay-line pass no longer excludes PT.
- ✅ **PT-B5 "accumulation could never exceed 1 frame" (two ends, both broken).** (a) The
  `!self.is_dirty → return` render gate meant PT dispatched once and froze (nothing marks dirty on
  convergence frames); (b) the reset condition `|| self.is_dirty` was ALWAYS true on any frame that
  passed the gate, so `pt_accumulated_frames` reset every dispatch. FIX: gate lets PT frames through
  while `pt_accumulated_frames < PT_MAX_ACCUM_FRAMES` (4096 — bounded, viewport idles once
  converged; repaint chain stops with it); `is_dirty` in the reset now genuinely means "something
  changed" because convergence frames run with it false.
- ✅ **PT-B10 first accumulated frame read the never-cleared accum texture** — `mix(garbage, new,
  1.0)` still evaluates `garbage*0.0`, and NaN/Inf bits in uninitialized memory poison pixels
  permanently (NaN*0=NaN). FIX: shader skips the `textureLoad` entirely when `pt_accumulated <= 1`.
- ✅ **PT-B13 `validate_pt_shader` was parse-only** — the same gap that let a voxel_mesh runtime
  validation crash ship green. FIX: upgraded to full naga validate (all 41 graphics tests pass).
- ✅ **PT-B14 silent no-op when PT pipeline/bind group missing** — FIX: one-shot eprintln.
- 📋 **OPEN (tracked in PATHTRACER_PLAN.md, Phases 1–3):** PT-B3 CRITICAL — PT still intersects
  ONLY analytical SDF prims (blind to DC/poly/voxel/imported triangles; the `nv > 0` gate stays
  until the Phase 2 triangle-BVH intersector lands). PT-B6 shallow 80-step march; PT-B7 material
  desync; PT-B8 `pt_clamp`/`pt_dof_aperture` sliders wired to nothing; PT-B9 denoiser normals;
  PT-B11 non-physical shading hacks; PT-B12 8-light cap.

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-15 (GPU depth-tested edit wireframe)
- ✅ **"I CAN SEE THROUGH THE MESH" — WIREFRAME EDGES BLED THROUGH THE SURFACE.** The shaded
  surface was always correct (the raster pipeline has depth fully enabled and the G-buffer pass
  clears/stores `raster.depth_view`). The defect was the WIREFRAME: `draw_poly.rs` (edit
  wireframe) and `draw_poly_wire.rs` (object overlay) painted flat 2D egui lines with NO depth
  test, faking occlusion with a per-face back-face cull (+ later an O(edges×tris) CPU
  ray-triangle hidden-line clip capped at 250 faces). Both are heuristics standing in for a
  depth test: they only ever asked "does this edge's own face point away?", never "is something
  else in front of it?" — so they could not hide the edges of a far island sitting behind a near
  one, at any face count. `draw_poly_wire.rs` was worse still: its face normal came from the
  FIRST 3 VERTICES, which returns garbage for a concave/knife-cut n-gon.
  FIX: a real GPU line pass (`render/src/line_overlay.rs` + `line_overlay.wgsl`), depth-tested
  (LessEqual, `depth_write_enabled=false`, slope-scaled bias) against the SAME depth buffer the
  raster pass wrote, drawn into the composited LDR texture after tonemap/FXAA and before egui
  presents it. Segments are gathered in `app/src/overlay_lines.rs` (world space — a camera orbit
  now costs ZERO CPU rebuild; the old path re-projected every edge every frame) and uploaded to a
  pooled instance buffer that grows/shrinks like `RasterPipeline.instance_buffer`. Both CPU
  heuristics DELETED (not kept as a fallback — two paths for one operation). Segments are
  expanded to screen-space quads in the VS, because WebGPU has no line-width state and a
  line-list would have silently dropped the 0.5–5.0px thickness sliders. X-Ray drives
  `depth_compare=Always` off the canonical `sel.visible_only` (ONE X-Ray concept for display AND
  picking — see the 2026-07-02 entry), NOT the dead `viewport.xray_mode` flag.
  Selection/hover/vertex-debug overlays deliberately stay flat egui (always-on-top, Blender
  parity). Picking is untouched (`PickingPipeline` owns its own depth texture).
  Verified: headless GPU tests on a real device assert a line behind a nearer surface is occluded,
  the same line in front is drawn, and X-Ray draws it through (`render/src/line_overlay.rs` tests).
  KNOWN GAP: PathTrace render mode gets no GPU wireframe — the tonemap is the sole writer of the
  LDR texture and PT skips it, so blending there would accumulate the lines every frame.

# 📋 BACKLOG — 2026-07-15 (found while building the Circle region op; NOT fixed — scope)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- 📋 **`poly_apply_inset_settled` pushes a no-op UNDO entry when the inset does nothing.**
  `transaction()` (undo.rs:362) snapshots and `history.push(entry)` **unconditionally** — it has no
  notion of "the closure mutated nothing". `poly_apply_inset_settled` (app/src/poly/inset.rs:58) calls
  `transaction(...)` and only THEN reports success via `!inner.is_empty()`. So an inset that legitimately
  does nothing (a selection `inset_region` refuses) still pushes an entry, and the user's next **Ctrl+Z
  silently does nothing** instead of undoing their previous action.
  **Repro:** Face mode → a selection inset_region refuses → `I` → nothing happens → Ctrl+Z → the
  PREVIOUS operation is not undone (the no-op entry is consumed first).
  **Fix shape:** decide BEFORE opening the transaction — dry-run the op on a scratch mesh and commit only
  on success (what `poly/circle.rs::poly_circle_faces` now does), or add a `*_has_candidates()` predicate
  (what `poly_join` does). Cheap either way: `transaction()` already clones the whole scene graph.
  **Same class, other callers:** any op wrapped in `transaction()` that has a legitimate refuse path.
  Worth an audit sweep. Flagged in POLY_POLISH_PLAN §7/§8 (2026-07-15).
- 📋 **Three copies of Newell's method** across the workspace: `half_edge::newell_normal` (now THE rule,
  used by `compute_face_normal` + `circle_region`), `bevel_op::newell_idx` (indices + a positions slice),
  and the app's `poly/fill.rs::best_fit_plane_normal` (adds a collinear-triple fallback). Fold the latter
  two into `newell_normal` when those files are next touched (bevel_op is BEVEL.md-governed; not folded
  now per the CLAUDE.md refactor budget). Flagged in-code with a TODO(dedup).

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-15 (Poly INSET was not Blender's EVEN OFFSET — poly audit #15)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **`inset_face` slid every vertex toward the face CENTROID by `amount`**, which only coincides with
  Blender on a REGULAR polygon. On any non-square face the edge gaps came out UNEVEN and wrong.
  **Blender oracle** (`docs/planning/poly/inset_ref.py` → `inset_ref.json`, Blender 4.5): box
  half-extents (2,1,1), inset the +Y top (4x2 = non-square) with `bpy.ops.mesh.inset(thickness=0.3,
  depth=0.0)` at UI defaults (`use_even_offset=True`) → inner ring **(±1.7, 1.0, ±0.7)** = a uniform
  0.3 gap from every edge. AZRA produced **(±1.7317, 1.0, ±0.8658)** = gaps of 0.268 / 0.134.
- ⚠️ **Why it survived:** `nv=12 nf=10`, watertight, and manifold ALL matched before and after — the
  topology was already correct, only the geometry was wrong. Exactly the POLY_POLISH_PLAN §0.1 trap
  ("watertight+manifold is necessary but NOT sufficient"); only a Blender vertex diff catches it.
- ✅ **Fix:** new `inset_face_depth(f, thickness, depth)` (`inset_face` delegates with depth=0) offsets
  each edge inward along its **in-plane** normal (`normal × (b−a)`) and intersects the two offset lines
  meeting at each vertex: `v' = v + t·(n1+n2)/(1 + dot(n1,n2))`. Winding-invariant; a ≈180° spike vertex
  (denom→0) falls back to a single-edge offset instead of exploding. Topology path unchanged.
- ✅ **Gates:** `inset_face_matches_blender_oracle_even_offset` (vertex-for-vertex + watertight +
  `is_manifold`) and `inset_face_even_offset_uniform_gap_on_irregular_ngon` (uniform-gap property on an
  irregular pentagon). 463 core_math green, 0 regressions, app builds.
- 📋 **REMAINING (poly audit #15, next increment):** the app insets each selected face INDIVIDUALLY, but
  Blender's `I` default is **REGION** inset (interior shared edges of a multi-face selection are not
  inset). Needs `inset_region(faces)` + an Individual toggle + expose `depth`. See POLY_POLISH_PLAN §4 2e.

# ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-14 (Polyline profile POINT HANDLES never show in viewport)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **"The Polyline (CurveExtrude) profile point handles do not show when the primitive is
  selected"** (owner, emphatic 2nd report). Root cause: `curve_edit_prim_index()`
  (`curve_point_edit.rs:32`) gated activation on `work_mode == WorkMode::Object`. But for SDF,
  individual prims are selectable ONLY in the per-prim EDIT mode (`WorkMode::Vertex`) —
  `switch_work_mode(Object)` (`ui_update.rs:254`) clears prim selection and selects the whole
  body Node, so in Object mode `selected_prim_indices_unified().len()` is 0. Worse,
  `add_primitive_immediate` (`creation.rs:129-130`) auto-enters `WorkMode::Vertex` right after
  creating the Polyline. So the Object-only gate could NEVER coincide with a single selected
  prim → `draw_curve_point_overlay` (called unconditionally at `viewport_overlays.rs:480`)
  early-returned every frame. FIX: broadened the gate to activate for a single selected
  CurveExtrude SDF prim in ANY non-sculpt SDF work mode (Object + Vertex/Edge/Face). Extracted
  the decision into the pure, unit-tested `curve_point_editor_active()` predicate; added an
  `AZRA_CURVE_DBG=1` eprintln trace of the gate decision. Shape check preserved (never hijacks
  box/cylinder/gizmo). Note: the box/cylinder bevel handles use the same Object+single-prim gate
  (`viewport_overlays.rs:487`) but stay reachable because bevel is adjusted with the prim clicked
  in Object mode; the curve editor's natural home is edit mode, which the old gate excluded.

    re-armed the settle each time, while trigger_bake's full-bake adaptive recompute (real
    recursive grid bounds) wrote the high res back → resolution ping-pong, never converges,
    surface never re-appears correctly. FIX: LOD sizes bodies from
    `collect_body_prims_recursive` (the SAME set the bake + settle re-tighten use — LOD and
    bake can no longer disagree); a truly empty subtree gets NO tier (skip, not a guess box).
    Test: `lod_uses_recursive_prims_for_grouped_body`.
  - **Root 2 — `pick_warming_candidate` picked NESTED sub-bodies** (warming.rs). A nested
    body never owns a grid (the bake loop skips it), so `has_cache` stays false forever →
    poll_warming ran `mark_body_dirty(sub)` + `clear_debounce()` + `trigger_body_vol_bake()`
    EVERY idle frame from the moment Group.001 existed — the idle pump that re-ran the LOD
    (root 1) each frame and forced `retighten_idle()==true` (the "while IDLE" arms). FIX:
    a warming candidate must be a live TOP-LEVEL SdfBody — enforced inside the picker for
    all three sources (hover / MRU / scan), same nested-scope rule as
    `mark_stale_bodies_dirty` and the bake loop. Test: `warming_never_picks_nested_sub_bodies`.
  Files: `body_volume_cache/mod.rs` (LOD bounds + `settle_quiescent()` test accessor),
  `warming.rs`, tests in `bake_dispatch.rs` + `sdf_gpu_mesh/tests_sparse_bake.rs`.
  Manual test: body with 2+ prims at 1024³ (SparseBricks ON), outliner-drag one prim onto the
  other → Group.001 created → surface must stay visible (re-baked sparse), console must NOT
  spam `[RetightenArm] … while IDLE`, and the resolution picker must stay at 1024.

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-13 (Outliner drop-target VISUALIZATION overhaul — Blender method)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **"Reordering is still very hard / no visualization at the last place inside a sub-body /
  dropping in between is weird"** (owner). Visualization overhaul, semantics untouched:
  every resolved drop slot now carries its INDICATOR GEOMETRY + human LABEL (`DropVisual` in
  app_types, built by the pure slot layer), rendered by ONE painter in outliner_dnd.rs.
  (1) *Depth-indented insertion line*: between-slots draw a line starting at the RECEIVING
  container's indent with a filled circle at its left end (Blender style) — depth is visible.
  (2) *Drop-INTO = full-row highlight, never a line* (prim-group center, reparent-into header,
  body nest — the old amber center LINE for nest is now a highlight). (3) *Gap-free zones*:
  rows own their rect + half the item spacing per side (`row_band`, half-open bands tile
  exactly — proven by `zone_coverage_no_dead_pixels_no_overlaps` sweep test); hit X gated by
  the panel clip rect (whole row width hittable, not just the label); end-of-body strip grown
  8px → half a row (11px). (4) *Blender X-resolution at the ambiguous end-of-nested-list*:
  the end strip enumerates candidates at every depth whose subtree ends there (end of group /
  after group in parent / … / root new-body) and the cursor X picks the depth
  (`pick_by_indent`, deepest whose indent ≤ x, else shallowest; tests at 2 and 3 nesting
  depths) — the "last place inside a sub-body" slot is now both REACHABLE and VISIBLE at its
  own indent. (5) *Hover-to-expand*: hovering a collapsed body header ~0.6s during any drag
  expands it (stays open, Blender-style). (6) *Live ghost verb*: the drag ghost appends the
  resolved action per-frame ("→ Move after Box.003", "→ Copy into Body.002", "→ New body" —
  `slot_label`, Ctrl flips Move→Copy); the root/new-body line also draws a faint inline hint.
  Manual tests: [a] Body>Group with prim as Group's last child: hover the strip below it —
  cursor right of child indent shows the line indented under Group ("Move to end of Group"),
  cursor left shows it at Body depth ("Move after Group"), release lands accordingly;
  [b] drag a prim slowly down a body — every pixel shows exactly one indicator (line or
  highlight), no dead gaps between rows; [c] drag over a collapsed body header, wait 0.6s —
  it expands, drop inside lands at the hovered slot; [d] drag below the whole tree — root
  line at root indent + faint "New body" hint; [e] hold Ctrl mid-drag — ghost verb flips to
  "Copy …". Gates: check green; core_math 443; app --bins 136 green single-threaded (23 slot
  tests incl. 9 new). (outliner_drop_slots.rs, outliner.rs, outliner_dnd.rs,
  outliner_draw.rs, outliner_draw_body.rs, app_types/types_selection.rs)

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-13 (Outliner interaction review: 4 correctness fixes + 1 pinned)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **X-key nest (2 bodies) bypassed the unified nest action → ghost volume** (external review #1).
  The keyboard nest-first-into-second path in `input_keyboard.rs` did a raw `scene_graph.reparent`
  and never dirtied the child's OLD parent — the exact ghost-volume class the outliner drag path
  fixed in b18fe74. Fix: routed through `scene_actions::reparent_body_node` (THE single nest/un-nest
  action; old parent gets child_order reconcile + origin recalc + vol-dirty), with the X-key's
  Union→Subtract conversion kept as the action's own semantic on top. Guards (self/no-op/cycle)
  checked up-front so a rejected nest toasts instead of half-applying. Audit of all other entry
  points: outliner DnD + move-into-parent already routed (b18fe74); `dissolve_sdf_body`'s
  grandchild reparent is a separate composite op (out of scope per review). Manual test: two
  top-level bodies, select both, X → nested Subtract, move the child — no ghost at old location;
  undo restores. (input_keyboard.rs)
- ✅ **Group gate rejected valid same-body selections** (review #2). `group_selected_into_body`
  (Ctrl+G / drop-prim-onto-prim) required the selection's body == `active_body_nid`, so clicking a
  body header mid-multi-select (which silently moves active_body) broke grouping even when ALL
  selected prims shared one body. Fix: new pure `scene_actions::shared_prim_body()` — all
  participants must share ONE body (whichever), THAT body becomes the group parent;
  active_body only as ambiguity fallback; genuinely cross-body selections still reject with the
  same toast. Click-enters-scope behavior itself unchanged. Unit-tested headlessly.
  (prim_actions.rs, scene_actions.rs)
- ✅ **Del deleted only the ACTIVE node (and only Body/Group/Empty kinds)** (review #3). Ctrl+X's
  node path looped the whole selection; Del didn't. Fix: extracted the single shared per-node
  deletion core `scene_actions::delete_node_no_undo` (SDF-subtree flat prims, subtree mesh +
  volume caches, active-voxel working set, sdf_body_nid/active/isolation reassign, shared-source
  purge, deselect) and `delete_selected` now loops ALL selected nodes — every kind except
  Root/Light (matches Cut) — through it in ONE transaction/undo, with the TOP-MOST ancestor filter
  (extracted from 3aafa67's duplicate into shared `top_most_nodes()`, now used by BOTH duplicate
  and delete) so parent+child selections don't double-delete. The weaker inline delete paths
  (keyboard poly/NURBS/imported-context Del, outliner context-menu delete) were re-routed through
  the same core — three duplicate code paths collapsed to one. Prims-first priority unchanged.
  Unit-tested (top_most_nodes). (gizmo.rs, scene_actions.rs, input_keyboard.rs, outliner_panel.rs)
- ✅ **Shift-range select silently no-oped** (review #4). Root cause: `visual_order` was CLEARED at
  the top of the outliner draw and repopulated row-by-row; click handlers fire MID-draw and cloned
  the partial list, so any anchor/target row drawn below the click wasn't registered yet →
  `position()` miss → silent return. Fix: double-buffered — rows push into `visual_order_next`
  during the draw, promoted to `visual_order` after the draw completes, so input always sees the
  last COMPLETE order; plus a fallback in `range_select_unified` (anchor/target still missing →
  additively select the clicked item — never a silent no-op). Manual test: shift-click a row BELOW
  the anchor immediately after expanding a body — full range selects. (outliner_draw.rs,
  outliner_draw_body/light/poly.rs, selection_unified.rs, types_selection.rs)
- ✅ **VERIFIED (already fixed by b18fe74, now pinned)** — last-row bottom-third drop (review #5,
  the "flat_idx+1" class): dragging the last prim of a body below itself resolves to the valid
  end-of-body slot and is a clean no-op (order unchanged); bottom-third of a LAST sub-body header
  resolves to index == len (valid end slot, no out-of-range). Pinned with 2 new unit tests on the
  pure slot fns (`last_prim_dropped_below_itself_is_clean_noop`,
  `bottom_third_of_last_subbody_is_valid_end_slot`). (outliner_drop_slots.rs)


# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-13 (Free-mode move dead in ORTHOGRAPHIC view)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **Alt "free mode" move did nothing in orthographic view** (owner, 2026-07-13). "Free mode" =
  the unconstrained workplane grab (Alt+LMB drag / armed-gizmo Center click / Alt+G) —
  `AxisConstraint::None` → `compute_plane_delta()` in `app/src/transform.rs`. Root cause: the
  helper `cam_ray_dir()` returned ONLY a ray direction; in ortho it returned camera-forward for
  every pixel while `compute_plane_delta` intersected both rays from the SAME origin (`cam.cam_pos`)
  — start and current rays identical → plane delta exactly `Vec3::ZERO` → selection never moved
  (Shift-plane grabs PlaneX/Y/Z were equally dead in ortho). The doc comment even said "origin is
  shifted" but the shift was never implemented. Fix: `cam_ray_dir` → `cam_ray(pos, cam) -> (origin,
  dir)` mirroring the canonical `AzraApp::cam_ray` (camera.rs) ortho math (origin shifted across the
  view plane by `ortho_hw = cam.distance`), and `compute_plane_delta` intersects each ray from its
  own origin. Perspective path unchanged. Camera nav (MMB orbit/pan/zoom) was never gated on ortho.
  Manual test: toggle Orthographic (backtick quick-tap), select a prim, Alt+LMB-drag it (or G then
  click empty space) — it follows the cursor on the workplane; same in perspective; undo = one entry
  per drag. (FIXED 2026-07-13, transform.rs)

  normal-parity coplanar resolution, and `greedy_merge_region` (dissolves internal coplanar edges in annulus
  regions). Verified vs Blender EXACT: sequential double corner-bite = clean 12v/8f L-prism (= Blender single
  slab cut, cleaner than Blender-sequential). Adversarial battery (triple bite / union chain / diff→intersect /
  rotated→axis) all watertight manifolds. 423/423 core_math green, deterministic, app compiles. Plan:

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-06 (SDF Intersect leaves stale geometry — feat/sdf-tools, SDF_TOOLS_PLAN Item 1)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **SDF Intersect boolean left stale geometry ("the mesh that should be gone is still there")** —
  the per-prim bounding-sphere cull in the two production paths (GPU bake + CPU) was NOT op-aware: an
  `Intersect`/`SmoothIntersect` prim (op==2) was `continue`-skipped when the sample point fell outside the
  cutter's bounding sphere. But `max(acc, d)` requires a far-outside point to yield `d` (large positive =
  empty); skipping it retained `acc` (the OTHER geometry), so everything outside the cutter survived
  un-intersected. Root cause: the cull was correct for Union (skip far → min unchanged) and Subtract
  (skip far → max(acc,-d)=acc) but was never made op-aware for Intersect. Fix: removed the op==2 branch
  from the far-skip in `graphics/src/volume_bake.wgsl` (~line 1044) and `core_math/src/sdf_math.rs`
  `eval_scene` (intersect match arm → no-op, never `continue`). Now matches the already-correct analytical
  paths (`sdf_scene.wgsl` / `glsl/sdf_functions.glsl` sphere-skip only Union/ChamferUnion, op==0u||op==3u).
  Builds + graphics shader-compile tests + core_math tests green. (FIXED 2026-07-06)

# ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-03 (nested sub-body properties edits — feat/sparse-3a)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **Properties edits (blend_k, radius, material, op flip) on a prim inside a NESTED sub-body were
  invisible ("blend doesn't work inside a sub-body")** — `mirror_prim_to_graph` (the canonical
  `write_prim`/properties-panel path) marked the prim's DIRECT body dirty. For a nested prim that body is
  the grid-less sub-body, which hits the `no_grid_in_mark_prim_dirty` fallback every frame (owner log:
  hundreds of `[DirtyFallback] body=NodeId(3) reason=no_grid_in_mark_prim_dirty`) and NEVER re-bakes,
  because `trigger_bake` skips nested bodies (their geometry is subsumed into the top-level ancestor's
  bake). So the edit never took effect. Fix: route nested prims through `mark_node_body_vol_dirty(nid)`
  (climbs to the top-level ancestor, full bake) — the same nested-ascend `write_prim_transform` already
  used for a nested-body MOVE; top-level bodies keep the tight partial-region path. `collect_body_prims_
  recursive` already clones each prim WITH its blend operation into the ancestor frame, so composition was
  always correct — only the dirty routing was wrong. (FIXED 2026-07-03, prim_actions.rs mirror_prim_to_graph)

# 2026-07-02 (Bevel: k=1 partial corner at a degree>3 far-endpoint)
# ════════════════════════════════════════

- ✅ **K=1 PARTIAL CORNER AT A degree>3 FAR-ENDPOINT FIXED 2026-07-02** (`bevel_op.rs`, the "octahedron-base
  hole"). Beveling all 4 apex edges of an octahedron capped the apex (N-way M_POLY) but opened a **9-edge hole**
  at the 4 base verts — each degree-4 with exactly ONE beveled edge (a k=1 partial corner at a degree>3
  far-endpoint). Was nv=13/nf=14/boundary=9. ROOT CAUSE: the partial-corner cap (delete-V + recessed center +
  fan) was gated on `n_seg>=2`, so a FLAT (seg=1) k=1 corner at degree>3 got no cap and the un-beveled back
  faces have no `same_edge` seal there → nothing bounds the chamfer → hole (degree-3 is sealed by the third
  face, so the bug only bites degree>3). FIX (3 surgical edits, zero `half_edge.rs`): (1) compute
  `has_same_edge_seal` for all k==1, cap iff `k==1 && !seal && (n_seg>=2 || degree>3)`; (2) new
  `partial_back_edge_slide()` — Blender `offset_on_edge_between`: the merged center slides off V by the offset
  along the unique "back" fan edge (matches oracle vertex-for-vertex); (3) STEP-5 rim gate `<3`→`<2` for a
  partial corner (flat 2-point rim fans to C). RESULT: octahedron bevel-4-apex nv=17/nf=17/boundary=0, matches
  Blender `nway_octa_ref.json` (max dev <2e-3). Gate `bevel_op::tests::octahedron_nway_matches_oracle`.
  **337 core_math GREEN, zero regression** (degree-3 partial gates + N-way pyramid cap untouched). See
  `docs/planning/poly/BEVEL.md` §11 (2026-07-02 PM2).

  VALIDATED before install (manifold + boundary guard, see below); properties/sliders `.changed()` → live
  `poly_bevel_regenerate`; false "Bevel applied" no-op detection; profile-slider semantics aligned across

  OPENS holes (the "boundary>0, valid=true" flap — `validate()` does not check boundary edges) is rejected,

  prevents a non-manifold flap from ever reaching the renderer.

  already-beveled (degree>3) vertex** is a MITER JOIN, not a corner cap. Implemented Blender's `build_boundary`/
  `offset_meet` as a clean-room **STEP 2b** in `bevel_op.rs` (`build_boundary_flat` + `inward_offset_line` +
  `isect_lines_3d`). The shared corner V is DELETED and replaced by its BoundVert ring: each consecutive
  beveled pair's inward offset rails MEET in **3D** (the old `solve_corner_lines` only met COPLANAR rails, so
  two edges on DIFFERENT faces — the degree>3 miter — never met → the tear). STEP 2 welds each rail to its
  BoundVert; STEP 3 replaces the 4-case corner with one `corner_boundvert[ce]` sector lookup (closes the
  "between" faces uniformly); a 2-edge miter emits NO cap (Blender M_NONE). RESULT: pair (9,29) sharing
  v3=(1,-0.75,-1) now 17→14 verts, **boundary 4→0** (was the flap). **+ LOOP SLIDE** (`loop_slide_meet`,
  Blender `offset_on_edge_between`): the miter verts were floating at the 3D rail-meet midpoint — overshooting
  OUTSIDE the ±1 cube (z=-1.006, y=-0.739); loop slide now pins them onto the intervening chamfer edge at
  (0.889,-0.75,-1)/(1,-0.75,-0.889), matching the Blender oracle (0.891,-0.75,-1)/(1,-0.75,-0.891) within
  0.002. Gate `miter_loop_slide_matches_oracle`. Verified test-first: `offset_meet` vs the
  Blender oracle (BoundVerts (0.8,0.8,1)+(1,1,0.8)), the ring walk on the real mesh, then integration. Locked

# ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-02 (Occlusion-aware "visible only" selection)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **SELECTION RAY WENT THROUGH ALL GEOMETRY** — poly sub-element click/hover picking
  (`poly_hover_pick` vertex + edge branches, `poly_selection.rs`) used pure screen-space distance
  with NO depth test, so occluded / back-facing verts and edges were selectable (X-ray always on).

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-06-29 (Voxel MOVE tool: Meta-Medium mesh-vertex grab → mesh→SDF re-voxelize)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **VOXEL MOVE COULD NOT PULL MATERIAL PAST THE BRUSH RADIUS** — the Move brush warped the voxel DENSITY field
  (`elastic_grab_preview`'s semi-Lagrangian gather `src = p − drag·falloff`), which mathematically folds the gather
  source back inside the footprint → a long pull creases/vanishes instead of stretching ("I cannot grab and move it
  as far as I want"). FIX (Meta-Medium approach — deform a TRIANGLE MESH, then convert the deformed mesh back to SDF):
  - **Phase 1 (live preview) — CORRECTED in pass 6 (commit `f816585`, 2026-06-29).** Passes 1–5 displaced a
    SEPARATE CPU mesh (`mesh_cache.update_chunk_verts_in_place`) and relied on a per-chunk render gate to swap the
    grabbed chunks off the resident GPU pool onto that CPU mesh. That was the entire failure class: the resident
    pool — *what is actually on screen* — kept drawing the UNDEFORMED verts, so Move was invisible ("does nothing /
    barely moves"), while Smudge worked because it writes density → re-meshes into the pool. Online research (Meta
    Medium Move tool; diegofloor voxel-editor log) confirmed a large non-rigid grab CANNOT be a field warp (it
    corrupts the SDF — Medium's rejected "inverse displacement") and that Medium does Phase 1 *"by modifying the
    sculpt vertex shader"*. **Pass-6 fix:** displace the EXACT drawn mesh in the G-buffer vertex shader. The grab's
    WORLD-space anchor/drag/radii ride on `CameraUniforms.grab_*` (appended → picking/fog reading the camera prefix
    are unaffected, no BGL change); `vs_main` pulls each vertex of the grabbed body by `falloff·drag`
    (`smoothstep(outer,inner,dist)`), gated by `INSTANCE_FLAG_GRAB_TARGET` (bit 1) set ONLY on that body — a
    structural no-op for all other geometry and whenever no grab is active. Grabbed chunks STAY resident (gate's grab
    condition dropped). The drag is the SAME proven cursor-ray ∩ view-plane projection Smudge uses (magnitude was
    never the bug). The snapshot captured at grab start is now ONLY the pristine-vert input for Phase 2 (not drawn).
  - **Phase 2 (release):** gather the WHOLE object's current mesh (affected chunks re-displaced deterministically
    from snapshot+final drag so it matches the preview; unaffected chunks verbatim), sample its signed distance back
    onto the grid lattice over the swept AABB (`anchor ± outer_r` expanded by `drag`, clamped to the sealed border
    `[1,res-2]`) via new `io_bridge::region_mesh_to_sdf`, convert SDF→density
    (`density = clamp(0.5 − sdf/W, 0, 1)`, `W = 2·voxel_size`; surface sdf=0 → density 0.5) writing ONLY the AABB
    via new `VoxelGrid::write_region_from_sdf` (records changed-voxel pre-values → ONE Cpu-lane sculpt-undo delta),
    then re-mesh the region authoritatively.
  - **Smudge is untouched** — it KEEPS the bounded `elastic_grab` density smear. **Move on a SPARSE grid (≥256³)**
    cleanly FALLS BACK to `elastic_grab` (no live chunk mesh to deform — sparse strokes raymarch), honest, no crash.
- ✅ **MASK BRUSH CRASHED ON FIRST STAMP (pre-existing P0, found during launch-verify)** — `handle_voxel_sculpt_input`
  built the density `BrushRecipe` via `brush.to_builtin()` UNCONDITIONALLY, but `VoxelBrush::Mask` has no
  `BuiltinBrush` (`to_builtin` is `unreachable!()` for it — it writes the protection mask, not density). Any Mask
  stroke panicked on the first stamp. FIX: build the recipe only for non-Mask brushes (`Option`, `None` for Mask;
  the per-stamp loop already forks Mask to `apply_mask_brush` before any recipe use), mirroring
  `VoxelGrid::apply_brush`'s own Mask fork. Structural — Mask is never fed to the recipe path.
- ✅ **mesh_to_sdf Raycast sign INVERTS axis-aligned voxel meshes** — Surface-Nets meshes are blocky / axis-aligned;
  `mesh_to_sdf::SignMethod::Raycast` counts crossings along grid axes that graze the coplanar faces → inverted sign
  on whole regions (cube centre returns +dist under Raycast, −dist under Normal). Would have inverted the committed
  Move surface. FIX: `region_mesh_to_sdf` always uses `SignMethod::Normal` (winding-based; Surface Nets winds quads
  consistently outward) so inside→sdf<0.
  Tests: new `VoxelGrid::write_region_from_sdf` unit test (SDF→density iso mapping + undo restore) + new
  `io_bridge::region_mesh_to_sdf` integration test (lattice alignment + signs); 257 core_math + 1 io_bridge pass;
  app builds; launch [Render] frame=1..5, no panic / device-loss. GUI feel (interactive grab) is owner-verified.
  Files: `core_engine/io_bridge/src/mesh_to_sdf.rs` (region_mesh_to_sdf), `core_engine/core_math/src/voxel_sculpt.rs`
  (flat_index, write_region_from_sdf), `core_engine/render/src/mesh_cache.rs` (chunk_mesh_data),
  `core_engine/app/src/main.rs` (MeshGrab), `core_engine/app/src/input_sculpt.rs` (Move arm, voxel_commit_move_grab,
  Mask recipe guard).

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-06-29 (CPU-forced sculpt brushes FREEZE on high-count geometry — zero-remesh vertex preview)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **CPU-FORCED VOXEL SCULPT BRUSHES FREEZE ON HIGH-COUNT GEOMETRY** — Move / Smudge / Mask / Paint (and
  deposit/carve while painting) re-extracted Surface-Nets topology FROM SCRATCH every drag frame for every touched
  chunk via `voxel_flush_dirty_chunks → grid.mesh_region(a0,a1)` — O((chunk+1)³) corner reads + quad emission per
  cell, on the UI thread, even for unchanged cells. The brush WRITE was cheap; the MESH was the freeze
  (`profile.mesh_ms`). FIX (3 honest brush classes, zero per-frame CPU remesh, no faked vertex offsets):
  (1) DISPLACEMENT (Move/Smudge) — `reproject_chunk_positions` re-derives ONLY the existing vertices'
      positions+normals in place from the live density via per-vertex cell-id provenance; an honest topology-drift
      guard (a cell stops crossing OR a new cell crosses) returns false → that chunk falls back to a full
      `mesh_region` (mandatory, not optional).
  (2) COLOUR-ONLY (Mask + show-mask tint) — `recolor_chunk_vertices` rewrites ONLY `verts[i][6..8]` in place; no
      remesh at all.
  (3) TOPOLOGY deposit/carve-while-painting (Decision B) — density+topology route through the GPU mesher
      (non-resident readback), then the per-voxel paint colour is a SEPARATE in-place vertex write
      (`recolor_vertices_by_position`, derives the anchor cell from the vertex position) AFTER the dispatch lands.
      "CPU-forced" now means only "colour is involved", never "CPU per-frame remesh".
  GPU buffer strategy: in-place sub-range vertex writes via `MeshCache::update_chunk_verts_in_place`
  (keeps `gpu_mesh`, same size ⇒ same buffer ⇒ no bind-group churn, indices untouched). The single colour-packing
  block was extracted to ONE shared `chunk_vertex_color` helper (No-Duplication) so recolor reproduces `mesh_region`
  byte-identically (no colour pop on release). Preview frames are DISPLAY-ONLY (no undo); per-stamp density/colour/
  mask deltas still record frame-by-frame; ONE authoritative full `mesh_region` of the stroke AABB fires on RELEASE
  → exactly one undo entry per stroke. Dense+chunked-gated (sparse strokes raymarch, untouched); `mesh_region` stays
  the no-GPU fallback. Tests: 6 new core_math unit tests incl. an end-to-end preview→release byte-identical "no pop"
  proof; 246 core_math tests pass; app builds; launch [Render] frame=1..5, no panic. Files:
  `core_math/src/voxel_sculpt.rs` (chunk_vertex_color, mesh_region_with_cells, recolor_chunk_vertices,
  reproject_chunk_positions, recolor_vertices_by_position, cell_corner_densities), `render/src/mesh_cache.rs`
  (imported_cells, set_chunk_cells/chunk_cells/chunk_verts, update_chunk_verts_in_place),
  `app/src/input_sculpt.rs` (preview branches + release remesh + Decision-B routing), `app/src/main.rs`
  (gpu_mesh_paint_topology, needs_gpu_vertex_recolor). 👁 awaiting eyeball (GUI interaction unverifiable headless).

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-06-29 (body SYMMETRY explodes the mesh — CPU cascade/fallback bake missed the mirror union)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **TURNING ON BODY SYMMETRY (Mirror) EXPLODES / FLAT-SLABS THE MESH** — enabling a body's body-level Mirror
  collapsed the surface to a flat plane with scattered/exploded DC triangle fragments. CONTEXT: commit 90522b5
  reworked the body mirror from a one-sided fold to a TRUE UNION (`min over 2ⁿ reflection combos`) and claimed it
  was "converted in lockstep across all FOUR eval paths" (CPU `eval_scene_body_mirrored`, GPU bake `volume_bake.wgsl`,
  WGSL analytical, GLSL BVH). The prime suspect was the GPU bake's stack-machine SCOPE re-seek. RULED OUT: a new
  headless GPU-bake↔CPU parity test (`body_mirror_bake_matches_cpu_eval`) bakes 8 mirrored bodies through the REAL
  `volume_bake.wgsl` (single/double/triple-axis, off-center, straddling, off-origin plane, sphere, two-prim) and
  compares every voxel to the canonical `SceneEvaluator` — ZERO sign flips, ZERO NaNs, <0.05 near-surface Δ. The GPU
  bake union is CORRECT. ACTUAL ROOT: there was a FIFTH eval path 90522b5 missed — the CPU grid bake
  `bake_body_grid` / `bake_body_grid_region` in `bake_utils.rs` called bare `eval_scene` (no mirror) while the grid
  BOUNDS were already expanded for both halves (`expand_aabb_for_mirror`). On first creation / mirror-toggle (a
  structural rebake → no existing grid) the synchronous 64³ CPU cascade coarse bake (`bake_dispatch.rs:574`) and the
  CPU rayon fallback (`app_poll.rs`) baked ONLY the original half into a 2×-expanded grid → reflected half empty (flat
  slab) + under-sampled offset geometry (scattered DC fragments). The async GPU bake that followed was correct, but
  the coarse CPU grid is what feeds the FIRST DC extraction shown. FIX (the missing 5th path, no bandaid): extended
  `bake_body_grid` / `bake_body_grid_region` with `mirror_flags`/`mirror_center` params and routed them through the
  SAME canonical `core_math::field_eval::eval_scene_body_mirrored` (made `pub`) the other paths use — single source of
  truth, `mirror_flags==0` is byte-identical (single `eval_scene`). Updated all 3 callers (cascade, CPU fallback ×2).
  Parity: 8/8 GPU↔CPU cases pass; 2 CPU regression tests (`bake_body_grid_applies_mirror_union`,
  `bake_body_grid_region_applies_mirror_union`); 5/5 core_math mirror tests; build clean; launch confirmed
  ([Render] frame=1..5, no panic/device loss). Non-mirror bodies byte-identical (mflags==0 fast path).
  Files: `core_math/src/field_eval.rs` (pub), `app/src/bake_utils.rs`, `app/src/body_volume_cache/bake_dispatch.rs`,
  `app/src/app_poll.rs`, `app/src/sdf_gpu_mesh.rs` (parity test). 👁 awaiting eyeball.

# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **PAINT COLOR DEPOSITED NOTHING VISIBLE (GPU-default conflict)** — with "Paint Color" on, painting showed
  no colour. ROOT: per-voxel paint deposits ONLY on the CPU brush path (`deposit_color_sphere`) and packs colour
  ONLY into the CPU mesher's vertex UV slot (`mesh_region`), but the 4 GPU sub-toggles now DEFAULT ON
  (gpu_brush / gpu_mesh / gpu_resident_mesh / gpu_brush_atlas) → the GPU brush ran (no colour deposit) AND the
  GPU mesher ran (no colour packing) AND the resident GPU buffer was drawn (no colour). FIX: a single
  `VoxelObject::cpu_paint_path()` source of truth (`paint_color_on || grid has colours`, dense-only) gates THREE
  sites — the brush dispatch excludes paint from `use_gpu_brush` (mirrors Move self-forcing CPU), the mesh flush
  skips the GPU mesher for that body so the CPU mesher packs colour, and the raster draw prefers the CPU mesh over
  the resident GPU buffer. Turning Paint ON also forces a one-shot full CPU re-mesh (`voxel_build_all_chunks`) so
  chunks previously meshed only as resident GPU buffers get a colour-carrying CPU mesh. Files: input_sculpt.rs
  (`use_gpu_brush`, `voxel_flush_dirty_chunks`), raster_render.rs (two resident-draw gates), main.rs
  (`cpu_paint_path`), ui_panels.rs (toggle → deferred full re-mesh). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-29
- ✅ **SMOOTH ALL (new)** — added a "Smooth All" button to the Sculpt Brush panel that runs N global Laplacian
  relax passes over the WHOLE sculpt (`VoxelGrid::smooth_all`, reuses the shared Smooth/`relax_region` stencil),
  marks RENDER + re-meshes, recorded as ONE sculpt-undo step on the CPU density-undo lane (its own path — NOT
  `transaction()`). Records only changed voxels (first-touch deduped) so undo reverts the whole smooth exactly.
  Files: core_math/voxel_sculpt.rs (`smooth_all`, `StrokeRecorder::len`), input_sculpt.rs (`voxel_smooth_all`,
  `SMOOTH_ALL_ITERS`), ui_panels.rs (button). Unit test: smooth_all_reduces_variance_records_reversible_delta. | ✅ DONE 2026-06-29
- ✅ **PER-BRUSH SETTINGS (new)** — added a "Per-brush settings" toggle. ON = each `VoxelBrush` remembers its own
  radius / strength / falloff / direction (saved on brush switch, restored on return, seeded from current values on
  first use); OFF = shared (prior behaviour). Hooked at the SINGLE brush-change primitive `set_active_brush`, routed
  through both brush pickers (panel + left strip). Toggle + saved map carry across body switches like other tool
  state. Files: main.rs (`VoxelBrushSettings`, `per_brush_settings`/`brush_settings`, `set_active_brush`),
  voxel_sculpt.rs (`VoxelBrush: Hash`), ui_panels.rs + workspace.rs (route brush picks through `set_active_brush`),

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-06-29 (deferred PBR light-linking stale surface_id)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
- ✅ **PBR LIGHT-LINKING DARKENS RASTER SURFACES (stale surface_id)** — with user Include/Exclude light-linking,
  a now-raster surface (voxel / poly / baked-SDF triangle) was wrongly skipped by a light → partial darkening, but
  ONLY in PBR (the default shading mode). ROOT: the raster G-buffer pass writes 4 of 7 channels (32B/sample limit)
  and physically cannot write `gbuf_surface_id` (R32Uint, TEXTURE+STORAGE usage only — no RENDER_ATTACHMENT/COPY_DST,
  so it is never cleared). Over a raster-covered pixel the SDF compute raymarch early-returns without writing it
  (`raymarch_entry.wgsl:181`, `raymarch_lite.wgsl:176`), so the channel holds a STALE prim index from a prior SDF
  frame. The deferred Lit branch already routed raster pixels through the `0xFFFFFFFF` all-lights sentinel
  (`deferred_entry.wgsl:259`), but the PBR branch read the raw stale id straight into `light_linked()`. FIX: read the
  surface_id as `prim_sid_raw`, then `prim_sid = select(prim_sid_raw, 0xFFFFFFFFu, is_raster_pixel)` — defined OUTSIDE
  every `#region` (so it survives the df_lite strip of DEFERRED_MATERIAL/SHADOW_AO) and consumed by the PBR light loop.
  Also corrected the false G-buffer header comment claiming raster pixels get the sentinel "from the clear color"
  (no clear exists) and annotated the two SDF-compute early-return sites. Files: `graphics/src/deferred_entry.wgsl`,
  `render/src/gbuffer.wgsl`, `graphics/src/raymarch_entry.wgsl`. Build + Naga (df_lite/df_full/raymarch) pass; launch
  confirmed ([Render] frame=1..5, no panic/device loss). 👁 awaiting eyeball.

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# ✅ FIXED — 2026-06-28 (SDF Object-Mode render/bake stabilization — P0.2 path, GATE 2 territory)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
A reactive marathon (~12 commits, 5b7c87a..5617bde) closed a cluster of SDF→bake→DC-mesh→raster gaps.
Invariants recorded in memory `project_sdf_object_mode_render_invariants`. All build-verified; ✅ = user-confirmed,
👁 = awaiting eyeball.

- ✅ **BOOLEAN-SUBTRACT BLANKS THE BODY** (this commit) — cube → duplicate prim → press X (Union→Subtract) made BOTH
  cubes vanish; only a resolution change (full re-tighten) brought the surface back. ROOT: the X-key handler routes
  the op change through `write_prim` → `mirror_prim_to_graph`, which ALWAYS issued a PARTIAL region bake keyed on the
  edited prim's own AABB (`mark_prim_dirty`). But a boolean-category flip is NOT a local edit: `compute_body_bake_bounds`
  counts only base + ADDITIVE prims, so Union→Subtract drops the prim from the bounds set AND re-carves the field
  globally — the partial region can't represent that, leaving a stale/empty field. The settle re-tighten then
  mis-compared bounds and logged `already tight, skipped redundant re-bake`, so the needed full bake never fired.
  FIX: `mirror_prim_to_graph` now compares the prim's boolean-op CATEGORY (new `BooleanOp::category()` — Additive /
  Subtractive / Intersective, ignoring `k`) + visibility before/after the edit; a category or visibility change marks
  the body for a FULL bake (`mark_body_dirty` + `clear_bake_debounce`) instead of a partial region. A pure blend-`k`
  drag stays in the same category → still takes the cheap partial path (no perf regression). The full bake recomputes
  tight bounds and clears `pending_retighten`, so the surface stays correct with no resolution-change workaround.
  Files: `core_math/src/primitives.rs` (BooleanOp::category), `app/src/prim_actions.rs` (mirror_prim_to_graph). 👁 awaiting eyeball.

- ✅ **WHITE-BOX GHOST** (1a7f4bd + 5617bde) — solid box enrobing the geometry with the body carved out, on
  additive-prim move / boolean re-bake; sticky until a full re-bake. TWO roots: (a) bake-bounds PROVENANCE race —
  `accept_gpu_result` read live `body_bounds` an `aabb_escape` had already mutated → old grid stamped with new (2×)
  bounds → scaled ghost; fix = `PendingBake` carries dispatch-time bounds. (b) `gpu_texture_upload_done` latched for
  ANY direct-write body incl. a NON-active atlas bake; the node-freeze fix then flipped the active body's STALE
  `rv.buffer` valid → field-direct meshed old field at wrong bounds; fix = guard the flag to the active body that
  actually wrote `rv.buffer` + tag `gpu_texture_upload_body`, consume only when ==active. **User-confirmed: "no white box".**
- ✅ **POST-EDIT SELECT FREEZE (~400ms)** (44b22d3) — settle re-tighten bake wrote `rv.buffer` but never restored
  `resident_buffer_valid` → `sdf_populate_resident` fell back to a whole-grid `to_vec` + `write_buffer`. Fix: restore
  the flag → field-direct. **User-confirmed** (poll 13-49ms, no SLOWPOLL).
- ✅ **POOL-HIT SELECT FREEZE** (e9bfe25) — body switch always cleared `resident_buffer_valid` → CPU-grid fallback
  re-mesh on every selection. Fix: keep it valid on a pool hit when the slot matches the body's res+bounds.
- ✅ **ADDED-BODY BLACK + ≤256 SELECT FREEZE + STEADY 36ms IDLE POLL** (d94fa3d) — the Phase-3B SPARSE mesh path
  engaged at ALL resolutions; ≤256 it's pure overhead (the 36ms churn + the freeze) AND renders BLACK (degenerate
  brick normals). Fix: gate sparse to `>256`; ≤256 uses dense. **User-confirmed.**
- ✅ **512³ BLACK** (7da4c98) — 512 still rode the black sparse path. Fix: route 512 through DENSE mesh (512MB field
  fits the 2.1GB binding; output surface-capped); sparse PARKED (`slot.res>512`) until a NORMAL-parity test + the
  brick-normal root fix land. **User-confirmed renders.**
- ✅ **SOLID-MODE BLACK / boolean "everything disappears"** (8f192f8 + 5617bde) — Solid multiplied the shade by the
  cast-shadow term; a boolean SUBTRACT cutter casts shadow → `final_shadow→0` → body went dark. Fix: Solid = clay
  preview, drop cast-shadow: `color = sc*0.55 + sc*0.45*final_ao`. 👁 awaiting eyeball.
- ✅ **ESCAPE BALLOON ("large cube enrobing all 3, size = movement")** (0269893) — `aabb_escape` inflated the grid by
  full extent + 8× velocity, never shrank → 3-10× the body. Fix: bounded escape anchored to the stable cached grid,
  hard-capped 2× (NEVER re-center on the moving body — that re-fires the escape every frame). **User-confirmed bounded.**
- ✅ **DRAG-GHOST / full-bake hitch** (b141eda + c2f0863) — path-A in-place full bake during interaction + dispatch-
  synchronous bounds (kills the bevel smear). Path-A + sparse defaults flipped on (0269893).
- ✅ **SUBTRACT-CREASE BLACK (GPU)** (6c3d8fe + 1a7f4bd) — GPU DC mesher had no degenerate-normal repair (CPU did).
  Fix: crossing-normal average + geometry-derived last-resort fallback. (Extends SUBTRACT-CREASE-NORMAL below.)
- ✅ **SCULPT PINCH TEARING** (6ff5311) — iso-preserving relax_region + atlas chunk apron (two roots).

checked vertex positions); pre-existing `validate_glsl_floats_per_prim_sync` test fails (GLSL/Rust FLOATS_PER_PRIM

# 📋 KNOWN — 2026-06-26 (visual notch bugs, owner-deferred — NOT the cache)
# ════════════════════════════════════════
Owner reported a visual corruption (concave notch/step) on bevel edits + layer-order changes; suspected
the cache. Investigation RULED OUT the cache (all reorder/group/reparent paths follow the Structural
Mutation Checklist, the bake hash is order-sensitive, and the bevel edit mirrors to graph + rebakes).
Two distinct roots — full detail in memory `project_subbody_eval_order_bug`:
- ✅ **BEVEL-NOTCH — FIXED 2026-07-17 (worktree cache-perf, uncommitted).** Fix = tri-planar max is kept
  (surface authority) but AUGMENTED with (1) an EXACT uniform roundbox-ρ corner term
  (ρ = min effective octant radius, None→0) maxed into the field, and (2) an EXACT 2D chamfer prism SDF
  (vertex sectors added — the plane-max form underestimated near chamfer vertices, which both fed the
  stripes and broke the corner term's octant-boundary domination). The combined field is continuous,
  1-Lipschitz (property-tested pairwise), never overestimates its own zero set, reduces EXACTLY to
  sdRoundBox for all-Round-equal radii, keeps None corners sharp, and lifts the corner-ridge march
  distance by ~24% (probe `bevel_notch_d`). Ported line-parallel to ALL 3 live eval paths in ONE task:
  CPU `sdf_shapes.rs` (the oracle, first), `sdf_prim_eval.wgsl`, `volume_bake.wgsl`. Surface moves ONLY
  inside corner blend neighborhoods (old tri-cylinder corner bulge ≤0.226·ρ shaved to the ρ-sphere —
  per the CLAUDE.md rule "same radius → sdRoundBox"). Gates: `bevel_notch_{a,b,c,d}` (core_math) +
  the 5 existing sparse beveled-subtract GPU gates (all green, CPU-as-oracle). NOTE the old fix sketch
  below named 5 paths — GLSL was deleted 2026-07-14, sdf_mesh.wgsl consumes baked grids, bevel_op.rs is
  the POLYGON bevel; the live set is exactly the 3 ported. `sdf_box_per_edge_profiled` (profile bevel)
  still uses hard max — tracked separately below. Session log: BEVEL.md §11 2026-07-17 (fix entry).
  *(Original report follows.)* per-edge box bevel `sdf_box_per_edge` (`core_engine/graphics/src/sdf_prim_eval.wgsl:418`)
  combines the 3 tri-planar 2D bevels with a HARD `max()`. With MIXED radii (filleted edge r + sharp
  edge 0) the max is discontinuous at the vertex → the notch. Violates the CLAUDE.md Per-Edge Bevel
  Corner Rule ("different radii → smooth interpolation, not hard max()"). Fix = smooth-blend the 3
  planar bevels by radius difference WITHOUT over-rounding, ported to ALL 5 eval paths (sdf_prim_eval.wgsl,
  volume_bake.wgsl, sdf_mesh.wgsl, GLSL sdf_functions.glsl, CPU bevel_op.rs/bake_utils.rs). Hard (a
  corner-sphere-via-max() attempt was already reverted 2026-03-22). Reproduces on a SINGLE plain box.
  **2026-07-17 update (beveled-SUBTRACT "stringy vertical sheets" diagnostic, worktree cache-perf):**
  the owner's carved-surface stripe sheets are the SAME root, manifesting through SHADING — deferred
  lighting marches `soft_shadow`/`calc_ao`/reflections on the ANALYTICAL `scene_sdf`
  (deferred_entry.wgsl:471-473,542,594-606) whose hard-max field has vertical C0 ridge surfaces + a
  concave-region distance UNDERESTIMATE. The GEOMETRY pipeline was exonerated with 5 new permanent
  gates (full/windowed/partial bake + O1 coarse cull + mesh-vertex-on-isosurface, all green —
  `tests_sparse_bake.rs` `sparse_beveled_*`, `tests_gpu_classify.rs`
  `gpu_classify_coarse_cull_matches_cpu_classifier`; the O1 coarse cull had ZERO prior coverage).
  Owner discriminator: stripes vanish in Solid/clay shading ⇒ confirmed shading-level. Full session
  log: BEVEL.md §11 2026-07-17 + docs/planning/sdf/CACHE_REMESH_512_REVIEW.md.
- 📋 **BEVEL-NOTCH-PROFILED (follow-up, low)** — `sdf_box_per_edge_profiled` (volume_bake.wgsl:357 +
  sdf_prim_eval.wgsl copy, CPU `curves.rs bevel_2d_profiled`) still combines its 3 planar profiled
  bevels with the bare hard `max()` (no corner term). Same stripe class is possible on profile-bevel
  boxes. Port the BEVEL-NOTCH corner term there in its own task (the profiled 2D field also needs its
  exact-vertex treatment for the domination bound — see BEVEL.md §6 #26 before attempting).
- ✅ **SUBBODY-EVAL-ORDER — CLOSED 2026-07-17 (diagnosed EXPECTED-MATH, worktree cache-perf, uncommitted).**
  The old text was STALE on both counts: (1) eval order is NOT `all_primitives_ordered()` (that feeds only
  the flat cache / uid maps) — every eval path walks `resolve_child_order()` which INTERLEAVES prims and
  sub-bodies; (2) `group_selected_into_body` (prim_actions.rs:565) already inserts the new sub-body at the
  earliest extracted prim's slot (`insert_slot`) — the proposed "interleave" fix shipped long ago.
  **Diagnosis (repro matrix, CPU dense-grid + GPU bake parity, all numbers in field_eval.rs [EvalOrder]
  tests + tests_bake.rs section (l)):**
  · Reorder within a HARD-union run → field-invariant, **exactly 0 delta** (min associative; culls exact). No bug.
  · Group a hard-union run into a Union{k:0} sub-body (non-zero origin) → max|d| = 6e-8 (float shift), 0 sign
    flips. No bug. Nested hard-union chain vs flat → **0 delta**. No bug.
  · Reorder within a SMOOTH-union run (equal k=0.25) → max|d| = 0.0084 (bounded by k) — pairwise smin is
    NON-ASSOCIATIVE. Intentional pairwise-fold math (all SDF DCCs); an order-canonical fold would alter every
    existing scene's look → OWNER DECISION, not shipped.
  · Group smooth-blended prims under the default hard Union{k:0} group op → max|d| = 0.062, 12/4913 grid sign
    flips — **THE owner-visible notch**: the blend across the group boundary hardens to a crease because the
    group joins its parent with the sub-body's `body_op` (k=0). Setting the group's op k to the prims' k
    shrinks the delta to the 0.0084 parenthesization residual. Intentional semantics (grouping IS
    parenthesization — and the OPPOSITE behavior was the "boolean tree inside a sub-body" defect, fixed).
  · Reorder a Subtract prim into slot 0 → seeds solid (first-operand rule, all 3 paths). Intentional.
  **Cross-path:** CPU `BodyField` ↔ GPU `volume_bake.wgsl` agree EXACTLY (0 sign flips, near-surface
  max|dv| = 0.0000) on all 4 eval-order trees (`evalorder_*` gates in `body_mirror_bake_matches_cpu_eval`);
  `sdf_scene.wgsl`'s scope machine reviewed line-by-line — same first-operand / empty-parent / mirror-union
  rules, conservative culls only. No path disagreement → nothing to fix.
  **UX mitigation (proposed, not implemented):** when grouping prims that carry a smooth k, default the new
  sub-body's `body_op` to Union{k = max prim k} instead of k:0 (kills the visible crease); and/or a
  "flatten group" tool. Escalated to owner. Regression net: the 6 [EvalOrder] core_math tests + the 4 GPU
  `evalorder_*` parity scenes are permanent gates.
- ✅ **SUBTRACT-CREASE-NORMAL** (jagged / spiky / "eroded organic" crater rim where a SUBTRACT carves — the
  "persistent white cube"; rest of the body smooth) — the GPU resident DC mesher `dc_vertex`
  (`graphics/src/sdf_mesh.wgsl:245`) set each vertex normal by RE-SAMPLING a central-difference gradient at
  the placed vertex. At a concave subtract crease the vertex sits on the `max(base,-cutter)` V-fold, so the
  wide 1.5×cell stencil straddles BOTH field branches → the gradient collapses to ~0 or flips erratically;
  `gradient_normal` returns `vec3(0)` and the GPU writes it RAW — there is no degenerate-normal repair on the
  GPU path (the CPU `chunked_dc.rs::repair_degenerate_normals` exists, GPU had no analog). Bad normals → broken
  deferred shading localized to cuts ONLY (convex bevels keep a clean gradient → stay smooth), exactly the
  reported asymmetry. RULED OUT first (workflow, 6 hyps + adversarial verify): bake noise (volume_bake.wgsl is
  neutralized), QEF vertex position (clamped to cell, chunked_dc.rs:616), smooth-blend field (default subtract
  is hard k=0), under-sampling (128³ default → subtract spans ~15-45 voxels). FIX: vertex normal = AVERAGE of
  the edge-crossing plane normals (the same unit normals already fed to the QEF) — the outward bisector of the
  meeting faces, which never collapses at a crease; gradient fallback only if the crossings cancel. Applied to
  BOTH GPU (sdf_mesh.wgsl) and CPU (chunked_dc.rs) for parity; smooth/flat surfaces unchanged (all crossings
  share one normal → average == that normal). Validated: 7/7 DC parity tests (incl. boolean_subtract) + core_math
  211/211. | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-27
- ✅ **STALE-ATLAS-SLOT-RES** (body INVISIBLE after Grid 128→64; "staggered ghost slabs" while moving at lower res;
  multi-resolution / multi-body broken) — on a resolution DOWN-switch, the atlas-slot realloc was gated behind
  `if max_res >= 128` (app_poll.rs:1186, meant to skip transient 64³ cascade drafts), so the stale higher-res slot
  persisted. `effective_res` (app_poll.rs:1306) reads the SLOT's resolution to drive the bake's grid_res / index
  math, while the output/staging/rv buffers are sized at the REAL request res. So the shader indexed with the OLD
  (larger) res into a buffer sized at the NEW (smaller) res → Naga bounds-robustness silently dropped every
  out-of-range write (all but the bottom octant) → corrupt/empty grid → body INVISIBLE when static, or only the
  bottom slab meshed + re-baked at each drag position (the staggered ghost slabs). FIX: also realloc when an
  EXISTING slot is LARGER than the request on any axis; legit atlas-clamp (slot < req) + first-time 64³ cascade
  drafts (no prior slot) untouched → no churn. Root-caused via a 7-hypothesis adversarial workflow (all obvious
  causes refuted; a verifier traced the stale-slot→effective_res chain). Confirmed by user: 64→128→64 stays
  visible; multi-res + multi-body work. | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-28
- ✅ **SUBTRACT-ESCAPE-BALLOON** (white "trailing cube" when dragging a SUBTRACT prim) — `compute_body_bake_bounds`
  (`app/src/bake_utils.rs:162`) included EVERY visible prim's AABB, **including cutters**. Dragging a Subtract/
  Intersect outward grew the body's bake bounds to chase it → `aabb_escape` (bake_dispatch.rs:385) fired every
  frame, inflating the grid by full-extent + ×8 velocity headroom; observed `grid_min` marching −1.9→−13.6,
  `grid_max`→+10.2. At fixed res the body under-sampled → a coarse solid "trailing cube" that cleared on the
  release re-tighten. ROOT: a cutter can only REMOVE/RESTRICT material — it never creates surface outside the
  additive silhouette, so its AABB must not expand the grid. FIX: bounds driven by base (first visible prim) +
  additive prims (Union/ChamferUnion) only; cutters clipped; margin widened by max cutter blend_k (constant →
  no chasing) so smooth-cut fillets stay sampled. Cutter still carves correctly (overlap is inside bounds by
  construction). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-27

**Stopgap fixes (CPU-DC path, committed `ae5d72b`):**
- ✅ **Prim-dup explosion / 2nd-prim shift** — `recalculate_body_origin` now translates BOTH the
  bake working-copy (`translate_body_cache`) AND the displayed `mesh_cache` entry
  (`MeshCache::translate_mesh_in_place`) so existing geometry doesn't jump on a recenter; add-prim
  clears the bake debounce so the new prim appears promptly.
- ✅ **Idle re-tighten** — after editing settles (~150ms), partially-baked bodies get one full
  re-tighten bake (`check_idle_retighten` + `pending_retighten`), restoring bounds + resolution.
- ✅ **Resolution → invisible (512/1024)** — Object Mode now clamps effective AND adaptive bake
  resolution to ≤256 (`gridbacked_only`) so a body never bakes TextureOnly (empty CPU grid = no
  triangles); the 512/1024 picker buttons are disabled in Object Mode. Partially addresses RESNOOP.
- ✅ **Brick Pool exposed toggle** — parked dev feature (23 bugs) was a one-click button in the normal
  panel; enabling it broke bake→DC→display. Gated behind Developer Tweaks + clean rebake on toggle.
- ↩️ Bevel-live debounce-bypass attempt REVERTED (full-bake-every-frame churned via the generation race).

**GPU mesh extraction (Phase G — the root fix; behind `gpu_sdf_mesh` flag, OFF by default):**
- The CPU Dual Contouring (~125ms, background) loses a generation race during continuous edits →
  the surface stalls/vanishes until a full rebake (resolution change). This is the ROOT of
  BOOLBREAK, BEVELLAG, prim-dup explosion, and the "surface missing/explosion until resolution change"
  class. A ~2-5ms GPU QEF DC mesh closes the race. Committed `adc98cd` `9bb2fe1` `ad8b1c5` `46c2829`
  `d7fa242` `fd46523` + readback-defer fix. Live behind the flag; two drag-gates fixed (bake suppress +
  readback defer) so it meshes live during edits. **Needs live user verification** (see
  `GPU_MESH_EXTRACTION_PLAN.md` Progress). When on, BOOLBREAK / BEVELLAG / surface-stall should resolve.
- **GPU meshing is now DEFAULT ON** (`gpu_sdf_mesh = true`, `998a338`); CPU DC = the Developer-Tweaks-OFF
  fallback. The async readback (`b0f2ed9`) removed the 66ms blocking stall ("steppy"), and a no-op
  transform-write guard killed the idle/held re-bake loop.
- **G2 — resident no-readback path DONE** (`569a091`), behind the OFF-by-default
  `gpu_sdf_mesh_resident` sub-flag (Developer Tweaks → "Resident no-readback"). Meshes into a persistent
  GpuCtx slot and draws via `draw_indexed_indirect` in the G-buffer AND picking passes (selection = P0
  preserved); shadow auto-skips. Removes BOTH the mesh readback and the per-frame 8MB grid re-upload (the
  residual drag cost). **Needs live verification:** toggle ON → buttery during drag + click-select works;
  toggle OFF = readback fallback. Orphaned slots pruned in `process_dirty` SCENE block (no leak).
- **Resident + field path DEFAULT ON** (`10506e4`); G3 step 1 reads the QEF-DC field straight from
  `ResidentVolume.buffer` (`6d401de`, content-identity guarded + CPU-grid fallback).
- **dc_dispatch 8MB-clone fix — the real win** (`9bbe07b`, verified live 2026-06-25). `[GpuMeshPath]`
  tracing proved the resident field-direct path runs and holds through a drag, yet `dc_dispatch` stayed
  ~2.7ms. Root cause (code-read, not the buffer ops first assumed): `dispatch_grid_dc_async` did an
  UNCONDITIONAL `grid.to_vec()` (8MB, ~2ms) before the path branch, inside the `dc_dispatch` timer — and
  the resident field-direct path never uses that CPU grid. Fix: cubic guard checks the borrowed
  `grid.len()`, the resident branch moves above the clone, `sdf_populate_resident` re-fetches the grid
  only on the rare fallback. **Measured: `dc_dispatch` 2.7ms → 0.2ms; `poll_primary_bake` ~8ms → ~5.5ms
  during partial-bake drag.** Diagnostics `[GpuMeshPath]` (changed-only) + `[DcResident]` (>2ms) kept.
- **Residual (next, optional):** the ~2.2ms `to_vec` bake readback still runs every bake; for the
  field-direct steady state it's only needed by CPU consumers (save/export/duplicate) + the rare
  fallback. Making it lazy (step 2) would drop the partial-bake poll to ~3ms — but it changes the DC
  trigger in the hot `poll_primary_bake` path (device-loss-critical), so it's gated on explicit go.

# ════════════════════════════════════════
# P0.2-FULL OBJECT-MODE BUG CLUSTER — FIXES — 2026-06-20
# All three surfaced testing the unified Object Mode (SDF baked→DC-mesh→raster). Build-verified
# (`cargo build -p app` green, 210/210 core_math tests incl. 2 new). Runtime-UNVERIFIED (await user test).
# Test build first STABILIZED: reverted the uncommitted v7→v8 SdfObject migration so this build = the
# committed foundation (ba6be84) + these fixes only — one change at a time. The SdfObject node type stays
# committed but dormant (nothing creates it) until the full feature (Phases 1–4) lands off-build.
# ════════════════════════════════════════

| # | File:Line | Description | Status |
|---|-----------|-------------|--------|
| DUPSDF | app_poll.rs (dispatch_pending_primary_bakes, ~852-866) | "Duplicated SDF object doesn't appear — only after toggling a cache setting." ROOT CAUSE (6-agent trace wf_0e143863; a first dirty-mark fix in `duplicate_subtree` was REVERTED — it was redundant, both dup paths already mark dirty, and ineffective): the **atlas instancing dedup** skips the duplicate's primary bake. A duplicate's `template_hash` excludes `prim_uid` (by design, so clones match), so it equals the source's; the source already owns a valid atlas slot → `if find_slot_by_hash(template_hash).is_some() && slot(body).is_none() { dirty_bodies.remove(body); continue; }` → the bake is SKIPPED, so `accept_gpu_result → dispatch_grid_dc_async` never fires → the duplicate's `mesh_cache_id` never receives a DC mesh → `raster_render.rs:399` skips it every frame → invisible. The dedup is valid ONLY when the VP-shader atlas raymarch is the consumer (the duplicate samples the shared atlas cell via its own world transform) — i.e. SDF Edit Mode. In Object Mode the consumer is a per-body DC RASTER mesh, which requires its own bake. A cache toggle re-dirties all bodies / invalidates slots → the skip no longer matches → bake runs → visible (hence "appears after a cache setting"). Fix: capture `allow_instancing_skip = self.force_volume_only` before the gpu borrow; gate the dedup `continue` on it, so the skip fires only in SDF Edit Mode and the bake always runs in Object Mode. Class-eliminating: covers all dup paths (gizmo Shift+D, outliner, menu, clipboard). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-20 |
| GRAYFACE | chunked_dc.rs (repair_degenerate_normals) | "Data corruption beveling/subtracting an SDF — concave/notch faces render flat GRAY." ROOT CAUSE (refuted material/culling/field-corruption; confirmed normals): DC vertex normals are the gradient of the CSG-combined SDF; on subtract (`max(d,-clip)`)/bevel (`smin/smax`) creases & clamped plateaus the 4 tetrahedron taps are equal (`Σkᵢ=0` ⇒ `Σkᵢ·d=0`) so `normalize_or_zero()` → **ZERO** → `normalize(0)`=NaN → `ndl=0` → ambient-only gray. Volume-raymarch masked it (analytic normal at the hit point); P0.2 raster exposed it. Voxel meshes unaffected (separate Surface-Nets path, smooth density field). Fix: new pure `repair_degenerate_normals()` — area-weighted geometric normals (oriented by a single winding-vote) replace ONLY the zero-length normals; smooth gradient normals on good surfaces are preserved exactly. 2 direct unit tests (proven to fail without the repair). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-20 |
| DUPCRASH | bake_dispatch.rs (res3 cubic gate) + app_poll.rs (dispatch_grid_dc_async guard) | "Crash after duplicating an SDF a second time" — `PANIC chunked_dc.rs:139 index out of bounds: len 156800, index 163840`. ROOT CAUSE (exposed by the DUPSDF fix — the duplicate now actually BAKES): the bake produces ASYMMETRIC per-axis resolution (`compute_asymmetric_resolution` → `[rx,ry,rz]` from AABB aspect ratio), but the DC raster-mesh path is CUBIC-ONLY — `FlatGridAccessor` indexes with one `nverts` per axis and `accept_gpu_result` infers `bake_resolution = cbrt(grid.len())`. For a non-cube grid (`rx·ry·rz`), the cube the DC walks (`cbrt(rx·ry·rz)³`) exceeds the packed buffer → out-of-bounds panic (and silently mis-indexes milder non-cubes — latent for ANY elongated SDF body; cube bodies are already cubic so it stayed hidden). The offset Shift+D triggers an `aabb_escape` that inflates the bounds hard on one axis (drag velocity headroom ×8) → extreme asymmetry → crash. Fix: (1) PRIMARY — GridBacked (≤256³, DC-fed) bakes forced CUBIC at the longest axis (`[max_axis;3]`); TextureOnly (>256³, VP-shader, normalized-space) keeps the asymmetric voxel-saving res. No-op for cube bodies, corrects all non-cube bodies. (2) DEFENSE — `dispatch_grid_dc_async` guards `grid.len()==nverts³`, skipping (not panicking) if a non-cubic grid ever reaches the cubic DC path. Follow-up (perf, not a bug): a per-axis DC accessor would restore asymmetric voxel savings for elongated bodies. | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-20 |
| DELFREEZE | viewport_render.rs (update_viewport_mode_auto) | "Deleting the last object — it doesn't go away, freezes in the viewport." ROOT CAUSE (G-Buffer Contract violation, NOT the delete path): delete leaves an empty placeholder body → `update_viewport_mode_auto` (no Object/Edit-mode awareness) sees no meshes/raster geometry → flips `viewport_mode` Hybrid→FullSdf → the raster pass (which alone CLEARS the G-buffer + refreshes `raster_depth`) is skipped → the `AnalyticalLite` primary pass early-returns on the stale `raster_depth.w>0` → deferred re-shades the previous frame = frozen ghost. Fix: Object Mode (`!sdf_edit_active`) is ALWAYS the unified raster path (Display Invariant: triangles-only; raster owns clear+floor+depth+picking) → force Hybrid; FullSdf is valid only in SDF Edit Mode. Eliminates the whole class (empty/mid-bake/all-deleted scenes keep clearing). Downstream raster dispatch is still gated by `!force_volume_only`, so volume paths are unaffected. | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-20 |

The device-loss class (analytical SDF march fused with voxel raster over one G-buffer) is eliminated STRUCTURALLY, not worked around. New `sdf_edit_active` flag (default false = Object Mode; true only inside SDF Edit Mode, wired in Step 2). STEP-1 TRADEOFFS (accepted): PathTrace neutralized to lite+raster in Object Mode; SDF prim edits use mesh re-bake (stale-until-release) — live volume editing returns with the Step-2 Edit-Mode entry. | ✅ DONE 2026-06-20 (runtime-unverified, crash-class) |

NARROWED (not yet fixed): NOT a double raster draw (a resident body is pushed to draw_calls once; the slot draw `continue`s past the mesh_cache block) and NOT a stale VP texture (the bake writes the 3D texture GPU-direct via textureStore → `gpu_texture_upload_done` → `update_resident_volume` skips the CPU upload, resident_volume.rs:233-238 — so the texture is CURRENT). Both the VP texture and the resident slot (rv.buffer) are current. So it's a **render-GATE oscillation**: across drag frames the body is rendered by the VP raymarch AND the raster resident slot (two techniques over one body = Display-Invariant violation), driven by `volume_preview_active`/`dirty_bodies` flipping; the lazy path's skipped `accept_gpu_result` perturbs that gating. Brick-pool-ON hides it (coarse bake → resolution mismatch → lazy filter fails → full readback → `accept_gpu_result` runs → gating stable). UPDATE (live [RenderPath] trace, db03862): the render-gate theory is DISPROVEN. During the ghost drag `force_volume_only=false` AND `volume_preview_active=false` are CONSTANT — pure Object-Mode raster, the VP raymarch never runs. So it is NOT two render techniques and NOT a gate flip. Puzzle: in Object Mode the resident-slot draw is identical lazy-on vs lazy-off (same rv.buffer, same bounds); lazy only leaves body_grids stale, which doesn't touch the slot draw — yet the ghost appears only with lazy ON. Mechanism still unidentified by log-tracing; needs a visual/frame-debugger capture or a precise user description of the ghost (offset? lagging? at the prim's old position?). **RESOLVED into COMBMESH (2026-06-25):** the user's screenshot + the decisive "toggle Resident GPU mesh (G2) OFF → it disappears, present with lazy on AND off" reframed it — the artifact is a comb/striped mesh from the **G2 resident draw path**, not lazy readback. See COMBMESH below; fix = G2 default reverted OFF. | ⏸️ SUPERSEDED by COMBMESH |
| COMBMESH | G2 resident path (cache_state.rs:115; sdf_gpu_mesh.rs dispatch_resident; raster_render.rs draw_sdf_resident_slot) | **Comb / venetian-blind of evenly-spaced slabs across the SDF body** (screenshot 2026-06-25). Decisive USER isolation: toggling **"Resident GPU mesh (G2, indirect draw)" OFF removes it**; present with lazy readback BOTH on and off → it is the **G2 resident draw**, NOT lazy/render-gate/dirty-region. Static analysis ruled OUT every structural cause: counters zeroed each dispatch (sdf_gpu_mesh.rs:280); full-grid dispatch self-clears `cell_vert` (identical `dc_params` both paths, :27-38); byte-identical 32-byte vertex format (`[f32;8]` = `RasterVertex` pos+normal+uv); single per-frame draw (2nd draw site = click-only picking); slot reallocated on res-change (app_poll.rs:612); `sdf_dc_resident_field_parity` proves field-direct==upload bit-for-bit. Code path correct as written → defect is a **GPU-level/timing subtlety** the single-dispatch parity tests can't catch. Open candidates: (a) resident DC meshes a **half-written field** (bake splits into 3 Z-slices; partial GPU2GPU `rv.buffer` copy covers only the dirty region but the DC meshes the whole buffer); (b) missing **STORAGE|VERTEX** barrier on persistent `slot.verts` (mesh_cache's vertex buffer is VERTEX-only so never hits this); (c) two dispatches/frame into one slot. **ROOT CAUSE (8-agent workflow wu6jlc42w + Opus synthesis):** during a drag the partial bake seeds `output_buf` from the CPU `body_grids` grid, but lazy readback FREEZES `body_grids` at the last full bake `F`. Every partial bake re-stamps `F`, applies only the current slab, and writes `F + slab` to `rv.buffer` — discarding prior partial edits → COMB (fresh/stale bands at the dirty-region stride) + TRAILING duplicate (prim's original position re-stamped from `F`). **FIX ATTEMPT (df814ec):** seed `output_buf` from live `rv.buffer` instead of the stale CPU grid. **REVERTED (8c739eb):** that introduced a NEW regression — the cube changes size + goes gray during drag, because `rv.buffer` can hold density baked at DIFFERENT bounds/resolution than the current bake (the bounds-tautology + realloc-timing holes the verifier flagged that the seed didn't guard). Seeding from it mixes world scales → distorted surface. **PIVOT:** the clean path to fast 256³ is **draft-resolution-while-dragging** (drop to 128³ during a prim drag, restore 256³ on release — full draft bakes, no partial-bake/lazy correctness coupling), NOT lazy+seed. Comb/trailing only occur on the lazy+resident path → kept OFF by default; clean mesh_cache path is correct. **RESOLVED (Phase 1, 2026-06-26):** the correct fix was PATH A — bake the dirty slab DIRECTLY into `rv.buffer` in place (no seed at all → no stale CPU grid, no cross-bounds seed). De-risked by `partial_bake_writes_exact_footprint` (proves the partial bake writes only `[bake_min,bake_max)`). Commits: spike `1b4f2de`, path A `a7c982c`, lazy ON `4c36a28`. A SECOND comb cause then surfaced — **Adaptive Resolution** auto-scaling the bake res mid-edit left the resident volume at a different res than the bake for a frame (`res_ok=false`), so path A fell back to the stale-seed path → bands. Fixed by **Adaptive Resolution OFF by default** (`ed91f8a`) → fixed res → path A always fires. Also cut the 64MB `base_grid` clone (the ~18ms TriggerBake → 0.7ms, `b6c7d13`) + locked adaptive res during interaction (`e752e0e`). 256³ editing is now smooth + comb-free. | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-26 (path A + adaptive-res-off) |
| EBEVELCRASH | input_viewport.rs:856,882 (start guards) → tool_mode.rs:96 (assert) | **CRASH (P1):** `start_operation(Bevel) called while Push/Pull is active` panic (confirmed via fourthlayer_panic.txt) when using the E tool (FacePushPull) on a box with edge bevel. ROOT CAUSE: the bevel-drag-START and falloff-drag-START `else if` branches were guarded only by `!is_gizmo() && !is_create()` — that guard predates the E-tool's `FacePushPull` (added in ELONG2). During a Push/Pull drag the cursor crosses a bevel edge (sets `hovered_bevel_edge`), the leading `if is_bevel()` is false, so the bevel-START branch fires `start_operation` while a transient op is active → trips the dev `debug_assert!` in `start_operation`. FIX (class-level, not instance): both start guards changed to `!self.tool.current.is_busy()` (= `!is_idle()`, covers every active op). `FacePushPull` clears on pointer-up (input_viewport.rs:1228) so a genuine fresh press is idle and the drag still starts. Assert kept intact (the caller violation is fixed, not silenced). NOT related to the G2/G3 GPU-mesh work (CPU tool-state-machine, no GPU). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-24 |

# SDF MODELING TOOLS — 2026-06-20
# Build-verified (`cargo check -p app` green). Runtime-unverified — user testing.
# ════════════════════════════════════════

| # | File:Line | Description | Status |
|---|-----------|-------------|--------|
| ELONG2 | face_ops.rs (try_start_box_face_extrude), input_viewport.rs (gizmo mouse-down) | E face-extrude on a BOX now resizes `half_extents` (via the proven `apply_face_drag`), not `elongation`. Elongation could only GROW (clamped ≥0; shader ignores negatives) and the bevel cage — drawn from `half_extents` — didn't follow it. So grabbing an Elongate face dot on a box now starts a FacePushPull on that face: `half_extents` grows AND shrinks (pull a face IN past original size; min 0.01), recenters to anchor the opposite face, is NOT `scale` (bevel + other tools stay valid), and the cage follows. On start it also folds any legacy `elongation` into `half_extents` (same size) so a box grown by the OLD path stops showing a too-small cage. Non-box prims keep the elongation path. Reuses face_ops — no duplicated resize math. | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-20 (runtime-unverified) |
| ELONG1 | gizmo.rs (apply_to_sdf_prim — graph mirror), transform.rs (compute_transform Elongate) | E (Elongate→face EXTRUDE) tool. (Superseded for BOXES by ELONG2; the graph-mirror fix still applies to non-box elongation.) **ROOT CAUSE (the actual bug under everything):** `apply_to_sdf_prim` wrote the new `elongation` only to the FLAT cache, and `write_prim_transform` mirrors ONLY pos/rot/scale to the scene graph — but the GPU bake serializes from the GRAPH. So the elongation change NEVER reached the baked surface: at first "E did nothing"; once a position offset was added it looked like the cube just TRANSLATED and wouldn't reverse. Fix #1: mirror `elongation` to the graph in `apply_to_sdf_prim` (the comment there falsely claimed write_prim_transform did it). Now elongation actually changes the rendered volume. Fix #2 (the tool itself): per-face EXTRUDE via elongation (NOT scale → keeps bevel/other tools valid). Grab a face dot, pull by world dist `disp` (drag projected onto the axis, camera-aware; ±faces sign-flipped); grow symmetric `elongation` by disp/(2·scale) so the grabbed face follows the cursor, then recenter the prim by (Δelong·scale) so the OPPOSITE face stays exactly put at any prim scale. Reversible. Threaded `elongate_face_negative` through `TransformInput` (9 sites). NOTE: world-axis offset assumes an unrotated body (rotated-body extrude is a known follow-up). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-20 (runtime-unverified) |

Cheap path on drag, smoothed pass on release. 4 new tests (T1 parity, T2 incremental==full, T3 occupancy-flips, T4 res-reset) — 11/11 green. **Limit:** `cell_slot` is a persistent dense alloc (~28 MB @192³, alongside grid density); 512³+ needs the future chunked/sparse path.
