| VXLIT | graphics/src/deferred_entry.wgsl (LIT_BRANCH ~240/255/287) | Voxel mesh **fully black in Lit mode**. Root cause (wf_afb59657): the raster pass writes 4 G-buffer color targets but NOT gbuf_surface_id (SDF compute writes that, and a voxel scene has 0 SDF prims → stale id). The Lit `light_linked(lit_sid, li)` gate then rejected EVERY light → only ~0 ambient survived. Fix: route raster pixels through the existing `0xFFFFFFFFu` "no-SDF-prim / all-lights" sentinel (`lit_sid = select(lit_sid_raw, 0xFFFFFFFFu, lit_is_raster)`) + skip the SDF shadow/AO recompute for raster pixels (they carry a baked shadow-map value). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-14 |
| VXSOLID | graphics/src/deferred_entry.wgsl (SHADOW_AO ~448) | Voxel **fully black in Solid (& dark in PBR)**. Root cause: the deferred SHADOW_AO block recomputed shadow/AO with `soft_shadow`/`calc_ao` (SDF scene queries) for raster pixels; against an empty prim buffer they return degenerate values that multiply `solid_hdr_color` to black. Fix: gate the recompute on `!is_raster_pixel` so raster pixels keep their shadow-map `shadow_ao`. SDF pixels still recompute (no regression). Both fixes in ONE deferred_entry.wgsl edit; `cargo test -p graphics` 36/36 (incl. df_full/df_lite Naga). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-14 |
| VXPT | graphics/src/glsl/pathtrace_primary_full.comp (~1146), pathtrace_primary.spv | Voxel **absent in Path-Tracing** (whole viewport = background). Root cause: the PT primary pass unconditionally cleared the G-buffer on a scene_bvh miss, clobbering the raster voxel — it declared `raster_depth_in` (binding 29) but, unlike the two raymarch shaders (raymarch_entry.wgsl:180, raymarch_bvh_full.comp:1701), never checked `raster_dist`. **FIXED:** installed glslangValidator (v16.3.0, local %LOCALAPPDATA%\glslang); ported the raster-preserve guard (sample raster_dist before the march, early-break past it, and `if (raster_dist>0 && (!hit||t>raster_dist)) return;` before the miss-clear) — verbatim parity with raymarch_bvh_full. Recompiled pathtrace_primary.spv (`glslangValidator --target-env vulkan1.0 -S comp`). Restores **primary-hit visibility** (voxel appears, shaded by the bounce pass). **Known limit:** full PT participation (voxel casting PT shadows / in reflections/GI) needs a triangle-mesh BVH (ImportedMesh isn't serialized into the prim/BVH buffers — serialize.rs collects only SdfBody) — separate future feature. | VXTDR | viewport_render.rs (resolve_render_mode) | **Path-Tracing a voxel object crashed the VIEWPORT (GPU device loss / TDR)** — not an app panic. Root cause (wf_c1da3235): a voxel scene has ZERO SDF prims (the voxel is a raster ImportedMesh), but selecting PT still dispatched the SDF path tracer on the empty scene; the GPU ran past the driver watchdog → TDR → wgpu lost the device → viewport dead (UI survives). Fix: gate `if shading_mode==PathTrace && nv > 0` — PT only runs when SDF geometry exists; a voxel/raster-only scene falls through to the Hybrid raster path (voxel still visible, just not path-traced — it can't be without a triangle BVH anyway). | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-14 |
| VXROTLAG | viewport_render.rs (resolve_render_mode) | **Persistent lag when orbiting a voxel** + wasted per-frame work. Root cause: `use_lite` hard-requires `nv > 0`, so a voxel scene (nv==0) was excluded from the light path and fell to AnalyticalMarch/Full EVERY frame — a full-screen raymarch of an EMPTY SDF scene on top of the raster pass + deferred + post. Orbit marks RENDER every frame, so it never idled out. Fix: `if nv == 0 { return AnalyticalLite }` (after the volume check) — the lite pipeline writes only background+floor (no marching) and already handles raster meshes; the raster pass draws the voxel. Removes the empty per-frame march. | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-14 |
| VXBGFLICK | viewport_render.rs (resolve_render_mode) | **Background flickered when orbiting a voxel.** Highest-confidence root cause: the raster pass clears the whole G-buffer each frame and the SDF march was the only thing repainting the background, so on mode-transition frames (march↔full) the deferred read "cleared = black". Largely fixed by VXROTLAG: forcing a single stable mode (AnalyticalLite) for nv==0 removes the per-frame march↔full transitions, so the background is repainted consistently. **Residual:** a possible one-frame flash at the instant orbit begins (half-res latch transition) — robust fix is G-buffer ownership (raster `LoadOp::Load` or a dedicated RasterOnly pass), deferred as a careful follow-up since that clear affects ALL scenes. 🔧 PARTIAL (transition flicker fixed; instant-of-orbit flash = follow-up) |

| VXSHADEFLIP | input_sculpt.rs (handle_voxel_sculpt_input), voxel_sculpt.rs (cell_surface_vertex) | While sculpting, the WHOLE surface's shading flipped faceted→smooth on every stroke release — the live drag used the cheap mesh (tight normals, no relaxation) and only the release applied the smooth pass. Fix: `cell_surface_vertex` now computes a WIDE-stencil normal (gradient_normal at 1.5·voxel — same 6-sample cost as the old tight normal_at), so the live drag is already smooth and matches the released mesh. | VXRESCAN | input_sculpt.rs (handle_voxel_sculpt_input) | **THE stroke "choke" (600ms spikes).** Profiler (user) showed `update(): 600ms (input=598ms, mesh=0.2ms)` — the lag was NOT meshing/upload, it was the INPUT phase. Root cause: when the cursor is held still mid-drag, no stamps apply → `grid.take_dirty()` returns None → the code passed None to `mesh_cache.update()`, which means "full rebuild" = a full **O(res³) re-scan** of the whole grid (~7M cells @192³ ≈ 600ms). Fix: only update+build when `take_dirty()` is Some (something actually changed); skip the re-mesh entirely otherwise. Eliminates the spike AND skips redundant builds on still frames. A 4-line fix — NOT the chunking refactor we thought we needed. | ✅ FIXED 2026-06-14 |

**PERF ROADMAP — reaching 3D-Coat-level (millions of polys) [P-A done; P-B DEPRIORITIZED]:**
> NOTE: Profiler proved the meshing/upload is already fast (`mesh=0.2ms`/frame). The stroke lag was the VXRESCAN full-rescan bug (now fixed), NOT mesh perf. P-B (chunked meshing) is now a **forward-looking** optimization for the steady-state `build()` on genuinely large meshes (user opted to build it anyway).
> - **P-B foundation: DONE 2026-06-14.** `VoxelGrid::mesh_region(a0, a1)` (voxel_sculpt.rs) meshes a cell sub-range into a self-contained sub-mesh with a duplicate-boundary halo (gap-free seams). 2 tests: whole-range == surface_nets parity; two chunks cover every quad exactly once. The hard part (seam correctness) is proven.
> - **VXSNAP — high-res sculpt freeze (undo capture was O(brush-box) + per-voxel HashMap): FIXED 2026-06-14.** Profiler at 192³ showed `mesh=0.1ms` but `input=20–80ms` steady with **2–4 SECOND** spikes. Root cause (read from code): the profiler `mesh` bucket only covers GPU upload; the entire voxel sculpt path is in `input`. There, `snapshot_brush` walked the whole brush **bounding box** (~440k voxels at 192³, ~half outside the brush) and the caller did a `HashMap` hash-probe per voxel, per stamp, per frame — a fast drag (up to 48 stamps) = ~20M HashMap ops → multi-second freeze. Fix: (1) new `StrokeRecorder` (core_math) captures pre-values via a **dense visited mask** (O(1), no hashing/rehash spikes); (2) folded capture INTO `apply_brush` so only ACTUALLY-modified voxels are recorded (kills the redundant full-box snapshot pass); (3) replaced the fast-drag fallback (`pts = vec![sample]` → collapsed fast strokes to one point/gaps) with a per-frame **voxel budget** (4M) that evenly subsamples stamps to bound total work. Voxel path uses new `voxel_stroke`; legacy cpu_volume path keeps `current_stroke` (untouched). Gated `[VOXEL] stamps=/brush=/remesh=` diag (>8ms only). check=0, 13/13 tests. *Per-stamp cost is still O(brush-box) — irreducible for dense CPU voxels; this removes 2 redundant box passes + the HashMap (~3× steady + no freezes). Further = GPU brush (future).*
> - **VXCLEANUP — diagnostics + dead `mesh_cache` removed: 2026-06-15.** Stripped all session diagnostic logging (`[VXCHUNK]`, `[VOXEL]`, `[WSPANEL]`/`[WSPANEL-INNER]`, the `lt!` `[LAYOUT]` macro + its panel wraps). Removed the dead `VoxelObject.mesh_cache: VoxelMeshCache` field (write-only since the chunk path landed — Explore-agent verified no reads); `voxel_create` now builds the node's initial single mesh straight from `grid.mesh_region(whole)` instead of a `VoxelMeshCache`. Kept `mesh_id` (load-bearing — see below). `bench_mesh_region_192` kept (`#[ignore]`, silent). check=0, 14/14 tests.
> - **VXSAVE — ⚠️ OPEN: sculpting is LOST on save/reload (data loss, pre-existing).** The voxel node's single mesh (`mesh_id`) is what gets serialized (the live `VoxelObject` — grid + chunks — is NOT persisted; reload turns the voxel into a static `ImportedMesh`). But sculpting + resample only update the CHUNK meshes, never `mesh_id` — so `mesh_id` stays the INITIAL 64³ sphere. Save → reload shows the initial sphere, not the sculpt. (Deleting the crashing `voxel_remesh` made this strictly worse — it used to refresh `mesh_id` on release, albeit from a stale cache.) Proper fix: on SAVE (one-shot, a brief pause is fine), rebuild `mesh_id` from `grid.mesh_region(whole)` so the persisted mesh matches the live surface. ✅ FIXED 2026-06-15: new `voxel_sync_node_mesh()` rebuilds `mesh_id` from `grid.mesh_region(whole)`, called before every `ProjectFile::from_app` (save_scene, save_as_default_scene, check_auto_save, Export JSON). Save/reload now preserves the sculpt. check=0, 14/14 tests. *Note: at high res the bake is ~0.5s; on auto-save (every 120s, only while scene_modified) that's an occasional brief hitch — make it async if it annoys.*
> - **VXPICK — ⚠️ OPEN: GPU picking uses the stale single mesh (pre-existing).** `raster_render.rs:~650` picking dispatch uses the node's `mesh_cache_id` (frozen initial sphere) with no `is_voxel`/chunk check, while rendering uses chunks — so click-to-select on a sculpted voxel hits stale geometry. Fix: mirror the render path's `is_voxel` chunk branch in the picking dispatch. ✅ FIXED 2026-06-15: the picking gather (`raster_render.rs`) now special-cases the voxel node and pushes a pick draw-call per non-empty CHUNK (same node id) instead of the single mesh — so click-to-select hits the live sculpted surface. mesh_id is now used ONLY for save/load. check=0, 14/14 tests.
> - **VXTARGET — activating sculpt grabbed the "first"/existing voxel, not the selected object: FIXED 2026-06-15.** User: "when i activated sculpt when selecting an object it is the first object that got the sculpt capacity not the selected one." Root cause: `enter_sculpt_mode` never consulted the selection — it unconditionally did `if self.voxel.is_none() { voxel_create() }`, so with a voxel already present it silently re-entered that one (the "first object"), and with none present it spawned a default sphere at the workplane — either way ignoring which node the user picked. Fix: `enter_sculpt_mode` (workspace.rs) is selection-aware but **non-blocking** — it ALWAYS switches into the sculpt layout (`work_mode=Sculpt`, Hybrid render, ensure a voxel exists), then classifies the selection only to add an informational toast: SDF selected → "voxelizing the selected SDF to sculpt it is coming — editing a voxel object for now"; mesh (polygon/imported/NURBS) → "surface-sculpting the selected mesh is coming …". The conversion/surface tools are future work. **Regression caught same day:** the first version *gated* entry on the route (toasted "coming soon" and never switched mode) — user reported "this is not activating the sculpt mode, this should bring the user to the sculpt layout." Corrected so entry is unconditional and the toast is advisory only. Also added the **SCULPT entry to the Poly tab-pie** (idx 4, key "5", 🧊): `pie_menu.rs` poly def + `tab_desc_poly`; `menus.rs apply_tab_pie_mode` Poly arm dispatches idx 4 → `enter_sculpt_mode`; `input_keyboard.rs` now derives the pie's `n_items` from the active def (was hardcoded 4) so the 5-item Poly pie lays out/hit-tests correctly. check=0.
> - **VXBORDER — hollow/open surface where a sculpted shape reaches the grid boundary: FIXED 2026-06-15.** User: a tube grown toward the camera came out as a hollow open-ended cylinder; same with GPU mesh OFF (so not the GPU path) and zoom-out didn't fix it (so not near-plane clipping) → camera-independent mesh bug. Root cause: Surface Nets only emits a face where density CROSSES the iso level. The brush could write density right up to the outermost grid layer; at the grid edge there is no cell beyond it to cross into "air", so geometry touching the boundary has no transition → the surface stays OPEN there (un-capped). "Toward the camera" just meant the user happened to push into a grid face. Fix: `brush_aabb` now clamps writes to `[1, res-2]`, keeping a 1-cell **sealed empty border** so the mesher always finds a solid→air crossing at the edge → watertight cap. 23/23 core_math tests, check=0. *Note: pre-existing geometry already written into the border stays open until re-sculpted; the fix prevents NEW boundary holes. Future hardening: auto-grow the volume (3D-Coat style) instead of a fixed sealed border.*
> - **VXINFLATE-FREEZE — Inflate brush stalls the frame (profiler: brush 244ms pk 293ms / 2 stamps): MITIGATED 2026-06-15.** The sculpt profiler localized it to the BRUSH phase (mesh was normal ~10ms). Cause: Inflate is a "snapshot brush" — it took a full pre-stamp density SNAPSHOT (an extra O(box) pass + alloc) plus a per-voxel 6-neighbour read, ~3× a plain deposit; at large radius × high res that's huge, and the per-frame voxel budget *under-counted* it (estimated the cost of a simple deposit) so it didn't subsample enough → pile-up/freeze. Fixes: (1) **Inflate now reads its gradient from the LIVE grid** (central difference via `at`, 0 outside) instead of a snapshot — the mild order dependence is invisible for a puff and it drops the whole snapshot pass + alloc (~halves cost); snapshot now only for Smooth/Pinch (+ `Vec::with_capacity`). (2) **Budget is brush-cost-aware**: `per_stamp *= {Pinch 4, Smooth 3, Inflate 2, else 1}` so expensive brushes subsample to stay bounded instead of freezing. 23/23 core_math tests (Inflate still correct), app check=0. **This is a CPU mitigation, not the cure** — a big-radius dense-grid brush is fundamentally heavy on CPU; the GPU compute pipeline (design workflow in progress) is the real fix.
> - **VXTEAR — chunk seams TEAR / holes when sculpting across a chunk boundary: FIXED 2026-06-15.** User (screenshot): a deep carve produced a torn surface with a chunk-sized hole exposing the interior. Root cause in `voxel_chunks_for_region` (input_sculpt.rs): a chunk's Surface-Nets mesh depends on a **±1 cell halo** around its anchor range — `mesh_region` reads the −1 low halo (`vx0 = a0-1`) AND the +1 corner of its last cell (`density[idx(cx+1,…)]` at `cx=a1`). The per-stamp dirty-chunk marking only expanded the region on the **min** side (`lo` used `v-1`); the **max** side (`hi`) wasn't expanded. So editing the LAST cell of a chunk never marked the NEXT chunk (which reads that cell as its low halo) → that neighbour's seam/surface stayed stale → torn seam, and (when carving through a previously-solid interior chunk) a full hole. Fix: expand the chunk span by +1 on the high side too — `hi(v) = (v.min(cmax)+1)/VOXEL_CHUNK` — giving symmetric ±1 coverage that exactly matches the halo dependency. 2 regression tests (`edit_marks_neighbour_chunk_on_both_boundaries`, `region_stays_in_bounds_at_grid_max`) lock it — both fail against the old code. Pre-existing (chunk infra predates the brush work); surfaced now via deep carves. Affects ALL brushes (shared marking path). check=0, app tests pass.
> - **VXRESAMPLE-STALL — the "tool_strip 1.5s freeze" was `resample()` on the UI thread: FIXED 2026-06-15.** A 3-step instrument chain (`lt!` layout sections → `[WSPANEL]` per-panel → `[WSPANEL-INNER]` content-vs-machinery) localized the recurring multi-second `layout`/`tool_strip` stall (present since the session's FIRST log) to: `[WSPANEL-INNER] Tools content render = 1397ms`. Root cause: the resolution buttons live in the sculpt Tools panel; clicking one runs `voxel_resample_to`, which called `v.grid.resample(new_res)` **synchronously on the UI thread** — trilinear-rebuilding a 192³ density grid (~7M samples) = 0.6–1.4s, executing right inside the panel's button handler. The VXBGMESH worker only meshed the *result*; the resample itself was still on the UI thread. So the "GPU stall" was never GPU — it was CPU resample in egui's draw, and it appeared "during sculpting" because the user was clicking resolution presets. Fix: `voxel_resample_to` now clones only the OLD grid (cheap) and the worker does resample + `surface_chunk_mask` + meshing, streaming `Total → Chunk* → Grid` (grid moved last, no clone) via `VoxelRebuildMsg`; `PendingVoxelRebuild.grid/total` are `Option` (filled as they arrive); swap fires when grid + all chunks land. Progress bar shows indeterminate "Remeshing…" during the resample phase, then fills. UI thread now does ~0 work for a resolution change. check=0, 14/14 tests.
> - **VXBGMESH — resolution rebuild moved to a worker thread (UI no longer stalls / CPU spike): 2026-06-15.** After the crash fix, a high-res resample still ran the rebuild meshing on the UI thread (`mesh=14ms`/frame sustained for ~50 frames = the "cpu warning", plus it fed GPU-upload bursts that worsened the pre-existing `tool_strip` GPU stalls). Per user choice, moved meshing OFF the UI thread: `voxel_resample_to` clones the new grid (VoxelGrid now `#[derive(Clone)]`), spawns a `std::thread` that meshes the surface chunks and streams `(chunk_idx, verts, idx)` over an mpsc channel; `PendingVoxelRebuild` holds the `Receiver` + `done`/`total`. `voxel_flush_pending_rebuild` no longer meshes — it just `try_recv`s ≤24 chunks/frame, uploads each (cheap), and swaps atomically when `done >= total` (old surface renders throughout; old buffers freed via `mesh_cache.remove`). Worker stops if the receiver is dropped (a newer resample supersedes it). Net: UI thread stays responsive during a high-res rebuild (no meshing on it), progress bar driven by `done/total`. check=0, 14/14 tests. *Total CPU is unchanged (a worker core does the meshing); GPU-upload stalls, if any persist, are the separate pre-existing backpressure issue.*
> - **VXCRASH — index OOB crash after resolution change (`voxel_sculpt.rs:862`, len 32768/idx 32782): FIXED 2026-06-15.** `panicked: index out of bounds: len is 32768 but index is 32782` (32768=32³, idx 32782 = z=32, one slice past a res-32 grid). Root cause: the DEAD single-mesh path. `voxel_remesh()` (called on stroke release) did `v.mesh_cache.build(&v.grid)`, but `v.mesh_cache` (a `VoxelMeshCache`) is never updated after `voxel_create` — so after a resolution change `v.grid` is the new res while the cache holds the OLD res's cell indices → `build()` indexes the new grid's density with old-res cells → OOB. The chunked path renders the surface; this single mesh was never even displayed. Fix: deleted `voxel_remesh()` and its stroke-release call (the chunked path already keeps every touched chunk current with smooth normals during the drag — nothing needed on release). The only remaining `VoxelMeshCache::build` is in `voxel_create` on a FRESH cache (res matches) → safe. Also lowered the rebuild drain `FRAME_BUDGET_MS` 22→14 so a high-res rebuild doesn't peg a core at 100% (the "cpu warning"); sculpt edits (~8 chunks) still drain in one frame. check=0. *TODO: remove the now-create-only `mesh_cache`/`mesh_id` dead fields entirely (verify save/load first) to eliminate the landmine class.*
> - **VXRESSWAP — resolution change "loads by chunk" (visible pop-in): FIXED 2026-06-15.** After the speed fix the rebuild was fast (~0.6s) but still visibly filled in chunk-by-chunk (the old surface was cleared, then new chunks popped in). User wanted both: keep the old model + a progress bar. Implemented a deferred-swap rebuild: `VoxelObject.pending_rebuild: Option<PendingVoxelRebuild>` holds the new-resolution grid + freshly-alloc'd chunk ids + the surface-chunk queue. `voxel_resample_to` builds it OFF-SCREEN (the live grid/chunks keep rendering); `voxel_flush_pending_rebuild` (priority branch in the flush) meshes its surface chunks time-budgeted, and on the last chunk **swaps grid/chunks/chunk_dim/chunk_tris in atomically + frees the old buffers via `mesh_cache.remove`** — so the change reads as one instant quality upgrade, never a pop-in or disappear. A "Remeshing NN%" bar (driven by `total - queue.len()`) draws over the live surface in `draw_viewport_overlays`. Sculpting is gated off while pending (the live grid is about to be replaced). check=0, 14/14 tests.
> - **VXRESFREEZE — resolution change freezes the UI ~2.4s: FIXED 2026-06-15.** The periodic `layout=2398ms` spikes turned out NOT to be a panel/GPU stall — `[LAYOUT] total=2397ms` fired with no section flagged, and the user identified the trigger: **changing the voxel resolution**. Root cause: Ctrl+R → `voxel_resample_to` → `voxel_build_all_chunks`, which meshed ALL ~1728 chunks (16³) **synchronously** in one call (~2.4s); since "Apply" runs inside the remesh popup's panel draw, the cost landed in the `layout` bucket (which is why the section timers — placed around the *other* panels — missed it), and the magnitude scaled with target res (90ms→2400ms). Fix: `voxel_build_all_chunks` now allocs chunk ids, zeroes tris, and **queues every chunk** (`dirty_chunks.extend(0..n)`) instead of meshing inline — the existing `voxel_flush_dirty_chunks` drains it at ≤16/frame, so the surface fills in progressively (~1s) while the app stays responsive (Frame Budget Rule). Resample toast → "Remeshing to N³…". **Follow-up (same day): the progressive rebuild felt slow (~1.8s, chunks popping one-at-a-time) because it meshed ALL ~1712 chunks — but ~1300 are empty interior/exterior (a sphere's surface is a thin shell). Added `VoxelGrid::surface_chunk_mask(chunk_size)`: one cheap sequential pass over the density grid computes per-chunk min/max and flags only chunks whose own cells or a face-neighbour's straddle iso (conservative → a flagged-false chunk is GUARANTEED to mesh empty; proven by `surface_chunk_mask_skips_only_empty_chunks`). `voxel_build_all_chunks` now queues only flagged chunks (~450-700 vs 1712), and `voxel_flush_dirty_chunks` switched to a 22ms TIME-BUDGET drain (small sculpt edits drain fully under budget = zero latency; rebuild fills as fast as the budget allows). ~2-3× faster rebuild. check=0, 14/14 tests.** *Floor is now the ~450 real surface chunks × ~1ms; below that needs a GPU mesher or a per-chunk incremental cache. If still too poppy, add a progress indicator.*
> - **VXFREEZE — fast-flick re-meshes the whole grid (1.8s freeze): FIXED 2026-06-15.** Live `[VXCHUNK]` after the 16³ change exposed two things: (a) shrinking chunks 32→16 did NOT cut the steady cost — per-chunk dropped 8× (8.8→1.1ms) but the brush now straddles 8 chunks instead of 1-4, so the total stayed ~9ms; (b) a fast flick produced `n=1728 mesh_region=1788ms` — re-meshing EVERY chunk. Root cause: the per-frame re-mesh used `take_dirty()`'s accumulated **bounding box**; a stroke across the model makes that box span the whole grid, so we re-scanned all 1728 chunks incl. the ~1300 empty ones. Fix: **chunk-level dirty tracking** — the brush queues only the chunks each STAMP passes through (`voxel_mark_chunks_in_region` per stamp, not the frame's AABB), drained at **≤16 chunks/frame** (`voxel_flush_dirty_chunks`, called in the per-frame mesh pass) so no frame does unbounded work (Frame Budget Rule). New `VoxelObject.dirty_chunks: HashSet<u32>`; undo marks via the same path; `voxel_build_all_chunks` clears the queue (synchronous full rebuild). Kept 16³ (steady ≤8 chunks ≈ 9ms, better than 32³'s 35ms worst). check=0, 13/13 tests. *Steady ~9ms remains (8 chunks × ~1.1ms cold); deeper fix = per-chunk incremental cache (mesh only dirty cells).*
> - **VXCHUNK — per-chunk re-mesh too slow (oversized chunk scan): FIXED 2026-06-14.** After VXSNAP, the live `[VOXEL]` diag showed `brush=0.0ms` (undo fix worked) but `remesh=8.8/17.7/35ms` stepping per chunk touched. Investigated with a core_math CPU benchmark (no GPU): `mesh_region` scans the WHOLE `(chunk+1)³` cell range every time a chunk is touched, regardless of edit size — the cost is the **cell scan**, NOT the normal (corner-gradient vs wide-stencil = only 3%, so kept the smoother wide-stencil) and NOT cache (a cache-local buffer was net-NEGATIVE due to alloc, reverted). Per small-brush edit @192³ (opt-3): **32³=5.8ms** (≈ live 8.8ms at opt-2, 4 chunks touched), **16³=0.84ms (7×)**, 8³=0.23ms. Fix: `VOXEL_CHUNK` 32→**16** so a re-meshed chunk ≈ brush-sized (~1.7k chunks for 192³ vs 8³'s 13.8k buffers). Also folded undo capture into `apply_brush` and split `cell_surface_vertex` into `cell_surface_pos_d` + wide-stencil normal (reuse). Kept a gated `[VXCHUNK] mesh_region=/update_mesh=` split timer to confirm live. check=0, 13/13 tests. *Deeper win available later: per-chunk incremental cache (mesh only dirty cells, not the whole touched chunk).*
> - **P-B integration: DONE 2026-06-14.** VoxelObject gained `chunk_dim`/`chunks`/`chunk_tris` (32-cell chunks). `voxel_build_all_chunks` (create/clear/resample) meshes every chunk; `voxel_remesh_dirty_chunks(region)` (the per-frame sculpt hot path + undo) re-meshes ONLY the chunks the brush touched via `mesh_region` → per-chunk `update_editable_mesh` (P-A persistent buffers, O(brush) upload). raster_render.rs draws the voxel node's non-empty chunks (one draw each). `MAX_MESH_UPLOADS_PER_FRAME` raised 2→64. Duplicate re-extracts the whole grid via mesh_region. Build-verified (app=0, 13/13 voxel tests). **Per-frame sculpt cost now scales with the brush, not the total surface — the 3D-Coat scaling goal.** *Minor cleanup left: the old single-mesh path (mesh_id + VoxelMeshCache field) is now dead during sculpt — voxel_remesh on release still does a harmless wasted build; remove the dead single-mesh path in a follow-up.*

The incremental mesher made the *re-scan* O(brush³), but two things still run over the WHOLE mesh every frame: (1) `build()` rebuilds the full flat vertex+index array (~115k verts @192³); (2) `GpuMesh::upload_raw` (mesh_gpu.rs:83) RECREATES both GPU buffers via `create_buffer_init` every frame (~9MB alloc/frame @192³). This caps interactive poly count far below 3D-Coat (4M+/layer). The fix is two staged pieces:
- **P-A: Persistent GPU buffers** — ✅ DONE 2026-06-14. `GpuMesh` is now capacity-backed (COPY_DST); `update_raw` rewrites in place via `queue.write_buffer` and only recreates buffers when the data outgrows capacity (grow to next power-of-two). `upload_pending` updates the existing mesh in place instead of `create_buffer_init` every frame. Killed the ~9MB/frame allocation churn at 192³ (the per-frame stall). Files: render/mesh_gpu.rs (GpuMesh + update_raw), render/mesh_cache.rs (upload_pending +queue), 4 callers (main/project_load/raster_render×2). Build-verified (render+app=0). *(Still re-uploads the full mesh bandwidth each frame — partial-range upload comes with P-B chunking.)*
- **P-B: Chunked meshing** — split the grid into fixed chunks; only re-mesh + re-upload the chunk(s) the brush touches (1-handful, not the whole surface). Per-frame cost scales with the BRUSH, not the total poly count — the 3D-Coat model. Touches VoxelMeshCache (per-chunk buffers) + the voxel node (multi-mesh) + raster draw. Seams via 1-cell chunk overlap.
Do P-A first (contained, big alloc win), then P-B (the real ceiling-breaker). 📋 BACKLOG (focused perf session)

**Follow-ups surfaced by review wf_794ef7b5 (pre-existing / out-of-scope, NOT regressions):**
- **IMPORTEDAABB** — ImportedMesh selection bbox is hardcoded `(-0.5..0.5)` for ALL imported meshes, not the real mesh extent. Affects File>Import meshes (voxel now suppressed). Fix: compute AABB from cached mesh verts or store one on insert_imported. 📋 BACKLOG
- **MESHCACHELEAK** — Undo of any alloc_id+insert_imported (voxel_create, VXDUP) orphans the mesh_cache entry (harmless: unreachable node never renders). Robust fix = reachability sweep pruning unreferenced mesh ids on undo/redo. ⏸️ DEFERRED
- **MODALGIZMOPARITY** — confirm_modal_transform (prim branch) calls recalculate_body_origin; finish_gizmo_drag (prim branch) does not (pre-dates these fixes; tension with H1.6 "no origin recalc on prim move"). Decide canonical policy + apply to both; ideally extract shared `finish_node_or_prim_transform`. ⏸️ DEFERRED
- **VXPRESSURE** — Tablet pressure→size/strength: apply path wired (`strength * pt.pressure`), source not built. Design in SCULPT_BRUSH_PLAN.md Phase 2 (PressureSource + Windows-Ink WM_POINTER bridge + PressureMap curve). 📋 BACKLOG
- **VXREMESH-UNDO** — Remesh/resolution change is destructive and wipes the voxel undo stack (necessary: density deltas are keyed to grid indices that change on resample). Popup warns "Resets sculpt undo". Proper undo needs a full-grid snapshot entry (different from the delta model) — out of scope for v1. 📋 BACKLOG

| KNIFECYCLICRUN | knife.rs:~506 (run walk / node stream) | Owner "the slice is a basic operation and must never fail" — `KNIFE FAIL.fl4` (rect slice) saved a mesh with TWO 16-gons carrying repeated vertices (`[…5,37,5,6,31,29,31,6…]`) and 2 COINCIDENT vertex clusters; `is_manifold()` = "degenerate face 0: repeated vertex 5". **Root cause: the run walk treats a CLOSED path's node stream as LINEAR.** A rect whose top side leaves the silhouette classifies as `I…B, BRK, B…I` — the off-surface side is a Break sitting BETWEEN the two edge crossings, so the real cut chain WRAPS around index 0. The linear scan (`while ci < pe.len()`) saw two runs, each with a single Bound anchor, and degraded the one through-cut into TWO DANGLING SLITS (face never divided = "the slice does nothing"); each half then re-materialised the closed polyline's first==last corner via `PE::Interior`'s unconditional fresh-position push → the coincident duplicate pair. Fix: when `closed`, rotate `nodes` left past the LAST Break so the wrap-around run is contiguous, then re-dedup consecutive nodes (the rotation is what makes the duplicated terminal pair adjacent). Verified against a NEW Blender oracle `docs/planning/poly/knife_rect_notch_oracle.py` (EXACT DIFFERENCE of the equivalent prism: nv=16 nf=10 pinched=0 coincident=0 boundary=0 non_manifold=0 arity{4:8,8:2} vol=0.760) — our slice now satisfies all three owner invariants and DIVIDES both notched sheets (`AZRA_KNIFE_DIAG` went from `head-slit`+`tail-slit` to one `through 4->5 span=13`). # ════════════════════════════════════════
# 30-AGENT PERFORMANCE AUDIT — 2026-03-23
# ════════════════════════════════════════

## Scope
Deployed 30 parallel agents to audit rendering performance across the entire
pipeline: WGSL shaders, GLSL BVH kernel, viewport dispatch, GPU synchronization,
and deferred shading. Target: match SDF Modeler's orbit smoothness at 51K prims
on RTX 4090.

## FIXES IMPLEMENTED (8)

| # | File:Line | Description | Status |
|---|-----------|-------------|--------|
| P1 | viewport_render.rs:728 | `device.poll(Wait)` blocks CPU until GPU done — prevents CPU/GPU pipelining. Changed to `Poll` (non-blocking). | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-23 |
| P2 | raymarch_entry.wgsl:48 | `step_mult` too conservative (0.7/0.6) — wastes march steps. Bumped to 0.85/0.7/0.5 by quality tier. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-23 |
| P3 | raymarch_march.wgsl:25 | Same `step_mult` conservatism in lean march kernel. Bumped to match. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-23 |
| P4 | raymarch_entry.wgsl:127 | Curvature (24 SDF evals) computed unconditionally even when matcap edge detection off. Gated behind `config.matcap_edge_enabled`. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-23 |
| P5 | viewport_render.rs:533 | `interaction_no_shadows` uniform was dead (always 0) — PBR paid full shadow cost during orbit/pan. Wired to 1 during `interaction_active`. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-23 |

| K122 | sdf_shared.wgsl, raymarch_bvh_full.comp, shader_build.rs | **Architecture fix: g_cull references removed from scene_analytical() permanently.** Root cause of 3 prior shader crashes: `scene_analytical()` referenced `g_cull_active`/`g_cull_mask` inside `#region RAY_CULL` tags. Different shader builds strip different regions — any build that stripped the declaration but kept the reference crashed. Previous fixes (bandaids) moved declarations outside regions or added flag gates. **Proper fix:** (1) `scene_analytical()` now has ZERO cull references — evaluates all prims unconditionally. (2) `scene_culled_analytical()` is a separate copy of the eval loop WITH cull check, living entirely inside `#region RAY_CULL`. (3) `g_cull_active` deleted — culled/uncullled split makes it unnecessary. (4) `g_cull_mask` declaration moved inside `#region RAY_CULL` — stripped atomically with all users. (5) Build-time validation `validate_no_dangling_region_refs()` panics if any stripped shader references undeclared cull symbols. (6) Same split applied to GLSL: `scene_culled_analytical_range`, `scene_culled_analytical`, `scene_bvh_culled`. CLAUDE.md updated with architecture rule. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-26 |

# SESSION 2026-03-26f — TDR Crash Fix (Naga Inlining Explosion)

## Root Cause Analysis

`apply_boolean_blend` calls `smin_noisy`→`eval_blend_noise`→`fbm_wgsl` (4-octave FBM with 3D noise). Naga inlines ALL WGSL function calls when translating to SPIR-V — this chain creates exponential code growth. NVIDIA Vulkan driver takes 5+ minutes and 19+ GB RAM to compile the resulting SPIR-V, triggering Windows TDR (exit code 0xcfffffff) or OOM. Affects ALL WGSL shader builds (RM, DF-full, DF-lite, PT, fog, volume bake). GLSL BVH path is unaffected (real function calls, no inlining).

Initial misdiagnosis: believed to be DF-full-specific compilation time on cold cache. Multiple guard approaches tried (empty encoder, device.poll, synchronous compilation) — all failed because the root cause was in every WGSL shader, not just DF-full.

## FIXES IMPLEMENTED (3)

| # | File:Line | Description | Status |
|---|-----------|-------------|--------|
| K123 | shader_build.rs (`neutralize_blend_noise_wgsl`) | **Naga inlining explosion from blend noise chain.** `neutralize_blend_noise_wgsl()` physically removes noise function definitions (`apply_boolean_blend`, `smin_noisy`, `smax_noisy`, `eval_blend_noise`) from WGSL source and injects a lightweight `apply_boolean_blend` stub that delegates to `apply_boolean`. Previous body-stub approach (v1) left noise functions in source — they could still bloat compilation. New approach (v2) ensures Naga never sees them. Applied in: `build_shared_wgsl()` (6 shader variants), `build_sdf_eval_block()` (volume preview — was missed in v1), `gpu_init.rs` (primary bake), `gpu_jobs.rs` (worker bake). `fbm_wgsl` kept for surface noise modifiers. 20 Naga tests pass including new neutralization + volume preview tests. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-26 |
| K124 | main.rs (background thread) | **DF-full restored in background thread with TDR guard.** DF-full compilation restored with `compiling_heavy_shader: Arc<AtomicBool>` flag. Flag set before DF-full compile, cleared after (even on panic via `catch_unwind`). `dispatch_gpu_render()` checks flag at top — if set, skips ALL GPU work, shows overlay, polls device. With blend noise neutralized, DF-full compiles in ~20-30ms. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-26 |
| K125 | shader_build.rs:321 | **Volume preview path missing blend noise treatment.** `build_sdf_eval_block()` used `SDF_SHARED_WGSL` directly without neutralization. The `SDF_PRIM_EVAL` region contains all noise function definitions. Fixed by applying `neutralize_blend_noise_wgsl()` before region extraction. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-26 |

| K126 | app_poll.rs:496, gpu_jobs.rs:496 | **Execution TDR from 256³ volume bake dispatch.** Single `dispatch_workgroups(64,64,64)` = 262K workgroups × 64 threads = 16.7M threads exceeds Windows ~2s TDR timeout. Fixed by splitting Z-axis into slices of 16 workgroups (64 voxels). Each slice dispatched + submitted separately with `device.poll(Wait)` between slices. Shader uses `gid + params.bake_min` for output indexing so updating `bake_min[2]/bake_max[2]` between slices writes to correct positions. Applied to both primary GPU (app_poll.rs) and worker GPU (gpu_jobs.rs) bake paths. Small bakes (≤128³) use single dispatch unchanged. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-26 |
| K127 | shader_build.rs:252 (`build_deferred_wgsl`) | **Execution TDR from DF-full shadow/AO re-march.** `soft_shadow()` (16/24/32 steps) and `calc_ao()` (3/5/8 samples) each call `scene_sdf()` per iteration. With Naga inlining, 32 steps × N prims = massive GPU workload. Fixed by reducing step counts via text replacement in `build_deferred_wgsl()`: soft_shadow 16/24/32 → 6/8/10, calc_ao 3/5/8 → 2/3/4. Only affects WGSL deferred path; GLSL BVH path (real function calls) is unaffected. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-26 |

| K129 | deferred_entry.wgsl:441 | **Roughness=0 NDF singularity.** Raw `mat_rough` used in GGX NDF without clamp. `a=0, a2=0` → near-singularity masked only by epsilon. Fixed: `let r = max(mat_rough, 0.01)`. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-26 |
| K130 | deferred_entry.wgsl:304,482 | **Hardcoded 0.15 ambient ignores env_brightness.** When no lights exist, `scene_ambient = 0.15` regardless of `env_brightness`. Fixed: `0.15 * config.env_brightness` when `env_brightness > 0.0`, else `0.0`. Both lit branch (line 304) and PBR branch (line 482) updated. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-26 |

# SESSION 2026-03-26h — 3-Tier Raymarch LOD System

## Architecture

3-tier LOD controlling raymarch quality via steps + hit threshold + pixel_scale. Two LOD sources combine → take the WORST quality (min steps, max threshold, max pixel_scale).

**Distance LOD (scene-wide):** CPU-computed `lod_scene_screen_size` (scene AABB radius / cam_dist × fov_scale) — placeholder formula. Controls steps + threshold ONLY (not pixel_scale, per Correction 1: multiple bodies can overlap same pixel → per-body pixel_scale is undefined behavior).

**Foveated LOD (per-pixel):** Smoothstep falloff from screen center. Controls steps + threshold + pixel_scale. Only LOD source allowed to change pixel_scale.

**Occlusion LOD:** Deferred to future — too aggressive for v1 (body center hidden but silhouette visible = wrongly skipped).

## FIXES IMPLEMENTED (1)

|---|-----------|-------------|--------|
| K136 | types.rs (GpuUniforms), types_render.rs (RenderSettings), viewport_render.rs, raymarch_bvh_full.comp, raymarch_bvh.comp, raymarch_bvh.spv, win_tweaks.rs | **3-tier raymarch LOD system.** Extended GpuUniforms from 512→576 bytes with 16 LOD fields (distance thresholds, foveated params, debug flags, CPU-computed screen size). Added `LodParams` struct (steps/threshold/pixel_scale), `combine_lod()`, `compute_distance_lod()` (steps+threshold only, no pixel_scale), `compute_foveated_lod()` (steps+threshold+pixel_scale) to both GLSL files. March loop uses LOD-derived steps/threshold. LOD debug visualization: distance tier coloring (green/yellow/orange/red), foveated edge tint (blue), pixel block grid lines. Developer Tweaks UI: 3 collapsible sections (Distance LOD, Foveated Rendering, LOD Debug) with safety-colored sliders. WGSL parity: foveated only (pending). | ✅ IMPLEMENTED 2026-03-26 |

Also noted: `ADAPTIVE_REFERENCE_EXTENT = 0.3` causes 256³ over-promotion for most bodies (any body > 1.2 units) — separate tuning issue, not fixed here. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-30 |

Prim_buf_stale flag persists (not cleared) so toggling volume-only OFF triggers immediate full re-serialize. Picking uses raster pipeline (unaffected). Gizmo overlay is egui paint (unaffected). | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-30 |
| CR-78 | Perf | body_volume_cache/mod.rs:532 | **Moving a prim is super laggy — 256³ bake for a single cube.** `ADAPTIVE_REFERENCE_EXTENT = 0.3` caused any body > 1.2 units to hit the 4.0x scale clamp → 256³ resolution (16M voxels, 65MB). Each bake cycle: 43ms readback + 24ms NaN scan + 8x47ms chunked upload = ~450ms. DC extraction: 2-8s. A default cube (~2 units padded) got `2.0/0.3=6.67` clamped to 4.0 → 256³. Fix: changed reference extent from 0.3 to 3.0. Now a 2-unit body gets `2.0/3.0=0.67` → 128*0.67=85 → rounded to 96³ (885K voxels, 3.4MB). 18x less data. Only bodies >12 units reach 256³. | ✅ FIXED 2026-03-30 |

Since `need` tracks the surface (~+12 %/step) while the multiplier is flat +50 %, `1.5×buffer` outran `need` at the first rebuild and `need` could never win again; each size became the next base, monotone, unbounded to `safe_max`. Owner's live 1024³ drag: verts **262→393→590→885 MB** + idx **197→295→443→664 MB** (~1.55 GB) while true need rose only 262→324 MB (bricks +23 %) — **2.74× over-allocated**. NOT an overflow bug: `grow_slot` never ran, the slot cap held at exactly 48.0 verts/brick, and `VERTS_PER_BRICK_HEADROOM`/counter-zeroing/the overflow predicate/`dc_output_caps_dense` were all cleared. Reproduced **8/8 exactly** from brick counts alone; corroborated by the log's consecutive gens 1,2,3,4 (a bump-append would have skipped one ⇒ the fast path never fired). **Fix:** anchor headroom to demand — `(need_v * 3 / 2).min(safe_max).max(need_v)` — so the output never re-enters the input; `buffer ≤ 1.5 × Σ live regions` always and a stable surface reaches a fixed point (849 MB vs 1 549 MB on the logged sequence). **Gate:** `sdf_pool_rebuild_sizing_tracks_demand_not_history`, proven to FAIL on the old code. - ✅ FIXED 2026-06-30 — Bevel flipped-face (inverted shading normal on partial edge bevels). Root cause: `compute_face_normal` first-3-vertex cross product → wrong sign on non-convex beveled faces. Fix: Newell's method (`half_edge.rs`, sanctioned scoped-lift edit d). Regression gate: `bevel_op::tests::bevel_output_faces_all_point_outward`.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-06-30 — Bevel twisted endpoint face ("two new edges slide along the wrong face"). Root cause: `(false,false)` corner re-trace ordered cut points around an external normal (handedness flip) → self-intersecting endpoint face. Fix: order by corner-derived axis `(pe.src−V)×(ce.dst−V)` in `bevel_op::order_arc_about_vertex`. Gate: `bevel_output_faces_are_simple`.

- ✅ DONE 2026-06-30 — Round bevel (segments + shape profile) via scroll. `bevel_op` now builds an n-segment Bézier arc (control toward the original edge). Contextual scroll (`is_poly_bevel()` branch) + live regen (`poly_bevel_regenerate`). v1: rounds isolated edges; shared-corner selections fall back to flat/watertight (rounded multi-edge corners = v2). Gate: `bevel_segments_produce_round_watertight`.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-06-30 — Bevel on already-beveled geometry tears at bevel-created (degree>3) corners. Root cause: `(false,false)` re-trace over-inserted the whole chamfer arc (correct only for degree-3). Fix: per-side rail insertion + a general residual-hole seal (STEP 6) in `bevel_op`. Gate: `bevel_on_beveled_watertight`.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-03 — Outliner: clicking a sub-body row "did nothing" visibly. Two halves: (a) the header bg is painted AFTER layout over the selectable_label's selected fill, so a selected body row looked identical to an unselected one — bg now reflects `sdf_sel` (`outliner_draw_body.rs`); (b) a selected NESTED body got no viewport outline — nested bodies never rasterize their own mesh and the top-level `is_selected` ignored descendants; the sel-bit now sets when any selected node is the body or one of its nested sub-bodies (`raster_gbuffer.rs`).

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-03 — Selecting one prim outlined the WHOLE body in Object Mode. Root cause: `raster_gbuffer.rs` sel-bit clause `nid == active_body_nid && any-prim-selected`. Removed — prim selection feedback is the gizmo + per-prim overlay (`draw_selection_highlights`); the body outline now means "this node (or a nested sub-body) is selected".

- ✅ DONE 2026-07-03 — Tab pie: context-sensitive mode (selection's modeling_context picks SDF/POLY/NURBS pie), BODY merged into OBJECT, OBJECT at top slot in all pies; poly pie now mirrors Blender's Tab pie (Object top, Face right, Edge bottom, Vertex left on an 8-sector ring), Sculpt demoted to a small icon button, compact Blender-size buttons (`pie_menu.rs`, `menus.rs`, `viewport_overlays.rs`, `input_keyboard.rs`).

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-03 — Regression from the prim-selection outline change: selecting a prim showed NO feedback. Root cause: production has no per-prim GPU outline (baked-triangle raster + volume raymarch both outline the whole fused body), and the only per-prim overlay (`draw_selection_highlights`) ran only in Object mode and drew a real wireframe only for Box shapes. Fix: the overlay now draws an oriented bounding-box wireframe for EVERY selected prim (all shapes) driven by the canonical `selected_prim_indices_for_gpu()` set (select one prim → its box; select a body → a box around each of its prims), and it now also runs in SDF Edit (Vertex) mode where prims are actually selected (`draw_selection.rs`, `viewport_overlays.rs`).

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-03 — Shift+RMB set-workplane ignored mesh surfaces. `place_workplane_on_surface` / `_at_surface_center` used `raycast_scene`, which only marches the analytical SDF prim field — poly/imported/voxel/NURBS bodies were invisible to it. Added `raycast_scene_meshes` (world-space triangle raycast over `renderable_meshes()`, reusing `ray_triangle`) + `raycast_scene_surface` (nearest of SDF march and mesh hit); both workplane placers (and the Home-key path) now use it. `camera.rs`, `workplane.rs`.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-09 — "Sphere doesn't use the same G/R/S": a ROTATED sphere's AABB inflated up to √3× because `bounding_aabb_half_extents()` ran every shape through the OBB→AABB rotation projection (a sphere is rotation-invariant). Owner-visible as fat dirty regions + tight bounds after any R on a sphere → near-full-grid partial bake windows (23-29ms/frame vs the cube's 6-14ms at 512 sparse). Fix: uniform-|scale| zero-elongation spheres skip the projection (exact r·s); ellipsoids/elongated keep it (`primitives.rs`, gate `sphere_aabb_rotation_invariant`). Commit d35bb0b (feat/sparse-3a).

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-09 — Mesh detaches from the gizmo during drags at dense res (128) — branch-local regression from the rigid-translate fast path (4a4fe78, never on master): the resident-mesh draw offset was DERIVED from bounds deltas (`entry.grid_min − slot.meshed_grid_min`), but bounds also move on escape-grow/settle-retighten where geometry does NOT move → the dense-path thrash left a bogus offset on the drawn mesh for frames. Fix: EXPLICIT `BodyCacheEntry.mesh_rigid_offset` — only the rigid fast path accumulates it, a mesh dispatched at the entry's current bounds clears it, all other bounds changes never touch it; picking reads the same offset (lockstep). Gates: `non_rigid_bounds_moves_leave_offset_zero` + extended rigid suite. Commit 46f4d1f (feat/sparse-3a).

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-09 — Per-prim selection wireframe (orange overlay) didn't follow BODY scaling/rotation: `draw_selection_highlights` ran only the prim CENTER through the body transform, then added the shape-outline offsets raw (prim scale/rotation only) — an Object-Mode S on the body scaled the mesh while the orange wire stayed at the old size (owner screenshot). - ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **Object-Mode Shift+D with MULTIPLE bodies/nodes selected duplicated only the ACTIVE node** (tracked follow-up from the multi-prim fix `d2e7d15`; also closes the node half of K71). FIX (mirrors the d2e7d15 pattern): READ PHASE collects all selected NodeIds up front (active node moved to front so the FIRST duplicate becomes the new active), applies a **TOP-MOST filter** — a selected node whose ANCESTOR is also selected is skipped, because `duplicate_subtree()` on the ancestor already copies the whole subtree (duplicating the descendant too would double it: once inside the ancestor's copy, once standalone — same rule Blender applies). Then loops the EXISTING per-node primitives inside ONE `transaction("Duplicate N objects")`: SdfBody → new `duplicate_sdf_body_no_undo()` (extraction of the old single-body block: canonical `duplicate_subtree` + origin offset + `sync_flat_cache` + fresh mesh-cache id + `mark_body_dirty`/`mark_node_body_vol_dirty` + SCENE — per-node marks unchanged); Poly/NURBS/Empty/Group → `duplicate_scene_node_no_undo()` (old `duplicate_scene_node` refactored to no-undo, sole caller was this arm — no second code path); unsupported kinds (Camera/Material/ImportedMesh; non-active VoxelBody keeps its dedicated arm) skip gracefully with a toast. Selection after: `select_after_create()` — all duplicates selected, originals deselected, active = first duplicate; `active_body_nid` switches to the first SDF duplicate (same as the single path; single path armed no gizmo mode, unchanged). ONE Ctrl+Z reverts all copies. Mixed prim+node selection dispatch unchanged (prim arm still wins). No headless harness for `AzraApp` (GPU-bound) — MANUAL TEST: (a) 2 SDF bodies + 1 poly body Ctrl-clicked, Shift+D → 3 duplicates offset +X, all selected, originals not, ONE Ctrl+Z removes all 3; (b) select a body AND its own nested sub-body, Shift+D → exactly ONE duplicate subtree (sub-body copied once, inside it). - ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — CPU vs GPU BOX SDF EVAL DIVERGENCE (field consistency): CPU `SdfShape::Box::distance` was TRI-PLANAR (max of three 2D plane distances — underestimated the true distance in 3-positive corner regions by up to ~22%), while every GPU eval (`sdf_box` in volume_bake.wgsl / sdf_prim_eval.wgsl / GLSL) is exact Euclidean — measured GPU−CPU up to +2.6e-2 near box corners at the classify threshold shell (spike `7ccbb86`). FIX: the plain-box CPU eval (all edge bevel modes None AND up_axis 0 — the exact predicate under which the GPU dispatches `sdf_box` via `mode_bits == 0`) now uses the same exact Euclidean form `length(max(q,0)) + min(max(q.x,max(q.y,q.z)),0)`, same op order as the WGSL. The beveled / permuted-up_axis path keeps the tri-planar per-edge formulation ON PURPOSE — the GPU `sdf_box_per_edge` is also tri-planar, so CPU/GPU are aligned on BOTH branches (do not "fix" the beveled branch to Euclidean). CPU-only change: baked GPU meshes and prim hashes unchanged; undo/save unaffected. The pinned divergence test was FLIPPED into the alignment gate `gpu_classify_box_euclidean_alignment_gate` (tests_gpu_classify.rs) — box scene now bit-agrees: ZERO per-brick verdict mismatches over 32768 bricks at 256³. Consumers (FieldEvaluator snapping/queries, CPU classify oracle, chunked_dc superset classifier, CPU bake fallback) audited — all gates green with no golden re-derivations needed (no test hand-computed a corner-region box distance).

- ✅ DONE 2026-07-13 (perf, GPU classify stage 3) — **sparse classify FINALIZE moved on-device for FULL classifies** — the ~20ms (512³) / ~88ms (1024³) worker-thread `sparse_index_from_verdicts` (26-ring dilation + dense-packed handle allocation) that every duplicate/structural edit paid as mesh-update latency now runs as four compute passes appended to the `classify_bricks` submission (same volume_bake.wgsl module, SAME bake BGL — the finalize bind group puts the verdict buffer at binding 6 (`brick_index`, read-only u32) and a transient work buffer at binding 2): `classify_finalize_dilate` (gather-form 26-ring, provably the CPU scatter's set), `classify_finalize_scan` (256-wide Hillis-Steele in-block exclusive scan), `classify_finalize_block_scan` (serial one-thread block-sum scan — ≤8192 blocks, deterministic), `classify_finalize_emit` (`emit_sparse_index` verbatim: store→handle, interior→0xFFFFFFFE, else 0xFFFFFFFF). SCAN-ORDER PROOF: CPU handles are `slot++` over brick-linear bi; the GPU handle = exclusive prefix count of handled bricks at smaller bi — the same integer count, so BIT-IDENTICAL. ONE readback: index tags + trailing `allocated` (total+1 u32 — same size class as the verdict readback it replaces); the frame thread only validates the dense-packing invariant structurally (handles must be exactly 0,1,2,… in scan order; any violation aborts the flight) and lands via `classify_tx` — the worker-thread finalize spawn is GONE on this path. FULLs only — fresh index, `freed: vec![]`; the PARTIAL walk's freed-list recycling stays CPU and consumes the frozen index unchanged (bit-identity ⇒ automatically safe). Pipelines compile as a set with `classify_bricks` (background hot-swap payload extended + lazy ensure; ONE shared helper `compile_classify_finalize_pipelines` used by background/ensure/tests). MEASURED (RTX 4090): 512³ full = submit→map 8.8ms total incl. verdicts+dilate+alloc+readback, frame validate 0.6ms (was verdicts ~2-4ms + ~20-33ms worker finalize); 1024³ = 10.8ms total, validate 4.0ms (was ~88ms worker finalize; CPU full classify+finalize oracle 169.5ms same scene). PARITY GATES (hardware, bit-identical `index`+`allocated`): all 5 tests_gpu_classify scenes at 256³ now ALSO gate GPU-finalize vs `sparse_index_from_verdicts` on the exact same verdicts; the 512³ production e2e runs GPU-finalized vs the CPU full classify; `sparse_1024_runs_like_512_end_to_end` gates 512³ AND 1024³ GPU-finalize vs CPU classify. Gates green: cargo check -p app, core_math (443), graphics Naga (43; pre-existing FLOATS_PER_PRIM fail only), app sparse (20) / sdf_dc (13) / tests_bake / gpu_classify (3) / full --bins (109, single-threaded). - ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER CRASH: add/drag a prim in a 1024³ sparse body → "surface never appeared, console panicked repeatedly, app crashed"** (day after the 174aa17 un-gate; reproduced by the owner again 2026-07-13 10:25 — `fourthlayer_gpu_error.txt` captured the cascade tail "Command encoder is invalid"). ROOT CAUSE (reproduced live via the new `AZRA_AUTOREPRO=1` in-app driver): an interactive prim edit whose dirty window grows large (create-drag / fast move) at 1024³ rode the frozen-index PARTIAL arm — (a) the S2.5b mini-classify walk runs ON THE FRAME THREAD, measured 200-300ms/frame for ~1.4M-brick windows ([TriggerBake] 298ms); (b) S2.5c incremental allocation APPENDS handles for the whole swept frontier every frame while reclaim lags (a growing surface vacates nothing) → the atlas pool ballooned 355MB → 1.43GB in seconds for ONE small cylinder; the next ×1.25 `ensure_capacity` grow crosses `max_storage_buffer_binding_size` (2.1GB) → wgpu validation error on every subsequent dispatch (the owner's repeated "panics" = the `[GPU] UNCAPTURED ERROR` stream) → "Command encoder is invalid" cascade → device loss → crash. 512 never hit it (windows + pool ≈ 4-8× smaller). NOT the suspected Edit-Mode dense fall-through: `sdf_edit_active` is never set true in production ("Step 2" never wired), so `force_volume_only` is always false outside Sculpt, `gridbacked_only` stays true, and a 1024 body keeps its sparse regime in WorkMode::Vertex; the dense binding-size assert is unreachable (verified by the new cache-level hardware gate). FIX (structural — enforces the S2.5 small-window premise): (1) **oversized-window escalation** in `trigger_bake`: a dilated window covering >1/8 of the grid's bricks skips the frame-thread walk and escalates to the async FULL classify (off-thread; a full RESETS `allocated` to the true surface count — observed 700k→327k bricks). Post-fix, same drag: max [TriggerBake] 29.7ms (was 298), pool bounded at 833MB caps. (2) **sparse pool ceiling** at the dispatch site (sibling of the dense binding assert): a Full/Partial whose pool would exceed the storage-binding limit SELF-HEALS — resolution dropped one notch (1024→512) + loud log + toast; an unbindable buffer is never handed to the driver. (3) **crash attribution hardened**: the `on_uncaptured_error` handler (which silently REPLACED the visdump-writing one) now appends with a 64KB cap (the ROOT error survives at the head, not just the cascade tail) and writes one visdump for the session's first error. (4) Permanent gates: `sparse_partial_oversized_window_escalates_to_full` (trigger-side + nudge-window control), `sparse_1024_add_prim_to_resident_body_end_to_end` (hardware: production request flow at 1024 — first-bake cascade → sparse divert → add-prim full re-classify → drag partials → mesh), plus the env-gated `AZRA_AUTOREPRO` full-app repro driver (dev_tools.rs). Commit on feat/sparse-3a.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER BUG: cylinder in body A → new body (N) → click-drag the cylinder → "surface breaks and STOPS UPDATING; changing the DC-mesh resolution no longer recovers it"** (on 459aac2+e07b13c). REPRODUCED headlessly via the new `AZRA_AUTOREPRO=2` multi-body driver (dev_tools.rs — the owner's exact sequence: add cylinder → create-drag → `create_new_sdf_body` (N) → per-frame `write_prim_transform` drag → Grid-picker res change), run at 128/512/1024, click and no-click variants. ROOT CAUSE (**NOT a 459aac2 regression** — audited line-by-line; the strip removed no load-bearing recovery, and the pre-459aac2 picker had identical per-body semantics): dense DC mesh buffers sized from SLOT CAPACITY instead of the DISPATCH resolution — `mesh_into_slot`/`mesh_into_slot_from_resident` requested `dc_caps(slot.capacity_res).0` for `cell_vert` (R3c, c9f7886) and `ensure_field` allocated `capacity_res³` (P0-R3a). Once a body's mesh slot has capacity 1024 (any sparse ≥512 session — the 174aa17 un-gate), the FIRST dense mesh of that slot (Grid-picker drop to ≤512, cascade coarse level, dense re-bake after regime change) requests a 4.28GB `cell_vert` / 4.29GB `field` → `sdf_dc_bg` **BufferRangeTooLarge** (binding 2 > 2.1GB `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`) → encoder-invalid cascade → the mesh silently never lands, and the GROW-ONLY watermark makes the poisoned cap PERMANENT: every later dense mesh of the slot fails, including the recovery re-bake — so the surface freezes and the resolution change (which correctly queues + bakes a clean 256 grid; CPU cache provably healthy in the repro) can never be SEEN. VERIFIED: pre-fix `AZRA_AUTOREPRO=2 AZRA_AUTOREPRO_RES=1024` logs the exact BufferRangeTooLarge cascade; post-fix all variants (512/1024 × click/no-click) pass with 0 uncaptured errors. Permanent gates: `sdf_dc_dense_into_1024_capacity_slot_stays_bindable` (hardware, sdf_gpu_mesh/tests_dc.rs), `multibody_drag_refreshes_dragged_body_at_1024` + `resolution_change_recovers_dragged_body` (cache-level, bake_dispatch.rs), plus the `AZRA_AUTOREPRO=2` full-app driver.
