- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER BUGS ×5: SDF outliner drag-and-drop slot map + nest/un-nest** (branch fix/outliner-sdf-dnd): (1) cannot drop a prim AFTER a sub-body group; (2) dragging a prim OUT of a sub-body always created a NEW top-level body; (3) no drop slot between a prim row and a group row; (4) top-level body dropped onto a body should nest as sub-body; (5) sub-body dragged to root should un-nest. ROOT CAUSE (1–3, one root): drop slots were enumerated ONLY on prim rows (`update_prim_drop_zone`, flat-index thirds) — a sub-body header row swallowed its whole rect as "reparent INTO this body" (`drop_reparent`) and no between-slot around/after a group ref could be expressed with flat prim indices at all; any drop in the uncovered space fell through to the root/new-body path (hence bug 2's "always a new body"). FIX (architecture, testable): NEW pure decision module `app/src/outliner_drop_slots.rs` (zero egui) — `resolve_prim_over_body_header` (sub-body header thirds → InsertIntoOrder before/after the group ref in the PARENT's `child_order`, center → ReparentInto; top-level headers stay whole-rect ReparentInto), `resolve_body_over_body_header` (top/bottom → PlaceNextTo, center → NestInto, **CYCLE GUARD at slot-enumeration level**: dragging over self/own-descendant returns Rejected — no indicator, no action), plus the slot math (`slot_anchor`/`slot_insert_position`/`insert_index_after_removal`/`slot_is_noop`). The egui layer only measures rects/zones and maps semantics onto new state `OutlinerState.drop_insert: (body, child_order idx)` + an END-OF-BODY catch strip inside each body's indent (the missing after-last-child / after-group-subtree slot). Mutations: NEW `move_prims_to_body_slot` (prim_actions.rs) — same-body = reorder via the canonical `reorder_child_in_body`, cross-body = `reparent_prim_to_body` (full Structural Mutation Checklist both bodies) + anchored order placement; multi-selection lands contiguously in flat/selection order; locked prims filtered with toast; single-prim no-op slots skip the transaction; ONE `transaction("Move in stack")` per drop. NEW `reparent_body_node` (scene_actions.rs) — THE single nest/un-nest action (graph reparent + child_order reconcile both parents + origins + sync_flat_cache + vol-dirty climbing for OLD parent, NEW parent, child; old parent was previously NOT dirtied — CR-74 class); routed through by: the nest center-zone (`d.reparent_body`), cross-parent edge drops (drop a sub-body between TOP-LEVEL rows = un-nest next to the target; drop a top-level body between a group's children = re-nest), and empty-area body drop (`body_drop_root_y`, amber line) = un-nest to root. **Behavior change (owner-directed): the moved body's `body_op` is PRESERVED on nest** — the old Union→Subtract auto-inheritance was removed. Boolean-chain semantics: moving a prim/body changes eval order by design; FIXED-origins policy respected (only `recalculate_body_origin` per existing flows, no extra compensation); an emptied source sub-body is KEPT (matches existing reparent convention; dissolve stays explicit). Drag-to-empty-space with prims = new-body path UNCHANGED. TESTS: 14 headless unit tests over the pure module (slot matrix: before/after/into group, top-level header, end-of-body, cross-body slot landing, multi-prim contiguity + anchor-skip, no-op detection, cycle-guard rejection, removal-index compensation). NOT covered headlessly (FourthLayerApp needs GPU; manual scenarios): undo one-entry-per-drop through the live transaction stack, indicator visuals, drag ergonomics (Ctrl-drag-duplicate / hover-expand / auto-scroll = NOT IMPLEMENTED follow-ups). MANUAL: with Body.001{Box.001, Group.001{Box.002,Box.003,Box.005}}, Body.002{Box.006} — drag Box.001 to the slot under Group.001 (line at group bottom or end strip) → lands after the group in the chain; drag Box.002 to the gap between Box.001 and Group.001 → moves into Body.001 at that slot; drag Box.002 to empty space → new Body (unchanged); drag Body.002 onto Body.001 center → nests keeping its op; drag Group.001 to empty space / between top-level rows → un-nests; Ctrl+Z after each = single revert. Gates: cargo check -p app, core_math (443), app full --bins 125 green single-threaded.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER BUG ×4 reports (one root): outliner between-row prim drops render the correct indicator but apply WRONG/NOTHING on release** (on 3e341b1). Symptoms: (1) drag first prim to "after <last prim>" (end slot, same body) → dead release; (2) cross-body drag to a between-slot → dead release; (3) cross-body "before Box.004" → applied but APPENDED to end instead of the slot; (4) multi-drag (2 prims) cross-body "after <last row>" → dead release. ROOT CAUSE (suspect #2/#3 hybrid — visualization fine, apply reads a DIFFERENT representation): the prim-ROW Top/Bottom zones (`update_prim_drop_zone`, outliner.rs) still stored the slot as a legacy FLAT prim index (`drop_target = flat_idx` / `flat_idx + 1`) while the label was computed from row geometry. A flat index cannot express "end of this body" (`flat_idx+1 == len` → `prim_body_map.get()` = None → the release's cross-body arm's `if let Some(target_nid)` silently falls through = case 1) and silently CROSSES body boundaries (on a body's last row, `flat_idx+1` = the NEXT body's first flat row — often the dragged prim itself → misclassified as same-body → `sel_indices.contains(&to)` skip / `from == to` skip = cases 2, 4); the one arm that did fire (cross-body with in-range index) called `reparent_prim_to_body(…, local_pos)` whose child_order reconcile APPENDS the moved ref (prims-first synthesis) — the insert position was never applied to `child_order` = case 3. FIX (class-eliminating): prim-row Top/Bottom zones now resolve through NEW pure `resolve_prim_over_prim_row()` (outliner_drop_slots.rs) to the CANONICAL `drop_insert = (body NodeId, child_order index)` — the same representation the sub-body slots + end-of-body strip already used — and the release applies via the ONE placement op `move_prims_to_body_slot` (same-body reorder, cross-body reparent+slot-place, multi-prim anchored contiguity, Ctrl-copy, locked filter, single-prim no-op guard all already handled there). The now-unreachable flat-index release arms (same-body single `d.reorder`, same-body multi block move, same-body Ctrl-copy, cross-body reparent arm) were DELETED along with `OutlinerDeferred.reorder` and `reorder_prim_in_graph` (no-two-paths rule; drop_target survives only for the center "group with prim" zone). Index math: Top of row = index(rowRef in child_order), Bottom = index+1, stale ref self-heals to len; end slot index == len flows through `slot_anchor` → None → append-after-removal (batch-1 pin unchanged). TESTS (+5 permanent, outliner_drop_slots.rs, order-exact): `prim_row_zones_resolve_to_child_order_slots`, `owner_case_first_prim_to_end_slot_applies` (first/middle/last × end slot; last = clean no-op), `owner_case_cross_body_before_first_lands_first_not_appended` ([B3,B4,B6,Cyl7]), `owner_case_multi_cross_body_after_last_applies_in_payload_order` ([B1,Cyl7,B3]), `between_slot_before_next_row_equals_after_this_row`. Same-class audit: sub-body-header slots, end-of-body strip, and body-reorder-to-end already carry (NodeId, child_order idx) end-to-end — unaffected. MANUAL: body [Cyl.007, Box.004, Box.006] — drag Cyl.007 below Box.006 → order becomes [Box.004, Box.006, Cyl.007]; drag a prim from body B to "before Box.004" in body A → lands FIRST; multi-drag 2 prims to "after <last row>" of body A → both land at end of A in payload order; Ctrl+Z single revert each. Gates: cargo check -p app (110 warnings, unchanged baseline), core_math 443 green, app --bins 141 green single-threaded (28/28 drop-slot tests). Commit on feat/sparse-3a.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER BUG: a drag APPLIES (scene mutates correctly) but the outliner shows STALE rows after the drop** (on 7972506). ROOT CAUSE: the DnD release handler (`outliner_dnd_release`) runs INSIDE the ScrollArea draw; its transaction correctly set `outliner_dirty` (via `move_prims_to_body_slot`/`reparent_body_node`), but `draw_right_panel`'s END-OF-FRAME clear (`if throttle_allows || !needs_rebuild { outliner_dirty = false }`) ran AFTER the release and — since `needs_rebuild` was latched false at frame START — unconditionally SWALLOWED the mid-draw dirty. Next frame `cached_root_children`/`cached_body_buckets` never rebuilt and the double-buffered `visual_order` promotion had no fresh draw → panel stuck on pre-drop rows until unrelated input re-dirtied it. FIX (structural, action-level): (a) `outliner_dirty` is now CONSUMED at the rebuild point (inside the `needs_rebuild && throttle_allows` block, before the tree draw) and the end-of-frame clear is DELETED — any dirty set during the draw/release/deferred processing survives to the next frame by construction; (b) `transaction()` itself calls `mark_outliner_dirty()` after the mutation closure (one action-level mark, mirrors undo/redo at undo.rs:336 — kills the whole "some action forgot to mark" class, not per-call-site); (c) end of `draw_right_panel`: `if outliner_dirty { ctx.request_repaint() }` so the rebuild + visual_order promotion frame happens immediately without waiting for input. MANUAL: drag a prim between rows, release, don't move the mouse → row order updates the very next frame. Gates: cargo check -p app, core_math 443, app --bins 144 green single-threaded.

- ✅ DONE 2026-07-13 — **FEATURE: outliner edge AUTO-SCROLL during drag-and-drop** (owner item 2). New `outliner_drag_autoscroll()` (outliner_actions.rs), called at the top of the outliner ScrollArea closure: while `dragging`/`dragging_body` is live and the pointer is within 24px of the scroll viewport's top/bottom edge (x gated to the viewport), feeds `ui.scroll_with_delta(vec2(0, ±v))` with v ramping linearly 2→12 px/frame by edge proximity (positive delta = view scrolls toward earlier rows at the top edge), plus `ctx.request_repaint()` for continuous motion while the pointer holds the band. Slot resolution unaffected: rows re-lay-out at their new offsets each frame and every drop-zone hit test reads fresh row rects. MANUAL: long tree, grab a prim, hold the cursor near the panel bottom → tree scrolls, accelerating toward the edge; indicators keep resolving during the scroll.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER BUG: undo of a prim REORDER never updates the surface (hide/show heals it; resolution change doesn't)** (on 8411386). Log proof: `[SparseLoop] FULL re-bake: hash X==X? true` across states with DIFFERENT boolean-chain orders. ROOT CAUSE: the body source hash was BLIND to `child_order` — `reorder_child_in_body` permutes ONLY `child_order` (the sequence `resolve_child_order` feeds the bake serializer — order IS the field), never the prims Vec, and all three source-hash sites (`trigger_bake` bake_dispatch.rs, cascade.rs's must-match-trigger hash, `compute_body_source_hash` used by `invalidate_for_undo`) hashed only the Vec via `hash_prim_slice`. Undo restored the original order → hash falsely equaled the reordered entry's stamp → body marked transform_safe, NEVER re-baked. FIX (elongation-hash pattern, drift-proof): NEW `bake_utils::hash_body_source()` is THE one implementation behind every source_hash (prim slice + mirror/bevel + lab_operand_gen + NEW `hash_body_child_order()` — recursive fold of `resolve_child_order`: prim uids + sub-body NodeIds in sequence + each sub-body's `body_op`, all stable across undo snapshot restore); the three sites now call it, so the field set structurally cannot drift. `hash_prim_slice_no_uid` (instancing/template hash — prim CONTENT identity) deliberately unchanged. Pre-reorder entry + undo back to pre-reorder state hashes EQUAL — legitimate dedup, kept. TESTS (+3, bake_dispatch.rs `order_hash_and_regime_tests`): `source_hash_covers_child_order` (reorder → hash changes; restore → hash equals original), `source_hash_covers_subbody_order_and_op`, `undo_of_reorder_rebakes` (cache-level owner scenario: reorder→stamp→undo → invalidate_for_undo marks dirty + NOT transform_safe → trigger_bake dispatches, no hash-skip). MANUAL: stack of prims, move first prim to last (surface updates), Ctrl+Z → surface updates back immediately. Gates: cargo check -p app; core_math green; app sparse 21 / sdf_dc 13 / tests_bake 3 / gpu_classify 3 / full --bins 149 green single-threaded.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER BUG: selection / Vertex↔Object work-mode changes re-bake the SAME body at 1024→512→256→1024 (`regime_ok=false` flips) — pure churn; also why "change resolution" didn't heal the reorder bug (the res-change bake landed then was superseded)** (on 8411386). TWO feeders: (1) `set_work_mode` → Object did a blanket `mark_all_bodies_dirty` + `trigger_body_vol_bake` on EVERY toggle — a mode switch changes NO bake input since the legacy VP regime was removed (Object Mode is the only render regime); (2) `effective_resolution` applied `draft_resolution` (global res/2) BEFORE the sparse-eligibility decision, so trigger_bake's per-body S2.5e `sparse_body` guard and the `all_dirty_sparse` check both saw the ALREADY-DRAFTED value and could never protect the body: rapid dirty marks (<200ms apart, e.g. the mode-switch blanket mark with any dense body present) engaged draft → the 1024 sparse body's target collapsed to 512/256 → dense bake destroyed `brick_resident` → `regime_ok=false` → full re-classify; draft promotion then re-baked at 1024 → the loop. FIX (one clamp policy, hysteresis-free): (a) `effective_resolution` — the single source every consumer reads — now decides draft on the UNDRAFTED base: a sparse-eligible base NEVER drafts (S2.5e enforced structurally at the policy site, documented there); dense bodies keep the draft speedup; (b) `set_work_mode` → NEW `mark_stale_bodies_dirty()` (resident_volume.rs, reuses `needs_rebake_on_leave`): only top-level bodies with a missing / draft-res / regime-unservable grid are marked — a body with a valid full-res grid is untouched by mode/selection switches. TESTS (+2, same module): `sparse_body_resolution_stable_under_draft` (1024 sparse ignores draft=256; dense regime still drafts), `mode_switch_marks_only_stale_bodies`. MANUAL: 1024 sparse body → click prim / click body / toggle Vertex↔Object repeatedly → ZERO `[SparseLoop]`/`[SparseBake]` lines, resolution stays 1024. Gates: same suite set as above, all green.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER BUG: default scene shows TWO lights both named "Sun.001"; the second cannot be deleted; deleting the first deletes BOTH** (owner item 3). ROOT CAUSE (not two lights — ONE light, TWO rows): the outliner drew every Light node TWICE — once in the dedicated Lights section (`draw_outliner_lights`) and once as a generic "LGT" node row in the root-children loop (`draw_right_panel` only skipped `Root`). Deleting via the light row removed the single node → both rows vanished ("deleting the first deletes both"); the generic LGT row's context delete path doesn't handle a Light payload's id-based selection cleanup ("the second cannot be deleted"). FIX: the root-children loop now skips `NodePayload::Light(_)` (lights are owned by the Lights section). HARDENING (id hygiene, same commit): (a) `LightData::default().id` 0 → 1 — the default light now carries a real allocator id matching "Sun.001" and the scenes' `next_light_id = 2` init (id 0 sat outside the allocator's range; any second id-0 light was unreachable via `light_nid` first-match-by-id); (b) NEW load-time SELF-HEAL `heal_duplicate_light_ids` (pure fn on `SceneGraph` in scene_actions.rs + app wrapper) — on project load, lights with colliding ids get fresh ids (first holder by NodeId keeps; logged `[SelfHeal]`), then `next_light_id` bumps past the max (called from project_load.rs where `recalculate_next_light_id` was); existing saved scenes with collisions heal on open; (c) verified `delete_light` removes exactly ONE node — it resolves `light_nid(id)` once and calls `scene_graph.remove(nid)` by NodeId. TESTS (+3 headless, scene_actions.rs): `default_light_id_is_allocated_range`, `heal_reassigns_duplicate_light_ids_first_holder_keeps` (dup id 1 → fresh id 4 > max, uniqueness, `light_by_id` resolves, idempotent), `heal_noop_on_unique_ids`. MANUAL: new scene → exactly ONE "Sun.001" row (in Lights section); delete it → gone; open an old save with colliding light ids → `[SelfHeal]` log, both lights selectable/deletable independently. Gates: cargo check -p app, core_math 443, app --bins 144 green single-threaded.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **Reorder above the base prim → green dot stuck on old first prim + X op-cycle "does nothing" on the new-second prim.** ROOT CAUSE: every "is the base prim" UI check keyed on FLAT/Vec index 0 (`i == 0` / `idx > 0`), but reorder (b18fe74) permutes ONLY `child_order` — the prims Vec never moves — so the UI base diverged from the FIELD base (first slot of `resolve_child_order`, which seeds the boolean fold regardless of its op: field_eval `build_scope` + volume_bake.wgsl scope machine). FIX (canonical helper, single source of truth): `SceneGraph::body_base_slot(nid) -> Option<Result<local_idx, NodeId>>` + `is_base_prim(nid, local_idx)` (scene_graph.rs, first slot of resolve_child_order) and app-side `SceneState::is_base_prim_flat(flat_idx)` (scene_state.rs, via prim_body_map). Re-routed ALL 4 flat-index base checks: outliner green dot + "(Base = no boolean op)" context menu (outliner.rs), X-key op-cycle gate (input_keyboard.rs — now gated on the CURRENT chain base, ex-base cyclable, base gets a toast), properties Boolean panel enablement (properties_sdf_shape.rs), raycast smart-cutter filter "base always selectable" (draw_selection.rs). SUB-BODY-FIRST DECISION: when the first chain slot is a sub-body, the sub-body result seeds the fold → NO prim is marked base (no green dot on any prim row; X works on every prim) — mirrors the evaluator. Ops are NEVER forced on reorder: a Subtract moved to base keeps its stored op (eval ignores it while base; acts again if moved away) — no forcing code existed, none added. Outliner rows already draw in resolve_child_order (post-b18fe74), so the dot sits on the TOP row of the chain. Test: `base_slot_follows_child_order_reorder` (scene_graph.rs) — base follows a prim reorder and the sub-body-first case. MANUAL: body with prims A,B (A first); drag B above A in the outliner → green dot moves to B, X on A cycles Union/Subtract/Intersect (toast), X on B toasts "Base of chain"; drag a sub-body to the top → no prim shows the green dot and X works on both prims.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-14 (second fix — 214c958 RE-OPENED by owner: "still doing it") — **REGRESSION (introduced by 3b05fa2): dragging an outliner row to reorder/reparent also MOVES/RESIZES the right panel** (owner, feat/sparse-3a). WHY 214c958 FAILED: it correctly diagnosed the hit-test mechanism (rows are `Sense::hover`, so a row press has no drag hit of its own and egui 0.29 latches ANOTHER drag widget as `potential_drag_id`) but fixed only ONE of the thieves — OUR splitter — by suppressing the app-side delta-read. The other thieves are egui-INTERNAL widgets whose drag deltas are consumed inside egui, unreachable by any app flag: (1) **detached mode — the `egui::Window`'s whole-body Area "move" widget** (`area.rs:453-481`: a window-sized `Sense::drag()` WidgetRect registered BEFORE contents; `*pivot_pos += move_response.drag_delta()` runs inside egui). Because it CONTAINS every press in the window, `hit_test_on_close`'s `(Some(click), Some(drag))` / `(None, Some(drag))` branches latch it for EVERY row press — label or empty space — so any row drag dragged the whole floating outliner ("all the right panel start to move"). (2) **docked mode — the SidePanel's `__resize` edge** (`panel.rs:310`, `ui.interact(resize_rect, .., Sense::drag())`, edge±5px full panel height, egui applies the width internally) — latched via the `(None,None)` nearest-widget fallback for presses near the panel's inner edge. (3) the Window's `edge_drag` resize rects (same class). REAL FIX (kills the CLASS — commit this entry): register ONE full-viewport `Sense::drag()` hit-test guard UNDER the tree rows, first thing inside the outliner ScrollArea (`outliner_draw.rs`, `outliner_tree_dnd_guard`, rect = content clip rect minus `clip_rect_margin`). Registered-first ⇒ bottom of the layer: every press on the tree now resolves `hits.drag` → the guard (a no-op — the raw-pointer row DnD keeps working on top), while clicks still resolve to the topmost click widget (label select, `check_double_click` rename, eye buttons, context menus — the "button in a movable window" branch), and later-registered widgets (scrollbar handle, height splitter, panel/window resize edges) still win DIRECT hits on their own rects, so genuine resizing is untouched. Same pattern egui itself uses for drag-to-scroll (`scroll_area.rs`: "we must do this BEFORE adding content, or we will steal input from the widgets we contain"). 214c958's splitter deferral (`outliner_drag_owns_press` gating) is REMOVED — dead once the guard exists (a row press can never latch the splitter anymore). One shared code path ⇒ docked AND detached are both covered; all 4 row DnD types (prim, body header, node, light) covered by the one guard. `outliner_draw.rs` only. Gates: cargo check -p app clean; app --bins 149 green single-threaded (verified on an isolated HEAD+fix worktree — the shared worktree carried unrelated in-flight Extrude WIP). MANUAL: docked — press anywhere on any row (label OR empty space, incl. bottom-most row and rows near the panel's left edge) and drag → row reorders, panel width AND outliner height never change; splitter strip below the tree still resizes + persists; detached (⇗) — drag rows → reorders with ZERO window movement; window still moves by title bar and resizes by edges.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-13 — **OWNER BUGS ×3: outliner auto-collapse on body selection + staggered eye icons + no resize/detach** (feat/sparse-3a). (1) AUTO-COLLAPSE: selecting/activating one body collapsed all others. ROOT CAUSE: `collapsed_bodies` had INVERTED semantics per row — active body: in-set = collapsed; non-active: in-set = expanded — plus `outliner_draw.rs` removed the active body from the set EVERY frame. The moment body A became active, every previously-active expanded body B (absent from the set) re-read under the non-active interpretation "absent = collapsed". FIX (class-eliminating): renamed to `expanded_bodies` with ONE uniform user-owned semantics (in-set = expanded, all bodies, all row states); activation auto-expands via a single INSERT on the active-change edge (`last_active_body` tracker) — never removes entries, and the user can still collapse the active body manually. All writers updated (arrow toggle, Shift+all, hover-to-expand-while-dragging, `outliner_expand_body` for Find-in-Outliner). Entering/leaving edit scope no longer touches other bodies' state. (2) EYE ALIGNMENT: eyes were inline per-row inside `ui.indent`, so they staggered with depth. FIX: NEW shared `eye_column_button()` (`outliner_actions.rs`, const `EYE_COL_W`) places every visibility toggle in ONE fixed column at the panel's left edge via `ui.put` + reserves leading space; wired into ALL 4 row types (SDF body header, prim row, generic node row poly/NURBS/group/empty/camera, light row) — one code path, inline eyes deleted. (3) OWN PANEL: outliner content extracted into ONE `draw_outliner_contents()` callable from both hosts. Docked: a drag splitter under the tree resizes it (writes the SAME `outliner_height_fraction` as the layout slider, clamps 0.2–0.8, saved to ~/.azra/layout.json on drag release). Detached: new header button (⇗/⇙) toggles `UiLayoutConfig.outliner_detached` (`#[serde(default)]`, persists in layout.json); outliner then lives in a floating resizable `egui::Window` — closing the window re-docks it. Window rect is egui-memory session-only (no cross-session UI-rect store exists; the detached FLAG does persist). MANUAL: expand bodies A+B, click body C → A+B stay open, C auto-opens once and can be re-collapsed; nest a body 2 deep → its eye + its prims' eyes align with root-level eyes in one column; drag the splitter → outliner grows/shrinks and height survives restart; click ⇗ → floating window, close it → docked again, flag survives restart. Gates: cargo check -p app clean, app --bins 149 green single-threaded (core_math untouched).

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-15 — **Ctrl+Shift+S fired Save-As AND Symmetrize in the same frame** (master; found by the input-architecture recon, independently re-verified twice before fixing). `ACT_SAVE_AS => KeyBind::ctrl_shift(S)` (keybindings.rs:354) and `ACT_SYM_SYMMETRIZE => KeyBind::ctrl_shift(S)` (:367) were BOTH `context: None`, and both are evaluated in the same upfront `ctx.input(...)` batch (input_keyboard.rs:113 / :202) then dispatched unguarded (`if save_as { self.save_scene_as(); }` :377; `if sym_symmetrize { self.symmetry_symmetrize(); }` :720). One press did both. **Severity corrected down from the recon's claim:** it reported this as priority-ladder rung 1/3 "destructive"; it is NOT — `symmetry_symmetrize` wraps its mutation in `transaction("Symmetrize")` (symmetry.rs:98) and early-returns unless symmetry is enabled and a poly body is selected, so it is undoable and gated. The real harm is rung 4 with a persistence tail: the Save-As dialog opens ON TOP of the "Symmetrized" toast, so the user saves the mutated mesh without ever seeing that it changed — the undo exists but you must know to use it. FIX: `ACT_SYM_SYMMETRIZE => KeyBind::ctrl_shift(K)`. Save-As keeps Ctrl+Shift+S (universal convention). K is admittedly arbitrary — Blender gives Symmetrize **no default hotkey at all** (Mesh > Symmetrize), which is the correct answer and is **unrepresentable today**: `KeyBind.key` is `egui::Key`, not `Option<egui::Key>`, so every action must own a chord. Revisit when the keymap plan (docs/planning/input/INPUT_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md) introduces an unbound state. **CONTEXT — this is one of 15 colliding chords, now 14** (audit over `default_bind`'s 94 binds → 75 distinct chords). Most of the other 14 are LEGITIMATE context splits that the new keymap must preserve, not "fix" (`F` = Focus + Poly Fill; `E` = Elongate + Extrude + Poly Extrude; `G` = Grab + NURBS Grab CV). At least one more is a genuine same-frame double-fire and is NOT fixed here per the one-bug-per-task rule: **`Ctrl+I` = ACT_INSTANCE + ACT_POLY_INVERT_SEL** (invert selection also creates an instance). The current `find_conflicts` (keybindings.rs:485) compares free-text `context` prose with `!=`, so it can distinguish neither case — it has both false positives and false negatives, which is why all 15 shipped. **TELL:** the symmetry family is `Ctrl+Shift+{X,Y,M,S,D,R}` but axis-Z is `Alt+Shift+Z` — because `Ctrl+Shift+Z` is Redo. Someone found ONE collision in this family and dodged it locally without auditing the other six. Gate: `cargo build -p app` green; scripted re-audit confirms `Ctrl+Shift+S -> [ACT_SAVE_AS]` alone and `Ctrl+Shift+K -> [ACT_SYM_SYMMETRIZE]` alone. MANUAL: enable symmetry (Ctrl+M) on a poly body, press Ctrl+Shift+S → Save-As dialog opens and the mesh is UNCHANGED; Ctrl+Shift+K symmetrizes with no dialog.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-16 — **Ctrl+I in poly edit dispatched BOTH Invert Selection and Create Instance (latent double-fire; the instance was NOT actually created)** (`input_keyboard.rs:1362`). The double-DISPATCH is real and confirmed: `ACT_INSTANCE => KeyBind::ctrl(I)` (keybindings.rs:348) and `ACT_POLY_INVERT_SEL => KeyBind::ctrl(I)` (:435) are both evaluated in the same upfront `ctx.input(...)` batch (:120 / :194); `KeyBindings::pressed()` (:472) is pure chord matching with NO context filtering (`ActionDef.context` is display-only prose for the rebind editor), so one Ctrl+I sets both flags. Both guards then passed simultaneously: `poly_invert_key` is gated on `poly_work_mode != Object` (:249) ✓, and `instance_key` was gated ONLY on `tool.work_mode == WorkMode::Object` (:1362) — which is **also true during poly edit**, because `poly_switch_work_mode()` sets only `self.poly_work_mode` (poly_selection.rs:1115) and never touches `tool.work_mode`; no path anywhere sets `tool.work_mode` for poly edit (`WorkMode::Face` is only the unrelated SDF extrude toggle, :1031). Both sites are live in the same frame: `poly_sub_mode` scope `[8,9,89]`, instance site `[8,9,89,645]` (the `else {}` "normal keyboard" branch, taken whenever no modal poly tool is dragging). **PREMISE CORRECTED — the reported user-visible effect ("invert selection also creates an instance", predicted in the 2026-07-15 entry above) does NOT reproduce.** `create_instance()` early-returns at `instance_actions.rs:7` unless `active_prim_index_unified()` is `Some`. `UnifiedSelection.active` is a single `Option<SceneItemId>` (types_selection.rs:22) whose `active_prim_uid()` and `active_node()` are mutually exclusive (:45-50); `derive_modeling_context()` (app_new.rs:355, run at app_update.rs:112 — BEFORE `handle_keyboard()` at :207, same frame) only yields `ModelingContext::Polygonal` from `active_node() == Some(PolygonalBody)` (:362-366) and short-circuits to `Sdf` whenever a prim is active (:358). Therefore `modeling_context == Polygonal` ⟹ active is a Node ⟹ `active_prim_index_unified() == None` ⟹ the instance call is a silent no-op. So this was a **latent** defect masked by an unrelated early-return 1000+ lines away in another file — not a live one. It is still worth fixing under No-Bandaids Q3 (tribal knowledge): the moment anyone teaches `create_instance()` to handle a selected *node* (instancing a whole PolygonalBody is an obvious, plausible feature), Ctrl+I in poly edit silently starts creating instances while inverting. FIX (mirrors the `H`/`Alt+H` precedent three lines away at :288-302 rather than inventing a second idiom): reuse the SAME in-scope `poly_sub_mode` binding — `if instance_key && self.tool.work_mode==WorkMode::Object && !poly_sub_mode`. One notion of "poly sub-mode owns this key", one code path, shared by H, Alt+H and Ctrl+I. Binding UNCHANGED — Ctrl+I stays on both actions deliberately, exactly like the legitimate context splits (`F` = Focus + Poly Fill) which must NOT be "fixed". **CLASS NOT CLOSED (filed, out of scope):** the root is four contradictory mode fields (`tool.work_mode` vs `poly_work_mode` vs `modeling_context` vs `sdf_sculpt_active`) that no invariant keeps consistent; collapsing them is an architecture task (`WorkMode::Sculpt` gates the entire voxel subsystem — blast radius exceeds the refactor budget). Until then every new global-context action must remember `!poly_sub_mode` by hand. Gate: `cargo build -p app` green (no LNK1104). NOT unit-testable — the guard lives in `handle_keyboard(&mut AzraApp, &egui::Context)` and none of the app crate's 182 tests construct an `AzraApp` (all pure-fn/cache); verified by static trace instead. MANUAL: select a polygon mesh, Tab into Vertex mode (1), select some vertices, press Ctrl+I → selection inverts, and NO ".inst" object appears in the outliner and NO "Instance created" toast fires. Then Tab back to Object mode, select an SDF prim, Ctrl+I → instance IS created (regression check: the guard must not break the Object-mode path).

## ✅ FIXED — 2026-07-16 (Ctrl+X dissolve — and every ctrl+X/C/V bind — could never fire)

- ✅ **`ACT_POLY_DISSOLVE` (Ctrl+X) NEVER DISPATCHED; owner reported "ctrl x do not work, nothing at all — no message, no change" on a FRESH cube.** ROOT CAUSE proven from the egui-winit source, not guessed: `egui-winit 0.29 src/lib.rs:759-774` intercepts `command+X/C/V`, pushes `Event::Cut`/`Event::Copy`/`Event::Paste`, and `return`s **without ever emitting the `Event::Key` for X/C/V**. So `InputState::key_pressed(Key::X)` is ALWAYS false under Ctrl, and `KeyBind::matches` — which keyed solely on `key_pressed` — could never match a `ctrl(X)` bind. That is why `ACT_POLY_DISSOLVE = ctrl(X)` (keybindings.rs:473) was dead while loop cut (`Ctrl+R`, R is not a clipboard command) worked. **NOT a regression from this session** — fundamental egui behavior + AZRA never reading Cut/Copy/Paste events (grep `Event::Cut` in app/src = 0). The earlier diagnostic's "clipboard cut clobbers the dissolve toast" theory is REFUTED by this: the clipboard handler (input_keyboard.rs:1336) uses the same dead `key_pressed(X)`, so it never fired either — nothing clobbers anything, the key is eaten before any handler sees it, hence "no message." FIX (root, one place): `KeyBind::matches` (app_types/src/keybindings.rs:110) now, when `key_pressed` fails, matches a `ctrl(X/C/V)` bind against the corresponding `Event::Cut`/`Copy`/`Paste`. Fixes dissolve AND any other ctrl(X/C/V) bind through the keymap, no call-site hardcoding. `is_cut_command` keys on `command+X` ignoring shift, so the modifier-equality check keeps `ctrl(X)` and `ctrl_shift(X)` distinct — which ALSO revives `ACT_SYM_AXIS_X = ctrl_shift(X)` (dead by the same root). Dispatch is gated on `!ctx.wants_keyboard_input()` (input_keyboard.rs:136), so a focused TextEdit's own cut does not double-fire an app action. Gate: `cargo build -p app` green (no LNK1104); `cargo test -p app_types` 11 passed. VERIFICATION IS OWNER-DRIVEN (input dispatch is not kernel-unit-testable; egui::InputState is impractical to hand-construct) — owner re-tests Ctrl+X on a cube edge. STILL OPEN, SEPARATE: the global clipboard cut/copy/paste (input_keyboard.rs:1333-1340, raw `key_pressed(X/C/V)`) is still dead by the same root — a follow-up should route it through the keymap or read the events; and subdivide-via-menu ("nothing happens") is a DIFFERENT path (no key involved) still to be diagnosed.

- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-27 — **Adding a Generator layer took ~45s (owner-reported, live-repro'd; the async-readback fix (57c1b97) had already killed the FREEZE but not the SLOWNESS).** ROOT CAUSE, proven with a new test exercising the ACTUAL panel path (not just the golden kernel gate): `curvature_key_for_graph` (node_graph_bake.rs, singular) required EVERY `SdfCurvature`/`Cavity` node in a material's graph to agree on ONE knob set, or it returned `None` and the WHOLE bake fell back to ~500 analytical CPU evals/pixel at 256×256 = 65 536 pixels (measured 6.1s on a 2-prim test body; scales past 45s on real production bodies/materials). **A material with a Generator layer on more than one channel — e.g. Roughness=Curvature at radius R1 and Bump=Cavity at radius R2, an entirely ordinary "worn surface" recipe — has two nodes with DIFFERENT knobs, so this fired on completely normal usage, not an edge case.** Proven empirically: `two_generators_different_radius_both_get_gpu_grids` reproduced `curvature_key_for_graph` returning `None` for exactly this shape before the fix. (First lead was a false trail: `lower_to_graph` — a different, scalar-only path used only by `derive_doc_from_material`'s round-trip tests — does NOT emit the Generator layer's subgraph at all; the real production entry point the live panel uses is `regen_channel_subgraph`, called from `mp_lower_rich_channels`.) The park/dispatch/drain async state machine itself (`spawn_or_park_graph_bake` / `poll_graph_curvature` / `drain_curvature_readbacks`) was already correct — it had simply never been exercised end-to-end by any test (`tests_gpu_curvature.rs` calls `dispatch_curvature_blocking` directly and never touches `sdf.curv_cache`/`sdf_curvature_masks`'s cache-consuming branch), so this coverage gap let an all-or-nothing eligibility design ship as a silent, un-caught permanent-CPU-fallback trap. FIX: `curvature_key_for_graph` → `curvature_keys_for_graph`, returning ONE grid per DISTINCT `CurvKey` (capped at `MAX_CURV_KEYS_PER_BAKE = 8`, Frame Budget Rule) instead of a single shared grid; `SdfFieldSources.curv_cache: Option<CurvGrid>` → `curv_caches: Vec<CurvGrid>`; `sdf_curvature_masks`'s fast-path lookup now finds the grid matching THAT node's own key, so two Generator layers with different settings each get their own dispatch+grid instead of both falling back. A per-key GPU miss (readback failure, no pipeline) now only drops that ONE node to the CPU path — never the whole bake. `PendingCurvBake`/`InFlightCurvBake` extended to track multiple in-flight readbacks per job, spawning the worker only once every key has settled (or failed), preserving the existing `MAX_CURV_READBACKS_PER_FRAME = 1` drain budget across ALL in-flight keys (not per-job) so the Frame Budget Rule still holds. REGRESSION GUARD ADDED (`node_graph_bake.rs::curvature_fast_path_regression`, 5 tests, permanent — not removed): (1) the exact panel-produced graph for a single fresh Generator layer stays GPU-eligible; (2) a `CurvGrid` seeded with values no CPU eval could produce is proven to be actually READ by the bake (byte-exact sRGB-encoded comparison), closing the "fast path reachable but never exercised" gap; (3) the fast path is ≥4x faster than the CPU fallback at production resolution (measured 8.5-8.8x on the synthetic test body — lower than the golden kernel test's bare 59-65x because this measures the full per-pixel node-graph-eval + sRGB-encode pipeline, not just the curvature inner loop); (4) the THE regression scenario — two Generator layers, different radii — now yields 2 keys and both bake through their own grid (non-degenerate output proven for both channels). Gate: `cargo check -p app` clean; `cargo test -p app tests_gpu_curvature` 6/6 green (golden kernel parity untouched); `cargo test -p app material_panel` 39/39 green; `cargo test -p app curvature_fast_path_regression` 5/5 green; `cargo test -p graphics` 63 pass / 4 pre-existing `rt_shadow` failures (unrelated bind-group-count mismatch, not touched); `cargo build -p app` compiles clean (LNK/file-lock at the final link step is the owner's app running — acceptable per gate). MANUAL TEST FOR OWNER: open a material with an SDF body assigned, add a Generator (Curvature) layer to Roughness, then ALSO add a Generator (Cavity) layer to Bump/Normal at a different radius — both should bake in well under a second each (watch for `[GpuCurvature] N² grid, K prims — dispatch submitted` in the console, one per generator, followed shortly by `dispatch→readback` lines — NOT a multi-second stall before any log line appears).
- ✅ FIXED 2026-07-27 — **"White gift-wrap cross" on SDF bodies (owner-reported): a curvature/cavity Generator layer painted bright bands across FLAT box face interiors, where true curvature ≈ 0.** ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in code, not speculation): the texture rung bakes over a PLANAR UV DOMAIN (`node_graph_bake.rs:9`, `is_planar_bake_domain`) — triplanar seeds through the body AABB, then reprojected onto the object via Box/triplanar. A curvature map CANNOT be bright where the surface is flat; the planar-domain bake + reprojection round-trip is the defect, not "expected" behavior. FIX (GPU_CURVATURE_KERNEL_PLAN.md P2/P3, this session): the owner's rule — "no UVs → Vertex, has UVs → UV" — is now real. **VERTEX RUNG (P2):** `gpu_curvature::encode_curvature_vertex_dispatch` feeds the ALREADY-SHIPPED `curvature_eval` kernel (a3ad48e) the DC mesh's OWN resident `verts` buffer directly at its `SEED_POSITIONS` (non-planar, single-seed) mode — zero upload, zero readback, SAME kernel the texture rung uses (structural parity, not a second WGSL port). Output lands in a NEW persistent per-body buffer (`GpuCtx.sdf_body_curvature`, generation-keyed against the mesh's own generation/vert_cap — rebuilt WHOLESALE on every re-bake rather than incrementally patched, deliberately sidestepping `pool.rs`'s bump/rebuild internals). Dispatched from `poll_vertex_curvature` (app_poll.rs, poll phase only). **CARRY:** a NEW group-2 bind group on the raster pipeline (`RasterPipeline::curvature_bgl`/`curvature_dummy_bind_group`, `pipeline.rs`) — `gbuffer.wgsl`'s `vs_main` reads `curv_vertex[vertex_index*4+1]` (the kernel's native `curv` channel) gated by a NEW independent instance flag `INSTANCE_FLAG_VERTEX_CURVATURE` (bit 2, composes with `VERTEX_COLOR`/`GRAB_TARGET`), carried FLAT to the fragment stage. Every draw site sharing the raster pipeline layout (main G-buffer pass, wire pass, `ssao.rs`'s GPU test harness) now binds group 2 — a body with no current curvature buffer gets the shared dummy; picking's separate camera-only pipeline layout correctly gets NO group-2 call at all (`CurvBind::None`). **RUNG UI (P3):** the "Vertex" combo entry is un-gated in `view.rs` (was `add_enabled(false, ..)`); new Generator layers now auto-default to `VertexCache` when the active body has no authored UVs (`GenCtx::has_uvs`, read honestly from `cache.poly_custom_data[nid].uv` — NOT the confirmed-bad "any poly body exists in the scene" heuristic at the texture-space projection gate, which was left as-is since fixing it is a separate P1-2 triage item). Every generator-eligible body today is SDF-only (`has_sdf` gates the "Add generator" button) and `sdf_mesh.wgsl` hardwires `uv=0` for every SDF vertex, so `has_uvs` is false for every eligible body today — Vertex is now the correct, honest default. **HONEST REMAINING GAP:** the UV-space texture bake (baking each texel at its REAL surface position via the UV→surface mapping, not the planar `p=(u,v,0)` domain) was NOT built this session — it is a separable project (the fragment shader samples ALL channel/layer content through ONE composited texture-map slot per channel; substituting a per-vertex value into that architecture for arbitrary multi-layer channels needs its own design, not a bolt-on). The planar-domain bake remains the "Texture" rung's implementation for the (currently nonexistent) case of a poly body with real UVs — it is simply no longer the DEFAULT for SDF bodies, which is where the cross actually appeared. Filed as the named follow-on: "UV-space Generator bake for poly bodies with authored UVs." SEMANTIC TEST (the class that would have caught the cross): `vertex_rung_box_flat_face_reads_zero_edge_reads_high` (tests_gpu_curvature.rs) dispatches the PRODUCTION vertex-rung kernel path over hand-placed box "vertices" — measured: face-center curv=+0.00000 mask=0.0000 (flat, correct), edge-midpoint curv=+0.98606 mask=1.0 convex=1.0 (strongly convex, correct), corner curv=+0.99293 (higher than a single edge, correct ordering). Gate: `cargo test -p graphics` 63/4 (4 pre-existing rt_shadow, untouched); `cargo test -p render` 53/0 (the `ssao.rs`/`gtao` GPU tests exercise the raster pipeline directly and needed the SAME group-2 dummy bind fix — this is exactly the device-loss audit the task demanded, and it caught a real gap immediately); `cargo test -p app tests_gpu_curvature` 7/7 (6 existing + 1 new); `cargo test -p app curvature_fast_path_regression` 4/4; `cargo test -p app material_panel` 39/39; `cargo check -p app` clean; `cargo build -p app` clean (verified via an alternate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` since the default target's exe was locked by the owner's running app — LNK1104 there is the documented acceptable case). MANUAL TEST FOR OWNER: on your box repro, add a Curvature Generator layer (now auto-defaults to Vertex rung) — the edges should trace the 12 dihedral edges as a cage, with NO cross/banding on the flat faces. Switch the rung combo to "Texture" to see the OLD planar-domain behavior for comparison (still available, now honestly labeled with a hover-text caveat about when it's wrong).

  44% of a uniform environment at grazing view (79% at n·v 0.5). ROOT: `pt_smith_G1` used the

  fed GGX alpha, so even a mirror kept k = 0.125. FIX: height-correlated Smith G2 (Heitz 2014,

- ✅ FIXED 2026-10-13 — **RASTER-MATERIAL-REASSIGN-STALE** (found by the AZRA_PARITY gate,

  `RasterMaterial` (last additive prim → `resolve_prim_material`) and re-gathers only on SCENE/MESH,
  transform/visibility marks, or a `material_generation` change. `add_material` bumps that generation —
  which is why a fresh material "worked" — but a reassign moved nothing: `hash_prim_slice` ignores
  materials, so the write is bake-identical (no bake, no mesh event), and PT only saw it because the
  callers set `prim_buf_stale`. Same class hit EMBEDDED-material edits (properties panel → mirror).
  FIX: `SceneGraph::note_prim_material_write(prev, new)` (next to the resolver, compares exactly the two
  prim fields it reads: `material_id`, embedded `material`) bumps `material_generation`. Called from the
  two mandated prim funnels: `mirror_prim_to_graph` (every `write_prim` + egui mirror, BEFORE the
  bake-identity early return) and `sync_flat_cache` (graph-direct body-wide assigns: Ctrl+M on a body,
  body combo, material import). `PbrMaterial`/`MaterialLayer`/`NoiseLayer` now derive `PartialEq`.
  GATES: parity gate reverted to ONE reused material per case; `sun,hdri_sun × 3 mats × base` —
  fixed build: the 3 `hdri_sun` raster shots (all reassigns of existing ids) differ (0.568 / 0.520 /
  0.978, distinct PNG hashes); SABOTAGE build (bump disabled): all 3 byte-identical at 0.978 (stuck on
  the last material) — the original symptom. Unit: `material_assign::reassign_tests` (write_prim
  reassign, body-wide sync_flat_cache reassign, embedded edit; non-material writes must NOT bump).
  OPEN: manual Ctrl+M reassign check in AZRA_UI=v2 not yet done by a human (desktop control declined
  in-session) — owner to confirm.

  ops): `prune_poly_sel_to_live` (poly_selection/pick.rs) enforces "every component id names a
  LIVE element of the active mesh" — selection, hidden set, hover, active vertex + history — via
  the kernel's O(1) `is_*_live`; runs inside the per-frame `reconcile_poly_sel_body` AND right
  before the overlay draw, so knife/boolean/dice/any future rebuild cannot leak a stale id. GATE:
  `stale_component_id_tests` reproduces delete → compacting rebuild with pre-rebuild ids; verified

  `poly_knife::…::classic_knife_keeps_selection_on_the_same_geometry` (real commit path +

## DF-full cold compile never finishes — 2026-10-13

- ✅ FIXED 2026-10-13 — **DFFULL-COLD-COMPILE** (owner "cold-mode freezes"; found by the isolated
  viewport probe). Entering PBR requests the DF-full deferred pipeline on a background thread; its
  NVIDIA cold compile **never finished** (killed at >5 min in a standalone bench; in the probe the
  process grew to ~90 GB RAM over 27 min). While it runs, `compiling_heavy_shader` blocks the PT
  warmup (`PtPipelineWarmup::can_request`), so Path Trace **never started** — the "frozen PT"
  symptom. PRE-EXISTING, not the SDK upgrade: the identical WGSL on HEAD's wgpu 22 also failed to
  finish in 5 min (a warm driver cache hid it); but the wgpu 25 upgrade changes the SPIR-V, so every
  cache misses and EVERY user would hit it on first launch. ROOT CAUSE (measured, not guessed): the
  driver inlines every `scene_sdf` call. `calc_curvature` made 11 calls and is reached from ~8
  material-eval sites (Lit and PBR each carried a full dna→node→[blended]→plain chain), so the
  inlined size was ~307K statements, ~240K of them curvature probes. FIX (graphics/src):
  `calc_curvature` = ONE `scene_sdf` call site in an 11-tap loop (same taps, order, summation);
  shared `sdf_central_diff_offset` stencil + `sdf_central_gradient` (one call site) replace the
  6-call reflection normal; ONE hoisted `surf_mat` evaluation (DEFERRED_MATERIAL) serves both
  Lit and PBR with the unchanged gates. Inlined size ~307K → ~37K; cold DF-full compile
  never → 35–42 s (5 runs, `graphics/examples/pt_compile_bench.rs`, salted to defeat the driver
  cache). GATE: `sdf_probe_loop_gpu_test` runs the production loop functions next to the original
  unrolled forms on GPU (4096 points, 4 tap steps incl. the 0.19 cavity radius): curvature within
  FMA rounding (0.74× tolerance), gradient ≤1.3e-7. graphics 95/95. OPEN: one of six bench runs
  ended in an access violation inside pipeline creation and did not reproduce in five reruns —
  unexplained, watch for it. The interactive PT variant still takes ~110 s / 3.6 GB cold.

## PT convergence and frame latency — 2026-10-12

- **PT-SAMPLE-PRECISION:** corrected large-index FP32 jitter quantization with the existing
  integer PCG generator; long-frame/4K-pixel GPU regressions pass.
- **PT-HISTORY-PRECISION:** raw FP32 history separated from FP16 display; removed 2048 cap,
  weighted actual variable-SPP counts and added Welford variance. History reset and small
  updates beyond 2048 covered on GPU.
- **PT-DENOISE-ORDER:** distinct ordered per-pass parameters; cached upload buffer, no per-pass
  submission or per-frame allocation. Colour/ReSTIR reprojection uniforms also separated.
- **PT-DENOISE-CONVERGENCE:** geometry-gradient and sample-variance guides; no age-only shutdown.
  GPU ordering, dark-detail and geometry-edge regressions pass.
- **PT-COLD-STALL:** heavy PT compile moved to capped background readiness work; raster draft
  persists and interaction latch prevents a readiness-driven mid-drag switch. Cold viewport
  verification remains a gate, not inferred from module tests.
- **PT-BUDGET-TIMING:** completed GPU intervals replace CPU encode/submit elapsed time.
  Idle bounce target remains stable; unused full-history GI warming removed.
- **PT-RTX-PARITY:** ✅ INTEGRATED + PARITY-VERIFIED 2026-10-13. Hardware ray queries
  (wgpu 25 BLAS/TLAS, `app_gpu::native_rt`) replace ONLY `pt_trace_scene`/`pt_occluded` in the
  SAME canonical WGSL; routed through one frame encoder/one submit (`pt_native::PtFrameEncoder`),
  backend latched outside interaction with an accumulation reset, software fallback when not
  ready. Isolated full-res viewport probe (3215×1710, noise-albedo box, 1 spp, 6 bounces):
  RTX vs `AZRA_PT_SOFTWARE_TRAVERSAL=1` captures identical — object mean |Δ| 0.00008 @129 spp,
  0.00001 @257 spp, zero bias, ~100× below the image noise. Zero GPU validation errors.
  **No speed claim:** on this one-box scene PT pass GPU time is ~1.5–2.6 ms either way; an RTX
  win needs a dense-geometry benchmark (OPEN).
- **PT-STRIPE-VIEWPORT:** banding metric on the full-res PT surface (row-coherent / column-
  coherent high-pass energy) = 0.50 at 129 spp and 0.90 at 257 spp (stripes would read ≫1);
  matches the raster reference (0.52); visual 1:1 inspection clean. CAVEAT: owner's original
  repro was a dark GLOSSY rail — that exact material is not in the harness scene (OPEN: re-check
  on the owner's scene). Variance convergence is proven by the GPU unit tests, not by these
  captures (C and D use different texture scales).
- **PT-COLD-READY (measured 2026-10-13, first-ever launch, cold driver cache):** DF-full 39–44 s
  (was: never — see DFFULL-COLD-COMPILE above), then PT full 7.6–9.1 s + interactive 118–127 s
  + native RTX full+interactive 121 s, compiled serially → ~4 min to PT-ready the first time
  (raster draft stays live; caches make later launches fast). OPEN: the interactive variant and
  the native pair dominate; the native compile also runs when software traversal is forced.

## PT held on the raster draft for ~5 min after a PT shader edit — 2026-10-13

- ✅ FIXED 2026-10-13 — **PT-COLD-WARMUP-BUNDLED** (owner: the path tracer "looks broken" after a
  PT shader edit). MEASURED cold (pipeline cache miss): `PtCompiledPipelines::compile` built, on the
  one warmup thread and in sequence, PT full (~8.8 s), PT interactive (~122 s), the native RT pair
  (~162 s), then denoise/upscale, and delivered NOTHING until all were done (app_poll.rs) — so
  `pt_cold` kept the viewport on the raster draft for ~293 s behind a 13 pt corner badge, although
  the display kernel existed after ~9 s. FIX (staged warmup, same single worker + channel):
  `gpu_init::compile_pt_warmup_stages` sends `PtWarmupStage::Full` (full kernel + denoise +
  upscale), then `Interactive`, then `Native`; `poll_background_tasks` installs each on arrival
  (`install_pt_warmup_stage`, Frame Ordering Contract; bind groups rebuilt in viewport_render).
  Readiness is per stage (`PtPendingStages`, `ensure_pt_tri_pipeline` = full only,
  `ensure_pt_interactive_pipeline`), so PT goes live at ~9 s. Until the interactive kernel lands,
  interaction runs the FULL kernel at the interaction budget (half-res, 1 spp, ≤2 bounces); the
  choice is latched like the native backend (`latched_pt_choice`, shared with the RTX backend latch
  it was extracted from): a kernel that lands mid-drag is adopted only after the episode + 8-frame
  cooldown, never mid-drag. Native RT keeps the software fallback until stage 3. A re-warm retires
  the stale interactive/native kernels so a new full kernel is never paired with old-source ones.
  UI: a large banner ("Preparing path tracer…") while the display kernel is missing, a small dim
  note while only interactive/native are pending. GATES (app_poll `pt_pipeline_readiness_tests`):
  `staged_warmup_delivers_full_first_and_tracks_each_stage`,
  `interaction_kernel_landing_mid_episode_is_adopted_only_after_the_latch`,
  `worker_lost_after_full_stage_reports_only_the_missing_stages`,
  `warmup_notice_is_prominent_only_while_the_display_kernel_is_missing`.
- OPEN (follow-up, out of scope): the ~122 s cold compile of the INTERACTIVE kernel itself
  (DFFULL-COLD-COMPILE class — driver inlining) is untouched; staging only stops it from gating
  the PT display. Not yet verified in the live app with a cold cache.

## RASTER-PT-BRIGHTNESS-GAP — "everything still feels dark" (raster vs PT), 2026-10-13

GATE (new, repeatable): `AZRA_PARITY` (`core_engine/app/src/parity_gate.rs`). Run the release exe with
`AZRA_UI=v2 AZRA_PARITY=<out> AZRA_SHOT_FULLRES=1 AZRA_PARITY_HDRI=<file.hdr>` (isolated `LOCALAPPDATA`
recommended). It builds one SDF sphere (r 0.8), camera on the sun azimuth 30° up, tonemapper None
(Linear), exposure 1, then for {sun, hdri, hdri_sun} × {diel_rough a0.5 r0.8, metal_smooth a0.9 r0.15,
metal_rough a0.9 r0.7} captures raster variants {base, nossao, nofill, noprobe, refine} + converged PT
(256 frames) and writes `parity_report.tsv` (centre-crop mean LINEAR luminance, raster/PT ratio, clip
fraction). All numbers below: AZRA_UI=v2, Barce_Rooftop_C_3k.hdr, RTX 4090, 3348x1989. The v2 shell
changes no render default (no init-time writes to exposure/SSAO/env/lights/tonemap; ui2 only edits them
from widgets).

- ✅ FIXED 2026-10-13 — **PT-SUN-INVERTED**: `pathtrace_tri_entry.wgsl` negated the directional light
  vector at all 4 directional sites (`pt_light_select_weight`, `pt_light_spatial_bin`,
  `pt_light_is_visible`, `pt_sample_light`). The packed vector is TO the sun (`LightData::direction()`,
  `render/src/shadows.rs` dir_to_sun, deferred N·L, `rt_shadow_entry` rays, analytic PT) → the path
  tracer lit the ANTI-sun hemisphere. Sun-facing sphere centre: PT 0.0000 → 0.1419 (analytic
  0.5/π·cos25°·0.98 = 0.141 ✓). This — not a dark raster — is the earlier "raster ~7× darker than PT"
  measurement: that harness's default camera sits BELOW the horizon (orbit pitch +0.3 ⇒ eye y −2.4),
  so raster correctly showed the sun-shadowed underside while PT lit it with the inverted sun. GUARD:
  `graphics::sun_direction_convention_gate` (all renderers read light_dir_v as to-sun).
- ✅ FIXED 2026-10-13 — **AUTO-PROBE-INSIDE-GEOMETRY** (the real raster darkening): with Progressive
  Refine ON (runtime toggle, default OFF) the auto reflection + light probe is centred on the union of
  instance AABBs — i.e. INSIDE a lone object — so the cube captured the object's interior. Light-probe
  SH (weight 1) replaced the HDRI diffuse and the probe replaced the HDRI reflection: HDRI-only
  raster/PT diel_rough 1.051 → 0.787, metal_smooth 0.996 → **0.449**, metal_rough 0.949 → **0.333**
  (chrome read as flat grey).
  FIX = a probe VALIDITY rule measured from the capture itself (Unity-APV-style back-face validity),
  failing CLOSED to the HDRI IBL — not a placement nudge, not a brightness fudge. In probe frames
  (`CameraUniforms.frame_flags.x`) `fs_gbuffer` writes `PROBE_BACKFACE_MARK` (−1) into the body_index
  target for back-facing fragments (same facing test as the two-sided normal flip, recorded before the
  flip); `probe_capture` stores the per-texel FREE fraction (miss or front-face hit) in cube alpha, the
  mip chain averages it, and `probe_sh_project` integrates it solid-angle-weighted into `probe_sh[9].y`.
  The GPU leaves SH valid = 0; a 16-B readback (`probe_collect_verdict`, map_async → mpsc) publishes the
  probe params + SH valid only when free ≥ `PROBE_MIN_FREE_FRACTION` (0.5). Facing, not point-in-mesh:
  a ROOM's walls face INTO the room (free ≈ 1) while a solid's interior shows only back faces (free ≈ 0).
  Gate (AZRA_UI=v2, Barce_Rooftop_C_3k, hdri, base vs refine): diel 1.050 / **1.046**, metal_smooth
  0.996 / **0.989**, metal_rough 0.950 / **0.945** — `[PROBE] REJECTED … free 0.000`. Closed room
  (`AZRA_PARITY_SCENE=room`, SDF box + Shell, eye in the air): `[PROBE] baked … free 1.000`,
  probe_ready=true, chrome reflects the walls (centre lum 0.186 HDRI-only → 0.090 with the probe).
  Also: toggle-off now resets a rejected/in-flight round (re-enable used to keep the old sig → never
  re-baked) and clears SH valid; probe capture BGs are dropped with the G-buffer/HDR rebuild.
  KNOWN LIMIT: a room modelled as an OUTWARD-wound closed box is a solid block by orientation → fails
  closed to the HDRI (correct-by-orientation; relocation/authored probes are the follow-up).
- OPEN — **RASTER-IBL-UNOCCLUDED-INDOORS** (found by the room gate, confirmed independently by session
  ee91f3): inside a closed room the raster HDRI IBL is not occluded by the walls (only SSAO darkens
  it), so raster is 8–20× brighter than PT (PT ≈ 0 with HDRI-only lighting). With refine ON the valid
  room probe replaces the HDRI specular + diffuse with the captured room, but the captured walls are
  themselves lit by the unoccluded IBL. Needs an occlusion/visibility term for the env IBL (design
  decision — not a probe bug).
- ✅ FIXED 2026-10-13 — **PARITY-GATE-WRONG-HDRI** (gate measured the default env): the gate requested
  AZRA_PARITY_HDRI on its first tick; that request was dropped as stale by the startup env reset and
  `LoadingEnv` accepted ANY env (`env_hdr_width > 0`), so a fresh isolated profile silently measured
  `neutral_dark_0.003.hdr` (every lum ≈ 0.0015, ratios ≈ 1.000 — a green on nothing). Now the HDRI is
  requested after scene setup and `LoadingEnv` waits for `env_source_path == AZRA_PARITY_HDRI`
  (prints `[PARITY] env ready`, panics naming the installed env otherwise).
  NOTE (import 2026-10-14): imported into root from worktree laughing-chaum-a5ce3c (uncommitted WIP).
  The gate's own room scene was NOT taken — root keeps the AZRA_PARITY_SCENE=room scene that came
  with the normalization patch; only the PARITY-GATE-WRONG-HDRI fix was ported into parity_gate.rs.
- ✅ FIXED 2026-10-13 (see the follow-up entry below; was "OPEN, owner decision") — **RASTER-DIRECT-UNNORMALIZED**: deferred direct light is
  `albedo·E·N·L` (no 1/π) and spec `F·D·N·L` (no G/(4·N·L·N·V)), while raster IBL and PT are
  normalized (albedo/π, full Cook-Torrance). After the PT fix, sun-only raster/PT: diel 3.41 (≈π·1.09;
  nofill 3.29), metal_smooth 9.24, metal_rough 4.41 (raster clips 61%). hdri_sun: 2.20 / 2.05 / 2.49.
  Raster is BRIGHTER than PT under the sun, not darker; normalizing it would dim sunlit raster ~3×.
- MEASURED, not causes: HDRI-only raster IBL matches PT (diel 1.051, metal_smooth 0.996, metal_rough
  0.949). SSAO on/off ≤0.3% on this scene (no occluders); procedural fill = 3.5% of sun diffuse;
  `noprobe` = `base` (probes only bake with Progressive Refine). PT bounce-0 ambient fill uses
  `amb·0.25·(1−metal)` vs raster `amb` (default ambient 0, not in the gate).
- OPEN — **RASTER-MATERIAL-REASSIGN-STALE** (found by the gate): re-assigning an EXISTING graph
  material to an SDF prim (write_prim + prim_buf_stale, the material_assign.rs sequence) leaves the
  RASTER on the previous material (byte-identical PNGs across 3 materials) while PT updates; assigning
  a freshly created material works. The gate creates a material per (condition, material) group.

### RASTER-DIRECT-UNNORMALIZED — ✅ FIXED 2026-10-13 (owner decision: normalize + physical defaults)

- FIX (`graphics/src/deferred_entry.wgsl`, one shader edit): every raster direct-light site now uses
  the path tracer's EXACT BRDF via new `direct_*` helpers (copies of `pt_fresnel_schlick`, `pt_ggx_D`,
  `pt_smith_G2`, `pt_eval_f_cos`): diffuse `(1 − F(v·h))(1 − metal)·albedo/π·N·L`, specular
  `F·D·G/(4·N·L·N·V)·N·L`, alpha `max(roughness², 0.001)`; sphere-light Karis widening kept. Sites:
  PBR light loop, Lit-branch loop, both procedural fills (now `(1 − metal)/π`), SDF_REFLECT hit
  shading. Removed the `1 − 0.7·metal` diffuse weight (metals kept 30% Lambert). Other raster paths
  checked: render/src/gbuffer.wgsl (shadow bias only), sculpt raymarch / voxel / SDF mesh shaders
  (G-buffer writers, no lighting), CPU material preview (`mat_preview.rs`, already normalized).
- DEFAULTS: light intensity = irradiance at normal incidence. Default sun = π
  (`core_math::scene_graph::DEFAULT_SUN_IRRADIANCE`, also `graphics::LightConfig`): a white card
  facing it has exit radiance 1.0 = display white at exposure 1 — exactly the old default look (the
  old shader's `albedo·1·N·L`). Point 1.5π, spot 2π (same factor). No save migration (pre-production).
- GATE (AZRA_PARITY, AZRA_UI=v2, default sun π), raster/PT centre crop, base variant:
  sun diel 1.039 (nofill 1.000) · metal_smooth 0.933 · metal_rough 0.998; hdri 1.049 · 0.996 · 0.951;
  hdri_sun 1.042 · 0.979 · 0.989. Before: sun 3.41 · 9.24 · 4.41, hdri_sun 2.20 · 2.05 · 2.49. Default
  diel sphere centre: 0.484 before (sun 1) → 0.463 now (sun π; −4% = the (1 − F) term).
  metal_smooth reads lowest because its sun highlight is a near-delta peak sitting at the crop edge.
  `refine` variant still 0.33–0.55 under HDRI = AUTO-PROBE-INSIDE-GEOMETRY (separate session — now ✅ FIXED, entry above: refine 1.046 / 0.989 / 0.945).
- GUARD: `graphics::direct_brdf_parity_gpu_test` evaluates the deferred `direct_*` and the PT
  `pt_eval_f_cos` (both sliced from the shipped WGSL) on 405 (θl, θv, φ, roughness, metal) cases —
  equal within 1e-4 relative.
- SIDE EFFECTS: metals under a plain sun read darker than before (they no longer get a fake Lambert
  term; this matches PT). Volumetric fog in-scatter is `E·phase` and scales with the sun irradiance
  (π× at the default sun). stress_test/soak scenes keep their hardcoded intensities (now ~π× dimmer).
- FOUND (not fixed here): in a closed room (gate `AZRA_PARITY_SCENE=room`) raster is 8–20× brighter
  than PT — the HDRI IBL/specular are not occluded by the walls (only SSAO/probe); PT is dark inside.
